title: Stepmother Supreme (AKA Yunchu's Vengeance)
author: Zhao Yunzi
synopsis:
[Film/TV rights already sold. Drama titled  Yunchu's Vengeance to be released 2026]

In her past life, Yun Chu devoted herself entirely to supporting her husband, raising his illegitimate children, and helping the Xie family rise to power and prominence — only to be repaid with the most brutal betrayal. The entire Yun clan, over a hundred people, was executed. And the very child she had raised with her own hands forced poisoned wine down her throat.
As the poison burned through her, she made one vow: if she ever got another life, she would make every one of them suffer a hundredfold.
She fought with everything she had to break free from the endless cycle of fate — and was reborn at the age of twenty.
She opens her eyes to find a row of Xie family children standing before her, each warmly calling her "Mother." These are the very people who destroyed the Yun clan, and she intends to spare not a single one.
The eldest loves studying? Then she'll cut off his path to a career in officialdom. The second loves martial arts? She'll make sure he can never set foot in the military. The eldest daughter craves power and status? She'll arrange a noble marriage — and a lifetime of widowhood. The youngest is useless? Then let him fend for himself.
On this path of revenge, Yun Chu will show no mercy.
But then —
"Mama!"
"You're our mama!"
Two soft little children press into her arms.
A man stands before her: "I raised them for four years. Now it's your turn."

chapters.title: Go Kneel in the Ancestral Hall
chapters.content:
Her head was splitting.

The pain cut straight to her core.

Yun Chu forced her eyes open with great effort.

A face slowly came into focus before her. It was the eldest son of the Xie family, Xie Shi'an.

The scenes from before she had lost consciousness replayed themselves in her mind, one after another. The Yun household had been raided. Her grandfather had taken his own life. Her parents had been thrown in chains and hauled off to prison. Every last soul of the Yun family, over a hundred people, had been sentenced to death by beheading.

All of it was the doing of the man now standing before her.

Without a moment's thought, she raised her hand and struck him across the face with every ounce of strength she had.

Xie Shi'an was caught completely off guard and was knocked to the ground.

"Mother?"

His face was written over with pure disbelief.

Yun Chu was equally stunned.

It was only then that she truly looked at him. The Xie Shi'an before her was young and unformed, with none of the commanding authority and imposing presence she remembered from his years of power. How could a man of twenty-six or twenty-seven look so boyish, so raw?

She looked down at her own hands. The skin was white as porcelain, without a single burn scar.

A wild, impossible thought rose in her mind.

Xie Shi'an picked himself up off the floor and clasped his hands in a respectful bow. "If I have done something wrong, I ask that Mother tell me plainly."

Yun Chu's lips moved. "How old are you this year?"

Xie Shi'an did not understand why she was asking this, but he answered all the same, obediently. "Twelve."

Yun Chu's hand clenched into a tight fist.

She was only eight years older than this son of hers. Did that mean she had returned to the year she turned twenty?

Her gaze settled on Xie Shi'an's face. She had struck him with everything she had, and his cheek was red and swollen.

And yet it could not extinguish even a ten-thousandth of the hatred burning in her heart.

"You are already twelve years old and you still do not know where you have gone wrong?" She pressed the towering fury back down inside her and spoke in a measured tone. "Go kneel in the ancestral hall and think carefully about where your fault lies."

Xie Shi'an's eyes widened in surprise.

He had been at his mother's side for four years now, and she had never once raised her hand against him. She had never even spoken a harsh word to him.

And yet today...

He parted his lips as if to say something, but then he met Yun Chu's gaze, and the chilling coldness in her eyes made the words die before they reached his tongue.

He lowered his head. "Yes."

A command from his mother was not to be defied.

He turned and walked out.

Yun Chu waved her hand wearily.

The two maidservants in the room did not dare breathe. They bowed their heads and quietly slipped out.

She sat on the edge of the bed and looked out at the courtyard beyond the window. The crabapple tree by the courtyard wall was one she had planted in the first year after she came to the Xie household as a bride.

When she thought about her past life, she found it pitiable and laughable, and most of all, utterly tragic.

She had been the eldest legitimate daughter of the Yun General's household, born with a silver spoon in her mouth. Her grandfather was a great general. Her father was a great general. The Yun family was deeply beloved by the people, and precisely because of that, the Emperor feared that their glory outshone his own. Her marriage had therefore been arranged with extraordinary caution.

Her mother had spent two years searching before she finally selected a match she felt was right: that year's top imperial scholar, Xie Jingyu.

The Xie family was of humble origin. By marrying him, she was marrying beneath her station, and her family had considered it an excellent arrangement. It would not invite the Emperor's suspicion, nor would it leave her at the mercy of a powerful husband's family.

The night of their wedding, she had conceived a child. Each day after that, she had imagined what the baby would be like.

But then, eight months into her pregnancy, she had taken a fall and bled so severely that the child was born early and did not survive. The physician told her she would never conceive again.

Barrenness was one of the seven grounds on which a husband could divorce his wife. Yet the Xie family had not cast her out. They had cared for her with great consideration and maintained her full honor as the legal wife of the household. At the time, she had felt nothing but gratitude.

And so, when she learned that Xie Jingyu had fathered a child before their wedding night, she had not allowed herself to feel any resentment.

When Xie Jingyu proposed that all his children born outside the marriage be registered under her name, she had been grateful that her husband was giving her a foothold in the Xie household.

At this thought, a scornful smile drifted across Yun Chu's face.

She had died at the age of thirty-four. The Xie family had been flourishing by then, with children and grandchildren filling the halls. Every single one of those children had been raised and educated by her own hands. She had poured her heart and soul into them. The scars on her hands were from saving one of the children from a fire. A daughter of the great General's household had bent herself into the shape of a virtuous wife, taken up the responsibilities of a stepmother, and given everything she had to give, asking only that the children grow up safe and bring honor to the family name.

And they had, indeed, done exactly that.

But once the Xie family rose to prominence at court, it was against the Yun family that they turned.

The eldest son had orchestrated a scheme to frame the Yun family for treason.

The second son had planted the fabricated evidence inside the Yun household.

The third son had placed the poison in her hands with his own.

The fourth, the fifth, the youngest... they had all watched with cold eyes as she drank it down.

The poisoned wine had barely passed her lips before the pain devoured her to the bone.

She had believed she was dying.

And then she had woken up at the age of twenty, four years after Xie Shi'an had first come to live under her roof.

She had poured boundless effort into raising Xie Shi'an after he was registered in her name. Had she not laid the groundwork and paved his path, how could he have achieved what he did? How could he have had the power to destroy the Yun family in the first place?

When it came down to it, she was the one who had brought ruin upon her own family.

Yun Chu forced back her tears.

The raid on the Yun household was still more than a decade away. Now that she had been reborn, she would not allow it to happen again.

The Xie Shi'an who would go on to top the imperial examinations three times in a row, enter the Grand Secretariat, and wield great power was, at this moment, nothing more than a twelve-year-old boy.

There was still time. Everything could still be changed.

Yun Chu sorted through her thoughts and slowly drifted off to sleep.

When she woke again, the amber light of dusk was pouring through the window into the bedchamber, and it all felt like something out of a dream.

"My lady, you are awake?"

At the sound of movement, a maidservant lifted the curtain and came inside.

"Half an hour ago, Zhou Mama from the old mistress's side came by. She asked that you go to Anshou Hall once you have risen."

Yun Chu looked at the two maidservants who had entered.

Of the four personal attendants she had brought with her from the General's household when she married into the Xie family, only Ting Feng and Ting Xue had remained by her side throughout.

Ting Yu had climbed into Xie Jingyu's bed the year she was pregnant, and had become Concubine Yu of the Xie household.

Ting Shuang had died during the great fire at the Xie estate, crushed by a burning beam that had fallen on her while she was trying to save Yun Chu.

Yun Chu looked into the mirror. Ting Shuang was combing her hair, her face creased with worry. "My lady, the old mistress has surely summoned you over the matter of the young master. You had the young master kneeling in the ancestral hall, and he had not even knelt for the length of a quarter hour before the old mistress had him stand up again. She is likely coming to call you to account."

Yun Chu smiled. "I am a little hungry. Have the meal brought in first."

In her past life, weighed down by guilt over her failure to bear children, she had dragged herself to the old mistress's summons no matter how ill she was.

Now that she had been reborn, if she was still going to be as careful and self-effacing as before, putting the Xie family above all else, then what was the point of living this second life?

Ting Shuang quickly called for the food to be brought in.

Looking at the table spread with dishes, Yun Chu found that she had quite an appetite.

Once she had eaten her fill, she changed her clothes and made her way to Anshou Hall.

In her past life, the old mistress had died peacefully in her sleep after Xie Shi'an entered the Grand Secretariat. Mourners had worn the threshold of the hall smooth, and her send-off had been a spectacle of grandeur.

But now, Xie Jingyu was only a minor fifth-rank official, and Xie Shi'an was twelve years old.

The Xie family was still nothing more than an unremarkable little household in the capital.

chapters.title: The Xie Family's Sinner
chapters.content:
Anshou Hall.

The old Madame Xie was seated at the head of the room. Below her sat Xie Shi'an, his cheek red and swollen. Maids and matrons clustered around on all sides.

"Mother."

Xie Shi'an rose and bowed in greeting to Yun Chu.

"An'er is such a good child. He is respectful and filial toward you in every way." The old mistress began her reproach at once. "How could you bring yourself to slap him? How could you make him kneel in the ancestral hall? Just look at this face of his, swollen up like that. The physician said it will take three days to go down."

"So this is what the old mistress called me here for." An inexplicable smile played at the corners of Yun Chu's lips. "An'er, did you not tell the old mistress why I punished you?"

Xie Shi'an kept his head bowed. "Your son did not know."

Yun Chu's voice cooled. "The whole point of kneeling in the ancestral hall is to think through where you have gone wrong. Since you have not thought it through, you may continue kneeling."

"Chu'er, you have always been generous and gentle. Why are you being so severe today?" The old mistress furrowed her brow. "What in the world did An'er do?"

Yun Chu smiled.

Indeed. She had been gentle with the concubines' children, magnanimous toward the concubines themselves. She had managed the household from within and cultivated connections beyond its walls, holding up half the sky above the Xie family. And yet, all that time, how had these people treated her?

The old mistress and Madame Xie, along with Xie Jingyu, respected her on the surface while quietly using her to drain the Yun family dry. Those sons and daughters called her Mother without ceasing, yet not one of them had ever truly held her in their hearts. And every one of those concubines, including her own attendant turned Concubine Yu, had mocked her in secret for her inability to bear children.

What had been called her generosity and magnanimity was, in truth, both the Xie family's way of controlling her and her own way of suppressing herself.

She spoke in an even tone. "Ting Shuang, go to Qingsong Pavilion and bring back the calligraphy and paintings the young master has been working on recently."

Ting Shuang accepted the order and went immediately.

The old Madame Xie frowned. If it had to do with calligraphy and paintings, then the matter was connected to his studies. An'er had been sharp since he was small, an excellent student praised by everyone. She truly could not imagine what he might have done wrong in that regard.

Before long, Ting Shuang returned with the calligraphy and paintings.

Yun Chu leafed through them, pulled out one piece of writing, and handed it to Xie Shi'an. "Read it aloud yourself."

The color had already drained from Xie Shi'an's face. His lips pressed together in a tight line. He began to recite in a measured voice. "He who wishes a tree to grow tall must first secure its roots. He who wishes a river to flow far..."

The old Madame Xie was no illiterate old woman. Her husband had been a xiucai, her son a juren, and her grandson Xie Jingyu had been the top imperial scholar. She had long prided herself on belonging to a family of scholarly refinement, and years of that influence meant she recognized these words at once. They were from a memorial written to the Emperor by an official of centuries past, urging the Emperor to remain vigilant in times of peace and to cultivate virtue and righteousness.

She frowned. "What is wrong with this admonition?"

"Nothing is wrong with the admonition itself." Yun Chu's voice was cold. "But at the end of the passage, he has written something treasonous."

The old mistress snatched the paper from Xie Shi'an's hands.

"...the Emperor Yang stripped the people of their livelihoods; Heaven's mandate cannot be appeased by force. I offer this counsel to Your Majesty: cease the taking of bribes and do not encroach upon what is not yours..." The old mistress went pale with shock as she read these lines. "An'er, why did you write this?"

Yun Chu's smile was cold.

In Xie Shi'an's study, such sentiments could be found everywhere. It was plain to see that he harbored a deep grievance against the reigning Emperor. And so the very first thing he had done after entering the Grand Secretariat was to engineer the destruction of the loyal Yun family and rally the imperial princes to stage a coup.

She had never been able to understand how a twelve-year-old boy could have developed such resentment toward the Son of Heaven.

"An'er, do you understand what would happen if someone outside this household were to see something like this?" Yun Chu's voice was sharp. "You are registered under my name. That makes you the legitimate eldest son of the Xie household. Your every word and deed represents the Xie family."

A powerful aura suddenly radiated from her. "You are denouncing the reigning Emperor as licentious and debauched, as one who puts his faith in treacherous ministers..."

Xie Shi'an's expression darkened. "I did not..."

"You cannot dismiss this with a simple denial!" Yun Chu's face grew sterner still. "Black ink on white paper is evidence, and if someone were to submit it as a report, at the lightest end your father would be stripped of his post, and at the worst the Xie household would be convicted and imprisoned. Whether light or severe, you cannot afford either outcome. The Xie family has produced scholars for three generations, and your father's generation finally achieved a place at court. These few lines of yours would reduce generations of effort to ashes. You would become the sinner of the entire Xie family."

She snatched the paper and threw it at Xie Shi'an's face.

The old Madame Xie sat in her chair as though struck by lightning. She had truly not anticipated consequences this grave. No wonder the usually gentle-natured young mistress had erupted so violently. An'er had genuinely committed a serious offense.

Yun Chu lowered her eyes.

Speaking of severity, the matter was actually not so dire in practice. Even if it came to light, the worst of it would be a few months' docked salary. And her husband Xie Jingyu was clever enough to find more than enough ways to smooth the whole thing over.

Being reborn meant many things needed to be carefully planned.

She spoke quietly. "Ever since An'er was formally entered into the family register, I have raised him with the utmost care. In four years, this is the only time I have lost my temper, and yet here we are, called before the old mistress over it. It seems that even I, as his mother, have no right to discipline my own child. Or perhaps, even though An'er is registered under my name, I do not have the standing to discipline him strictly? If that is the case, then I no longer dare to claim this son."

A moment before she had been thunder and lightning; now she looked bereft, as though her heart had been hurt.

The old mistress was alarmed at once. "Chu'er, I did not mean to reproach you."

If Yun Chu refused An'er, he would be nothing more than a concubine's son, and concubine's sons were looked down upon everywhere and found it difficult to make their way in officialdom. Though he was already on the family register, and it was not as simple as Yun Chu merely saying she did not want him, only Yun Chu's genuine acceptance would secure the Yun family's acceptance of him in turn.

And the Yun family was a first-rank General's household. It was not something a fifth-rank Xie household could compare with.

The old mistress turned her head. "An'er, why are you just standing there?"

Xie Shi'an stepped forward. "The books say that strict mothers produce talented sons, and indulgent ones produce failures. Mother disciplines me strictly because she hopes I will amount to something great. I did not understand her painstaking care. The fault is mine. I will return to kneel in the ancestral hall."

Yun Chu's lips curved faintly.

Xie Shi'an had refused to accept her punishment from the start, and that was why he had brought the old mistress into it. Only when the evidence was placed before him, leaving no room for argument, did he bow his head and make the choice that served him best.

This child took after Xie Jingyu. He was deep of mind, subtle of thought, and an excellent student. He would not have otherwise topped the imperial examinations three times in a row and entered the Grand Secretariat at such a young age.

She spoke in a mild tone. "An'er need not kneel any longer. The old mistress will worry."

The old mistress was indeed worried.

As far back as anyone could remember, there had never been a precedent of kneeling in the ancestral hall in the Xie household.

But a mother disciplining her son was only natural. If she as a great-grandmother were to interfere, would that not be hurtful?

She said, against her own feelings, "He should still kneel."

"Since even the old mistress agrees." Yun Chu sighed. "The spring air is still cold. He need not kneel too long. Two days should be enough."

The old mistress nearly had her eyes pop out of her head.

Two full hours was already too much in her view, and now the girl was saying two entire days. That would kill the child.

But Xie Shi'an had already accepted. "Yes. I will come and pay my respects to Mother again in two days."

The depth in Yun Chu's eyes was unfathomable.

Only two days.

In the days before her death, she had knelt for well over two months, begging the Xie family to submit a plea on the Yun family's behalf. What she received in return was a cup of poisoned wine.

Leaving Anshou Hall, Ting Shuang spoke with concern. "My lady, punishing the young master this way may cause him to turn away from you."

Yun Chu smiled.

Xie Shi'an had never been on her side to begin with. How could he turn away from her?

In her past life, she had poured her whole heart into him, and what she got in return was scheming and betrayal. There was no need to offer genuine affection again.

chapters.title: The Child Had No Breath
chapters.content:
By the time she returned to Yusheng Residence, the sky had gone completely dark.

The room had been lit. The moment she stepped inside, she saw a man seated in the side parlor, drinking tea.

This was Xie Jingyu at twenty-eight years old.

When her mother had been searching for a match for her, she had secretly managed to catch a glimpse of him: a graceful, accomplished young scholar in the full bloom of his success, with nothing to fault. But had she known then that Xie Jingyu had already fathered children before their wedding, she would never have agreed to marry into the Xie family.

She looked at the woman standing behind Xie Jingyu.

Everyone in the Xie household knew this woman as Xie Jingyu's most capable steward. They all called her He Mama.

It was only after the Yun family fell, in her previous life, that she learned the truth. This woman was Xie Shi'an's birth mother.

When Xie Jingyu had brought Xie Shi'an and the two others back to the household four years ago, he had told her with his own mouth that the children's mother was dead.

At the time, she had just lost her own child, and Xie Shi'an and the two siblings were newly motherless. It had seemed entirely natural for all three to be placed under her name, calling her Mother.

She had been deceived for all those years, so that Xie Jingyu's children born out of wedlock could be elevated to legitimate standing, so that she would dedicate herself wholeheartedly to raising them, and so that no rift would develop between her family and his.

"Husband."

Yun Chu greeted him in a measured tone.

After their wedding, Xie Jingyu had never again entered her bedchamber. At first, while she was with child, she had been grateful for what she took as consideration on his part. Then, as one night followed another and one year followed the next, she waited for him and he never came, until at last she had let go of all hope and turned her whole heart toward the children.

If Xie Shi'an was the primary cause of the Yun family's destruction, then the beginning of her life's tragedy could be traced back to Xie Jingyu.

"Did you come because of An'er?"

Yun Chu asked calmly. She sat down at the table and said in a cool voice, "An'er did something so deeply wrong. Do you think I should not have punished him?"

Xie Jingyu was somewhat taken aback.

Ever since the loss of the child, Yun Chu had shed the spirit she once carried as the eldest daughter of a great General's household. She had grown quiet and compliant. In four years, this was the first time he had felt even a flicker of the Yun family's young mistress he had known before, as though something inside her had come back to life.

"The mistress was right to punish him." He Mama, standing behind Xie Jingyu, spoke when he did not. "Only, it is just the start of spring, and the nights are still cold. The young master's constitution is not strong..."

Before she could finish, she felt the cut of a cold glance.

Yun Chu's expression was flat. "In our Yun household, when the master is speaking, any servant who interjects receives a slap across the mouth."

"He Mama only cares about An'er," Xie Jingyu said. "An'er was indeed wrong. Two days of kneeling in the ancestral hall is certain to make him understand the gravity of it. I came hoping the mistress would not let the Yun family hear of this matter."

He still hoped the Yun family would continue to support An'er. He could not afford for An'er's failing to become something that others might use against him.

"Husband may rest easy. I understand." Yun Chu took a sip of tea, a faint smile on her lips. "Come to think of it, I still don't know He Mama's name."

He Mama lowered her eyes and answered with practiced deference. "I am nothing but a servant. A lowly name would only soil your ears, my lady. It is not fitting for you to know."

"He Mama cannot be thirty yet. Word is she has never married?" Yun Chu kept her gaze fixed on her. "As it happens, I know of a rather good match."

"I am undeserving, my lady!" He Mama bent lower at the waist. "I was born under an unlucky star. I will not marry in this lifetime. And besides, at my age, I have long since put such thoughts out of my mind. I am grateful for your ladyship's kindness, but I could not accept."

Xie Jingyu rose from his seat. "I still have official matters to attend to. I will take my leave. Please do not overtire yourself, my lady."

She watched as the two of them walked out of Yusheng Residence one after the other, and Yun Chu narrowed her eyes.

She could sense that the woman had no desire to become the mistress of the household.

Any woman who bore a man's children and found ways to remain at his side surely harbored some wish to become his legitimate wife. So why did this He woman seem content to live as a servant, without even a trace of grievance?

In her past life, she had been so consumed with the Yun family's affairs in her final days that she had never given He's identity any serious thought.

This time around, she could no longer afford to be so muddled.

That night, Yun Chu turned over every memory of her past life in her mind, and it was not until the first gray light of dawn that she finally slept.

She dreamed of her wedding night.

The tenderness of that night had sunk deep into her bones.

She dreamed of herself during the pregnancy, learning embroidery for the very first time, stitching tiger-head shoes one after another, hands clumsy but determined.

Then the dream shifted.

A vast tide of crimson blood spread across everything. From all around her came voices layering over one another.

"No, this is bad. The mistress is bleeding too much. The child has come early. Quick, someone come!"

"The little young master is finally born... Why isn't he crying? Why does he look like he has no breath?"

"There is another child still inside the mistress. That one seems to have no breath either."

"The mistress will hemorrhage with grief if she sees the stillborns. Take the children away quickly!"

"No! No!"

Yun Chu's eyes flew open.

Her abdomen had been so large during the pregnancy. It was only in the delivery room that she discovered she had been carrying twins. But she, their birth mother, had not been allowed to look upon her own flesh and blood even once before they were taken away, already gone.

Where they were buried, she had never learned, not even in her dying moments.

"My lady, what is wrong?"

Hearing her voice, Ting Shuang rushed in. Seeing the sheen of perspiration covering her, she quickly brought water to help her wash and dress.

Yun Chu soaked in the bathtub for a long time before she was finally able to push down the grief that the dream had stirred.

By then, the sky had grown light.

Once she was fully dressed and presentable, those who came each morning to pay their respects had already begun to arrive.

"My lady."

"Mother."

At her appearance, everyone rose and bowed in greeting.

Yun Chu's gaze moved across the faces before her.

Xie Jingyu was not a man of excessive appetites. He kept only three concubines. Her eyes came to rest on one of them, her former attendant Ting Yu, who had entered the household as Concubine Yu.

Five years ago, when she was still with child, Ting Yu had crept into Xie Jingyu's bed behind her back.

Her own child had not survived, while Ting Yu successfully delivered the Xie family's third son. Xie Jingyu had then placed the boy in her care.

She had chosen his name herself: Xie Shiyun.

If Xie Shi'an was the son into whom she had poured the most of herself, then Xie Shiyun was the child she had loved most dearly, the one who lived closest to her heart.

That child had mended her grief over losing her own. He had pulled her back from the bottomless despair she had been drowning in and given her life something to hold on to. She had truly loved Xie Shiyun as though he were her own son.

But later...

"Mother."

Xie Shiyun buried himself in Yun Chu's embrace, nestling against her and seeking affection.

The smile on Yun Chu's face did not reach her eyes. "Yun'er is four now. It is time to learn a little propriety."

Ting Yu looked up.

The mistress had always doted most on Yun'er. Any time he sought her affection, she would hold him in her arms and spoil him with tender warmth.

But now, the mistress had not so much as touched the child. Her eyes held something distant, something guarded.

Had Ting Yu not grown up serving the mistress since childhood, she would never have noticed such a subtle shift.

"Concubine Yu has given the Xie family children, yet she has never had a proper courtyard of her own." Yun Chu said lightly, with a smile. "Let the small courtyard on the east side of the estate be given to Concubine Yu and Yun'er from now on."

Ting Yu went still.

Since becoming a concubine, she had always lived within the mistress's own courtyard, and Yun'er had been raised here too, which was why they shared such closeness with the mistress.

If they moved to the east side, even a visit to the mistress would no longer be easy. Would the mistress still favor Yun'er then?

chapters.title: Jujube Trees Are Hardy
chapters.content:
Yun Chu did not look at Ting Yu again.

Her gaze moved to the children gathered before her.

The eldest daughter, Xie Pin, was thirteen, already growing into a graceful young woman.

The eldest son, Xie Shi'an, was still kneeling in the ancestral hall.

The second son, Xie Shiwei, was eight years old and had not come to pay his respects. He was most likely still asleep.

The three eldest children were all He's.

The third son was Xie Shiyun.

The second daughter, Xie Xian, was the child of Concubine Jiang, and only three years old.

Concubine Tao was with child, carrying the future fourth son.

Yun Chu let her gaze pass over everyone in turn, then said in a mild voice, "I still have matters to attend to. You may all go about your business."

After she had come to the Xie household as a bride, she had taken over the management of the estate's affairs. Because of this, the old mistress and Madame Xie had long since excused her from daily morning greetings.

No sooner had the morning callers departed than the household stewardesses arrived.

They filed in one by one to report on their respective matters.

Yun Chu blew lightly on the surface of her tea.

The Xie family was what might be called a farming-and-scholars household. After Xie Jingyu's father had passed the juren examination, the neighboring farmers and landowners in the area had registered their fields under the Xie family's name to avoid taxation, which had brought in considerable income. When Xie Jingyu entered officialdom, his father used that money to acquire farmland on the outskirts of the capital and purchase several shops.

The annual income from those shops came to roughly five thousand taels of silver, and the greater part of that was taken by Xie Jingyu to smooth his way through the ranks of officialdom. What remained was nowhere near enough to sustain the lavish life of so many people under the Xie roof.

In her past life, she had always felt a gnawing sense of debt to the Xie family and had done whatever she could to fill the gaps.

And so, piece by piece, her dowry had been quietly hollowed out.

By the time the Yun family's catastrophe struck and she tried to use money to bribe the prison guards, barely a thousand taels remained.

"My lady?"

The stewardess who had been reporting grew a little uneasy when Yun Chu only drank her tea and said nothing.

Yun Chu drew her thoughts back. "Where were we?"

The stewardess quickly said, "Spring has come. It is time to replant the courtyard flowers. Does my lady prefer orchids or azaleas this year?"

Yun Chu smiled faintly.

The Xie family was of humble origin, still with mud on their heels, yet they aspired to imitate the great capital families by changing out flowers each season and hosting viewing banquets. Each spring, orchids; each autumn, chrysanthemums. Simple enough in principle, yet costly to execute.

For the past four or five years, she had used her own dowry to maintain the Xie family's face.

But now...

She set down her teacup. "Changing flowers in and out is more trouble than it is worth. I do not see the point. This year, everything will be replanted with fruit trees."

The stewardess thought she had misheard. "Fruit... fruit trees?"

Yun Chu considered for a moment. "Jujube trees are hardy and easy to keep. Jujube trees it is."

The stewardess was left speechless.

All the great ladies of the capital loved their flowers. Every spring, the households of the city competed with one another to host the most beautiful viewing banquets, and the Xie family was no exception. It was an important occasion for cultivating social ties.

When the mistress had said fruit trees, the stewardess had imagined peach or pear trees at worst, since peach and pear blossoms could at least pass for scenery.

But jujube flowers were small and plain, hiding beneath the leaves. Not a single household in the capital grew jujube trees. She had never heard of such a thing in her life.

"Is there anything else?" Yun Chu's voice was unhurried. "If there is nothing further, you are all dismissed."

The stewardesses had already heard that the mistress had been in a fierce temper the day before over the young master. Not one of them dared say another word. They bowed their heads and withdrew.

"Ting Feng, please ask Old Chen to come see me." Yun Chu gave her instructions. "Ting Shuang, Ting Xue, you two go through my dowry inventory. Write down clearly what is there, what is missing, and what has been spent on the Xie household. Every item accounted for."

Ting Feng went to fetch the man right away.

Ting Shuang hesitated. "My lady, has something happened?"

Something about the mistress had seemed off since yesterday. Punishing the eldest young master had its reasons, but then ordering Concubine Yu and the third young master to move out was unusual. And now going through the dowry... something of consequence must have occurred.

Yun Chu looked at Ting Shuang.

Of the four dowry attendants, Ting Shuang was the sharpest and the most steadfast. Yet she had died young in that fire. Had she lived, her keen eye might well have seen through the wolf in fine clothing that Xie Shi'an had always been.

Yun Chu looked at her and said gently, "Nothing has happened. Do not let your mind run away with you. Go and keep busy."

Ting Shuang put away the concern in her eyes and went with Ting Xue toward the storeroom where the dowry was kept.

A quarter of an hour later, Ting Feng returned with Old Chen.

Old Chen was also someone Yun Chu had brought with her into the Xie household. His name was Chen Defu, and he was approaching fifty years of age. He had been managing her dowry assets for her from the beginning.

After she had taken charge of the Xie estate's affairs, she had turned the Xie family's several shops over to Chen Defu to manage as well.

Her father-in-law was a man of letters, not a businessman. Under his watch, the shops had brought in barely a thousand or so taels a year. Under Chen Defu's management, that figure had grown to four or five thousand.

"My greetings to my lady," Chen Defu said as he entered. "Is there something urgent that my lady summoned this old servant for?"

Yun Chu spoke. "Is there not a junior steward under your management by the surname He?"

"There is one, He Xu by name." Chen Defu raised his head. "Has this person done something?"

Yun Chu lowered her eyes.

She had not known until after the Yun family's fall, in her previous life, that He, the steward of the Xie household, was He's own elder brother.

While she knelt at the door of Xie Jingyu's study, begging for some chance at saving her family, He Xu had taken advantage of his standing as Xie Shi'an's maternal uncle to harass and humiliate her on more than one occasion. She was still the lawful mistress of the Xie household, so He Xu had not dared to go beyond words. But Ting Xue and Ting Feng were only maidservants, with no power to resist at all. He Xu had violated them. And later, when she was killed by the poisoned wine, those two girls had surely followed her in death.

Seeing that Yun Chu's expression had darkened, Chen Defu knew the matter was serious.

He clenched his fist. "My lady, you need only give the command."

"There is no need to do anything in particular." Yun Chu pressed down the chill in her voice. "Give him opportunities to climb higher. The higher he climbs, the harder he will fall when the time comes."

Chen Defu was a man of the business world and understood perfectly what those words meant. He accepted the order immediately.

Yun Chu set down her teacup and stood. "Old Chen, take me to have a look at the dowry shops."

In her past life, her dowry shops had been sold off one by one, the proceeds spent largely on furthering Xie Jingyu's career at court.

The seven or eight dowry estates in the outskirts of the capital, half of them had gone to Xie Shi'an's wife, and the other half had become Xie Pin's bridal dowry.

All of it had been painstakingly prepared for her by her mother, representing the better part of the Yun family's fortune. In the end, every last piece of it had passed into the hands of the Xie family.

She had not understood the worth of money until she had lived through the despair of the Yun family's destruction.

In this life, she would not only guard her dowry. She would make it grow, three times over, ten times over, a hundred times over.

chapters.title: You Owe Me a Cricket
chapters.content:
The streets of the capital were alive with the bustle of the crowd.

Yun Chu had not taken a palanquin. She walked along the street, watching the lively flow of people around her, and it confirmed once more, beyond any doubt, that this rebirth was no dream.

Chen Defu took her on a full tour of her dowry shops.

A tea shop, a silk and fabric shop, a grain shop, a blacksmith's shop, and more, eleven shops in total, large and small.

Chen Defu managed them all extremely well, and together they brought in over ten thousand taels a year. But it was still not enough.

The Emperor harbored wariness toward the Yun family, and even without Xie Shi'an pushing things along, the Yun family would sooner or later find themselves in trouble. She had to accumulate enough silver before that day came.

"My lady, it has started to rain. It's a little cold." Ting Feng drew a cape over Yun Chu's shoulders. "Shall we sit in the tea house for a while?"

Yun Chu looked up at the sky.

If her memory was right, this year was a cold spring. It would not turn warm until the fifth month, and then the heat would set in with a fury and not let up until the tenth month.

If one wanted to know which business brought in the most profit, the answer was simple: storing ice and selling ice.

With a plan taking shape in her mind, Yun Chu felt a calm certainty settle over her. She stepped into the tea house and sat down by a window on the second floor, watching the rain and drinking tea.

"What? My lady, you want to deal in ice?" Chen Defu stood behind her, his face full of surprise. "The nobles and powerful lords maintain their own ice cellars, and all the great households have already begun purchasing ice this time of year. But with the spring being this cold, the summer is sure to be cool as well, and most families have only ordered a third or even a fifth of what they would normally buy. I am afraid there is not much profit to be made in this business."

Yun Chu's smile did not waver. "Just follow my lead, Old Chen. Whatever ice the market has, we buy all of it."

Seeing her with that air of perfect confidence, Chen Defu knew there was no persuading her.

He went along with what she said. "How much silver does my lady plan to put into purchasing ice?"

"Use everything available in the accounts." Yun Chu continued, "I will give you more silver later."

Chen Defu was startled. "But my lady, did you not say the silver in the accounts was all set aside for an important purpose?"

Yun Chu smiled coldly.

The so-called important purpose was the fact that Xie Jingyu was soon to attend his superior's birthday banquet, and the money had been earmarked for a suitable gift.

She was never going to spend another coin on the Xie family.

As the two of them were speaking, an opulent carriage pulled up outside the tea house. Before it had even come to a full stop, the curtain was flung aside and a chubby little child tumbled out at a run.

The maids and matrons trailing behind the small figure could not catch up with the little ancestor. They called out loudly, "Young lord, please slow down! Mind you don't fall!"

Yun Chu's attention drifted to the child.

The boy was small and slight, likely no more than three years old, yet he ran with extraordinary speed, vanishing around a corner in the blink of an eye.

She turned back and continued talking with Chen Defu.

Mid-conversation, she suddenly felt something land in her hair.

"My lady, don't be frightened!" Ting Feng gave a start. "A cricket has jumped onto your head! Let me get it off for you!"

Yun Chu went rigid with fear.

She was the eldest daughter of a great General's household, bold in the face of most things, the sky itself not enough to intimidate her. Her one weakness was small creatures, crickets included.

Her scalp crawled. She could not bring herself to move a single inch.

"Don't touch my Jumpy!"

A small, soft voice rang out. Then a little cannonball came flying directly into Yun Chu, crashing hard against her body.

She looked down in astonishment. It was the little young lord from downstairs, and he was charging straight for her.

In an instant he had clambered up onto her knees.

Then both his little hands came swatting at the top of her head.

All of this happened in the space of a single breath.

Yun Chu was caught completely off guard. She toppled backward.

By instinct she wrapped her arms around the small child, cushioning him as they landed together on the floor.

"My lady!"

Ting Feng was mortified. Not only had she failed to stop this inexplicable child, but she had let her mistress be knocked off her seat in broad view of everyone.

She hurried to help Yun Chu up and quickly set her hair and clothes to rights.

"Wah, wah, wah!"

The small child, dressed in finery, was suddenly lying face down on the floor, sobbing with great force.

For reasons she could not explain, something in Yun Chu's chest gave a sudden ache.

She reached down, lifted her skirts, and crouched beside him. She asked in a gentle voice, "Where does it hurt? Let me blow on it."

"You are bad! You are a bad person!" The little one looked up at her through a blur of tears, his eyes full of accusation. "You squashed Jumpy to death. Wah, wah, wah. I hate you!"

Yun Chu looked down.

A cricket lay crushed flat on the floor. Ignoring the moisture beneath it, the little figure scooped the cricket up with both hands and cradled it.

Yun Chu stumbled backward in fright.

"Give me back my Jumpy!" The little one glared at her through his tears. "You have to give me a cricket exactly like this one!"

Yun Chu was speechless.

She had forgotten to check her almanac before leaving the house this morning. How had she walked straight into something like this?

"Young lord, why are you crying?"

"My little ancestor, I told you to be careful! Are you hurt?"

A great crowd of attendants came rushing up the stairs at last, clustered around the little one, fussing over him from every side.

The little figure cried even harder. "She... she squashed my Jumpy to death!"

The matron had just been cooing soothing words at the young master, but at this, her expression changed entirely. She turned on Yun Chu with eyes like a fierce deity. "Where has this blind woman come from? How dare she squash our young lord's most beloved treasure? You..."

But before she could finish, the little young lord, who had just been wailing with great vigor, stopped his crying all at once.

Those round, dark eyes turned toward the matron. He was clearly displeased. "Who gave you permission to scold her? Apologize."

The matron was at a complete loss.

The woman before them had squashed the young master's favorite cricket. Saying a few harsh words was only taking the young master's side. Why would the young master ask her to apologize?

But when she met her young master's displeased gaze, she had no choice but to step forward. "My lady, I was presumptuous just now. Please do not take offense."

Yun Chu's expression was calm. "It is of no consequence."

Although she was the eldest legitimate daughter of a first-rank General's household, after marriage, being the Mistress Xie was her primary identity. No matter how little fault lay with her, the wife of a minor fifth-rank official had to keep her head lower than any person of rank.

She continued, "I will find a cricket just like it and have it sent to the young lord. May I ask where your household is located?"

"I live in the Prince Pingxi's residence." The little one lifted his chin. "Remember that, the Prince Pingxi's residence. Find me the cricket and bring it over right away."

Yun Chu was taken aback.

This child was actually the son of Prince Pingxi?

Prince Pingxi was the current Emperor's third prince. He had led troops in battle and repelled the forces that had invaded Xichuan, and it was for that military achievement that he had received his title.

Four years ago, Prince Pingxi had suddenly appeared with a son and daughter. He had defied the protests of both civil and military officials and petitioned to have his son, whose mother's identity was unknown, formally invested as the Young Lord. The uproar it caused in the capital had been considerable.

"Young lord, it is time to return to the residence," the matron said softly. "If the Prince comes home and cannot find the young lord..."

Fear flickered across the small face. "Go, go, let's go quickly!"

The matron swept the little one up in her arms. The whole group swept downstairs, piled into the carriage, and were gone in a cloud of dust.

"My lady, leave this matter to this old servant," Chen Defu offered. "I will have a cricket for you to inspect by tomorrow morning."

Yun Chu nodded.

Sitting in the carriage on the way back to the estate, she found herself thinking of her past life.

Prince Pingxi had entered the battlefield at fifteen and had shared a friendship with her father across the gap in their years. After the Yun family was convicted of their crimes, the Prince had done his best to advocate on their behalf.

But before any resolution could be reached in the Yun family's case, someone had exposed Prince Pingxi for concealing weapons and plotting rebellion.

What had become of him after that, she did not know. She had already been killed by the poisoned wine.

chapters.title: The Dowry Went Into the Public Account
chapters.content:
Yun Chu had just returned to the Xie estate.

Zhou Mama from the old mistress's side came at once to bring her to Anshou Hall.

The old Madame Xie was seated in the head position. Across from her sat the eldest daughter of the household, Xie Pin.

"You are here." The old mistress opened with a mild tone. "Sit."

Yun Chu sat down. Zhou Mama brought tea.

She took a sip. The leaves were from a variety the Emperor had gifted to the Yun family several years ago. Her mother had sent some to her as a gesture of care, and she had presented it to the old mistress out of respect. The old mistress had kept it tucked away for years before finally deigning to open it.

She set down the teacup. "I wonder what the old mistress has called me here to discuss."

"Chu'er, the Li stewardess who manages the courtyard says you have given orders to plant jujube trees throughout the entire yard this year." The old mistress spoke in an unhurried tone. "Was this your instruction?"

Yun Chu nodded. "I gave that order."

"Mother!" Xie Pin could no longer hold herself in check. "Our family holds a flower-viewing banquet every spring. If we plant jujube trees this year, how can we host the banquet?"

The old Madame Xie frowned.

On account of the Yun family's first-rank standing, each year's flower-viewing banquet drew ladies and young misses from a number of distinguished households who came to enjoy the occasion. She had been quietly preparing for this year's banquet for some time. But with no flowers to speak of, what was there to hold a banquet for?

Were they to gather and admire jujube blossoms? That would invite nothing but ridicule.

Yet in her heart, she had always known that Yun Chu was not someone who acted without reason. She softened her tone. "Chu'er, what is behind this?"

"Does the old mistress know how much it costs each day to sustain so many masters and so many servants under this roof?" Yun Chu let out a quiet sigh. "More goes out than comes in. If we do not find ways to reduce our spending, there will come a day when there is simply nothing left. I gave the order for jujube trees because they are inexpensive and easy to keep. We will never again need to replace the plantings each season, which should save five or six hundred taels a year. What is more, when the trees bear fruit, the dates can be sold, which adds a small income."

The old mistress was visibly astonished. "Our shops are doing very well. How can we possibly be bringing in less than we spend?"

Xie Pin chimed in, "The cosmetics shop in Guihua Lane is the busiest one on the street. The shopkeeper says it earns over a thousand taels a year. How can we not even afford to grow flowers?"

"Over a thousand taels." Yun Chu smiled. "Pin'er, you have never managed a household, so you do not know how much it costs just to keep it running. A thousand taels cannot sustain even one month of the Xie family's life, let alone leave anything over for flowers. If I had not been supplementing with my own dowry, how do you think the past three years' banquets were so grand?"

Xie Pin's eyes went wide. "Mother used her own dowry to fill the gap for the Xie family?"

The old mistress set down her teacup with a firm clack. "That is impossible. The Xie family would never touch a daughter-in-law's dowry. Chu'er, one must be careful about what one says."

They prided themselves on being a family of scholarly refinement. Dignity meant everything. If word of this got out, how would Jingyu hold his head up at court?

Yun Chu raised her hand. "Ting Shuang, the account books."

Ting Shuang presented a set of carefully prepared ledgers at once.

"These are the household accounts. Every month's income and expenditure is written down in full." She had Ting Shuang place the books before the old mistress's table. "Each month, there is more going out than coming in. Not wishing to burden the old mistress with these domestic concerns, I said nothing for a long time. Today, however, the conversation has come this far, and I would rather lay it out plainly than be questioned."

The old mistress had spent her years immersed in the Four Books and Five Classics, and the workings of commerce were beyond her. As for Xie Pin, at thirteen and with no one to have taught her such things, she understood nothing of the matter.

"Send for An'er," the old mistress said. "The tutor says An'er is very good at the abacus. Let him come and look at the household accounts."

Using a daughter-in-law's dowry was deeply shameful. She could not simply take Yun Chu's word for it.

Since neither she nor Pin'er could read the numbers, she would call someone who could.

Zhou Mama accepted the errand and went immediately to fetch him from the ancestral hall.

Xie Shi'an was still kneeling there, and without much else to do, he came right away.

Having already understood the general situation on the way, he gave his greetings to the elders upon arriving, then picked up the account books and went through them quickly.

"Our Xie family is indeed spending more than it earns." Xie Shi'an spoke carefully. "Last year's total income was five thousand six hundred taels, while expenditures reached thirteen thousand."

The old Madame Xie was shocked. "How can there be such a gap?"

Yun Chu might deceive her, but An'er would not.

Xie Shi'an went on, holding the account books. "The Xie household has only the shops' income, the master's official salary, and the estates outside the capital. None of these appear in this ledger."

The old mistress had nothing to say to this, for it was the truth.

Ting Feng, standing behind Yun Chu, muttered under her breath, "The master's and the lord's silver ought to go into the public account. Instead it is somehow our mistress, an outsider by surname, whose dowry has been used for the public good."

Her voice was barely above a whisper, yet everyone in the room heard it clearly.

Without waiting for the old mistress to speak, Yun Chu rose to her feet.

She walked to the center of the room and gave a slight bow. "Since the day I entered the Xie household, whether in serving my elders, in raising the children, in helping my husband build his connections, or in managing every large and small affair of this estate, I do not believe I have failed in a single duty. Now I am questioned at such length merely for planting jujube trees to save a little money. Old mistress, my abilities are limited. I return the keys to household management to you today."

Ting Shuang stepped forward and placed the box of household tallies before the old mistress.

The old mistress's brow furrowed.

In the early days, the Xie household had only seven or eight maids and matrons, and managing them had been simple enough. But now, with Jingyu in officialdom and the estate grown large, there were too many people and too much to oversee. It was no small matter to manage properly.

"Chu'er, you have taken this the wrong way." The old mistress weighed her options carefully, yet kept a look of warm affection on her face. She took Yun Chu's hand and spoke with earnest tenderness. "These past four or five years, it is because of you that our Xie family has grown more prosperous with each passing day. You are the greatest contributor this family has. Today's business was Grandmother's misstep, and Grandmother apologizes to you. Do not say such things in a moment of irritation."

"Old mistress, I am not saying it in irritation." Yun Chu kept her head lowered. "An'er has seen the accounts. He knows what the situation of the Xie household is. If I continue managing the household, my dowry will eventually be depleted entirely, and at that point I will have no choice but to go back to the Yun family and ask my mother for more silver. I do not imagine the old mistress wishes for it to come to that."

The old mistress felt some discomfort.

If the Yun family learned that Xie Jingyu's household had been living off Yun Chu's dowry, the consequences, at the lightest, would mean the end of the Yun family's support for the Xie family. At the worst, a formal written complaint to the Emperor.

The Xie family had climbed three generations to reach the capital, and they could not afford the smallest misstep.

With that in mind, the old mistress spoke. "An'er, calculate how much of her dowry your mother has put in over the years."

Xie Shi'an called for an abacus and worked the beads briskly. Before long he had the number. "In total, it comes to twenty-one thousand two hundred and thirty-five taels."

The old Madame Xie felt a pain in her heart.

But she understood clearly that, as much as she hated to part with the amount, it had to be paid back.

The one consolation she allowed herself was this: the young mistress was so devoted to all the children. This money would find its way back into the Xie family's hands in the end.

She waved her hand. Behind her, Zhou Mama accepted the signal, went into the inner room, and returned carrying a thick stack of banknotes.

chapters.title: From Now On, Call It Sheng Residence
chapters.content:
Yun Chu gave a self-mocking smile.

In her past life, she had believed the Xie family was genuinely poor, and had willingly supplemented them from her own dowry, too afraid of wounding their pride to ever bring it up. Yet the fact that the old mistress could produce twenty thousand taels without blinking was proof enough that the Xie family had its own reserves.

Looking back now, her father-in-law had been the only juren within a considerable radius. Xie Jingyu had been the youngest top imperial scholar the examinations had seen. In the capital, the Xie name carried little weight, but in their home region, they commanded great respect, and with so many landowners and gentry registering their farmland under the Xie name, the income from that alone would have been no small sum year after year.

Zhou Mama brought the banknotes forward.

Yun Chu took one step back and gave a small bow. "If this silver is given to me, it will only go into the household's daily expenses in any case. Please keep it, old mistress."

The old mistress had the nagging feeling that her daughter-in-law was somehow not quite the same as before.

Ever since the loss of the child in her womb, Yun Chu had become particularly gentle and yielding, respectful and obedient toward her as an elder.

This was the first time, the very first, that Yun Chu had used the art of retreat to press her forward.

Pressing her?

The moment that phrase formed in the old mistress's mind, she dismissed it with a shake of her head.

Yun Chu had no children of her own and never would. All her life, it was the Xie family who would hold sway over her, not the other way around.

"Chu'er, now you are making me feel ashamed." The old mistress spoke. "I simply did not know before. Had I known earlier, none of this would have happened. Take this silver and add it back to your dowry register. I will have Zhou Mama see to it that all income from your father-in-law's estates is placed into the public account from now on. And if you ever find yourself short of money, come to me. You are not to touch your own personal funds again. Do you understand?"

Yun Chu reached over and held the old mistress's hand in return, her face a picture of being deeply moved. "The old mistress is truly good to me. Just the other day, my mother asked after a peony screen from my dowry, and I had been wracking my brain trying to think of what excuse to give her. Now that I have the silver, I can go and find something close enough to replace it."

At this, the old mistress felt a cold sweat break out.

Thank goodness she had been generous in returning the money. Had the Yun mistress grown suspicious and decided to come to the Xie household herself, there would have been no covering it up.

"Good child." The old mistress patted Yun Chu's hand warmly. "Placing this household in your hands, I have peace of mind. You have worked very hard. Now, I have an idea. Pin'er is getting older, and it will not be long before we are making inquiries about a match for her. Let her come alongside you in managing the household."

The old mistress showed no immediate reaction, for to agree too quickly would appear as though she had no trust in Yun Chu at all.

Zhou Mama, standing to the side, spoke on her behalf. "The eldest young miss will one day be the mistress of some household. She must learn these things."

Only after a sip of tea did the old mistress say, "Pin'er, what do you think yourself?"

Xie Pin's face was bright with eagerness. "I am very willing to learn!"

If she could learn even a fraction of what Mother had mastered, it would make entering a good family upon marriage all the easier.

Yun Chu smiled. "Tomorrow morning, after you have paid your respects, come and stay at Sheng Residence with me."

With the business concluded, she rose and took her leave.

Ting Shuang followed behind, the household tallies in her arms and a thick sheaf of banknotes on top.

The old mistress let out a quiet sigh. She had summoned Yun Chu meaning to call her to account, yet in the end it was she who had bled over twenty thousand taels in the exchange.

Xie Shi'an's gaze was shadowed and unreadable. He truly felt it now. His mother was different.

Yun Chu walked slowly back toward Sheng Residence.

Approaching the gate of the courtyard, she found several maidservants gathered there.

The character for "yu" on the signboard above the gate had lost a stroke, and the maids and serving boys were trying to figure out how to repair it.

"My lady, what a strange thing it is," Ting Xue remarked. "Yusheng Residence has become Wangsheng Residence. It is rather odd. Shall we ask the master to write a new board?"

Yun Chu looked up at the three characters.

The courtyard had existed before she arrived as a bride. It had originally been Xie Jingyu's own quarters, and after she moved in, he had relocated to the neighboring courtyard.

She spoke. "Remove the 'yu' altogether. From now on, it is called Sheng Residence."

The maids and serving boys exchanged glances, and every face wore the same quiet disbelief.

The "yu" in Yusheng Residence was one of the characters in the master's own name. To simply remove it like this, was that really all right?

Ting Shuang said coolly, "Did you not hear what my lady said? What are you all standing there for?"

The group immediately scrambled for ladders and tools and set to work.

Yun Chu had barely settled into her chair when an attendant from her mother-in-law Madam Yuan's courtyard arrived carrying two thousand taels of silver. "The mistress has always labored inside and out for the Xie household, and Madame knows it well. She has sent this silver specially so that you might have a headpiece made to your liking, or buy yourself some fine fabric."

She pressed her lips together.

After she had come to the Xie household as a bride, her mother-in-law, who had been bedridden for over a decade, had suddenly recovered. From that point on, her mother-in-law had believed her to carry an auspicious fate.

That mother-in-law, as mothers-in-law went, did hold a small genuine fondness for her. A small one. Which had vanished entirely when the Yun family's disaster struck.

Yun Chu gathered all the silver together and placed it in Ting Shuang's hands. "Take it to Old Chen. However much ice he can buy, let him buy it all. If the silver runs short, he may borrow from the money lender."

Ting Shuang slipped away under cover of the darkening evening.

That night, Yun Chu slept reasonably well.

She woke in the morning before the sky had fully brightened, dressed, and went out. Xie Shi'an was sitting in the side parlor, waiting to pay his respects.

When he saw her come out, he stood at once. "Mother."

Yun Chu asked him warmly, "Have you eaten?"

Xie Shi'an shook his head. "I came straight here from the ancestral hall. These two days, I have thought through a great many things. I thank Mother for her teaching and her correction."

"It is good that you have thought it through." Yun Chu smiled. "Sit down and share a meal with me."

Xie Shi'an exhaled in a way that was barely perceptible.

Mother was still as kind to him as she had always been. It seemed he had worried for nothing.

Halfway through the meal, Yun Chu set down her chopsticks. "Yesterday I was reading and came across a story. Would you like to hear it?"

Xie Shi'an put down his chopsticks as well and composed himself to listen.

Yun Chu had occasionally shared with him tales of court affairs and events from the battlefield in the past, so this sudden announcement of a story did not strike him as unusual.

Yun Chu spoke in an unhurried voice. "It is said that a woman raised three children. But when the children were grown, they killed her over a small grievance. What do you think: were the children right to do so?"

"Of course they were not!" Xie Shi'an looked outraged. "Those three are utterly conscienceless, undeserving to call themselves human beings!"

Yun Chu asked, "What if those three children were not the woman's own flesh and blood?"

Xie Shi'an replied, "The debt of being raised surpasses the debt of being born. The woman raised them. She was their mother. No matter the circumstances, one should never kill one's own mother."

Yun Chu nodded. "And what if the woman may have been involved in a treasonous plot, and the three children killed her only to protect themselves and the entire family? Would you still say they were wrong?"

Xie Shi'an did not answer so quickly this time.

He considered for a moment before lifting his head and speaking carefully. "The lives of an entire family, weighed against one woman, naturally make the family the more important. If the woman understood that the children killed her for the sake of the family's prosperity, I believe she would have been willing to die."

Yun Chu smiled. "Thank you."

Xie Shi'an suddenly sensed that something was not quite right. "What is Mother thanking me for?"

Yun Chu's smile curved gently.

For making the same choice he had made in their past life, of course.

For still being, in this life, the same person he had been. Because of that, when the time came for her to act, she would do so without the slightest hesitation.

chapters.title: Bring the Family Rod
chapters.content:
After his morning greeting, Xie Shi'an still had to go to the schoolroom.

He arrived every day more than half an hour before the appointed time, reading and practicing his calligraphy there. He was diligent to a rare degree.

He was about to leave when a commotion suddenly broke out in the courtyard.

Yun Chu's brow drew together.

Ting Feng hurried in from outside. "My lady, the second young master has taken a liking to Old Chen's cricket. What is to be done?"

The moment crickets were mentioned, the image of that chubby, soft little child from the day before floated up in Yun Chu's mind.

The boy had no sense of etiquette or restraint; he had hurled himself onto her without a moment's thought. And yet, for reasons she could not quite explain, she found she felt no irritation toward him at all.

She rose and walked out into the courtyard.

The morning light was full and bright. The concubines had brought the young masters and misses to pay their respects, and the yard was lively. Chen Defu had arrived at the same moment carrying the cricket cage, and the two groups had crossed paths, giving Xie Shiwei a clear view of the cricket.

Xie Shiwei, eight years old and tilting his chin up with authority, issued his command. "Give me that cricket."

Chen Defu looked pained. "In reply to the second young master, this cricket was specially sought out by my lady's order for..."

"I told you to hand it over, why are you making such a fuss about it!" Xie Shiwei let out a snort. "Mother is always so generous. Why would she begrudge a single cricket?"

"Wow, this cricket looks really impressive!" Xie Shiyun stared with wide eyes. "Second brother, can I play with the cricket too?"

Xie Shiwei was not pleased.

Mother always doted on third brother most. Third brother wanted for nothing. And now here he was, coming to compete with him over a single cricket.

"A little thing like you, what do you know about playing with crickets? Get out of the way."

He shot Xie Shiyun a glare and strode toward Chen Defu.

Chen Defu was, at the end of it all, only a servant. And he knew that the mistress had always been indulgent with the young masters. He was not certain whether the mistress would let the second young master have the cricket and simply send him out to find another one.

In his moment of hesitation, the cage was snatched out of his hands.

Xie Shiwei threw the cage open. The cricket leapt out and bolted for the grass along the edge of the courtyard.

"How dare you run!"

He dropped the cage and gave chase.

An eight-year-old boy was at his most nimble, and with one lunge forward, he had the cricket pinned under his palm.

He stood up from the ground and lifted his eyes to find Yun Chu standing on the steps not far away.

He bowed to her at once. "Mother."

The others in the courtyard only noticed then that the mistress had come out. They all bowed their heads in greeting.

Yun Chu's gaze settled on Xie Shiwei.

The Xie family's second son had not inherited Xie Jingyu's sharp mind or his diligence. He was wild by nature, with no love for reading. At eight years old, he was still unwilling to attend the schoolroom.

He slept until the sun was well past the horizon every day, and if he made it to morning greetings three or four times in a fortnight, that was considered quite good.

Though Xie Shiwei was not the child she had loved most, she had never shown favoritism. She had done her best to raise and educate every single one of them.

Xie Shiwei had no gift for scholarship, so she had called on her elder brother to use the Yun family's influence to place this son in the military camp. It was precisely that mistaken decision which had given Xie Shiwei free access to the Yun family's garrison, and the evidence that sealed the verdict of the Yun family's treason was something Xie Shiwei had planted personally within her father's correspondence.

The memories turned over and over in her mind, and the air around Yun Chu seemed to shift into something formidable.

Xie Shi'an, standing behind her, was sharp enough to sense the change in her mood.

"Shiwei." Xie Shi'an stepped forward, speaking in the manner of an elder brother. "Taking something without permission is not the conduct of a gentleman. Our Xie household has upheld scholarly virtues across generations. What you have done brings shame upon the Xie family. If Grandfather and Father were to hear of it, they would certainly order you to stand facing the wall in penance. You should return the cricket to the cage at once and apologize to Mother."

Xie Shiwei first glanced at Yun Chu.

On any other occasion, Mother would have said it was only a cricket, nothing to make a fuss over, and let him take it.

But right now, Mother's face was set like stone, and her eyes held something in them that made him uneasy.

He had no choice but to open his hand.

"How come the cricket is not moving?" Xie Shiyun exclaimed from the side. "Oh no, it looks like second brother suffocated it."

Xie Shiwei prodded it. The cricket lay perfectly still.

He frowned. "How could it die so easily..."

"Kneel."

Yun Chu said the two words with cold precision.

Xie Shiwei could not believe it. "Why?"

"All these years, it is because I have been too lenient with you that you have grown into someone who does as he pleases with no regard for rules!" Yun Chu's voice was severe. "Taking without asking is stealing. The laws of this dynasty are written clearly: a thief is branded on the forehead, a mark of disgrace for the rest of his life. How would your father hold his head up at court? How would your elder brother pursue a career through the examinations?"

"I did not steal anything!"

Xie Shiwei's composure cracked a little. No matter how unruly he was, he knew well enough that he could not have the word "thief" attached to his name.

"Mother, I was just being childish. I was wrong. I will never do it again..."

He had taken Mother's things before just like this, plenty of times. Mother had only smiled and let him keep them.

Why was she making such a spectacle of it this time?

He dared not ask. All he could do was bow his head and admit his fault, hoping Mother would let the matter drop.

Yun Chu tilted her head slightly and looked at Xie Shi'an beside her. "An'er, how do you think this should be handled?"

Xie Shi'an lowered his head. "To know one's error and correct it is a great virtue. Since Shiwei knows he was wrong, let him replace the cricket at his own expense."

Xie Shiwei's face fell.

His own elder brother, sharing the same mother, and he would not even put in a word on his behalf. He had actually suggested making him pay for a replacement. Where was he supposed to find money? He spent everything he had on food, drink, and amusement. This was only making things harder for him.

Yun Chu smiled. "An'er, do you know who this cricket was meant for?"

Xie Shi'an shook his head.

"It was to be sent to the young lord of Prince Pingxi's household." The smile on Yun Chu's face disappeared. Her voice went cold. "My belongings, if Shiwei takes them, then he takes them. We are family, and I would not make an issue of it. But Prince Pingxi, that is not a name anyone needs to be told twice. Is our Xie family in any position to offend someone of that household? Today Shiwei suffocates the young lord's cricket; tomorrow he may ruin the dress of some princess; and the day after, who knows, he may pluck the flowers a royal consort has tended with care. If he is not properly punished for this, do you think he will ever learn his lesson?"

Xie Shi'an was visibly startled.

Mother had managed to cultivate a connection with a household of Prince Pingxi's standing. That must have taken considerable effort. And the cricket she had worked so hard to procure as a gift for the young lord had died at Shiwei's hands. No wonder she was furious.

Xie Shi'an spoke carefully. "Then let the family rod be applied."

Yun Chu's lips curved. "As expected, An'er always sees the larger picture. Bring the family rod."

"No!" Xie Shiwei's eyes flew wide with terror. "I don't want to be beaten! I'll pay for the cricket! Isn't that enough? Or two crickets!"

The Xie household had established its rules from the time of its founding: serious offenses were met with the family rod, with twenty strokes as the minimum.

Some time ago, a matron had colluded with the outside staff to embezzle household silver, and the old mistress had beaten her so severely she never walked properly again. She had been bedridden ever since.

That incident had left a lasting shadow in Xie Shiwei's mind.

He was terrified of being beaten raw and bloodied, terrified of never being able to get out of bed again.

chapters.title: How to Cut Spending
chapters.content:
At Yun Chu's command, the serving boys carried a long bench into the courtyard.

Xie Shiwei was held down on it by two attendants as he struggled with all his might. "Mother, I was wrong, I truly was wrong. Please, Mother, spare me this once..."

Yun Chu said coldly, "Begin."

Two well-built serving boys took their positions on either side, each holding a thick wooden board.

Thwack.

The first stroke landed hard across Xie Shiwei's backside.

He let out a yelp of pure anguish.

"Stop!"

He dressed in the plain garments of a servant came running in through the courtyard gate at that moment, shoved aside the boy wielding the board, and stepped before Yun Chu. She lowered her head to conceal her frantic expression and bent her knees in a bow. "My lady, using the family rod is no small matter. Should my lady not first consult the old mistress and Madame? And the second young master is young; I fear he may not be able to endure all twenty strokes. If he is harmed by them and the old mistress inquires..."

Yun Chu gave a quiet smile. "How curious it is that He Mama seems to care for Shiwei even more than I, his mother. Anyone watching might think He Mama is his true mother, and I the unfeeling stepmother."

He's face went abruptly white. "My lady, that is not what I meant. I was only concerned that the old mistress might fault my lady for injuring the second young master..."

"The master's affairs are not for a servant to worry over. Step back." Yun Chu's voice was ice cold. "Continue."

The two serving boys stepped forward again. Another crack rang out, and Xie Shiwei's cries followed one after the other.

He bit down on her lower lip.

He was not the mistress's own child, after all. That was why she felt nothing.

She turned and ran toward Anshou Hall.

Yun Chu watched the serving boys apply the rod with perfect composure, one stroke, then two, then three. At first Xie Shiwei's screaming was sharp and desperate, then it grew fainter with each blow.

At the tenth stroke, he passed out entirely.

"Shiwei!"

The old Madame Xie arrived leaning on her walking stick, moving as fast as she could. At the sight of the scene before her, she was terribly shaken.

"Quickly, someone go fetch the physician!"

She was in a state of great agitation, calling for people to carry Xie Shiwei back to his room.

"If I had come any later, were you planning to beat Shiwei to death!" The old mistress fixed her eyes on Yun Chu, enunciating each word. "It was one cricket. Dead is dead. Can't you buy another one? Was there any need to reduce the child to this state? Even if punishment was warranted, there are a hundred other ways to do it. Who gave you permission to bring out the family rod? Are you trying to kill Shiwei?"

Xie Shi'an stepped forward. "Great-grandmother, this was my suggestion."

The old mistress was taken aback.

He Mama had come gasping to report that Chu'er intended to beat Shiwei to death, and she had assumed it was Chu'er who had ordered the family rod.

How had it been An'er?

"Shiwei's temperament really does need to be brought under control," Xie Shi'an said. "Otherwise, who can say what trouble he might cause in the future. With Father's transfer approaching, if someone in the household offends the Prince Pingxi estate, the consequences are unthinkable. These twenty strokes, Shiwei has to take them."

The old mistress gripped her walking stick tightly.

Prince Pingxi was the current Emperor's third son, a man of great military achievement and great imperial favor, a figure the Xie family could not have hoped to approach even in their most ambitious dreams.

And yet the young mistress had made a connection with the young lord of that very household.

Yun Chu lowered her eyes. "Whether I punish An'er by making him kneel in the ancestral hall, or punish Shiwei with the rod, the old mistress always fears I am injuring the children. When it comes down to it, it is because I am not their birth mother. Perhaps from now on, the only way to keep peace in this household is for me to spoil them and indulge them, and give them whatever they want."

The old mistress was somewhat at a loss for words.

In recent days she had come to Chu'er more than once to press her with questions, and each time the facts had proved her own assumptions wrong.

"Chu'er, these children are registered under your name. That makes them your own. To discipline them, to scold them, that is entirely your right. I am a great-grandmother once removed. It is not my place to interfere." She sighed. "Come then, back to Anshou Hall."

He, standing behind the old mistress, pressed her lips tightly together.
