If even the old mistress had stepped back, Madame Xie would not possibly intervene either. Did that mean her children were left entirely at the mercy of the mistress?

But as a mere servant, what could she say?

As she was leaving Sheng Residence, she heard Yun Chu instruct the servants: "Ten strokes remain. Once Shiwei has recovered, they will be carried out."

He stumbled forward and nearly fell.

The concubines in the courtyard looked at one another, each one lowering her head as much as possible and trying to make herself invisible.

Yun Chu waved them all away, keeping only Xie Pin behind.

"Mother."

Xie Pin was a little nervous.

She had always found Mother easy to be around, but she no longer dared to think that way.

She stood at Yun Chu's side, making a good show of being quiet and well-behaved.

Yun Chu sent Chen Defu off to buy another, superior cricket to be delivered to Prince Pingxi's estate, then sat with Xie Pin and began to teach her how to read the account books.

Xie Pin had studied and could read and write. She only lacked experience with arithmetic. Ting Shuang walked her through the calculations step by step.

For someone who had received an education, it was actually not difficult at all once someone was there to guide her.

Xie Pin caught on quickly, and before long she had a solid grasp of it. She worked her way through the previous year's accounts and looked up with wide eyes. "I had no idea. Our Xie household is such a modest family, and yet the yearly expenses come to this much. If it were just the shops, the entire household would be living on nothing. How lucky that we have Mother."

Yun Chu put down what she was working on and said gently, "So for now, the most important thing is to increase our income while reducing our spending. You are a young miss from the inner chambers and have no experience in expanding income, but perhaps you can help Mother think about where to cut costs?"

Xie Pin felt a sense of being trusted and relied upon. She nodded with full confidence. "Leave it to me, Mother. I will come up with a plan."

She spent the entire afternoon in Yun Chu's side parlor, going through the account books.

As the first shadows of dusk settled in, she came to Yun Chu in excitement. "Mother, there are over twenty rough-work matrons in our household. Every afternoon they are given tea and pastries, which works out to about ten-odd copper coins per person. That comes to over two hundred coins a day, and nearly ten taels of silver per month. If we cut this expense, we can save close to a hundred taels a year."

Yun Chu smiled. "A hundred taels is not a great sum, but if we find several more places like this to trim, it will add up to a considerable amount over the course of a year. Pin'er, this task is yours to carry out. Can you manage it?"

Xie Pin was encouraged. "I will do my best."

Yun Chu nodded. "You are young, so even if you make a mistake, it is no great matter. Come to me whenever you are uncertain about anything."

"Thank you, Mother."

Xie Pin brimmed with determination.

Between An'er's kneeling in the hall and Shiwei's rod, she alone had earned Mother's praise. She was going to make sure she handled what Mother had given her well.

She headed back to her own courtyard, arms full of account books, to keep studying.

Yun Chu turned back to her own reading with a faint smile, lowering her head over the ledgers once more.

But the accounts she was reading were not the Xie household's. They were the accounts for her own shops and estates.

The Xie family's affairs were something she could perform for appearances. What truly mattered was planning carefully what to do with what she herself held.

She was still deep in work when the sky had gone fully dark. Ting Shuang reminded her gently that it was time for the evening meal.

The food had only just been set out when Ting Xue came in from outside. "My lady, Old Chen just returned. He says the young lord of Prince Pingxi's estate does not want the cricket..."

chapters.title: If That Night
chapters.content:
Yun Chu took a sip of tea.

Ting Xue gave the details carefully. "Old Chen went to Prince Pingxi's estate twice. The first time, the young lord received him in person, but said the cricket was too small. So Old Chen went and bought a larger and sturdier one and sent it over, only to find that the young lord would not even come out to see him. He simply had his people turn Old Chen away, and sent word that if a satisfactory cricket was not delivered, the matter would not be considered closed."

Ting Feng frowned. "Why is the young lord of Prince Pingxi's estate so difficult to deal with?"

"Mind what you say," Ting Shuang cautioned her. "Words like that, you may say them in front of my lady, but you must never say them outside, or you will bring trouble down on my lady's head."

Yun Chu ate a little of the food before setting her chopsticks down. "The young lord has seen treasures beyond counting, so naturally a common cricket from the market will not impress him. Ting Xue, go and tell Old Chen to take a few people out to the hills and meadows beyond the city and search for crickets in the wild. Only something out of the ordinary is likely to catch the young lord's eye."

Ting Xue was about to accept the order.

The curtain over the dining room doorway was suddenly lifted.

A man with the bearing of carved jade stepped inside.

It was Xie Jingyu.

He settled himself at the dining table. "Bring another set of chopsticks and a bowl."

Ting Feng was quietly delighted.

It had been a very long time since the master had come to dine with the mistress in her quarters.

Husband and wife sharing a meal together, cultivating a little warmth between them; perhaps tonight the master would stay on at Sheng Residence after all.

She moved quickly to bring a full place setting and set it respectfully before Xie Jingyu.

Yun Chu, who had wanted to eat a little more, found that the moment she saw Xie Jingyu, her appetite vanished entirely.

She asked in an even voice, "What brings my husband here?"

"Prince Pingxi is occupied with official duties and has not yet taken a consort, so the young lord has no one to rein him in. His temperament is inevitably a little difficult." Xie Jingyu spoke unhurriedly. "Sending Old Chen, a servant, to the estate will make the young lord feel slighted, which is why he is giving Old Chen such a hard time. If you trust me, my lady, tomorrow happens to be my day of rest. Allow me to make the trip on your behalf."

An imperceptible cold smile touched the corner of Yun Chu's lips.

This was so like Xie Jingyu. He was plainly going for his own reasons, to cultivate a connection with the Prince Pingxi estate, yet the way he said it made it sound as though he was sacrificing himself for her sake.

Though, would a single cricket truly be enough to get a foot in the door of the Prince Pingxi estate?

She set aside her contempt and replied, "Thank you, husband, for helping me out of this difficulty."

Xie Jingyu looked at her. "You and I are husband and wife. Between family, there is no need for thanks."

It occurred to him suddenly that there was something about the pale beauty of his wife's face today that did not quite belong to the woman who had come to be known as Mistress Xie. She had worn that same look the first time he had seen her at the General's household, as though she had drawn all the light in the room toward herself, her beauty something almost beyond belief.

His throat moved. Without meaning to, he reached out and closed his hand around Yun Chu's.

In that instant, it was as though a poisonous snake had crept up from her palm. Yun Chu's skin rose in goose bumps. Her body moved of its own accord, pulling her hand free.

Xie Jingyu let go first.

His eyes were dark and unreadable.

He, too, had once wanted this: husband and wife in love, children filling the halls, growing old together.

But who could have foreseen what happened...

If that night...

Xie Jingyu rose. "I still have matters to attend to. I will be going."

He walked out with a hurried step.

At the gate of Sheng Residence, he turned back and looked. He saw Ting Shuang bring out a basin of water and set it on the table, and Yun Chu began to wash her hands with vigorous effort.

His expression darkened at once.

He had not even thought to hold her loss of purity against her, and she dared to...

He raised his head and noticed that Yusheng Residence had become Sheng Residence at some point he had not observed.

An emotion he could not quite name rose in his chest.

"My lord."

A figure appeared in the night: He.

Seeing him come out of Sheng Residence, there was a sourness in her voice. "My lord came straight to the mistress's quarters the moment you returned?"

Xie Jingyu walked forward with his hands clasped behind his back. "What is wrong with coming to see my wife?"

"Does my lord know what the mistress did today?" He bit down on her lower lip. "She used the family rod on Shiwei. His backside was cut open and bleeding. The physician says it will take at least half a month to heal. She is not his birth mother, so she feels no pain at all. But I do feel pain, my lord. Could you not speak to the mistress? Ask her not to..."

"She is the children's legitimate mother. Disciplining them is entirely within her right." Xie Jingyu's sharp eyes swept toward her. "Whether An'er can find a good teacher, whether Shiwei can be made into something useful, whether Pin'er can marry into a good family, all of it rests on her. What can you as the birth mother give them?"

He lowered her head. A bitter smile spread slowly across her face.

She turned away and walked toward Xie Shiwei's courtyard.

Before she had even stepped inside, she could hear the sounds of pained cries coming from within.

"All of you, go."

She sent all the servants away, closed the door, and went straight to the bed. "Shiwei, does it hurt?"

"Mama. Mama." Xie Shiwei threw himself into He's arms. "Why do we have to have that woman as my mother? I hate her. She is the person I hate most in the world..."

He covered his mouth with her hand. "Shiwei, she is your stepmother, and you must respect her. You are never to say such things again."

Whatever dislike she herself harbored for Yun Chu, she had to acknowledge that having Yun Chu as their mother was the choice that served her children best.

Xie Shiwei bit He's hand, then said with all the resentment he could muster, "She would not even give me one cricket. She has never treated me like a son. Why should I have to respect her? I hate her, I hate her..."

The words were barely finished when the door to the room was suddenly pushed open.

He opened her mouth to scold whatever servant had burst in without manners.

She turned, and there were Ting Shuang and Ting Xue, one on either side, stepping inside. Then the door swung fully open, and Yun Chu walked in.

The color drained entirely from He's face. She stumbled and fell to her knees before she could steady herself.

"My, my lady!"

She bowed her head in greeting, and in her heart she prayed, fervently, that the mistress had not heard the word Shiwei had cried out to her: Mama.

"Why is He Mama bowing so deeply to me? You are my husband's woman. I could not possibly accept such a deep bow." Yun Chu looked past her and toward the figure lying face down on the bed. "Shiwei just said he hates me most of all, did he?"

Xie Shiwei pressed his lips together and said nothing.

He had said it, but he had not truly meant it at full measure.

Before the age of four, he had lived with his mother on a farm estate outside the city, and life had been hard and sparse. After he came to live at the Xie household at four years old, every aspect of his life, in clothing and food, in lodging and daily care, had been better than it had ever been before.

He knew he could not afford to offend his mother. But after so many strokes of the rod, his grievance was genuine.

"It seems Shiwei has still not learned his lesson." Yun Chu shook her head with detached calm. "I had actually intended to cancel the remaining ten strokes. Since you still have no understanding of propriety, we will wait until your injury has healed and then continue the punishment."

Xie Shiwei's eyes went wide.

He had assumed his mother had come to comfort him. He had not expected her to be so merciless, to still intend to go through with the beating.

He did not dare say anything improper again. He turned over and scrambled out of the bed, grabbed hold of Yun Chu's sleeve, and held on. "Mother, I really do know I was wrong. I have learned my lesson. I truly remember it this time. Please, Mother, cancel the remaining strokes. Please, Mother!"

He opened and closed her mouth, swallowing the plea before it could come out.

Yun Chu bent down and helped Xie Shiwei lie back on his stomach on the bed. Her voice turned gentle. "That cricket was the most expensive one available on the market. It was priced at five hundred taels. Compared to that, twenty strokes of the rod is really nothing at all."

Xie Shiwei dissolved into a wail of despair. "Five hundred taels! I will pay it back to Mother! If five hundred is not enough, then a thousand!"

chapters.title: What Did She Gain
chapters.content:
Yun Chu smiled faintly.

She looked around the room. Aside from the four walls, which belonged to the Xie family, every single thing in it had been purchased by her own hand.

All of it, even if fed to the dogs, would be better than leaving it for this pack of ingrates.

She spoke. "Since Shiwei has said as much, I would be truly heartless to still have you beaten. But tell me, can you actually produce a thousand taels of silver?"

Xie Shiwei was instantly speechless.

His monthly allowance was only a few taels. The old mistress and his grandmother each gave him a little as well. All of it added up to twenty or thirty taels, and he had already spent every coin on food and entertainment. He could not produce a single copper.

Yun Chu raised her hand slightly. "Since you cannot, we will just have to make do with what we have."

Ting Shuang and Ting Xue stepped forward and began moving things out.

Several serving boys and matrons came in from outside to help.

The once-fine bedchamber was stripped bare in no time at all.

Xie Shiwei endured the pain and asked, keeping his voice in check, "Mother, what are you doing?"

"First, these things are worth a little silver, so consider them payment for the cricket." Yun Chu continued at a measured pace. "Second, the books say that when Heaven is about to entrust a man with a great task, it first afflicts his mind with suffering, tires his sinews and bones, and starves his body. When you first came to the Xie household, you were well-behaved and obedient. Now you grow more unruly by the day, which tells me I have raised you with too much coddling and softness. From today onward, your food, clothing, and daily comforts will all be reduced by half. When you have shown improvement, they will be restored."

Xie Shiwei wailed openly. "Mother, no, please. I know I was wrong!"

Yun Chu turned and left, taking the attendants with her.

"Mother, please don't go. I truly will change. I promise I will change. Please, Mother, don't do this to me..."

Xie Shiwei scrambled off the bed on all fours, and He caught him in her arms.

"Shiwei, the mistress is doing this for your own good..."

He struggled to say the words.

Compared to An'er, Shiwei was indeed far too undisciplined. This time she would not go running to the old mistress to make a complaint. She could only hope that under the mistress's firm hand, Shiwei would truly turn himself around.

He soothed him for quite some time before he finally quieted down and drifted off to sleep.

She walked out into the courtyard and let out a long breath.

So many things had happened in these past few days, more than in the past four years combined. She felt she could hardly keep up.

Stepping outside, she caught the sound of several matrons murmuring among themselves.

"What do you mean? Starting tomorrow, there will be no more afternoon tea and sunflower seeds?"

"That is what someone from the eldest young miss's courtyard said. She is going to bring it up tomorrow morning. The eldest young miss has barely started managing the household and she is already taking it out on us?"

"What is a few cups of tea and some seeds worth? The eldest young miss has no regard for us rough-work matrons at all."

"If she really takes away even a cup of tea, I am not going to lift a finger for whatever she asks of me from now on."

"..."

"What are you all gathered here for at this hour of the night!" He stepped out of the shadows and said coldly, "Get back to work, all of you."

Everyone knew she was the most trusted He Mama in the master's household. Not one of them dared say another word. They bowed their heads and scattered.

Under cover of the night, she made her way to Xie Pin's courtyard.

Xie Pin was still reading through account books. The moment she saw He come in, her brow furrowed. "Have I not told you? Come here as little as possible."

She was the legitimate eldest daughter of the Xie household now, and she was reluctant to be seen keeping close company with a servant, even if that servant was her own birth mother.

He chose her words carefully. "Pin'er, I..."

"Watch what you call me." Xie Pin was displeased. "You are the head stewardess of Father's courtyard. It is proper for you to address me as Eldest Young Miss. Must I keep reminding you?"

"Yes, Eldest Young Miss." He pressed down her dejection and continued, "I overheard the matrons in the courtyard saying that you have cancelled the daily afternoon tea?"

Xie Pin nodded. "I have. What of it?"

"This will not do," He said carefully. "You have only just started helping the mistress manage the household. Making such sweeping changes this early will cause the servants to resent you. When you need something done later, they will not obey you willingly. They will find endless ways to create trouble for you. Do not think those rough-work matrons are beneath consideration just because their standing is low. They can..."

"That is enough from you." Xie Pin's face was full of impatience. "Mother herself said my plan was excellent. What standing do you have to say otherwise? Mother is from a great General's household. She understands everything. You are nothing but a rough-work servant. Do you really think I should listen to you over Mother? I still have account books to read. I have no time to talk to you. Someone, please show He Mama out."

A maidservant stepped in and gestured toward the door.

He wanted to say more, but Xie Pin gave her no opening, gathering her account books and retreating directly into the inner chamber.

He walked out of the courtyard, her eyes narrowing as she went.

She turned over in her mind everything that had happened in the past few days.

Although the mistress had always had good reason for every action she took, something made He feel, with a creeping unease, that the mistress seemed to be deliberately targeting her children one by one.

The old mistress and Madame Xie both deferred to the mistress in all things. The master let the mistress discipline the children as she saw fit. Even if the mistress beat the children until they were crippled, the Xie family would probably tell themselves she was doing it for the children's future.

Whether or not she was overthinking it, she could not afford to sit back and do nothing.

An idea surfaced in He's mind.

When she rose the next morning, rain was falling softly outside the window, and the fresh, cool air lifted Yun Chu's mood a little.

As Ting Shuang combed her hair, she said quietly, "Last night, He Mama personally sent a pot of flowers to Concubine Tao on the master's behalf."

Concubine Tao was Xie Jingyu's third concubine, a well-born woman gifted to him by his superior. She was with child, and the birth was still a little over three months away.

Yun Chu chose a hairpin and put it on. "Keep watching He."

She had known all along that, with her actions coming one after the other, He would eventually make a move.

In her past life, it was Concubine Tao's child who had suffered a mishap. Every piece of evidence had pointed at her, as though she had deliberately tried to harm the unborn child. Before that incident, the Xie family had treated her with some measure of respect. Afterward, her standing in the household had plummeted.

Concubine Tao's child had not died, but the child's mind had been damaged. The child could not speak, could not walk, and wore a blank, vacant expression at all times. It was she who had searched far and wide for renowned physicians. It was she who had moved heaven and earth to obtain the services of a celebrated healer. It was she who had nursed the child without rest, barely sleeping. And after the child had recovered, what had she gained?

Yun Chu gave a derisive smile.

In this life, He had made her move more than a month earlier than in the last. She wondered whether the Xie family's fourth young master had the fate to be born alive.

She had barely finished washing and dressing when Xie Shi'an came to pay his morning respects.

Since he had schoolroom to attend, he came earliest each day, waiting properly in the side parlor for Yun Chu to come out.

She exchanged a few casual words with him, and noticing he did not seem in a hurry to leave for the schoolroom, she asked, "Is there something else?"

"I am waiting for Father." Xie Shi'an replied. "Father is going to Prince Pingxi's residence, and he asked me to go with him. Does Mother have any instructions for me?"

Yun Chu said warmly, "Just be careful on the road."

Xie Jingyu placed more importance on this eldest son than on anything else. To be already laying the groundwork for him so early, his devoted fatherly love truly moved her.

A pity, then, that Xie Shi'an was never going to achieve what he had in their past life again.

chapters.title: Tell Her to Come Herself
chapters.content:
The morning streets of the capital were full of bustle.

Xie Jingyu and Xie Shi'an sat together in the carriage, father and son cast from the same mold, even their bearing nearly identical.

The carriage passed through the most bustling thoroughfares and rolled into the most prized district of the capital, where every household belonged to a high official, the lowest of them holding a second-rank post.

"Once we are inside the Prince's residence, mind your words and conduct carefully," Xie Jingyu reminded him. "A royal household has strict protocols. You are young; do not speak unless spoken to."

Xie Shi'an nodded. "I understand, Father."

As the two of them approached the residence gate, Xie Jingyu was about to step up to the entrance when the guards stationed on either side called out sharply, "Who goes there? State your purpose. Do you have a visiting card?"

Xie Jingyu clasped his hands in a bow. "I am Xie Jingyu, Bureau Director of the Ministry of Revenue. My wife inadvertently caused offense to the young lord of this household the other day. I have come to offer my apologies."

"So you have no visiting card, then." The guard looked down at him. "Wait at the gate. I will go in and inquire first."

Xie Jingyu's expression became strained.

He was, after all, a fifth-rank official of the imperial court. That a guard should look at him with such unconcealed contempt, and tell him to wait at the gate on top of it, was an affront that was difficult to bear.

"So this is what they mean when they say even a third-rank official must bow before a prime minister's doorman," Xie Shi'an said quietly. "Great-grandfather was a xiucai; grandfather was a juren; Father passed the examinations as top scholar, and in just over five years has risen to a fifth-rank court post. By my generation, I will make the Xie family a new power in the imperial court. But when that day comes, I will never allow a Xie servant to look down upon anyone."

Xie Jingyu's face was full of warmth. "It is not for nothing that I have invested so much in you."

As they spoke, footsteps approached. The two of them fell quiet and composed themselves into an attitude of respectful waiting.

A small, round little figure in fine clothes emerged from the gate of the Prince's residence. It was the four-year-old young lord of the Pingxi Prince's household.

The moment he caught sight of the two people waiting at the gate, the eager anticipation on his delicate little face turned to outright indignation.

"Greetings to the young lord." Xie Jingyu lifted the cage he was carrying and presented it with both hands. "This is a rare iron-headed, green-backed fighting cricket of exceptional temper and ferocity. Please allow the young lord to inspect it."

The little one came thumping down the steps, took the cage, and then hurled it to the ground.

"This cricket is ugly and I do not want it!" The young lord's face was full of fury. He pointed straight at Xie Jingyu's nose. "Go back and tell that woman to come to the Prince's residence herself!"

He had seen every kind of fine cricket in existence. What he wanted was for that woman to bring one to him with her own hands.

At the thought of the woman he had glimpsed at the tea house that day, his eyes grew unexpectedly bright with the threat of tears. For reasons he could not name, he simply wanted to see her.

The stronger the grievance, the more furious he became. He raised his voice. "Tell her that if she does not come, I will go to her!"

"And who exactly are you going to go find?"

A cold, sharp voice cut through the air without warning.

Immediately after, a horse of extraordinary breeding came to a stop before the residence gate, and a man in dark purple-black court robes swung down from the saddle.

Xie Jingyu turned around and bent his spine as low as it would go. "Your subordinate pays his respects to Your Highness!"

This was the first time he had ever been at such close quarters with Prince Pingxi.

This was a magnificent opportunity to make the Prince's acquaintance.

And yet.

Prince Pingxi did not spare him so much as a glance. He walked forward and scooped the little figure up with one hand.

His voice was very low. "What did you just say? You are going to go find whom?"

"Father..." The little one shrank his neck down into his shoulders. "I, I was not going to find anyone. Father must have misheard."

The man gave a cold smile, turned and tossed the child into the arms of a nearby attendant. "If he sets so much as one foot outside this residence, the lot of you who serve him can forget about ever coming back through this gate."

With that, he glanced over at Xie Jingyu. "Children say foolish things. Think nothing of it, Director Xie. Please do not come again."

Xie Jingyu was about to say something, but Prince Pingxi had already strode back inside the residence.

The two gate guards pulled the doors closed.

Xie Jingyu's face was written over with disappointment.

Such a good opportunity, and he had failed to make use of it.

Xie Shi'an ventured, "Perhaps if Mother..."

Xie Jingyu pressed his lips together. "There is no need."

He was a grown man. To be unable to handle a matter this small and then have his wife come to his rescue would be a profound humiliation.

But Yun Chu was no fool who knew nothing of the world.

The carriage driver who had taken Xie Jingyu and Xie Shi'an to the Prince's residence was someone she had brought from the Yun household, and he gave her a complete account of everything that had happened at the gate.

"The young lord demanded that our mistress come to the Prince's residence in person?" Ting Shuang was clearly astonished. "There is no consort in the Prince's residence, so for my lady to call upon them would be entirely improper. How could the young lord make such a demand?"

The carriage driver bowed his head. "Prince Pingxi gave the young lord a thorough scolding and told the Xie household not to come calling again."

Ting Xue exhaled in relief. "It seems the matter has been put to rest. The Prince is reasonable after all. He understood that the fault lay with the young lord, and he has not made things difficult for our mistress."

Yun Chu gave a quiet nod.

Prince Pingxi had always been a reasonable man. In her past life, when the Yun family found themselves in dire straits, he was the only one willing to fight on their behalf.

While they were still talking, Ting Yu came through the doorway. "My lady, I have made this soup especially for you. Please drink it while it is warm."

Yun Chu's voice was flat. "I have already had my soup. Take it away."

Ting Yu's lips moved in a flutter of hesitation. She fidgeted and said, "My lady, has this concubine done something wrong? Or has Yun'er violated some rule?"

These past few days, the mistress had been handing out punishments to the eldest and second young masters. She worried that Yun'er might have done something to displease the mistress, and that was why she had driven them out of the Yusheng Residence.

Living in the Yusheng Residence had given her a place of closeness and standing within the Xie household. Since being moved out, not only had her daily living become somewhat less comfortable, but some of the senior maids and matrons had started giving her looks.

That was why she had worked up the courage to come and ask the mistress what was going on.

Yun Chu looked at her. "Since the birth of Yun'er, you have not attended to the master at all. I have thought it over, and I believe it is more convenient for you to have your own courtyard, so that the master may visit with more ease."

Ting Yu bit down on her lower lip.

Yun Chu picked up an account book and opened it. Ting Yu knew the mistress was about to get busy, so she had no choice but to bow her head and withdraw.

She had barely stepped outside the courtyard when she heard the sound of a snort of laughter.

"Well, if it is not our Concubine Yu." Ting Feng said with cold amusement. "Concubine Jiang and Concubine Tao both stay quietly in their own courtyards. Only you are always trying to push yourself in front of the mistress. You would not happen to think that just because you grew up serving the mistress, you are somehow different from the other concubines, would you? From the day you climbed into the master's bed behind the mistress's back, the mistress has never looked at you the same way. Whatever consideration she shows you now is purely for the sake of the third young master. You ought to be grateful you bore a good son."

Ting Yu tried painfully to explain. "That night, it really was not intentional. The master had been drinking, and..."

"Do not explain matters of the bedchamber to me, an unmarried girl." Ting Feng gave a thin smile. "I am just a maidservant; such an explanation from a concubine is entirely wasted on me. Concubine Yu, do take care on your way out."

Ting Yu left Sheng Residence with her dignity in pieces, biting her lip against the humiliation.

Yun Chu sat on the daybed, her mind drifting.

Ting Shuang was twenty this year. Even Ting Feng, the youngest, was sixteen. It was time to start looking for suitable husbands for them.

In her past life, after Ting Shuang had died, Ting Feng and Ting Xue had both vowed never to marry, keeping vigil by Yun Chu's side. In this life, she would not allow her girls to follow her into a solitary and bitter existence.

chapters.title: He Mama's Thoughtfulness
chapters.content:
Chen Defu was efficient. The more than twenty thousand taels Yun Chu had given him, along with some of the income from the shops, had all been used to purchase ice.

In an ordinary summer, ice sold for roughly one tael per jin. In spring the price was lower, around five or six hundred copper coins, but this particular spring was so cold that everyone assumed the summer would not be too warm either, and the price had dropped again and again. Chen Defu had bought in enormous quantities at three hundred and fifty copper coins per jin, and every ice cellar in the vicinity of the capital had been rented out.

Yun Chu still remembered clearly: in her past life, that summer had been one of savage, unbearable heat. Ice had been driven to a price comparable to gold itself, so steep that most people could only look on helplessly.

The ice she had purchased for just over thirty thousand taels would sell for at least two or three hundred thousand.

With that kind of money, many problems that lay ahead could be solved.

She had stayed up late the night before, so she woke a little later than usual that morning. By the time she came out, the concubines had all gathered.

"My lady."

"Mother."

Everyone bowed in greeting.

Yun Chu lifted her hand slightly, and only then did the room dare take their seats.

None of them wanted to earn a punishment from the mistress by failing to observe proper decorum.

She swept a glance around the room. "Where is Concubine Tao?"

Concubine Jiang, who lived next door to Concubine Tao, stood up quickly to reply. "Concubine Tao was sick through the night, with both vomiting and stomach trouble. She asked to come later this morning, as she was feeling unwell. Please do not hold it against her, my lady."

Yun Chu's brow drew together. "Women do suffer all manner of discomforts during pregnancy. With the birth still three months away, a body that is too weak will make a difficult delivery."

She turned to the maidservant at her side. "Ting Xue, take some tonics from my storeroom to Concubine Tao's courtyard."

Ting Xue nodded and went to see to it.

Yun Chu's gaze settled on the small girl at Concubine Jiang's side. This was the Xie household's second daughter, Xie Xian, a child of almost no presence in the household.

She had a dim recollection: just before her death, when Xie Shiyun had forced the poison into her hands, it was Xie Xian who had come running with great sobs and knocked the bowl to the ground.

In the entire Xie household, only Xian'er had wept without ceasing for her.

Sensing Yun Chu's gaze, Xie Xian hid behind Concubine Jiang and called out in a small voice, "Mother."

"Xian'er is a little too timid." Yun Chu smiled. "Three years old is old enough to begin her education. Let Xian'er start attending lessons."

The family had engaged a tutor to teach the children to read, and after that foundational stage, the older children went on to study at the academies run by the court's Ministry of Education, as Xie Shi'an did.

Concubine Jiang had in truth long wished for the child to begin her studies.

But since Xie Pin had not started learning to read and write until the age of five, she had been afraid that starting Xian'er too early might earn the eldest young miss's displeasure.

Now that the mistress herself had spoken, however, she accepted immediately, pulling Xie Xian forward. "Come now, thank your Mother."

"We are family. No need for thanks." Yun Chu waved her hand. "Stop standing about in my rooms. All of you may go."

Everyone withdrew.

Xie Pin stayed behind to continue her studies in household management with Yun Chu.

Once the lesson was largely finished, Yun Chu spoke. "Early this morning, Stewardess Li brought in several cartloads of jujube trees. Take the accounts and go verify them. Small discrepancies you may handle yourself; larger issues bring back to me."

Xie Pin stood. "Yes, Mother."

She took the account books and went.

The moment she left, Ting Shuang came over and said in a low voice, "My lady, the tonics you ordered have been sent to Concubine Tao's courtyard. The maidservants have been preparing a bird's nest dish. Concubine Tao had barely had a few spoonfuls when He Mama arrived with several bolts of fine brocade, saying the master had sent them for Concubine Tao to have some new clothes made."

Ting Feng muttered under her breath, "When our mistress was with child, the master was never this thoughtful..."

She caught herself midway through the sentence, realizing it would pain the mistress, and clapped her hand over her own mouth.

Ting Shuang lowered her head. "The master is occupied with official affairs. He cannot be expected to attend to every small thing himself. It would be more accurate to say it is He Mama who is being thoughtful."

Yun Chu took a sip of tea.

It seemed He was already eager to make her move.

She had done her best to make it easy for her. She could only hope He would not disappoint.

At that moment, a commotion broke out in the courtyard.

A moment later, Xie Pin came running in with a dark expression. "Mother, those matrons have no respect for me whatsoever. They have been saying the most infuriating things. You really must do something about them."

From outside came the voices of the matrons, calling out, "My lady, please do right by us! We may be rough-work servants, but we are still people. The Xie household cannot treat us this way..."

Xie Pin's face had gone red with indignation.

Yun Chu patted her hand, signaling her to be calm, then stepped outside.

The matrons all spoke at once, and between them they laid out the whole affair clearly.

The matter was simple enough. Xie Pin had gone to verify the jujube tree delivery earlier. The numbers matched, the matter was settled, and she had been about to leave. One of the matrons had then said she was thirsty and asked whether the kitchen could send some tea.

The question was clearly a deliberate test. The woman had obviously heard about the cancelled afternoon tea.

Xie Pin had not thought anything of it. Taking the woman's question as her cue, she had announced the cancellation of the daily afternoon tea and pastries.

The announcement was like pouring oil into boiling water. The whole group erupted at once.

"My lady, we work the hardest jobs for the lowest wages, and now even a cup of tea to wet our lips is being taken from us. One cannot help but feel bitter."

"The maids who attend the inner chambers earn much higher wages, and they still get to drink the masters' tea and eat their leftover pastries. Why not start with them?"

"The eldest young miss has barely started managing the household and already our lives have taken a turn for the worse. What is it to be next?"

"If you ask me, the eldest young miss is simply not suited to running a household!"

"The eldest young miss was born to a woman kept outside. Only an illegitimate young miss would torment us servants over a few copper coins..."

Xie Pin gripped her handkerchief until her knuckles went white.

The one thing she could not bear was a servant calling her the child of an outside woman. That cut deeper than a slap to the face.

Yun Chu set her teacup down on the table with a firm sound, and the matrons fell silent at once.

"You matrons still have your bond papers in the Xie family's hands, and yet you dare to show such contempt for the masters of this household?" A coldness radiated from her. "The eldest young miss of the Xie household is registered under my name, which makes her fully and properly the legitimate eldest daughter. If I hear another word of this nonsense from any of you, you will be sold off immediately."

The matrons, who had been talking over one another moments before, went completely silent.

They were not afraid of the eldest young miss because her standing was not impressive enough to inspire real fear. But the mistress was different. This was the true-born legitimate daughter of a General's household.

Xie Pin looked at Yun Chu with profound gratitude.

Mother had been quick to anger these past two days, and Xie Pin had worried she might be blamed. She had feared Mother might strip her of her household duties just as she had punished An'er and Shiwei.

"However," Yun Chu's voice softened, "I gave Pin'er the authority to manage this matter, and since she has decided to cancel the afternoon tea and pastries, I have no objection."

The matrons' faces fell.

Even the mistress would not take their side. Were they just to accept this then?

"But you do work hard." Yun Chu's tone became gentle. "How about this: every rough-work matron will receive a monthly pay increase of fifty copper coins. Any objections?"

At these words, the matrons stared with eyes as wide as they would go.

A few cups of tea in the afternoon, a handful of seeds and pastries, and then they were gone. But monthly wages were real copper coins you could feel in your pocket. That kind of security was worth far more.

"No objections, none at all!" The matrons broke into smiles. "We are grateful to my lady! We will get back to work right away."

Once everyone had gone, Yun Chu turned to Xie Pin. "Any new policy will face resistance when it is first put in place. Do not let those matrons frighten you. Go ahead boldly and do what you need to do. I will always be here."

Xie Pin said with feeling, "I understand, Mother."

chapters.title: Concubine Tao's Mishap
chapters.content:
The monthly wages of the Xie household's rough-work matrons were not high, just a little over five hundred copper coins.

An increase of fifty coins per month meant they would take home nearly one tael of silver more over the course of a year. How could anyone not be pleased by that?

"The mistress truly cares for us servants."

"Our mistress is a daughter of the General's household. She would not bother over a little money like this."

"I really cannot understand why the mistress would want the eldest young miss helping her manage the household. The way the eldest young miss is going, things are going to be in an uproar."

"The eldest young miss will be married off sooner or later anyway. As long as the mistress is the one running this household, there is nothing to worry about."

"I hope the eldest young miss gets married soon."

"..."

He, standing not far away, was seething.

Xie Pin had just saved three hundred copper coins a month per matron by cutting the afternoon tea. Now the mistress had given those matrons a raise of fifty coins each. Was she not simply using Xie Pin's effort to buy goodwill for herself?

The mistress was too calculating by half. She had made herself look magnanimous by stepping on Xie Pin.

If word spread that Xie Pin had no idea how to run a household, what great family would want to take her as its mistress and wife?

Shiwei was still laid up in bed nursing his injuries, and now Pin'er's reputation was close to ruined. What exactly was the mistress trying to do?

She could not wait until things had gone too far to act. That would be too late.

He's eyes darkened. She turned and walked away quickly.

Before long, a serving boy from the outer courtyard came to Sheng Residence to report. "My lady, He Mama has just gone out of the estate on her own to visit a medicine hall."

Yun Chu's lips curved into a smile. "Bring the chicken soup that was made at noon. We are going to Anshou Hall."

It was after the evening meal, and dusk was beginning to settle. The courtyard had not yet been lit. Every servant who passed by stopped to bow respectfully and call out a greeting to the mistress.

They reached Anshou Hall quickly. Two matrons stood guard at the door, and two maidservants were sweeping the courtyard. At the door of the main room, two more maidservants stood at attention. When they lifted the curtain, two more maids and matrons could be seen attending inside.

Anshou Hall alone employed more than ten people to wait upon the old mistress.

A household without the means for this kind of display was doing its best to perform it anyway.

Yun Chu pulled her lips into a slight smile and stepped inside.

The old Madame Xie was seated at the head of the room, with her daughter-in-law Madam Yuan seated beside her. The two women were in the middle of a conversation.

"Ah, so Mother is here too." Yun Chu smiled. "I only brought one bowl of chicken soup. This puts me in a difficult position."

The old mistress said, "Your mother brought me a bowl of rock sugar bird's nest when she arrived. I could not possibly drink another thing. Let your mother have it."

Ting Shuang brought the chicken soup and set it before Madam Yuan.

Madam Yuan drank a few sips and praised the soup for being rich and tender. Then she said, "Chu'er, how is Pin'er getting on with managing the household? I have been hearing a few things..."

"Mother, have you forgotten that when I first took over the household affairs, I went through all the same difficulties." Yun Chu replied. "When Pin'er eventually becomes the mistress of her own household, she will face the deliberate obstruction of servants sooner or later. Here in our Xie household, she has me standing behind her and teaching her every step of the way. What reason does Mother have to worry?"

Madam Yuan's face relaxed with relief. "Jingyu's greatest achievement was not passing the examinations at the top of the list. It was marrying a helpmate like you."

Yun Chu looked toward the old mistress. "It will soon be the old mistress's birthday. This year, I was thinking of putting Pin'er in charge of the arrangements. What does the old mistress think?"

The old Madame Xie frowned slightly. "Can Pin'er manage it?"

"Is Chu'er not right there?" Madam Yuan said with complete confidence. "If Pin'er does anything wrong, Chu'er can offer a word or two of guidance. Nothing is going to go amiss."

The old mistress considered for a moment. "Very well."

Pin'er's marriage was of great importance. A good match would be a considerable advantage for the Xie family, and she had to learn household management properly.

Yun Chu sipped her tea and looked up. "Old mistress, I heard from the servants that you sent some things to Shiwei's courtyard this morning?"

The old mistress was momentarily at a loss.

She had declared so firmly before that she would not interfere with Yun Chu's discipline of the children, and here she was, having turned around and done exactly that.

"Shiwei has been spoiled rotten. That temperament of his needs to be firmly checked." Yun Chu continued, "I will keep the things the old mistress sent for now. Once Shiwei has shown improvement, I will pass them along on your behalf."

The items she was taking back were things she herself had once given to the old mistress as a gesture of filial respect. Reclaiming them was entirely within her right.

The old mistress's expression was not pleasant.

Everything she had sent to Shiwei's room had been exceptional, and here it was, taken back by her daughter-in-law without hesitation.

The three women were still in conversation when a matron came rushing in from outside. "Old mistress, something has happened!"

The old mistress, still smarting from her exchange with Yun Chu, turned her irritation on the matron and snapped, "I am sitting here perfectly well. What do you mean something has happened? Have you no manners at all!"

The matron struck herself across the mouth before continuing. "Concubine Tao is in a very bad way. There is a great deal of blood. I have already taken it upon myself to send for the physician!"

The old mistress rose to her feet abruptly. "The child is only six or seven months along. How can there be bleeding? Come, let us go and see!"

Yun Chu and Madam Yuan quickly rose as well and followed her out toward Concubine Tao's courtyard.

The mistress of the household had arrived. Concubine Tao's maidservant hurried to pay her respects. "Old mistress, Madame, my lady, Concubine Tao had been unwell since last night, but it was only a little vomiting and stomach trouble. Just now she suddenly complained of abdominal pain, and there is bleeding."

It was not yet time for the birth. Everyone present understood what bleeding at this stage meant, and every face in the courtyard turned grave.

While the maidservant was still speaking, the physician arrived at last, hurrying inside to take the patient's pulse.

After a short while, the physician emerged. "The concubine appears to have ingested something that has disturbed the fetus. Fortunately, the amount was small, and most of it has been expelled through vomiting. With the proper stabilizing herbs and careful rest, the child should be preserved."

The old mistress exhaled with relief.

In her old age, she loved nothing more than to be surrounded by children and grandchildren. The more descendants, the more prosperous the family; and if there were many to mourn her when she was gone, she could face her ancestors with pride.

For that reason, she would not allow a single child to come to harm.

The old mistress spoke. "Bring everything Concubine Tao consumed today and lay it before the physician. Let him determine what it was that caused the problem."

The maidservant went quickly. What remained of the food was brought out; what had already been finished was described in detail for the physician's review.

"This chicken soup..." The physician's gaze came to rest on a large bowl of soup that was mostly uneaten. He touched his finger to the surface of the broth and tasted it. His expression changed at once. "Did the abdominal pain begin after she drank this soup?"

The maidservant nodded. "The concubine drank a few sips and felt worse, so she put it down. She had only just lain down when the pain and the bleeding started."

"There is saffron in this soup." The physician's face was deeply troubled. "Old mistress, I would strongly advise a thorough investigation. If this were to happen again, there would be no saving the child."

After leaving the prescription, the physician took his medicine case and departed.

The old mistress had someone slip the physician a sum of money. The meaning was plain: she hoped he would not carry tales of the Xie household's dirty affairs.

Madam Yuan stepped forward, her face showing that she could hardly believe what she was hearing. "This is the same as the chicken soup Chu'er just brought, is it not?"

The old mistress's gaze moved to Yun Chu, filled with suspicion and scrutiny.

Yun Chu met that gaze without flinching. "I did send that soup. One bowl to Anshou Hall, and another to Concubine Tao's courtyard."

The old mistress's face was heavy. "The physician says the soup you sent contained saffron. What do you have to say for yourself?"

In recent days, Yun Chu had punished one child after another, and the old mistress had told herself it was all for the children's benefit, choosing to overlook it.

She had never imagined that Yun Chu would move against an unborn child.

chapters.title: Fear of Father's Anger
chapters.content:
Dusk fell.

The lanterns in the courtyard came alive one by one.

With Concubine Tao in trouble, every member of the Xie household had come, save for Xie Jingyu: Concubine Jiang and Concubine Yu, Xie Shi'an and Xie Pin. The small courtyard was packed.

Every gaze rested on Yun Chu.

She stood with complete composure. "So you suspect it was I who tried to end Concubine Tao's pregnancy?"

"It is not that I suspect you; it is that the evidence points to you." The old mistress spoke. "Chu'er, you know how much trust I have placed in you. I would not have handed over the full management of this household otherwise. And is this how you repay my trust?"

"I..." Concubine Jiang ventured carefully, "I would like to say a word in fairness. The mistress has absolutely no motive to do such a thing."

If the mistress had children of her own, one might understand a fear of concubine-born sons. But the mistress was childless, and she would never have children. Furthermore, the master had always decreed that any child born to any concubine was to be registered under the mistress's name. One child or a dozen, they were all hers to raise. There was simply no reason to deliberately end Concubine Tao's pregnancy.

Madam Yuan nodded. "Chu'er has always been generous and forgiving. She would never commit such a thing."

The old mistress gave a cold smile.

Yun Chu had once been generous, certainly. But in recent days she had become more and more difficult to deal with. Committing something like this was not outside the realm of possibility.

At that moment, Concubine Tao called out from inside the room. "Old mistress, I know why the mistress wanted to harm my child..."

The old mistress had someone open the door. Concubine Tao's voice came through more clearly now. "These past few days, the master has been sending me things constantly, a pot of flowers, several bolts of fabric, jewelry and hair ornaments. The mistress must have seen that the master was paying such particular attention to a concubine, and feared it would be a case of the master favoring the concubine over the wife. That is why she moved against my child."

Madam Yuan let out a quiet sigh.

Four or five years ago, when Chu'er had been with child, Jingyu had not shown this kind of attentiveness. It was not altogether unreasonable that she might have acted out of jealousy.

Ting Yu pressed her lips together.

When she herself had been with child, she had hidden it from the mistress for as long as she could, fearing the mistress might do something to the baby out of desperation. It seemed, looking back, that she had not been wrong to worry.

"Jealousy is one of the seven grounds for divorce." The old Madame Xie's face was full of disappointment. "Chu'er, you are the legitimate daughter of the Yun General's household. You are the head mistress of our Xie household. How could you be so foolish?"

Yun Chu looked around the courtyard and took in the expression on every face.

She touched her dark hair and spoke. "The Xie family also prides itself on scholarship. Surely the books do not teach us to condemn someone on evidence this thin?"

Her unruffled demeanor grated on the old mistress's nerves.

She had been far more comfortable with the Yun Chu who emerged after losing her child, that quiet and compliant mistress of the household, the daughter-in-law who could be shaped however one wished.

She had to secure this evidence against Yun Chu, to put her back into that obedient state.

With that thought in mind, she spoke. "Someone go and search the Yusheng Residence."

Zhou Mama gave Yun Chu a slight bow. "My lady, forgive this old servant."

With that, she took six or seven matrons and maidservants from the courtyard and walked toward Sheng Residence.

It was not a great distance. Zhou Mama returned before long, shaking her head. "Old mistress, nothing was found."

The old mistress frowned. "How can that be? Was the storeroom searched?"

Zhou Mama bowed her head. "That is my lady's dowry storeroom. Without her permission, this servant dared not..."

The old mistress's expression darkened.

Perhaps Yun Chu had already disposed of any evidence.

"Even if you had gone into my dowry storeroom, you would not have found what the old mistress is looking for. Because..." Yun Chu paused, "you searched the wrong place."

The old mistress narrowed her eyes. "What do you mean?"

Yun Chu raised her head and looked beyond the courtyard. "He Mama, since you are here, why are you standing outside?"

He was startled.

She had been standing in the shadows. Under ordinary circumstances, no one should have been able to spot her at a glance.

The mistress was in the middle of being questioned, and yet she had noticed her presence.

She lowered her head and stepped inside. "This servant feared the master would ask questions upon his return and find me unable to answer, so I came to..."

Before she could finish, Yun Chu clapped her hands.

Ting Shuang, who had been standing at the courtyard gate, came in with two people.

One was a man dressed in the manner of a shop proprietor. The other was a small beggar child of about seven or eight years old.

When the two of them entered and looked around at everyone present, their gaze came to rest on He.

In that instant, He's breath caught entirely.

"It was her who gave me twenty copper coins and told me to go to Shande Hall to buy medicine." The beggar child pointed at He. "I have a good memory for faces. I could not be wrong."

The man dressed like a proprietor spoke. "Half an hour ago, this child came to my shop to purchase medicine. He had no prescription, but named several herbs. I measured out a portion of each for him, and saffron was among them."

The moment these two finished speaking, every face in the courtyard showed disbelief.

"It was not me. He has the wrong person." He fought to keep her voice steady. "I left the estate to purchase an inkstone for the master. I ask the old mistress to investigate properly."

The old mistress gripped her walking stick. "He is a servant. She would have no motive to harm a child of the masters. This is impossible."

Yun Chu's voice was measured. "I would naturally never follow the old mistress's example of condemning someone without evidence. We now have a witness. We only need to find the physical evidence. Ting Shuang, take a few people and search He Mama's room carefully."

"Mother!" Xie Pin could hold herself back no longer. "He Mama has been utterly loyal to Father. She would not harm Father's child. Even a search will turn up nothing."

Xie Shi'an stepped forward. "He Mama is Father's person, Mother. Searching her room without cause, I am afraid it will anger Father."

Yun Chu's lips curved into a faint smile. "I am your father's wife, wed to him by proper ceremony and full rites. When people searched my rooms just now, why was that not going to anger your father? Or is it that in your father's eyes, a household servant carries more importance than I, his own lawful wife?"

Xie Shi'an was left without a word.

Yun Chu shook her head slowly. "An'er, you would rather put your trust in a servant than in me, your own mother. That truly breaks my heart."

She made a gesture.

Ting Shuang immediately led several people toward the room where He lived.

Not a single person in the courtyard spoke.

The old mistress gripped her walking stick with both hands. The evidence was not yet in hand, but she already knew how this was going to turn out.

Those clouded old eyes passed over He like the edge of a blade.

She truly had not imagined that He would dare move against the unborn child of this household and then plant the blame on the mistress.

She should never have allowed He to remain at the Xie estate, not even for the sake of An'er and the two younger siblings.

Ting Shuang moved quickly. In less than a quarter of an hour, she was back with her people, several herbs bundled together and presented for everyone to see. "These were found beneath He Mama's bed."

The man dressed like a proprietor stepped forward and looked them over. "Yes, those are the exact herbs the beggar child purchased, saffron included. I would not be mistaken."

"Thank you both for making the trip." Yun Chu produced two small money pouches and handed them over. "Please treat everything that happened today as though it never occurred. I am grateful."

The payment was a clear silencing fee. Both the proprietor and the beggar child understood that perfectly well.

But once outside the Xie estate, they opened their pouches and found only a few dozen copper coins between them. The proprietor's expression shifted at once. He had never intended to go around gossiping about someone else's household affairs, but to be dismissed with such a pittance was a genuine insult.

chapters.title: You Are Like the Rain from Heaven
chapters.content:
Every servant was dismissed from the courtyard.

He stood at the center of it, head bowed, repeating over and over, "I truly did not do this. This evidence has been planted against me..."

"It certainly was not He Mama." Xie Pin struggled to get the words out. "He Mama is a servant. What reason would she have to harm Father's child? Something has gone wrong somewhere. This must be a misunderstanding!"

She gripped her handkerchief until her knuckles ached, her heart full of bitter frustration.

She did not understand it. An'er was already so accomplished, Father's proudest son. An unborn concubine-born child was no threat to An'er's position at all. Why would He take such a reckless risk?

Unless, perhaps, because the master had been paying such particular attention to Concubine Tao recently, He had acted out of jealousy and done this foolish thing in a moment of desperation?

No matter how much it galled her, Xie Pin knew she had to protect He. She could not allow her to be sold off carrying a charge this serious, or sent to the magistrate's office.

Xie Pin cast a meaningful glance at Xie Shi'an.

Xie Shi'an pressed his lips together.

Just now, he had hurt his mother by choosing to trust He over her. If he opened his mouth again to speak on He's behalf, his mother would be even more hurt, and might never warm to him again.

Four years ago, He had stayed at the Xie estate out of fear that the three siblings might be neglected or mistreated under the mistress's care. But the years had proved that the mistress had treated them as her own.

Now that they were older, this incident was perhaps a suitable occasion to have He leave the Xie estate. He had used allowance money over the years to quietly set up a small courtyard outside. It would be a perfectly suitable place for He to live.

The old Madame Xie let out a slow breath. "He does not have a plausible motive for harming a child of this household. This matter needs to be investigated more carefully."

Yun Chu raised her hand. "Since she had no motive, and it is on that basis that you believe she is innocent, then let us present the motive."

He froze.

What was her motive? If she were honest, she could not even say with certainty herself. Was it for the children, so that they might no longer be under the mistress's thumb? Was it for An'er's position in the household? Or was it something as simple as envy of the mistress?

Ting Xue came in carrying a tray. On it lay more than a dozen envelopes.

Yun Chu opened one and handed it to Xie Shi'an without ceremony. "These were found during the search of the room. An'er, read it aloud."

Xie Shi'an's heart contracted sharply.

Had He's correspondence with her own family been found?

But when his eyes fell on the writing within, the thing lodged in his throat finally dropped back down to his stomach. He read aloud slowly: "You are like the rain that falls from heaven, and I am like the well that waits below the roof. There is no way for our waters to join and flow as one; I can only wish to be your shadow, and follow where you go."

Everyone present had some degree of education, and they all understood: this was a love poem, written by a woman to a man.

Xie Shi'an's voice lodged in his throat. He could not read another word. The color in his face cycled through several shades, each one more extraordinary than the last.

Yun Chu spoke. "Compare this with He Mama's usual handwriting and it will be confirmed that this letter is in her hand. As for who it was written to, look at the very beginning. Two characters are written there: Yu Lang. I imagine I need not say more. Old mistress, Madame, you should both know who Yu Lang refers to."

Madam Yuan looked as though she had swallowed something revolting. "He, you... you actually harbored such shameless thoughts?"

Concubine Jiang covered her mouth. "No wonder He Mama is so old and still unmarried. It turns out... it turns out..."

"You are not even a concubine. What right do you have to be consumed by jealousy? And you had the audacity to move against a child!" Concubine Tao wept loudly from inside the room. "If anything happens to my child, I will never let this rest!"

He snapped her head up and looked toward Yun Chu.

In that moment, everything became clear.

All of this had been a trap.

The moment she moved against Concubine Tao, the mistress had already known about her plan, had already arranged for people to keep watch, which was why she could produce both witness and physical evidence so swiftly.

Was it because the mistress had seen this letter she had written to the master? Had she felt threatened by her presence and decided to lure her into this trap?

With all the evidence laid out before everyone, she had no argument left to make.

"He, as a servant, harboring feelings you should not have for the master is one thing. But to lay your hands on an unborn child!" Yun Chu's words came out one by one, deliberate and precise. "Our Xie household cannot keep you. Someone, take He to the magistrate's office."

"Mother!" Xie Shi'an clenched his fist. "When all is said and done, this is a private matter of the Xie household. To bring it before the magistrate is to make it known to the whole world. With Father's evaluation coming up, it would be better not to create complications."

Yun Chu looked at him. "Then An'er, what do you think should be done with He?"

Xie Shi'an unclenched his fist. "It might be best to send her away."

"She nearly killed my child, and just sending her away is all she gets?" Concubine Tao's voice came from inside. "Even if we cannot go to the magistrate, she cannot be let off this easily! Old mistress, Madame, my lady, please, I beg you to seek justice for the child in my womb!"

The old mistress's temple was pulsing visibly.

He truly was not a woman who could be left in peace. Best that she be sent away.

But was sending her away truly the best outcome? This kind of wretched woman should never have been brought into their lives in the first place.

Yun Chu looked toward the old mistress. "May I ask where He Mama's bond papers are kept?"

The old mistress did not know how to answer.

Because He had no bond papers at all. She appeared to be a servant of the Xie household, but she was in truth a free person.

"Let us wait for Jingyu to return and hear what he thinks," the old mistress said, closing her eyes. "Have He kept under watch for the time being. Everyone else is dismissed."

Yun Chu turned and left, taking those from Sheng Residence with her.

Once everyone had gone, the old mistress raised her walking stick and struck He hard across the back. "When I first offered to let you enter this household as an outside concubine, it was you yourself who refused. So be it. But then why write such disgusting things? I was generous and patient, I let you stay at the Xie estate, I let you remain at An'er's side. How dare you move against a child of my Xie household? Who gave you the nerve?"

She struck her again with the walking stick.

Xie Shi'an stepped in front of He to take the blow, and went down on his knees with a thud. "Great-grandmother, please, let my mother go..."

"No, I will not go!" He burst into weeping. "If I leave, what becomes of my three children? You can beat me to death, but I will not leave the Xie estate..."

The old mistress was furious. "Are you going to live out your days as Jingyu's concubine at your age?"

"No, I will not be a concubine either." He pressed herself flat against the ground. "Old mistress, I will accept any punishment, so long as I am allowed to stay in the Xie household!"

The old mistress could have struck her dead where she lay.

Refusing to leave, refusing to become a concubine, refusing to be sent to the magistrate. Then what was to be done with her?

Xie Pin said in a furious voice, "If you want to stay in the Xie household, then behave yourself and stop causing us trouble. If people ever learn that you are our birth mother, how are An'er and Shiwei and I supposed to live our lives?"

Xie Shi'an said, word by deliberate word, "I can persuade Father to let you stay. But understand this: you will not be given another chance."

chapters.title: I Want to See the Children
chapters.content:
The night deepened.

Yun Chu closed the last account book and looked up toward the doorway. As she had expected, Xie Jingyu walked in.

He was still in his court robes. It was plain he had come straight from official duties outside, without even time to change, and had been called to the old mistress before coming directly here.

"You are here about He, I imagine." Yun Chu rose. "He nearly killed someone. Sparing her from the magistrate is already an act of generosity on the Xie family's part. I hope you will not let Concubine Tao down."

Xie Jingyu's face was marked by exhaustion. He took the clear tea Ting Shuang brought him and drank, his voice rougher than usual. "He watched An'er, Pin'er, and Shiwei grow up. If we sell her off, I worry it will leave a wound in all three of them."

Yun Chu gave a quiet laugh. "And you are not worried about the wound it would leave in the heart of the child still inside Concubine Tao?"

Xie Jingyu was left without a reply.

An unborn child, compared to An'er? There was simply no comparison.

An'er was his firstborn son, possessed of the same brilliance he himself had shown in youth, and outpacing him already. Whatever heights the Xie family might reach in the years to come depended entirely on An'er.

"How about this." Yun Chu's face took on a smile. "Since the children are all so protective of He, and you place so much trust in her, let her become Concubine He."

Xie Jingyu's expression shifted sharply. "I have no feelings of that kind toward her. My lady should not make such a jest."

The depth in Yun Chu's eyes was unfathomable.

Things had reached this point, and the most sensible solution would have been for Xie Jingyu to acknowledge a relationship with He, which would at least give He a legitimate standing in the household. Yet he refused outright to make her a concubine.

Did he intend to wait until she was dead, and then let He step into the role of head mistress?

But would a woman who harbored ambitions to become head mistress truly content herself with the life of a servant until that day came?

"There is a small shrine at the southeast corner of the Xie estate." Xie Jingyu pinched the bridge of his nose. "Let He take up a life of devotion there. I will place her under house confinement. She is not to set foot outside the shrine for three years."

Yun Chu made a show of hesitating before she finally nodded. "Then I will defer to my husband."

She had never intended to drive He out of the Xie household from the very beginning.

Only by keeping He within sight, only by pressing her until she was cornered with nowhere to turn, would Yun Chu be able to find out what she truly wanted to know.

"Thank you, my lady." Xie Jingyu's gaze rested on her. "You do so much for the Xie household. I am deeply grateful."

He stepped forward, closing the distance between them, and reached out to place his hand on her shoulder.

Yun Chu stepped back at once, and his hand met only air.

The image that had been in his mind since the other day surfaced again: her scrubbing her hands with desperate urgency. He understood once more that she found him repellent.

So it was that she could so casually suggest making He a concubine.

The awareness of it stirred something in Xie Jingyu's chest that he could not name.

He withdrew his hand and said in a measured tone, "I hear the Empress has been ill, and that a physician is being sought from far and wide to treat her. If an opportunity presents itself, I will arrange for that physician to examine you. Perhaps there is a way to treat the condition."

Yun Chu lowered her eyes. "I am likely destined to have no children. My husband need not go to the trouble."

Perhaps because Xie Jingyu had mentioned children, she dreamed that night of two small figures.

A boy and a girl, both four years old, soft and round and bright. They circled her, calling out Mama again and again without stopping, and the happiness overflowed from the dream into something warm and complete.

But the happiness did not last. The two children vanished without warning.

The white mist surrounding her turned to a deep red haze.

"Mama, why did you not want us?"

"Mama, I miss you so much. Please come and bring us home!"

"Mama, it is so cold here..."

The crying echoed from all around her.

Yun Chu felt her heart being torn apart. "Children, where are you? Tell Mother where you are..."

The crying faded and grew distant.

Yun Chu's eyes flew open. She sat up straight.

She looked outside. Everything was pitch dark. It had only just passed the middle of the night.

In the four years since, she had never once dreamed of the two children who had died. But in recent days, this was the second time.

She had lived past thirty in her last life. What could she not come to terms with? She needed to make her peace. She needed to face it. She needed to go and see the children one final time.

Yun Chu leaned against the headboard and sat like that until the sky grew light.

When Ting Shuang slipped quietly into the room, she found her sitting on the bed fully dressed, and gave a small start. "My lady, when did you rise? Why did you not call for me to come and attend to you?"

She hurried to help Yun Chu with her hair.

Sitting before the mirror, Yun Chu asked in a quiet voice, "Where were my two children buried? The ones I lost four years ago?"

Ting Shuang's hand trembled. The comb slipped and fell to the floor.

She picked it up quickly and said softly, "My lady, that is all in the past now. Please do not dwell on it. Too much grief is bad for the body."

"The Qingming festival is nearly upon us." Yun Chu's lips curved gently. "I want to go and see the children. Let them know what their mother looks like. I want to talk with them a little."

Ting Shuang bowed her head. "After the little young master and the little young miss passed, it was the master who had them buried. I do not know exactly where."

A dull ache pressed down on Yun Chu.

She had been unable to face it after the children were gone, and had not dared to ask about the arrangements. Now, when she wanted nothing more than to see them once, she did not even know where to go.

She was truly such a terrible mother.

No wonder the children came to her in her dreams.

After the concubines' morning greeting ended, Yun Chu went directly to her mother-in-law's courtyard.

Madam Yuan assumed she had come about the previous night's events, and said with a sigh, "He has been with Jingyu for a number of years. Jingyu kept her here out of sentiment. From now on she will be the shrine's devotee within our Xie estate. She will not cause any more trouble. Put it out of your mind."

"Mother," Yun Chu said, "I have come about something else. The two children I lost four years ago when they were born early, I do not know where they were buried."

"Why are you asking about something from four years ago?" Seeing her eyes rimmed with red, Madam Yuan softened her voice. "I heard from Jingyu that the Empress has been searching for a physician who specializes in women's conditions. Once that physician comes to the capital, Jingyu will find a way to arrange a consultation. Perhaps your condition can be treated after all."

Yun Chu's voice was thick. "Mother, I only want to see the children who were lost."

Madam Yuan let out a quiet sigh. "By custom, children who have not reached adulthood cannot be buried in the ancestral grounds and cannot have a gravestone. Too much importance placed on such things would prevent the child from being reborn. Jingyu had He take the children's remains back to the Xie family's ancestral home in the countryside and find a place to bury them there. If you wish to visit, arrange for a couple of servants to make the journey."

Yun Chu's grip tightened around her sleeve.

Her children had been buried by He's own hands.

The children in her dreams said it was so cold. Where had they been laid to rest that they should feel such cold?

Her heart felt as though it had been carved apart with a blade, the pain almost more than she could bear.

Self-blame, distress, regret: every kind of anguish rose inside her at once.

Leaving Madam Yuan's courtyard, Yun Chu went straight to the front of the estate and had the carriage arranged. She was going back to the Yun household.

The Xie estate was in the southern part of the city. The Yun household sat close to the imperial city, in one of the most prized locations in the capital. The distance across half the city meant she had not gone home often.

And in her past life, burdened with the guilt of having brought ruin upon more than a hundred souls of the Yun household, she had not once thought to go back after her rebirth.

chapters.title: How Do You Want to Live
chapters.content:
The carriage stopped at the gates of the General's residence.

"It is the eldest young miss!"

"The eldest young miss has come home!"

The two guards at the gate bowed to her and immediately turned and ran inside to report.

Yun Chu had barely stepped through when her mother, Lin Shi, and her eldest sister-in-law, Liu Qianqian, came out together to meet her.

Lin Shi took her hands and said with delight, "Chu'er, why did you not send word that you were coming?"

"Mother has been talking about you just these past few days." Liu Qianqian smiled. "If your elder brother knew you were coming today, he would have pushed aside every engagement outside."

The moment her elder brother was mentioned, Yun Chu's eyes filled with tears.

The Yun family had served in the military for generations. Her great-grandfather had died on the battlefield. By her grandfather's generation, her grandfather was the only one left from his branch. Her father guarded the frontier lines with his injuries. Because the Yun family had lost so many of its men to the battlefield, her brother's generation was no longer permitted to take up arms. Her brother had studied and taken the civil path, passed the metropolitan examination and become a third-tier jinshi the previous year, and now held a seventh-rank post at court.

When the charge of treason fell upon the Yun family, her brother had been the first to know. He had submitted a memorial immediately, arguing for the family's innocence, and had been thrown into prison for it.

The day after her brother's imprisonment, word came from the jail for the Yun family to come and collect his body.

She had never even seen her brother one last time.

"What is the matter? Why are you crying, out of nowhere like this?" Lin Shi was alarmed. "Chu'er, has the Xie family been treating you badly?"

Only then did Yun Chu realize her face was wet. She wiped it hurriedly with her sleeve, then threw herself into Lin Shi's arms. "Mama, it has been so long since I came home. I missed you. I missed home."

"You foolish girl, if you want to come home, come home." Lin Shi rubbed her back gently. "Even though a married daughter does not have an excuse to come home at every turn, the Xie family has no authority over the Yun household. From now on, I will send someone to the Xie estate to bring you back every few days."

In the warmth and safety she felt from her mother's presence, Yun Chu's emotions gradually settled.

The Yun family's fall was still more than a decade away. In this lifetime it would not happen again. There was nothing to grieve over.

She spoke, her voice still a little rough. "I want to go and see Grandfather."

Grandfather had fought on the battlefield in his youth, and his body was covered in old wounds. Now that he was older, his legs and feet gave him trouble, and he spent most of his time lying in bed.

In her previous life, he had been supposed to pass with dignity, surrounded by the honor of his achievements. Instead, to prove the Yun family's loyalty, he had used the very sword that had cut down his enemies to cut his own throat.

"Chu'er is back." The old General Yun was half-reclining on the daybed. When he smiled, the scar on his face was hidden in the folds of his expression. "Come here. Let Grandfather test what you still remember."

Yun Chu felt a pang of guilt. "Grandfather, please spare me."
