When she was small, Grandfather had been recovering from his injuries and unable to return to the battlefield, and spent most of his time at home. Her brother had his studies to attend to, so Grandfather had turned his attention to teaching her martial arts.

She was a restless child who could not sit still, and while Grandmother was still alive, she had often come to Yun Chu's defense, forbidding Grandfather from training her. It had all been two days of fish and three days of drying the nets, as the saying went, resulting in something that could barely pass as a foundation. By the time she married, she had forgotten most of it.

"A person must have some skill of their own to fall back on." The old general spoke. "Relying on others will always let you down; relying on wealth means relying on something that can run out. Only talent and martial skill that go deep into the bone will stay with you for life."

"I am sorry, Grandfather. I was too immature before." Yun Chu raised her eyes. "Can you arrange for someone to teach me martial arts?"

The old general looked at her. "Are those sincere words, or are you just trying to make an old man happy?"

Yun Chu pressed close to him playfully. "Even if it is to make you happy, I will still learn with everything I have. I will come by every few days to spar with you. You are not allowed to say I am a bother."

The old General Yun laughed heartily and promised to find a suitable person to send to the Xie estate within three days.

Yun Chu shared a meal with the family and afterward sat in the main hall with her mother and sister-in-law, talking over the events of recent weeks, her mood lightening considerably.

Lin Shi sighed. "Your younger sister Ran'er fell ill two years ago and her marriage has been delayed. She is nearly seventeen now. If we do not start looking soon, she will end up an old maid."

Liu Qianqian said, "Tomorrow the eldest princess is hosting a flower-viewing banquet, which is really just an occasion for the families of the capital to take stock of suitable matches. We can find Ran'er a good family there. Mother need not worry."

Yun Chu's fingers paused.

Yun Ran was her younger half-sister, but her birth mother had died in childbirth, and she had been raised entirely by Lin Shi. The two of them were as close as full sisters.

Because of her fragile constitution, Yun Ran had fallen ill two years ago and her marriage had been put off. The delay had made everyone anxious about finding a match, and in the end a poor decision had been made.

"Mother, could I come with you to the flower-viewing banquet?" Yun Chu spoke. "Since becoming Madame Xie, I have barely seen any of the friends from my younger days."

As the wife of a fifth-rank official, she was no longer in the same circles as the daughters of second and third-rank officials she had grown up with. The eldest princess's flower-viewing banquet, for instance, would never have extended an invitation to her.

She could only go by borrowing the Yun family's invitation.

Lin Shi nodded. "Good. You can also look over the two families I have in mind for Ran'er and help me decide."

As they were speaking, Yun Ze came home.

Yun Ze was the eldest young master of the Yun household, four years older than Yun Chu. He had passed the examination and earned his jinshi degree just the year before at the age of twenty-three, which was not particularly remarkable in a city like the capital.

But Yun Chu knew her brother was far more able than that. He could have passed easily at eighteen, could have placed at least as the second scholar on the list, yet he had deliberately held himself back for five years before sitting the examination, out of fear that too brilliant a showing would draw the Emperor's suspicion.

"Your brother is home. You two catch up for a while." Lin Shi rose. "Qianqian, come with me to the kitchen and see whether the desserts are ready."

She knew that her daughter had come home with something important to say, otherwise she would not have been waiting all this time.

Yun Chu had indeed been waiting for Yun Ze.

"Brother, I need to ask your help with something." She pressed her lips together before speaking. "Could you arrange for someone to make a trip to Jizhou?"

"Jizhou, is that not where the Xie family's ancestral home is?" Yun Ze looked at her. "Has something happened?"

Yun Chu lowered her head. "I dreamed of the children I lost. They said they were so cold, so cold. The children were born early and did not survive. They could not be buried in the Xie family's ancestral grounds, so someone found a random place in the old home county to bury them. I want to ask you to arrange for people to bring the children's remains back to the capital. I want to give them a proper burial."

Xie Jingyu had sons and daughters. He would not care about two children who had died. So this was something she could only ask her brother for.

"Do not tell Mother or Grandfather," she said quietly. "I do not want them to worry. And brother, do not worry about me either. I only want the children to have a proper resting place. Please grant me this wish."

Yun Ze let out a quiet breath.

He reached over and ruffled her hair the way he had done when they were young, his voice gentle. "Jizhou has been suffering from flooding, and the court is sending people there to assess the situation. I will go myself, and bring my nephew and niece home. I will find them a place with good fengshui."

Yun Chu's voice broke. "Thank you, Brother."

"Chu'er, you must remember: the Yun family will always be your strongest support. If the Xie family wrongs you, you can walk away from the marriage. Your inability to bear children is not your fault. Do not let it make you feel less than anyone in the Xie household. You are the eldest daughter of the Yun family, my proudest sister, the apple of our parents' eyes." Yun Ze spoke with quiet warmth. "Live however you want to live."

Leaving the Yun household, sitting in the carriage, Yun Chu finally let herself cry without holding back.

chapters.title: The Eldest Princess's Banquet
chapters.content:
Yun Chu had the carriage drive in circles around the streets for a while before finally returning to the Xie estate.

Aside from a faint redness around her eyes, there was no sign at all that she had just wept until she could not breathe.

The moment she came back to the courtyard, Ting Feng came in to report. "My lady, while you were at the General's residence, the eldest young miss quietly made a trip to the old shrine and brought He Mama a great many things."

The mistress treated the eldest young miss as her own child. Ting Feng could not fathom why the eldest young miss would be so kind to a servant who had tried to frame the mistress.

Yun Chu sat on the daybed. "Ask Pin'er to come and see me."

Since Xie Pin had taken on part of the household management, she had become genuinely busy, either reading account books or summoning the outer courtyard matrons for discussions.

She was in the middle of one such task when Ting Xue came to ask her to come over.

On any ordinary day, it was she who went to the mistress on her own initiative. The mistress had never sent a maidservant to summon her before.

Xie Pin set down her account books, a little uneasy in her heart.

Perhaps the mistress had learned she had gone to bring things to He, and was now asking her to account for it?

She should never have let herself be soft-hearted and gone to see He in the first place. Now what was she to say to the mistress?

A great many thoughts ran through Xie Pin's mind on the way over.

But when she entered Sheng Residence, she found Yun Chu looking at her with a warm smile. "Pin'er, sit."

Xie Pin sat and took a sip of tea.

"Tomorrow the eldest princess is holding a flower-viewing banquet. Do you have time to come with me?" Yun Chu said with a smile. "If you would rather not go, that is perfectly fine."

Xie Pin could hardly believe it. She pressed down her excitement. "Did the eldest princess invite Mother?"

Yun Chu shook her head. "The eldest princess invited the Yun family. Your grandmother has asked me to go along. If you would like to come, one more person makes no difference. It would be a good chance to see something of the world."

Xie Pin nodded with great enthusiasm. "I want to go."

Her father was a fifth-rank official, and the young ladies she ordinarily met were daughters of fifth and sixth-rank officials. At the eldest princess's flower-viewing banquet, virtually everyone would be the female relatives of officials holding third rank or above.

With the mistress by her side, she was sure to meet many women from prominent and powerful families.

And if she made a good impression on those great ladies, some of them might well have a son in mind for her.

At this thought, Xie Pin felt an eagerness she could not quite contain. She rose at once. "Mother, I will go back and tend to my work."

Watching her retreat out the door, a cold smile drifted across Yun Chu's lips.

In her past life, it was at the Yun family's spring banquet that Xie Pin had caught her first sight of the fourth prince, and had fallen for him on the spot.

A fifth-rank official's daughter and the current emperor's fourth son had no prospect of a future together whatsoever. Even the position of side consort would have been out of reach. So Xie Pin had devised a desperate scheme: she had found an occasion when the fourth prince was not paying attention, and slipped something into his drink, intending to engineer a fait accompli. It was only because Yun Chu had discovered the plot by chance and intervened in time that the whole debacle had been averted.

Shortly after that incident, the fourth prince had come to ruin.

Yun Chu had chosen a good family for Xie Pin. The man in question was only a seventh-rank official, but the family's values were sound and his prospects were solid. Xie Pin, however, had not been able to bring herself to accept it. When the match was almost finalized, Xie Pin had used the pretext of paying a call on her great-aunt in the palace to gain an audience with the Emperor, and then... she had become a new favorite at the Emperor's side.

The so-called great-aunt was Yun Chu's own paternal aunt, who had entered the palace through the imperial selection years before, and was one of the four imperial consorts, having given birth to the eighth prince.

Xie Pin had climbed over her own great-aunt to become the Emperor's favored concubine.

In her previous life, her aunt had been brought to ruin at Xie Pin's hands, and had suffered in ways no ordinary person could endure.

At the thought of it, Yun Chu's expression filled with a quiet sorrow.

In this life, she would not give Xie Pin a path into the palace. She would not let her aunt be threatened by Xie Pin again.

Xie Pin was so fond of the fourth prince, was she? Then let her become the fourth prince's consort. However glorious that title might sound today, it would prove to be equally short-lived.

The night passed without event.

Just as the sky was beginning to lighten, Yun Chu had washed and dressed and come out to find Xie Shi'an already waiting to pay his morning respects.

"With the prefectural examination coming up, you do not need to come for morning greetings during this period." Yun Chu said warmly. "Study well. Do the Xie family proud."

Xie Shi'an clasped his hands in a bow. "Morning greetings are part of one's filial duty. Such propriety should not be neglected. Mother need not worry. I am confident about the examination. Earning the xiucai title is no great difficulty."

Yun Chu knew he was not speaking idly.

He would not merely earn the xiucai title. He would earn it as the top-ranked student. The following year at the provincial examination, he would again place first, earning the juren title with honors. Two years after that, at the metropolitan examination, he would take first place once more as the huiyuan. And at the palace examination that followed, the Emperor would name him top of the list as the zhuangyuan.

He was the only scholar in the dynasty to have topped all three successive imperial examinations, and the youngest zhuangyuan in its history.

With Xie Shi'an ascending into the Grand Secretariat, with Xie Pin as the palace favorite, with Xie Shiwei placed inside the military, the Xie family's rise in the years ahead had been something that no force could check.

After Xie Shi'an left, the rest of the inner household came to pay their respects.

Yun Chu's gaze settled on Xie Pin and she spoke quietly. "Go back and change out of this dress. Ting Shuang, go and help her with her presentation."

Xie Pin was a little at a loss. "Mother, is something wrong with this dress?"

"Eldest young miss, this is too vivid in color." Ting Yu said softly. She had spent many years in the General's household, and she understood these things. "The eldest princess's flower-viewing banquet is intended to honor the flowers. It is not a competition among young ladies to outshine one another."

Yun Chu said, "It is Pin'er's first time attending a banquet with me. Not knowing these things is entirely natural. Go and change first, then come back."

Ting Shuang went with Xie Pin back to her courtyard and chose a soft pink spring dress for her, arranged her hair in a simple style, and added only a slanted jade hairpin and a pair of pearl earrings no larger than grains of rice.

Xie Pin pressed her lips together. "Is it not too plain?"

Ting Shuang said, with her hands clasped at her sides, "My lady is attending the eldest princess's residence in the Yun family's name. Keeping a low profile is what is appropriate. This style of dress suits the occasion."

Xie Pin was quietly unhappy.

Dressed this plainly, she would blend into the crowd and no one would notice her. How was she supposed to meet any great ladies from distinguished families?

But the mistress had given the instruction, and if she insisted on dressing the way she wanted, she might very well find herself not going to the banquet at all.

Yun Chu brought Xie Pin in the carriage to the Yun household first, where they met up with the Yun family, and then all of them set out together for the eldest princess's residence.

The eldest princess was the Emperor's full sister, the foremost figure in the entire circle of the capital's prominent ladies, and her banquets were always packed.

The carriage came to a stop at the gate.

Yun Chu helped Lin Shi down.

Behind them followed two unmarried young ladies: Yun Ran, second daughter of the General's household, and Xie Pin, eldest daughter of the Xie household.

The four of them walked inside together. There was no need to present an invitation. Lin Shi simply stepped into view and the servant boys called out, "The General's wife has arrived!"

A matron came out at once to receive them and led Yun Chu and her party inside.

It was Xie Pin's first time inside a household of this grandeur, and her eyes kept moving from one thing to the next, never satisfied.

Lin Shi frowned slightly and said in a low voice, "Pin'er, this is not quite the proper behavior. I will have Qi Mama go to the Xie estate to teach you after this."

Yun Chu replied with a smile, "Such a small thing need not trouble you, Mother."

The embarrassment was the Xie family's to bear, and she had no obligation to protect the Xie family's face.

Still, on this occasion Xie Pin was appearing alongside the Yun family, so a little guidance was necessary to prevent the Yun family from being mocked.

Yun Chu gave Ting Shuang a glance.

Ting Shuang stepped back and moved to Xie Pin's side, murmuring a few quiet words of guidance.

chapters.title: Step Out for Some Air
chapters.content:
Yun Chu followed Lin Shi into the eldest princess's residence.

By now, a great many guests had already arrived. The moment they entered, people came forward from all sides to exchange pleasantries.

"Madam Yun, it has been quite some time since I have seen you."

"Is this Chu'er? Goodness, she has grown so much in the blink of an eye. Time truly spares no one."

"And this must be Ran'er. She should be sixteen now if I recall correctly. What a graceful young woman she has become."

The Yun family was a first-rank General's residence. The old General Yun had accumulated more battle honors than anyone could count, and General Yun was currently holding the frontier lines. The Yun family's standing at court was unshakeable.

It was no surprise then that so many people came forward to pay their respects.

They spoke to Lin Shi with a measure of deference and flattery, but the moment their gaze moved to Yun Chu, it carried a thread of quiet sympathy.

The legitimate daughter of a General's household, who had not only married down into a family of humble origin, but had also lost the ability to bear children, and was therefore left to register all the concubine-born children under her own name and raise them.

One woman's gaze settled on Xie Pin. "And this young lady is?"

Lin Shi smiled. "This is my granddaughter."

Xie Pin stepped forward and gave a slight curtsy in greeting.

Everyone present registered visible surprise.

They had all known that the General's legitimate daughter had a number of concubine-born children in her name, but they had not realized the eldest daughter was already this grown. She stood barely a half-finger shorter than Yun Chu herself, and were it not for the youthfulness still present in her face, the two of them might have been mistaken for sisters of similar age.

The sympathy in those onlookers' eyes deepened.

Lin Shi felt a weight pressing against her heart. She had originally arranged this match for her daughter precisely to avoid drawing the Emperor's suspicion, and because Xie Jingyu had seemed genuinely promising. But who could have foreseen that he had three children before the wedding? Had Chu'er not lost her ability to have children of her own, nothing would have stopped her from making the Xie family answer for it.

Lin Shi gave the gathered women a faint smile and steered Yun Chu in another direction.

"Chu'er, do you see those two ladies over there?" Lin Shi said quietly. "The one is Madame Zhang. Her husband is a seventh-rank academician at the Directorate of Education. Her eldest legitimate son passed the xiucai examination last year. I have met the young man; he knows how to conduct himself and makes a good impression. The other is Madame Qian. Her husband is the fourth-rank chief of the Court of State Ceremonial. His two legitimate sons are already married, and he has one concubine-born son of marrying age."

Xie Pin, who had been listening as she walked, looked up in surprise.

She had gathered on the way over that the purpose of coming to the eldest princess's residence was primarily to find a suitable match for Yun Ran. But a daughter of a first-rank General's household, and these were the families being considered? A seventh-rank academician's son, and a fourth-rank official's concubine-born son? In her view, even the legitimate son of a fourth-rank official was not worthy of a first-rank General's young miss.

But then, she thought of the fact that even a General's legitimate daughter, namely her own stepmother, had only married into the Xie household. Seen in that light, perhaps it was not entirely unreasonable.

Yun Chu's gaze rested on Madame Qian's face. In her past life, this woman had been Yun Ran's mother-in-law.

Whatever could be said of Yun Ran's husband, Madame Qian's particular brand of cruelty alone could fill ten days and ten nights of telling.

Her younger sister was gentle by nature, and under Madame Qian's daily demands and impositions she had been worn down to a shadow of herself. In the fourth year of her marriage, while newly pregnant and before anyone knew of it, she had been ordered to kneel as punishment. She had knelt in the frozen snow for three hours. The baby was lost, and Yun Ran had contracted a severe illness. She had lain in bed for three or four years before finally slipping away.

"The Qian family will not do." Yun Chu said. "As for the Zhang household, I would need to make more inquiries before deciding."

Lin Shi had been most favorably inclined toward the Qian family, and she could not help asking, "Why not?"

Yun Chu shook her head. "Have someone look into Madame Qian's character, Mother, and you will understand."

Lin Shi had been planning to bring Yun Ran over to meet Madame Qian, but at Yun Chu's words, she set that idea aside entirely. The four of them settled themselves in their seats.

No sooner had they sat down than the eldest princess made her entrance.

The princess was accompanied by two men in richly embroidered court dress: the third prince, Prince Pingxi, and the fourth prince, Prince Anjing.

Everyone rose at once.

"We greet the eldest princess! We greet Prince Pingxi! We greet Prince Anjing!"

The princess smiled and raised her hand. "There is no need for formality in my home. Please, everyone be seated."

The ladies present all understood perfectly well that the real purpose of the eldest princess's banquet this time was most likely to find suitable consorts for Prince Pingxi and Prince Anjing. Since Prince Pingxi already had a son and daughter, he was not many people's first choice, and so most of the eager glances flew toward Prince Anjing.

"Third brother, why did you bring Yu'er?" The eldest princess looked at Prince Pingxi with some exasperation. "Are you afraid people will not know you have a son? Are you worried that some lady here might want to give her daughter to you in marriage?"

Prince Pingxi raised his cup and took a measured sip. "He insisted on coming. What was I supposed to do?"

The princess's gaze settled on the small, round, fine-featured child. Had he not been the image of his father in every feature of his face, she was not sure she could have found a single ounce of warmth toward him.

"Yu'er," the princess called out, "are you looking for someone?"

Chu Hongyu quickly drew his gaze back and broke into a guileless smile. "Imperial great-aunt, I just thought it looked so lively here. May I go and play?"

"Go and play then." The princess indicated a matron at her side. "Keep close to the young lord. Make sure he does not bump or scrape or take a fall."

The little one had barely received permission before his short legs were already carrying him off at a run toward the garden paths to the side.

Yun Chu's gaze drifted to follow the child without her meaning it to, and it was only after he had disappeared down a garden path that she realized she had been watching him for quite some time.

"Prince Pingxi went to the battlefield with your father at fifteen years old." Lin Shi said quietly. "He has always been a steady-tempered young man. No one knows quite how he came to have a son and daughter, the mother's identity entirely unknown. He still had his son invested as young lord despite a court full of objections, and that caused quite a stir in the capital. The great families of this city are unlikely to be eager to give their daughters to Prince Pingxi when those daughters would step into the role of stepmother from the very beginning."

Yun Chu nodded in full agreement.

In her past life, Prince Pingxi had remained unmarried until the day she died.

The great families did not want their daughters raising another woman's children. The daughters of humbler families were not what Prince Pingxi had in mind. And so it had remained.

While Yun Chu spoke with Lin Shi, she caught from the corner of her eye that Xie Pin's gaze had not left the fourth prince, Prince Anjing, who sat at the seat of honor above.

She let her lips curve.

Exactly the same as in her past life. Xie Pin had fallen for the fourth prince at first sight.

At that moment, the fourth prince rose and excused himself from the gathering.

Yun Chu felt Xie Pin begin to stir beside her.

She could lend a hand here.

She set down her chopsticks. "Mother, I find it a little stifling in here. I would like to step outside for some air."

Lin Shi said at once, "Are you feeling unwell somewhere? I will say a word to the eldest princess and we can go home early."

"A little fresh air is all I need." Yun Chu stood. "Let Pin'er walk with me for a while. We will be back shortly. Mother need not worry."

A look of quiet pleasure crossed Xie Pin's face.

Yun Chu brought Xie Pin out from the banquet, Ting Shuang following close behind the two of them.

They had barely stepped into a nearby garden courtyard when Xie Pin gasped. "Mother, one of my earrings has come loose! What am I to do?"

Ting Shuang lowered her head. "This servant will go back and look for it."

"I could not trouble Ting Shuang for something like this," Xie Pin said. "It must have fallen among the flower beds. I will find it myself."

Since Xie Pin had brought no personal attendant of her own to the eldest princess's residence, she turned and walked back alone.

Ting Shuang felt this was not quite appropriate and opened her mouth to say so. Then she saw Yun Chu give a small shake of her head, and swallowed what she had been about to say.

chapters.title: I Only Wanted to See Her
chapters.content:
After Xie Ping's figure disappeared from view, Yun Chu led Ting Shuang to stand at the mouth of the path, admiring the flowers.

If anyone came, she would know at once, and no one would see Xie Ping attempting to seduce the prince.

She had gone this far for the girl; she could only hope Xie Ping would not disappoint her.

The begonia blossoms were vivid and lovely. Yun Chu was admiring them when she suddenly felt a sharp pain at her ankle. She looked down to see a small pebble rolling away.

Ting Shuang looked toward where the pebble had come from. "Who is hiding there?"

The broad green leaves rustled, and a short little figure wriggled out.

Yun Chu's face filled with disbelief.

It was the young heir of the Prince of Pingxi's household.

The little fellow held a slingshot in one hand and a fistful of smooth round pebbles in the other.

He straightened up, fitted a pebble into the slingshot, and aimed it directly at Yun Chu's face.

Ting Shuang hurried to step in front of Yun Chu.

"Hmph!" The little one puffed out his chest. "You promised to replace my cricket. Where is it?"

Yun Chu: "......"

Was this cricket business never going to end?

"You woman, you don't keep your word!" The little fellow released the slingshot.

The pebble shot toward Yun Chu but missed, landing in the grass by the roadside.

"Young heir." Yun Chu walked two steps forward and crouched down before him, her tone calm and even. "Three crickets were already sent to the Prince of Pingxi's household, and the young heir was not satisfied with any of them. You may as well tell me plainly: just what kind of cricket are you looking for?"

Chu Hongyu pressed his lips together.

He did not actually want any cricket. He only wanted to see this woman.

He had done everything he could to follow his father to the flower-viewing banquet, intending to slip away the moment his father was not looking and find her.

Who could have expected that this woman would be here at the Princess's estate as well.

He really was lucky today.

Seeing that the little one said nothing, Yun Chu thought for a moment and said, "Then I shall give the young heir a one-of-a-kind cricket, the likes of which cannot be found anywhere else in the world."

She walked to the edge of the path and plucked two long, slender leaves. Her hands moved quickly, folding and weaving, and in no time at all a green cricket sat in her palm.

She held it out to him. "Do you like it?"

Chu Hongyu's round, dark eyes went wide. "How are you so clever? Can you teach me?"

"It is quite simple," Yun Chu said patiently. "You lay two leaves over each other like this, then fold here, then like so, and then..."

Within just a few words of instruction, a second cricket was already done.

Chu Hongyu followed her step by step, but what he ended up with was not a cricket at all. It looked more like a dog.

She could not help but laugh.

"Don't laugh!"

The little fellow was furious. He plucked two more leaves and tried again with a look that said he would not give up until he had mastered it.

Just then, a matron came hurrying down the small path. "Young heir, oh young heir, this old servant has finally found you."

Chu Hongyu's face was full of displeasure. "I told you not to follow me. What are you looking for me for? Go stand somewhere else."

The old matron bowed low and came forward with a respectful air. "This old servant will take the liberty of asking: was it the young heir who killed the koi in the Clear Flower Pond?"

The little fellow's expression shifted abruptly. He let out a huff and went back to fiddling with the leaves in his hands.

The matron needed no further answer from that attitude, and bowed even lower. "Those koi were brought at great expense all the way from the south by the Grand Princess. For them to die like this, the Grand Princess will certainly want to hold someone accountable. I only ask that the young heir come with this old servant and explain the matter to the Grand Princess."

Chu Hongyu sat down on the ground. "I am not going. I refuse."

The matron was nearly in tears. Two koi were dead. Not only would the maidservant who tended the fish be in trouble, but she, the matron charged with minding the young heir, would be punished too.

"It is not the absence of fault that is most admirable, but the willingness to correct one's faults." Yun Chu's voice was warm and gentle. "Does the young heir know what those words mean?"

Chu Hongyu shook his head blankly. Though his father had engaged a tutor to teach him to read and write, he slept through lessons often enough that very little had actually gone in.

"The greatest thing is not to have never made a mistake, but to know one's mistake and make it right." Yun Chu looked at him steadily. "If the death of the Grand Princess's koi had something to do with the young heir, and the young heir comes forward bravely to admit his mistake, I believe the Grand Princess will not hold it against him."

Chu Hongyu pressed his lips together.

The Grand Princess would certainly not blame him. The trouble was that his father was there too.

He looked up and met Yun Chu's gaze. Under that gentle look, he felt a flicker of shame.

He stood. "Come, Matron."

The matron looked at Yun Chu with boundless gratitude. "Thank you, Madam."

Yun Chu glanced toward the end of the small path and saw Xie Ping emerging from the depths of the grove, her face flushed pink, the very picture of a young girl in the first blush of love.

"Did you find your earring, Ping'er?"

Xie Ping felt a pang of guilt and quickly bowed her head to hide the soft light in her eyes. "Yes, Mother. I found it."

"Then let us return to the banquet." Yun Chu turned and walked ahead.

Xie Ping glanced back once over her shoulder, then quickly fell into step behind Yun Chu.

The moment they returned to the banquet, Yun Chu saw the little fellow nestled in the Grand Princess's lap, coaxing her with his sweetest manner. "Imperial great-aunt, I did something wrong. Will you forgive me?"

The Grand Princess's heart melted. She had not taken to the child at first, given that his mother's origins were unknown, but the boy was sweet-tongued and knew how to please people, and in time she had naturally grown fond of him.

She pinched the little fellow's cheek. "What did our little Yu'er do wrong?"

"I was playing with my slingshot, and I accidentally... killed two of the koi in the pond." Chu Hongyu bowed his head and twisted his fingers together. "Grand Imperial Aunt, I was wrong."

Before the Grand Princess could speak, the Prince of Pingxi, who was seated beside her, let his gaze go cold and reached out to haul Chu Hongyu up by the back of his collar.

"Third brother, what do you think you are doing?" The Grand Princess drew the child into her arms. "They are only two fish. There is no need for such a fuss."

The Prince of Pingxi spoke coldly. "If he can kill two fish today, he can kill two people tomorrow. Indulging him will only make him more and more lawless."

"If the child is not taught, the fault lies with the father. When all is said and done, the blame is yours." The Grand Princess let out a dismissive sound. "You have no time to discipline the child, so you ought to take a wang fei to manage him in your place, rather than resorting to beatings at every turn. Look at the state the poor child has been reduced to."

At those words, every lady seated in the hall found somewhere else to look.

Only a daughter born of a legitimate wife could be a suitable match for the Prince of Pingxi, but none of them wished to send their own daughter to be a stepmother. Each one feared being singled out by the Grand Princess.

The Grand Princess swept her gaze across the room and let it settle on Yun Chu.

She smiled. "I have heard that Huaide Academy has a student of whom the teachers are exceedingly proud, the eldest son of the Xie household. If all goes as expected, he will place first in this year's prefectural examinations. A child so accomplished owes it entirely to the excellence of his mother's guidance. And so, third brother, if you are to take a wife, you ought to take a woman like Chu'er."

Yun Chu rose at once. "Your Highness flatters me far beyond what I deserve."

The Prince of Pingxi lifted his gaze, those hawk-sharp eyes of his coming to rest on Yun Chu.

chapters.title: It Is Not My Fault
chapters.content:
The Prince of Pingxi's gaze rested on Yun Chu.

She was dressed as a married woman, her long black hair pinned high and held in place by a gold and jade hairpin, her pale violet gown embroidered all over with camellia blossoms.

He found himself thinking of many years ago, before she had married, when they had met once.

He had gone to the Yun household to call on General Yun, and she happened to be bringing the old general his tea.

She had been wearing pale yellow maiden's dress then, quick and bright and full of life, like an entirely different person from the woman before him now.

"I think she is wonderful too." Chu Hongyu blinked his big eyes. "Grand Imperial Aunt, can she be my wang fei?"

The Grand Princess laughed. "You really are just a child, saying such childish things. Chu'er, don't mind what the boy says."

Yun Chu inclined her head. "To receive even such a word of praise from the young heir is an honor this subject's wife does not take lightly."

When she was small, she had often accompanied Lady Lin to the Grand Princess's estate, and the Grand Princess still called her Chu'er as she always had. But she was a married woman now, the wife of a fifth-rank official, and when speaking with the Grand Princess, she naturally could not carry on as she once had.

The banquet drew to a close before long.

After Lady Lin had taken her leave of the Grand Princess, the party made their way out.

They had not yet left the Grand Princess's estate when, at the inner gate, Yun Chu heard a child crying. She turned toward the sound and saw, at a nearby pavilion, a tall figure standing over a small one.

The Prince of Pingxi stared down at the child with a cold expression. The child wailed and stumbled back in fear.

"You promised you would behave, and only then did I bring you to the Grand Princess's estate," the Prince of Pingxi said, his voice like ice. "Tearing the roof tiles off at home is one thing, but coming here to run wild: who gave you the nerve?"

The little fellow's crying came in heaves. "Father, I have admitted my mistake. The Grand Imperial Aunt has forgiven me. I will never dare do it again."

The Prince of Pingxi's face grew darker still.

Those koi had been worth a fortune, transported all the way to the capital at a cost of tens of thousands of taels, and only two had survived the journey, only to die at this boy's hands.

If he did not deal with this firmly, there was no telling what greater trouble would come later.

He seized the child up in one hand.

"Let go of me, let go!" Chu Hongyu kicked his legs wildly, sobbing and shouting. "Grand Imperial Aunt said it is not my fault! It is your fault! Who told you not to find me a wang fei..."

The Prince of Pingxi's expression turned even darker.

He had been occupied with official business for years and had neglected the child's upbringing. That part, at least, was indeed his fault.

Without another word, he hauled the little fellow off toward the gate.

The child's crying grew louder and louder.

A sudden pain clenched at Yun Chu's chest, and before she even realized it her legs had already carried her forward, toward the Prince of Pingxi.

"Chu'er!" Lady Lin caught her arm. "Where do you think you are going?"

Yun Chu came back to herself. She pressed her lips together and said, "It was I who persuaded the young heir to go and admit his mistake, and I told him that as long as he owned up to it and reformed, everything would be fine."

Lady Lin spoke. "Do you think you were wrong to persuade him to admit his mistake?"

Yun Chu shook her head.

Lady Lin continued. "And do you think the Prince of Pingxi is wrong to discipline his own child?"

Yun Chu shook her head again.

"Well then, there is your answer." Lady Lin patted her hand. "A father disciplining his son is entirely as it should be. What would you achieve by going over there? Do you think the Prince of Pingxi would listen to you? He would only think you were meddling. Besides, look around you."

Only then did Yun Chu notice that quite a number of ladies and young misses had stopped on this very path.

She understood. The Prince of Pingxi was disciplining his child in front of everyone, intent on stamping out any notion these families might have of offering their daughters to him as wang fei.

The Prince of Pingxi carried the child away and was soon gone from the Grand Princess's estate.

Many of the noblewomen began to murmur among themselves.

"I had long heard that the young heir was troublesome. Now I have seen it for myself."

"Was it not said that the young heir's birth mother is someone of no standing, and that the imperial family holds no affection for the child? Yet I see the Grand Princess is very fond of him."

"The Grand Princess is fond of the Prince of Pingxi, and her affection extends to the young heir as well. Otherwise, why would she be fretting day and night about finding him a wang fei?"

"What a pity. The Prince of Pingxi already has a son so grown; no highborn girl would be willing to marry into that."

"If the boy were not the heir apparent it might be one thing, but with him occupying that position, any legitimate son born of a future wang fei would find himself in a most awkward place."

"......"

After leaving the Grand Princess's estate, Yun Chu's mood refused to settle.

She could not explain it, but she kept thinking of that child.

"Mother." Xie Ping suddenly spoke up, pulling Yun Chu from her thoughts. "Just now I saw the Grand Princess in very pleasant conversation with Lady Li. Could it be that the Grand Princess wishes to see the eldest legitimate daughter of the Li family married to the Prince of Pingxi as wang fei?"

Yun Chu replied lightly, "Since when do you concern yourself with the affairs of the imperial family?"

Xie Ping felt a twinge of guilt and forced a smile. "I was simply a little curious about what kind of woman would be worthy of the title of wang fei."

"Of the princes who have taken a principal wife, the Crown Prince's consort is the eldest legitimate daughter of the Grand Preceptor, and the second prince's wife is the second daughter of the Grand Scholar." Yun Chu looked at her steadily. "At the very least, the legitimate daughter of a family of the second rank would be worthy of the title of wang fei, and even then, a third rank family would be the lowest acceptable."

Xie Ping's fingers tightened.

Her father had taken five years to rise to the fifth rank, and the higher one climbed the harder it became. Reaching the third rank: there was no knowing how many more years that would take.

She bowed her head, afraid that the disappointment in her eyes would be noticed by Yun Chu.

The carriage soon stopped before the gates of the Xie household. The moment they stepped through the entrance, Matron Zhou came to escort them both to the Hall of Longevity.

The Hall of Longevity was lively. Not only was Xie Shi'an there, but Xie Jingyu was there as well, which made it plain enough that they had been waiting for the two of them to return.

Old Madam Xie smiled and said, "Chu'er, how was the Grand Princess's flower-viewing banquet? What distinguished guests attended?"

"The third prince, the Prince of Pingxi, and the fourth prince, the Prince of An'jing, were both in attendance." Yun Chu saw the eager gleam in the Xie family's eyes. "The noblewomen present were all the wives of officials of the first, second, and third rank. I was the only exception."

"You are the daughter of a first-rank general's household. Such gatherings are your rightful place." The old madam smiled. "Chu'er, did you have occasion to speak with Lady Yu?"

Xie Jingyu also looked her way.

Yun Chu's lips curved slightly. Lady Yu's husband was Xie Jingyu's superior, and with the performance review approaching, Xie Jingyu would have to pass through Magistrate Yu's hands if he wished to advance further.

With the magistrate's approval, he could move from the upper fifth rank to the fifth rank above. There was no fundamental difference between the two, but when a promotion became available, officials of the upper fifth rank would be considered first.

After passing the highest imperial examination, Xie Jingyu had risen from the seventh rank to the fifth in barely five years. Setting aside the connection to the Yun family through marriage, the greater reason was his own skill at cultivating relationships.

In the past, she had helped him tend to those relationships at every banquet she attended.

Lady Yu was the wife of a third-rank official and could not enter the inner circle of the highest-ranking noblewomen; she lingered always on its edges. In former times, Yun Chu would have taken the initiative to draw Lady Yu into that circle.

But at this banquet, she had done nothing more than glance at Lady Yu from afar.

Lady Yu, unable to join the circle of first-rank noblewomen, would certainly be vexed, and would whisper her grievances into her husband's ear. Xie Jingyu could forget about his promotion.

Yun Chu allowed a smile to cross her face. "I did exchange a few words with Lady Yu."

Xie Jingyu rose and clasped his hands in salute. "I thank Madam for her efforts."

"What is there to thank? We are all one family." The old madam beamed. "Once Jingyu has risen to the fourth rank, then our Xie family will truly be able to hold its head high."

Yun Chu's smile deepened.

That day, she suspected, would never come.

chapters.title: Nothing in the World Is Difficult
chapters.content:
While Yun Chu was speaking in the Hall of Longevity, He Shi had pulled Xie Ping away into the small grove behind the hall.

"What are you doing?" Xie Ping was startled, and looked left and right before saying in a lower voice, "Did Father not confine you to the small temple? How did you get out?"

He Shi was clearly uneasy. "Why would Madam suddenly take you to the Grand Princess's estate? Nothing happened, did it?"

Xie Ping's face was all impatience. "Mother took me to broaden my horizons. What could have happened?"

He Shi did not believe a word of it.

In recent times, Madam had moved against her children one thing after another. She absolutely refused to believe that Madam would be so generous as to take Ping'er out simply to broaden her horizons.

"I saw the fourth prince, the Prince of An'jing." Xie Ping said what she had not dared tell Yun Chu. "Do you think I could become the Prince of An'jing's wang fei?"

He Shi's eyes went wide. "You... what are you talking about?"

What sort of standing did the fourth prince hold? How could the daughter of a mere fifth-rank official possibly dream of such a thing?

What was more, though Ping'er now held the position of the eldest legitimate daughter of the Xie household, anyone who inquired carefully would know that Ping'er had been born to a concubine outside the family.

The imperial family placed the utmost importance on birth and rank. With Ping'er's origins, she could never be entered into the imperial register of blood relations.

Xie Ping bit her lip. "Nothing in the world is difficult for one who sets their mind to it."

"My dear Ping'er, please do not do anything reckless." He Shi was frightened nearly out of her wits. "Your marriage will be decided by the old madam and Madam. Don't go filling your head with thoughts you shouldn't have."

The two of them were still talking when a voice suddenly reached them.

"Is that not He Mama? Did the master not punish you with confinement to the small temple? How is it you have come out? What boldness!"

The speaker was Concubine Tao. She had heard that Madam was back from the Grand Princess's estate and had come to see what was happening, never expecting she would find He Shi, who was supposed to be confined to the small temple.

The moment she laid eyes on He Shi, fury ignited behind her gaze.

The child in her womb had nearly lost its life, and yet this lowly creature who had coveted the master had come away without a scratch.

She raised her hand and swung it in a hard slap.

Xie Ping was quick, and stepped in to block it.

Concubine Tao's eyes narrowed. "What does the eldest young miss mean by this?"

"It was I who asked He Mama to bring me some things," Xie Ping said. "Concubine Tao is with child; best not to work yourself into a temper. You could disturb the baby."

"It is most astonishing that the eldest young miss should go to such lengths to protect a woman who coveted her own father and framed her own mother." Concubine Tao looked He Shi over, then looked at Xie Ping again, and her brow suddenly creased. Looking more closely, she saw that the two of them shared a faint but unmistakable resemblance.

Xie Ping's heart hammered in her chest.

She shot He Shi a furious glare.

She had told her not to come looking for her. Yet He Shi had done exactly that, in the middle of her confinement.

If anyone came to suspect the nature of her relationship with He Shi, her entire future would be ruined.

She said coldly, "What are you still standing there for? Get back to the small temple at once!"

He Shi bowed her head and left.

A thoughtful expression settled over Concubine Tao's face.

Rain fell in the middle of the night, a soft and steady sound, and Yun Chu slept well to the sound of it. In the morning, the rain had not yet stopped. The air carried a fine mist that brought with it a faint chill, a foretaste of early winter.

Ting Shuang's face was shadowed with worry. As far as she knew, Steward Chen had stockpiled nearly forty thousand taels' worth of ice, and Madam's private accounts were now empty of a single tael. If the weather stayed cool like this, summer would not be hot enough, and there was every chance the ice would not sell and they would take a loss.

Heavy with these thoughts, she helped Yun Chu with her hair and makeup. When she stepped outside, the morning callers had already arrived.

After a brief exchange of pleasantries, the concubines prepared to take their leave as custom required. At that moment Concubine Tao rose to her feet. "Madam, this concubine would like to ask: has it been permitted by Madam for the eldest young miss to send things to the small temple?"

The color drained from Xie Ping's face.

She had sent things through a discreet messenger just that once, and had been very careful about it. How had Concubine Tao found out?

Yun Chu took a sip of tea.

She had arranged this herself, quietly letting the matter reach Concubine Tao's ears. If she was going to push He Shi into a corner, she needed a good blade to do it with. Concubine Tao, there was no question, was an excellent blade.

She saw it all clearly, but let her face show only surprise. "Ping'er, is what Concubine Tao says true?"

Xie Ping could not deny it, and stumbled over her words. "Mother, I... He Mama practically raised me, and I could see that the small temple was so bare and mean, so I..."

"Your father sent her there because she attempted to harm a child. Confining her to the small temple is her punishment, and by secretly sending her things, you have made light of your father's authority." Yun Chu's voice grew cool. "She nearly caused the death of a child not yet born, a child who would have been your own younger brother. You have chilled Concubine Tao's heart with this, and you have chilled that unborn child's heart. Ping'er, do you understand what you did wrong?"

Concubine Tao added her voice. "The eldest young miss truly cannot tell close from distant. To go out of her way to protect a servant of no standing: how very strange."

In all these recent days, Yun Chu had kept a kind and gentle manner toward Xie Ping. This was the first time she had spoken so sharply.

Xie Ping bowed her head and said quietly, "Mother, I am sorry. I should not have sent He Mama things without permission. I was wrong, and I will never do it again."

Yun Chu spoke calmly. "He Shi has committed a grave offense. That she was not handed over to the authorities is already a mercy on the part of the Xie family. It is not possible to allow her to go on enjoying the treatment of a first-class servant. Concubine Tao, if you have time, pay a visit to the small temple and take back anything that ought to be taken back. There is no need to turn it over to the household accounts; you may keep it for yourself, as a gift to steady the nerves of the child you are carrying."

Concubine Tao was overjoyed. "Thank you, Madam!"

With Yun Chu's permission, Concubine Tao set off at once for the small temple within the Xie estate grounds, accompanied by two stout matrons. The old madam was a devout Buddhist and had had the temple built when the household was first established, but since they could not afford to maintain many people there, only a young novice nun resided within. He Shi had now been added to the occupants.

He Shi occupied the western side room. She was sitting inside, lost in thought.

Without warning, the door was kicked open.

Concubine Tao walked in with one hand supporting her belly, looking around with a click of her tongue. "A servant who plotted against the household, living in rooms this comfortable. I am not as charitable as the master and Madam. Come, take it all."

At her word, the two matrons came inside and carried out every visible object. They went further still, pulling the clothes and shoes from the wardrobe, then rolling up the bedding and tossing it out into the courtyard.

"What are you doing..." He Shi stared, wide-eyed. "Don't touch my things!"

As the bedding was rolled up, a coin pouch fell out.

Concubine Tao bent to pick it up. She opened it, and inside, alongside the silver coins, were several hundred-tael banknotes.

"You treacherous creature!" Concubine Tao raged. "Hiding away this much money! So not only did you plot against the household, you were stealing silver all along. And to think how much the master trusted you!"

He Shi lunged forward to grab the money.

That was every bit of savings she had accumulated over the years. Not a coin of it was stolen.

Everything she owned in the world was in that pouch.

She threw herself at Concubine Tao without thinking.

"Help! She is trying to harm me!" Concubine Tao stepped back and let the two stout matrons move forward.

One of them kicked out, and He Shi screamed and crashed to the ground.

chapters.title: Rising to Dance at Cockcrow
chapters.content:
Yun Chu was reviewing her dowry inventory, intending to sell off whatever was unnecessary and convert it to silver.

She was in the middle of this when Ting Feng came in. "Madam, Concubine Tao found seven hundred and eighty taels of silver on He Shi. How would you like it handled?"

Yun Chu said carelessly, "Let Concubine Tao keep it."

If she wanted Concubine Tao to serve willingly as this blade, she naturally had to offer some reward. A blade treated well would only grow sharper.

Ting Feng continued, "Concubine Tao had her people beat He Shi until she spat blood. Should a physician be called?"

"Spitting a bit of blood will not kill her." Yun Chu's expression was entirely unmoved.

He Shi had three birth children: Xie Ping, Xie Shi'an, and Xie Shiwei. She rather wanted to see which of them would be the first to lose composure and send medicine to the small temple.

She paused, then added, "Concubine Tao was given quite a fright over at He Shi's place. Take some cordyceps from the storeroom and send them to her to restore her strength."

When the tonic arrived from Yun Chu, the last of Concubine Tao's anxiety settled back into her chest.

She understood now: Madam also despised He Shi in her heart. Madam was simply like the clear moon in the sky, too radiant for a creature as lowly as He Shi to be worth her direct attention.

With Madam's blessing, what did she have left to worry about?

Concubine Tao beckoned one of her maids over and murmured a few words.

That evening, the matron who delivered supper dropped a bowl of moldy rice outside the door of He Shi's side room.

"Stop right there!" He Shi called after her. "Is this fit for a human being to eat? How dare you treat me this way?"

The matron spat. "Oh, listen to you. Thinks she's still the master's head managing mama, does she? Look at yourself: confined to a broken-down temple, lower than the meanest scullery maid. Be grateful anyone gives you anything to eat at all, and still complaining?"

He Shi could scarcely believe it. That vile Tao woman had taken every last coin of her savings, beaten her half to death, and now was cutting off her food.

Truly, a tiger fallen to the plains is bullied by dogs.

"What's that look for?" The matron kicked the bowl of moldy rice over. "Ungrateful wretch. If you don't want it, then go without. You nearly killed the young mistress's child, and you still expect a full belly? There is much worse in store for you!"

The matron walked off, grumbling all the way.

He Shi felt her blood surge upward and nearly fainted.

On the morning of the following day, Old General Yun sent over a vigorous young woman.

She was called Qiu Tong, about twenty years of age, dressed in a dark short-hemmed jacket with a sword hanging at her waist.

"Greetings, Madam!"

Qiu Tong saluted with clasped fists, carrying herself with a bold, clean energy.

Yun Chu had grown up in a military household, and one look at Qiu Tong told her the woman's skills were no trifle.

"You will be my martial arts teacher from now on," she said. "Consider yourself in the position of a teacher, and we will train however you see fit."

Qiu Tong agreed, stepped forward to feel Yun Chu's pulse, and ran her hands carefully over her bones and sinews, shaking her head as she went. "Madam does have some foundation. It is simply that the body has been idle too long, and the tendons and meridians have gone stiff. The most important thing now is to restore the flexibility you once had."

And just like that, Yun Chu was brought out into the courtyard.

For all that Qiu Tong was a woman, her hands were no gentler than Yun Chu's grandfather's had ever been. Working to unblock her meridians and acupoints nearly did Yun Chu in with pain.

By the end of the hour, Yun Chu no longer had the strength to stand.

Qiu Tong's face remained completely expressionless. "I will be waiting for Madam in the courtyard at cockcrow tomorrow morning."

Yun Chu's vision went dark.

Cockcrow was around the second watch of the night, barely past midnight.

She had barely felt herself fall asleep when Ting Shuang was already waking her. "Madam, it is time to rise. Sister Qiu Tong is already waiting outside."

Yun Chu scrambled out of bed.

This was the path she had chosen of her own accord. She had no choice but to press forward and never look back.

Her grandfather had always said: a skill you have truly learned is something that belongs to you, and no one can take it away.

The courtyard was lit up, and Qiu Tong stood there with quiet gravity, demonstrating the proper horse stance. She had Yun Chu hold it for a quarter of an hour first, to be extended gradually over time.

Yun Chu had held a horse stance as a child too, and every time her grandfather looked away she would slack off.

The shortcuts taken in childhood are the suffering that must be borne in adulthood.

"Come join Madam, all of you." Qiu Tong glanced at the maidservants standing to one side. "If Madam ever truly finds herself in danger, it will help for you to be able to assist her."

At that, Ting Shuang, Ting Xue, and Ting Feng came over at once and lined up to hold the horse stance together.

When the quarter hour ended, the three maidservants who had never touched martial arts were drenched in sweat and gasping for breath. Qiu Tong let them rest for the time being.

Yun Chu had some foundation, and managed to hold the stance for a good half-hour before she began to waver.

After nearly an hour of training, she went back and lay down on the bed, asleep the instant her head touched the pillow. A little over an hour later, the sky was already light.

The morning callers arrived one by one.

"Mother, the old madam's birthday is nearly here." Xie Ping brought over several sheets of paper. "I would like to hold a grand birthday celebration for the old madam and invite all the notable noblewomen in the capital to make it a proper occasion. What does Mother think?"

Yun Chu looked at the invitation list she had drawn up. "You have put down the wife of the Minister of Revenue, the wife of the Grand Preceptor... these are all first-rank noblewomen. A family of our standing cannot expect to draw guests like these."

Xie Ping said, "Grandmother and these ladies are all old acquaintances, and they all watched Mother grow up. If Mother were to extend the invitations herself, I believe those ladies would do her the courtesy of coming."

Concubine Tao let out a short laugh. "The eldest young miss is still too young; she does not understand these things."

Being laughed at by a concubine was enough to make Xie Ping feel the sting of humiliation.

Ting Yu spoke up, "If it were Madam's own birthday celebration, it might be worth extending such invitations, but for the old madam, it is perhaps not quite appropriate."

"Ping'er, write up a new guest list." Yun Chu looked at her. "Also, the menu you have drawn up is identical to last year's. That needs to be rethought as well. Surely there should be something fresh and new?"

Xie Ping felt somewhat deflated.

Whatever she had done before, Mother had always found a word of praise for it.

Yet ever since she had secretly sent things to He Shi, Mother's manner toward her seemed to have changed.

She bowed her head. "Yes, Mother. I will go back and think on it further."

Yun Chu left the matter of the birthday banquet entirely in Xie Ping's hands and said nothing more about it, offering only the most minor of suggestions at morning calls. She gave the whole of her attention to learning from Qiu Tong.

What surprised her was that three or four days passed, and He Shi's three birth children, Xie Ping, Xie Shi'an, and Xie Shiwei, had none of them sent so much as a remedy to the small temple.

Yun Chu smiled to herself.

These three ungrateful creatures cared nothing for her, their adoptive mother. It was plain enough that they felt no very deep affection for He Shi, their birth mother, either.

He Shi's days were difficult indeed.

She had spat blood and her body ached constantly. With not a proper meal in days, she was growing thinner at a visible rate.

She knew she could not go on like this. She had to find a way to save herself, or one day she would starve to death in that small temple and no one would know.

When the temple's only young novice was asleep, she slipped out under cover of darkness, avoiding the maids and menservants at every turn, and made her way to the window of Xie Jingyu's study.

Xie Jingyu always came home very late.

She had just arrived at the study door when she saw a tall silhouette approaching from a distance.

chapters.title: The Xie Family Has Deceived You
chapters.content:
He Shi felt a pang of sorrow.

She and Xie Jingyu were the same age. At the same number of years, he was still the elegant young gentleman he had always been, while she had already grown old and worn.

"What are you doing here?"

Seeing her standing at the courtyard gate, Xie Jingyu's exhausted face shifted into irritation.

He Shi bowed her head. "Master, I accept whatever punishment I deserve for what I have done wrong. But that does not mean I am willing to be tortured to death. Concubine Tao, with Madam's tacit approval, has cut off the food supply to the small temple. She means to cut off my way of living."

Xie Jingyu pressed his fingers to the bridge of his nose.

He had just come back from Magistrate Yu's estate, where he had spent the better part of a day without laying eyes on the man even once.

In the past, Magistrate Yu had treated him reasonably well, always bringing him along to social engagements, introducing him to influential figures in official circles.

With the performance review drawing near, Magistrate Yu had suddenly lost all interest in him.

He truly could not understand what he had done wrong.

He had endured a full day of frustration with no one to vent it to, and now, the moment he came home, He Shi was there pulling him into these trivial domestic matters.

He was not a man who lost his temper easily, but even he was struggling to hold himself together at that moment. He spoke coldly. "You chose to stay in the Xie household yourself. Whatever treatment you receive is a consequence of your own choice. Furthermore, I instructed you to remain confined to the small temple, and yet here you are at the door of my study. Since you do not take my words seriously, I will simply have someone posted at the small temple door to keep watch."

He Shi's lips went rigid.

She thought of their very first meeting, long ago, and of the look of wonder in his eyes when he had looked at her.

She thought of the tenderness in this man's gaze after she had given birth to An'er.

She thought of the years she had spent with their three children in the countryside outside the capital, and of the warmth he had shown on his visits once a month.

From the day she had moved into the Xie household, the two of them had become master and servant. The name by which she called him, once Yu-lang, had become "Master."

Only now, in this moment, did she understand that they could probably never go back to what they had once been.

"Are you not leaving?"

Xie Jingyu's voice was full of impatience.

He Shi's tears came then, sudden and uncontrolled.

She had gone to such lengths to have her children recognized by the family. She had found every means to stay at Xie Jingyu's side. She had been willing to serve as a slave as long as they could all be together. Had this man ever truly seen the sacrifices she had made?

"Yes, Master. I will go now."

He Shi curtsied, turned away, and let the tears fall.

Watching her retreating figure, Xie Jingyu sighed. Keeping her in the Xie household was already a concession he had made out of regard for what they had once shared.

If he did any more for He Shi, it would surely arouse Yun Chu's suspicion, and he still needed the Yun family's influence to smooth his path in officialdom. He could not afford to break with Yun Chu.

He Shi returned to the small temple, her heart reduced to cold ash.

She still had to live to see An'er pass the imperial examinations and become an official. She still had to see Ping'er married in person. She still had to watch Shiwei make something of himself. She could not die in this small temple.

Since Xie Jingyu could not be relied upon, she would have to rely on herself.

She wrote a letter, and gave the only bracelet left on her wrist to the young novice, begging the girl to deliver it for her.

"She wishes to send a letter to Steward He in the outer courtyard?" Yun Chu looked at the young novice who had come to report. "Then go ahead and deliver it for her."

The young novice agreed, took the letter, and set off for the outer courtyard.

Ting Shuang said, with some surprise, "He Shi and the steward of the outer courtyard share the same surname. Could the two of them be related?"

Yun Chu nodded. "They are likely brother and sister. If we want to get to the bottom of He Shi's origins, we will need to start with He Xu."

He Shi's background was certainly no ordinary one. Otherwise she would never have set her sights on the position of principal wife, and even if that was out of reach, she would surely have been willing to serve as a concubine.

There was a conjecture forming in her mind, but without evidence it was worth nothing to anyone.

Whether Xie Shi'an's path in officialdom could be cut off entirely depended on what He Shi's background turned out to be.

Just then a young manservant from the front courtyard came in to report. "Madam, this servant went to the Yun household, and the family said the eldest young master will be returning to the capital tomorrow morning."

Yun Chu rose abruptly to her feet.

Although Jizhou was not terribly far from the capital, her elder brother had business to attend to there. That he was able to return so early was well beyond what she had expected.

The rest of that day passed with painful slowness. Early the next morning she took the carriage back to the Yun family home.

But after returning to the capital, Yun Ze first had to go to the palace to report, and it was midday before he came back at last. He was exhausted all over, and her sister-in-law Liu Qianqian took him away first to change his clothes.

Lady Lin asked with curiosity, "Chu'er, do you and your brother have some urgent matter to discuss?"

From the moment her daughter had returned home, she had been distracted, glancing repeatedly toward the door, and it was only when Yun Ze came back that the anxiety in her manner eased a little.

Yun Chu quickly produced a smile. "The Xie family's ancestral home is in Jizhou. My husband has not been back in many years, and I wanted to ask Elder Brother about how things stand there."

Lady Lin nodded thoughtfully.

When Yun Ze had changed his clothes and come through to the parlor, Lady Lin and Liu Qianqian stepped out, leaving the room to the two of them.

"Elder Brother." The moment Yun Chu spoke, her voice came out slightly hoarse. "The children, have they come back?"

Yun Ze opened his lips, but could not bring out a single word.

Had he brought back those two unfortunate children, he would have told his sister the moment he saw her, rather than using the excuse of changing clothes to think over how to soften the news.

The light in Yun Chu's eyes slowly went out. Her voice grew even more hoarse. "Elder Brother?"

Yun Ze let out a long breath. "Chu'er, I went myself to the Xie family's ancestral home in Jizhou and asked the clan elders where the children were buried. But the clan elders told me that four years ago, no one from the capital branch of the Xie family had ever come back, and they had never heard a word about Xie Jingyu's legitimate son and daughter dying in infancy. The Xie family has deceived you."

It was as if something exploded inside her head.

Yun Chu felt the room tilt. She caught the edge of the table and barely kept herself from falling.

She closed her eyes, drew several slow, deep breaths, and gradually brought herself back into stillness.

"Thank you, thank you, Elder Brother!"

She forced the words out with difficulty, turned, and walked toward the door.

"Chu'er."

Yun Ze set aside all propriety between siblings and caught her by the wrist.

"Let Elder Brother go back with you."

Yun Chu pressed her hand over his arm, her voice so hoarse it was barely there. "This is something I can face on my own. If I truly cannot manage, I will come home and ask for Elder Brother's help."

She turned, squared her shoulders, and walked outside.

On any other day she would have gone to say goodbye to her mother and sister-in-law before leaving. Today she had no room in her for even that.

Ting Shuang steadied her as they walked quickly to the gate of the Yun estate. She climbed into the carriage and told the coachman to drive faster, faster still.

The carriage flew through the streets and soon arrived at the Xie household.

She walked in quickly and sank into the chair in the parlor, all the strength gone out of her body. When she spoke, her voice carried a deep, bitter cold. "Bring He Shi here."

The two matrons had never seen Madam like this. They exchanged a look and hurried off to fetch He Shi from the small temple.

He Shi was lying on her bed, her body too weak to hold itself up. She had not been treated for her injuries, and with not a proper meal in days, she was barely managing.

She had just closed her eyes when the door of her room was kicked open.

She startled badly, thinking it was Concubine Tao coming again with her people, but when she looked up she saw it was the rough-work matrons from Yun Chu's courtyard.

These were Madam's people.

Madam had always operated through others. Even when she wanted to move against He Shi, she used Concubine Tao. When had she ever sent her own people directly?

Before she could think any further, He Shi was hauled up by both arms and dragged out the door.

chapters.title: Dying Young Is an Ill Omen
chapters.content:
Yun Chu sat in the rattan chair in the courtyard.

She had drunk four or five cups of cool tea in a row, and still could not quiet the storm inside her.

The moment she thought of her children lying buried in some unknown place, her heart was as if cut to pieces by a blade.

In her previous life, she had never asked about the children, not once. When she died, they still had not been laid to rest in peace. She hated the person she had been in that life with everything she had.

He Shi was dragged in through the door.

The pain in Yun Chu's chest turned to fury. Her gaze was like a drawn blade, fixed on He Shi without mercy.

He Shi trembled involuntarily.

The Yun Chu she had known was always warm and composed, gracious even to the lowest serving boy in the household. Even when He Shi had framed her, Madam had never looked at her like this.

One of the two matrons behind her gave her a shove, and her knees buckled. She dropped to the ground.

Yun Chu stared at her, ice in her voice. "Four years ago, two children I carried were lost. He Mama, you took the children back to be buried in their ancestral home. I am asking you: where are they buried?"

He Shi's composure tightened. Why would Madam suddenly be asking about something four years old?

She kept her eyes cast down. "The master was occupied with official matters and entrusted this servant to make the journey in his place. This servant brought the young master and the young miss back to the ancestral home in Jizhou and buried them on the hillside behind the Xie family's ancestral shrine. There was no gravestone put up, so this servant cannot say exactly where."

Bang.

Yun Chu brought the teacup down hard on the table.

Her expression was cold as frost. "It seems He Mama has no intention of telling me the truth. Someone come."

At her word, two of the rough-work matrons brought out a long plank bench and pressed He Shi down onto it, then each took up a long wooden board.

He Shi was badly frightened. "Madam, this servant is telling the truth."

Yun Chu made a small gesture.

The two matrons obeyed, and the boards began to fall, one to either side.

These women were used to hard labor, and the strength in their arms was something to behold. Three or four strokes in, and all the breath had gone out of He Shi.

"He Mama, I will give you one more chance." Yun Chu spoke each word clearly and separately. "Tell me where the children are buried, and I will release you."

He Shi's pain was nearly enough to make her lose consciousness.

She knew perfectly well that Madam must have confirmed that the children were not buried in Jizhou before daring to question her openly like this.

There was no point in holding to her original account.

"Madam, this servant... this servant does not know either." He Shi struggled to get the words out. "The master told me to see to the burial of the young master and young miss, but before I could set out for Jizhou, the master had already taken the children's remains away himself. This servant truly knows nothing."

Yun Chu shook her head. "Continue."

The two matrons put all their strength behind the boards, and He Shi's screams did not stop. Before long she fainted.

Yun Chu's face showed no emotion at all. "Pour water over her. Keep going."

A basin of ice-cold water was splashed over He Shi's face. She had not yet come back to herself when the boards fell again, and wave after wave of pain swallowed her whole.

Yun Chu dug her nails into her own palm.

All she wanted was to know where her children were laid to rest. Why had even this small wish become something impossible to have?

What could possibly be keeping He Shi from speaking, what was there in this that she still did not know?

Never before had Yun Chu hated herself like this.

She hated her own weakness. She hated herself for being foolish enough to be deceived. She hated herself for not deserving the name of mother.

Outside the courtyard, Xie Ping paced in anguish.

If this went on, He Shi would lose at least half her life even if she did not die outright.

She could not understand it: they were only two children who had died young, barely worth mentioning after four years. Why would He Shi be so desperately unwilling to give up the answer?

She stamped her foot, turned, and headed for the Hall of Longevity.

When the old madam heard that Yun Chu had had He Shi flogged, she was not particularly bothered. But when she heard that Yun Chu had been driven to anger over two children who had died in infancy, an uncomfortable expression crossed her face.

Those two children were dead. What did it matter where they were buried?

The old madam took up her walking stick and made her way to Yun Chu's courtyard. As she arrived at the entrance, she noticed that the characters on the gate had changed at some point to simply read Sheng Residence.

But that was a small thing, and not the time to raise it.

"Chu'er!"

The old madam stepped briskly inside.

"What has He Shi done, that you should make such a commotion?"

Yun Chu looked at her calmly. "If the old madam knows where the children are buried, I can let He Shi go."

"Children who drew no breath from the moment they were born are viewed as inauspicious. Every family handles them the same way: buried wherever is convenient, to keep them from affecting the family's fortunes. Even in the imperial household, princes or princesses who die young are buried in whatever spot outside the city can be found, to say nothing of a family of our modest fifth rank."

"The old madam has so many grandchildren that naturally you have no feeling for children who die young." Yun Chu's voice was very cold. "But those two were my only children. Until I know where they are buried, I will not rest, and if they are not at peace, this Xie household will never know peace either."

She rose and withdrew into the inner chamber.

Old Madam Xie felt a surge of fury rise up and nearly topple her. "She... what does she mean by that? How dare she speak so disrespectfully to an elder?"

"Madam has been respectful and dutiful toward you ever since she married into the Xie family, old madam. This discourtesy comes from an excess of grief." Ting Shuang bowed her head. "The matter of the young master and young miss not being found in Jizhou was personally investigated by Madam's elder brother. If the Xie family cannot provide an explanation, the Yun family will come to the door and demand one themselves."

The old madam felt a knot form in her chest.

This was a naked threat.

She looked toward He Shi, who lay slumped across the bench, and said coldly, "Tell them everything you know. Do not let this damage the bond between the Xie and Yun families."

He Shi's cracked lips pressed together hard.

If she told the truth, the bond between the Yun and Xie families would be truly, irreparably broken.

Her son An'er still needed to lean on the Yun family connection to make his way in officialdom. Much as she despised Yun Chu, she knew she could not afford to let Yun Chu abandon the Xie family.

"Old madam, He Mama is nearly done for." Xie Ping could not hold herself back any longer. "Please have a physician brought."

"The eldest young miss had better not let her good intentions cause more trouble." Ting Shuang's voice was cold. "Without Madam's permission, no one is to remove He Shi from this place."

The old madam's expression was dark.

She was the elder here, but if this granddaughter-in-law had made up her mind to do something, there was genuinely little she could do about it.

The Yun family was the mountain standing behind her granddaughter-in-law.

Thinking of this, the old madam turned away, leaned on her walking stick, and left.

Xie Ping was frantic inside, but dared not let it show too plainly.

She simply could not understand why He Shi always managed to stir up such trouble. If she were not the one who had come out of He Shi's womb, she would not bother with any of this.

But even the old madam had no power over her mother, so certainly she, a junior, had none.

The only option was to fetch her father.

Xie Ping hurried to the Blue Pine Pavilion to find Xie Shi'an.

Xie Shi'an was practicing his calligraphy. He had heard what was happening at Sheng Residence from the serving boys.

He kept his expression composed. "Do you know why Mother has suddenly grown so concerned about two children who have been dead four years?"

Xie Ping shook her head.

"Last time, all of us chose to believe a servant over her." Xie Shi'an looked at Xie Ping. "She likely feels that we, none of us being her own, are all ingrates who cannot be won over by kindness, and so her thoughts have turned to those two children she lost. At a time like this, if you speak up again on He Shi's behalf, Mother will probably lose all hope in you entirely, and she will most likely not bring you along when she attends the great families' gatherings in the future."

chapters.title: Striking Xie Jingyu
chapters.content:
Xie Shi'an lowered his head and returned to his calligraphy.

Xie Ping pressed her lips together.

This younger brother was only a year apart from her in age, yet he was far more mature, and far colder.

He Shi was their birth mother, after all. She lay right now under the boards, half a life's worth of breath being beaten out of her, and this brother had not so much as furrowed his brow.

And yet Xie Ping also knew perfectly well that speaking up for a servant in front of her mother would only arouse suspicion.

She said nothing more, turned, and went back to her own courtyard.

Xie Shi'an held the brush, barely managing to finish the piece of calligraphy, then let his dark eyes go still and deep. He stood up abruptly and walked out.

"Bring my horse!"

A serving boy led the horse to the gate, and he swung up into the saddle, riding directly for Magistrate Yu's estate.
