Magistrate Yu was a third-rank official, and it seemed a banquet was underway; the gate was busy with carriages coming and going.

Xie Shi'an stopped under a large tree across from the magistrate's estate and waited quietly.

Before long, the banquet came to an end.

He saw Xie Jingyu emerge with a slightly downcast air, and hurried forward. "Father."

Xie Jingyu composed himself, looking mildly surprised. "What brought you here?"

"Something has happened at home." Xie Shi'an kept his voice low. "Mother is questioning He Shi about the two children who died in infancy four years ago."

Xie Jingyu's expression shifted.

He steadied himself. "What is the situation now?"

"The old madam went to intercede with Mother, and Mother said that if He Shi does not confess, the Xie household will have no peace." Xie Shi'an raised his head. "Father, are those two children not properly buried, and is He Shi too afraid to confess it because of how much worse it would make things?"

Xie Jingyu looked at his son with a complicated expression.

Even twelve-year-old An'er had guessed it. Yun Chu, in all likelihood, had guessed it too.

If Yun Chu were to learn what had become of those two children, she would not hesitate to dissolve the marriage, and his career in officialdom would probably end there as well.

"While Mother is questioning He Shi, she is also waiting for Father to return home." Xie Shi'an continued. "If Father walks in looking the way he looks now, she will be able to infer quite a bit without you saying a word, and the Xie household will truly have no peace."

Xie Jingyu took Xie Shi'an with him into the carriage.

The two of them sat inside alone, listening to the rumble of the wheels and the unbroken sounds of people talking in the streets outside.

"I was the one who instructed He Shi to dispose of those children." Xie Jingyu closed his eyes. "They were never given a proper burial."

Xie Shi'an felt a weight drop in his chest.

His guess had been right after all.

Yet he could not understand it. Those two children carried their father's blood. Even if they could not be buried in the Xie family's ancestral ground, how could they simply be discarded?

But there was no point in examining the past. What mattered now was how to handle the situation before them.

"An'er, I am going back to deal with your mother as quickly as I can. You ride out to the villages near the capital at once and make inquiries. Children who die young in the countryside are usually buried in one place. Try to find two infant remains." Xie Jingyu pressed his hand onto Xie Shi'an's shoulder. "I know this is asking something difficult of you, but right now, you are the only one I can trust."

Xie Shi'an's expression was complicated. "Alright."

He pushed back the carriage curtain, stepped down, and rode off at a gallop.

Xie Jingyu told the driver to return home.

The moment the carriage arrived at the gate, the serving boy who attended him came hurrying over. "Master, Madam's matrons have come by several times. They say as soon as you return home, you are to go to Sheng Residence at once."

Xie Jingyu nodded to show he understood.

Without even changing his clothes, he walked directly toward Sheng Residence.

His mind turned over many thoughts as he went.

He arrived at Yun Chu's quarters before long. At a glance he took in He Shi, strapped to the long bench in the courtyard.

He Shi's back was a field of red, her clothes beaten to rags. The sight of it was difficult to look at.

Yet the two matrons standing watch had not relented: they sloshed a bucket of water over He Shi's face and, once she had come around, brought the boards down again.

"All of you, stop."

Xie Jingyu said three cold words.

The two matrons bent immediately at the waist. "We greet the master."

Xie Jingyu's expression was tangled past untangling.

In his mind, Yun Chu had always been gentle and tolerant, a wise and capable partner who ran the household. She was as vast as the open sky, able to contain all manner of people and things.

In five years of marriage, he had never once seen her punish a single servant.

This was the first time. He was seeing her fury.

It burned and blazed, and it stirred an unease in his chest.

He stepped up onto the raised walkway and came to the door of Yun Chu's bedchamber. He knocked lightly and said, "Madam?"

He heard footsteps, and then the door was pulled open.

Before he could say a word.

Suddenly.

A gust of movement came at him.

The crack of a sharp slap struck his face.

Everyone in the courtyard froze. The whole space went quiet, the only sound the wind.

Xie Jingyu's face was filled with complete disbelief.

He had been slapped by a woman.

He was probably the first husband in this dynasty to have been slapped by his own wife.

It was an intolerable humiliation.

Yun Chu's palm stung. Her eyes were red as coals, fixed on Xie Jingyu and burning.

She spoke each word separately. "I will ask you once, and only once. Where are the children buried?"

The side of Xie Jingyu's face flared with heat.

He clenched his fists with all his strength, pressing the outrage down.

He drew a slow breath. "Madam, your emotions are running very high. Let us speak when you have calmed down."

Yun Chu said coldly, "You are my husband; I cannot question you the way I can question He Shi. But I can request that my grandfather come forward."

Xie Jingyu's lips pressed together.

His grandmother had once warned him: marry into a highborn family, and a husband will always be overshadowed. But in five years of marriage, Yun Chu had never once used the Yun family's influence to force him into anything, and he had always been grateful to her for respecting him as a husband.

Now Yun Chu had invoked Old General Yun.

She was clearly not prepared to let this go.

And he...

Magistrate Yu had withdrawn his favor. The only thing he could still lean on now was the Yun family.

He marshaled everything he had and forced all feeling down.

When he raised his head again, he had put on an expression of humility and warmth. "In the matter of the children's burial, I did conceal things from you, and it is something I cannot forgive myself for. The slap you gave me is what I deserved. My original intention was to have the children buried beside the ancestral shrine at the Xie family's old home, but afterward, someone told me that children who die young, buried near the ancestral ground, will affect the fortune of the whole clan. At the time I had only just found my footing in officialdom, and I was genuinely afraid..."

Yun Chu had run out of patience. She cut him off, her voice cold. "I only need you to tell me where the children are."

"Four years ago, I had someone find a spot in a village outside the capital and bury the children there." Xie Jingyu lowered his gaze to hide what lay behind his eyes. "It is late now, and going there tonight would be inconvenient. First thing tomorrow morning, I will take you to see the children."

Yun Chu's lips were as white as clay.

Her fingers trembled slightly. One word came out: "Get out."

Then came the slam of the door.

She leaned against it from the inside, and slowly sank to the floor.

She ought to be grateful, ought she not? Grateful that Xie Jingyu had not simply abandoned the children's remains, grateful that they had some place to lie...

chapters.title: The Xie Family Wants to Cast Out His Wife
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu turned and walked down from the raised walkway.

The servants in the courtyard stole a glance at him, then quickly looked down.

The mark on his face was red and swollen, painfully visible.

He walked over to where He Shi lay and said, "Two of you: take He Shi back to the small temple."

The two matrons looked at each other and did not move.

They had by now fully understood: though this was the Xie household, the authority rested with Madam. Even if Madam had not given the Xie family a single son or daughter, even if Madam had just struck the master across the face, the way the household operated made it clear that Madam was the one who truly held the power here.

Without Madam's word, they did not dare move He Shi.

Ting Shuang came forward. "You two may take He Shi back."

Only then did the two matrons dare to go and carry the unconscious He Shi away.

Xie Jingyu's expression was very ugly.

He walked ahead and personally saw He Shi to the small temple, where the matrons deposited her onto the hard bed. Dragged along that whole way, she had roused somewhat, and when she opened her eyes to find Xie Jingyu standing by the bed, her tears began to fall. Her voice was raw. "Master, I am in such pain."

Xie Jingyu drew a small vial of salve from his sleeve and held it out to her. "This is a fine medicine from the palace. Have a maidservant apply it for you in a moment."

He Shi reached up with a trembling hand and brushed his face. "How could Madam dare to strike you? Only a crude, common woman would do such a thing. Master, cast her out. Cast her out."

Xie Jingyu pulled away from her touch. "She is overwhelmed by grief for her children. It is understandable."

He Shi ground her teeth. "Can you not see that Madam is completely different from before? She is no longer that Madam Xie who devoted herself wholeheartedly to this household. She is as though she bears a grudge against the entire Xie family. Has there been a single person she has not moved against? Even you have taken a slap from her. What else would she be capable of as things go on, no matter how high her birth? She is no longer fit to be the mistress of this house. In any other family she would have been cast out long ago. What right does she have to go on doing as she pleases? Master, when the time comes to cut the cord, cut it."

Xie Jingyu looked toward the window.

He had of course noticed how different Yun Chu had become. He had not been able to understand at first why she seemed to have turned into another person entirely. Now, at last, he understood.

Yun Chu must have begun to suspect the truth about the children some time ago and had spent months investigating without being able to find where they were buried, until finally she could hold herself back no longer.

"Whatever happened to those children four years ago will stay buried. You are not to bring it up again." Xie Jingyu turned to go. "Rest and heal your injuries. Do not let your mind run wild, and do not stir up any more trouble. I will arrange for someone to see that you are not too ill-treated."

He Shi lay on her stomach, squeezing the little vial of medicine in her fist.

Xie Jingyu walked out of the small temple and returned to his study.

The mark of five fingers on his face was becoming more and more distinct. Nearly every servant who passed by could see it.

And so, word that Xie Jingyu had been slapped by his wife in Sheng Residence spread to every corner of the Xie household, and naturally made its way to the Hall of Longevity as well.

"What?!" Old Madam Xie flung the teacup from her hand. "Yun Chu dared to slap Jingyu? How could she? Where did she get the nerve?"

Yuan Shi offered, "Husbands and wives do quarrel, it is not so unusual."

"Quarrel is one thing. Who gave her permission to raise her hand? She struck him across the face. How is Jingyu supposed to appear at court tomorrow?" The old madam was nearly beside herself with fury. "She has not produced a child, she has long since violated the grounds for dismissal, and for a wife to strike her husband is enough to call her coarse and contemptible, would it not? A woman like her is not fit to be the mistress of this house. In any other family she would have been dismissed long ago. What right does she have to carry on this way?"

Yuan Shi said gently, "Do not say such things, old madam, someone might hear. Chu'er is a girl with good fortune behind her. After she came into this family, your illness suddenly improved, and Jingyu's path in officialdom has been smooth ever since. She carries good fortune with her; she brings the Xie family up with her. Cast her out, and where would you find another daughter-in-law half as good?"

"My illness ran its course, what has she to do with it?" the old madam said coldly. "Jingyu's rise is Jingyu's own ability. The Yun family has hardly been of any help at all. This time, I will let it pass and say it is because of those two children who died young. But if she goes on in the future making everyone miserable as she has today, even if it means offending the Yun family, I will have Jingyu dismiss her."

Yuan Shi said quickly, "Chu'er is not someone who is unreasonable."

The two women were still talking when the sky had gone completely dark outside.

Yun Chu's emotions had swung wildly all day, and she was left feeling as though all the energy had been drained from her body. She lay down on the bed, exhausted through and through.

She had planned to practice the horse stance for a while that evening, but she simply could not get up.

She closed her eyes, and kept hearing the sound of her children crying in her dreams. At some point, without knowing when, she fell asleep.

"Mama, where are you? We miss you so much."

"Mama, will you hold us? We are so cold."

Yun Chu's heart felt as though it were being wrung out. She knew this was a dream, and yet she refused to wake. She wanted so desperately to find her children, to hold them, to tell them she had not forgotten them for a single day, that she missed them terribly.

She struggled forward through the fog of the dream.

A white mist surrounded everything, stretching without end. She did not know how long she walked before, finally, a thread of brightness appeared ahead.

Yun Chu ran toward it.

She saw a blue sky and wide sweeping fields of green, flowers blooming everywhere. In the midst of the flowers sat two children of about four years old, delicately beautiful as carved jade.

A boy and a girl, heads bowed together over something they were playing with.

Yun Chu's heart softened in an instant. She walked toward them carefully, afraid that a sudden movement might shatter this beautiful dream.

"Children, Mama is here."

Her voice was as gentle as she could make it. She crouched down in front of them.

It was the boy who looked up first, and a familiar face filled her sight. "Little heir?" she said in bewilderment.

Her son's face had somehow become the face of the little heir of the Prince of Pingxi's household.

"Mama!"

The child threw himself into her arms.

She jerked awake.

She realized it was already light outside.

Ting Shuang heard the movement and came in quietly. "Madam, if you are not feeling well, you may sleep a little longer. I will have the morning callers leave."

Yun Chu pressed her fingers to her temples. "Tell them I am ill. They need not come for morning calls these next few days."

Ting Shuang's face was heavy with worry.

She tiptoed back to the door and stepped outside. "Madam is unwell. Everyone may go for now. Morning calls will not be necessary for the next few days."

Ting Yu, who was holding Xie Shiyu'n's hand, looked up with surprise. "Was Madam not perfectly well just yesterday? How can she suddenly be ill? Is it serious?"

Ting Feng thought Ting Yu was being truly tiresome. Something that enormous had happened yesterday; every person in the household knew perfectly well why Madam had fallen ill. Did she need it explained to her?

"The spring air still carries a chill. Madam has caught cold," Ting Shuang said evenly. "You may all go."

Everyone else took the hint and left. Ting Yu held onto Xie Shiyu'n and stayed behind, saying, "Madam is ill; I could stay to nurse her. Madam loves Yun'er best; let Yun'er cheer her up."

Ting Shuang's expression was cool. "Madam is resting and does not require nursing. Concubine Yu, please withdraw."

Ting Yu lowered her eyes.

She had once thought Madam clever. Now she only thought Madam was utterly foolish.

A woman who could not give birth ought to hold tight to whatever children were in the household and hold tight to her husband's heart. Yet Madam was doing the exact opposite of all that.

Madam had slapped the master in front of everyone. Whatever thread of feeling had remained between them as husband and wife was probably gone entirely now.

While Ting Yu was still turning this over in her mind, she saw Xie Jingyu, who had just returned from court, come striding quickly through the gate of Sheng Residence.

chapters.title: Laid to Rest at Last
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu was still dressed in his fifth-rank official's robes, clearly having come straight from court without stopping to change.

A flicker of pleasure rose in Ting Yu's eyes.

When she had still lived in Madam's courtyard, Xie Jingyu would sometimes come to discuss official matters with Madam, and she would get to see him. Since moving to the small courtyard, she had not seen the master for a long time, and she had truly feared he had forgotten all about her as a concubine.

She pushed Xie Shiyu'n forward. "Yun'er, did you not say just last night how much you miss your father? Go and greet him, quickly."

Xie Shiyu'n went obediently. "Greetings, Father."

Xie Jingyu gave a mild nod and walked straight into Sheng Residence's courtyard, stepping up onto the walkway and going to the outer reception room of Yun Chu's quarters.

Ting Yu, overlooked from first to last, dug her fingers hard into the handkerchief in her hand.

She could not understand it: the master had been slapped by Madam, and not only did he show no resentment, he had come hurrying straight to her.

Simply because Madam was the daughter of a great general, everyone had to coddle her?

"What are you still standing here for?" Ting Feng walked toward her, her voice sharp with contempt. "You cannot seriously think that giving the Xie family a son means the master will look at you any differently? Someone who betrayed her mistress is someone people will always despise."

Ting Yu pressed her lips together, took the child's hand, and turned away.

Xie Jingyu sat in the outer reception room for a while before Yun Chu came out of the bedchamber.

She was wearing a plain white robe, with nothing in her hair and no powder on her face. She had been stripped of every ornament, every cosmetic, down to her truest appearance, and that appearance, at a first glance, was clear and quietly lovely; at a second glance it was a beauty that could bring down kingdoms.

A feeling rose in his chest that he could not suppress.

Yun Chu's face held no expression. Her voice was cold. "Let us go."

Xie Jingyu pushed the feeling back down, and went out with her.

In front of the household gate stood a carriage, and behind it another conveyance. When Yun Chu saw what was on it, her face finally shifted.

"I spent the night finding these nanmu wood coffins. They will not rot for a thousand years." Xie Jingyu said. "I have wronged the children; I will do everything I can to make it right."

Yun Chu lowered her eyes, lifted her hem, and got into the carriage.

They drove steadily out of the city. After a good half-hour, they arrived at last at the village Xie Jingyu had spoken of.

Ting Shuang and Ting Feng helped Yun Chu down from the carriage, one to each side.

Xie Jingyu looked toward a hill ahead. "The children's remains are up on the hill. The path is rough; please watch your step, Madam."

He led the way. Yun Chu and both maidservants followed behind, and behind them four strong men, two pairs of them bearing the small nanmu coffins. The group made their way slowly up the hill.

It had been raining for many days on end, and the path was slick with mud. After only a few steps, Yun Chu's shoes were soaked through, and the hem of her white gown had taken on a layer of dark mud.

She gave none of it any notice. She waved aside the maidservants who moved to help her and made her own way, step by step.

Nearly half an hour of climbing brought them at last to a relatively level stretch of ground. Xie Jingyu stopped. "This is the place."

Yun Chu looked around. There was not a single rise in the earth, not the smallest mound; only the lush growth of spring and the flowers beginning to bloom. In one spot, the wildflowers had come early, a vivid tangle of purples and reds, achingly lovely.

Her heart began to tremble.

"Madam, please step back a little," said Xie Jingyu.

Yun Chu shook her head. "Begin."

The four strong men came forward with their tools, carefully clearing away the wildflowers, and began to dig.

The moment the earth broke open, water began to seep in from below.

Yun Chu thought of the dream, of the children saying they were cold. Was it because they had lain in water all this time?

Every time she thought of her children finding no peace even in death, her eyes burned and the tears fell without her being able to stop them.

The sight of her, reflected in Xie Jingyu's eyes, made something clench in his chest.

He moved toward her and put his arm around her shoulders. She moved away.

He withdrew his hand. "Madam, my father has an estate that is considered auspicious ground. We could have the children buried somewhere with birdsong and flowers..."

"That will not be necessary."

A low, steady voice carried from the direction of the path.

Xie Jingyu turned to see Yun Ze coming up the hill with a group of attendants.

The moment she saw Yun Ze, Yun Chu's unmoored heart settled. Her throat was thick. "Elder Brother."

Yun Ze raised a hand and gave her shoulder a quiet pat, then looked at Xie Jingyu. "I know I am an outsider and have no standing to interfere in the affairs of the Xie family. But Xie Jingyu, what you have done goes too far. Four years ago, if you had no desire to see to the burial yourself, you could have told me, and I would have taken care of it. You did not have to leave them on the first hillside you came across. In these four years, who knows what hardships those children have endured lying here, who knows whether their souls have found any peace. If they are unable to be reborn into their next life, you have their own father to blame for it."

Gentle Yun Ze, delivering a rebuke with no softening whatsoever. It left Xie Jingyu with nowhere to look.

He was twenty-eight years old, several years older than Yun Ze. And yet he had been dressed down in a way he could not begin to argue against.

"Of course, I can understand you." Yun Ze's tone shifted slightly, cooling further. "At the time, your promotion was imminent; you could not permit something so trivial to take up your time. And besides, you already had three children; a little indifference toward two who had died is not without reason."

Words that sounded like understanding, but struck right at the heart of things. Xie Jingyu opened his mouth with difficulty. "Elder Brother, I..."

"That is enough. Say no more." Yun Ze released the full weight of his presence. "The children your family did not treasure, the Yun family will cherish in their place. These two children will be laid to rest in the Yun family's burial ground. We will not trouble Magistrate Xie to concern himself any further."

The dozen or so attendants he had brought moved forward and edged out Xie Jingyu's four men.

Xie Jingyu's expression was very ugly, but no one there cared.

The Yun family's attendants worked with careful hands, slowly opening the earth, and before long two small sets of infant remains came into view, tiny as a pair of palms.

Yun Chu's tears broke free all at once, beyond all possibility of holding back.

Her knees gave way and her body began to slide downward.

"Chu'er, you are their mother. To kneel before them would bring misfortune to their next life." Yun Ze caught her and pulled her back up. "Ting Shuang, hold your mistress."

In his heart, Chu'er would always be their Yun family's precious little miss.

This sister of his, who should have lived a life of happiness and ease, why had she been made to suffer such loss?

Yun Ze's heart was as though cut by a blade.

Yun Chu wept until she could barely breathe.

She held onto Ting Shuang's hand and made her way, one small step at a time, to the edge of the small hollow.

She crouched down. With her own hands she gathered those tiny bones. With her own hands she laid her children to rest in their new coffins.

Her hands shook the whole time. The tears did not stop. Her legs stayed barely able to hold her.

When the children had been buried, with her own hands, in the grounds beside the Yun family's ancestral plot, Yun Chu lost consciousness and knew nothing more.

chapters.title: Madam Xie Has Fallen Ill
chapters.content:
Yun Chu fell ill after returning to the Xie household.

The illness came on with the force of a mountain falling. Every part of her body ached, and her sleep was fitful.

The morning callers waited in the outer reception room. Ting Shuang came out and said quietly, "Madam is ill. There is no need to come for morning calls for the time being."

Everyone understood: this time, Madam was truly ill. Multiple physicians had already been called in, and the smell of medicine hung throughout the courtyard.

Concubine Jiang's face was full of worry. "The residence is in such a state of disorder; would it not be better for me to stay and tend to Madam?"

Ting Shuang shook her head. "We are several servants to care for Madam already. There is no need to trouble Concubine Jiang. Everyone may go."

Xie Ping rose. "Mother is ill, and I would not normally wish to bother her with small matters, but I truly do not know how to proceed. Could Sister Ting Shuang help settle things?"

"The eldest young miss is asking about the old madam's birthday, I expect." Ting Shuang replied. "Madam has already instructed that if the eldest young miss is uncertain about something, she may consult the Madam and the old madam."

Xie Ping pressed her lips together.

She simply could not understand it. These were two children who had been dead for four years. Why had Mother suddenly begun to grieve so?

For the sake of those two dead children, she had slapped Father without a second thought, and now she was pleading illness to leave all the household business alone. Did she truly intend to drive a final wedge between herself and Father?

Was Mother not afraid of losing her authority as the mistress of this house?

After leaving Sheng Residence, Xie Ping took her account books and lists to the Hall of Longevity.

The old madam and Yuan Shi were in the middle of a conversation.

"Those two children may have died young, but they are still of Xie blood. How can they be buried beside the Yun family's ancestral ground?" The old madam spoke through gritted teeth. "Yun Chu has long since ceased to be a Yun woman; she is the Xie family's principal wife. How dare she bring such humiliation upon the Xie name?"

Yuan Shi let out a sigh. "If we look at it carefully, it really is the Xie family that was in the wrong."

The children's remains should have been brought back to the Xie ancestral home in Jizhou and buried beside the Xie family's shrine. But, as it was, Jingyu had simply not taken those two children seriously enough, and one could understand why the Yun family had made such a fuss.

"Jingyu was due to be promoted to the upper fifth rank, and now because of all this, he has become a target for censure at court," the old madam said, her anger sharp. "If Yun Chu had not suddenly taken it into her head to have the children re-buried, the Xie family would not have been dragged into all of this. Now she is hiding behind illness and refusing to deal with anything, perfectly comfortable, while Jingyu struggles at court with his hands tied. And it is all because of her."

Yuan Shi did not know what to say.

Just then, Xie Ping stepped in, greeted both elders, and said, "The old madam's birthday is nearly upon us. There are two things I have not yet been able to decide, and I had planned to ask Mother, but Mother is ill and cannot get out of bed. I can only trouble the old madam and grandmother instead."

The old madam's expression was not good.

The Xie household was growing larger and its affairs more numerous. With Yun Chu refusing to manage even something as important as the birthday celebration, and leaving it all in the hands of an unmarried girl, she was making it plain, the old madam thought, that she believed the household could not function without its mistress, a form of deliberate retaliation for the Xie family's failure to properly bury those children four years ago.

She should never have taken out twenty thousand taels to keep Yun Chu managing the household the last time; now Yun Chu believed she had the entire Xie family in her grip.

A cold smile crossed the old madam's face. "Ping'er, what two things have not been settled? Tell me and we will think it through together."

Xie Ping said, "One is the guest list, and the other is the menu. My thinking is this..."

She laid out her ideas carefully.

She still wanted to invite some prominent figures. Whether they came or not was their own business; the invitations ought to go out, on the chance that someone might be willing to come and give their support.

The old madam shook her head. "Because of what happened the other day, the Xie family is the talk of the capital. Who would be willing to come and celebrate?"

Xie Ping dared say no more, and moved to the second matter. "I would like to make the birthday banquet a generous one, but a spread of a dozen or more tables would cost at least two thousand taels, and that kind of money is not in the household accounts."

The old madam did not hesitate. A birthday came only once a year; naturally it should be done properly.

The past three years' celebrations had been particularly lavish, and it was to be supposed that Yun Chu had supplemented the costs from her own dowry.

This year, with Yun Chu pleading illness and refusing to involve herself, if the banquet was poorly done, the first to laugh at the Xie family would certainly be the Yun family.

She turned to Matron Zhou at her side. "Bring three thousand taels for Ping'er."

Xie Ping's face broke into a smile. "Thank you, old madam. I will make this a banquet worthy of your name."

If she managed the birthday banquet well, word of her household ability would spread, and families seeking a match would be lining up at the Xie family's door.

With the money secured, things moved much more smoothly for Xie Ping. She threw herself into preparations for the banquet.

After three days of rest, Yun Chu's body began to recover, though her spirits were still low. She spent her days sitting by the window reading, which left her three maidservants sick with worry.

"Madam." Qiu Tong summoned her courage and stepped inside, bowing her head. "You have rested three days. Now that Madam is better, the training cannot be put off any longer."

Yun Chu set down her book. "Look at me, how could I forget something so important? Come. Let us go and train."

She changed into a practical set of clothes and followed Qiu Tong out to the courtyard to hold the horse stance.

It was spring, with a nip still in the air, but after holding the stance in the courtyard for a good half-hour she was damp all over with a fine sweat.

"Madam, time is up." Qiu Tong said.

Yun Chu did not move. "I can keep going a little longer."

She had let three or four days go to waste; she meant to make up for it all.

At first she held her form steadily, but gradually her strength began to flag, and her body swayed now and then.

Ting Shuang came over several times to persuade her, and each time she was refused. She was determined to hold the full two hours.

After midday, Yun Chu finally rested. Ting Shuang drew her a bath, helped her change, and at last some color came back into her face.

"Madam, the old madam's birthday banquet is only a few days away." Ting Shuang said, drying her hair as she spoke. "This year the banquet is entirely in the eldest young miss's hands. I have made a few small inquiries, and already I can see a good number of problems. Madam really ought to give the eldest young miss a few pointers, or there is likely to be trouble on the day."

Yun Chu looked at herself in the mirror. "Let word go out that Madam Xie is ill, bedridden and unable to rise."

Ting Shuang said quickly, "Madam, you must not speak such things about yourself."

"If saying something were all it took to make it come true, would the world not be in a terrible state?" Yun Chu's face held the faint trace of a smile. "If I am said to be ill, then whatever goes wrong with this banquet has nothing to do with me. Do you understand?"

Ting Shuang's eyes brightened. "This servant understands."

She finished drying Yun Chu's hair, then hurried out to the back courtyard and had a word with Chen Defu.

Word that the daughter of the General's household, Madam Xie of the Ministry of Revenue's Bureau of Affairs, had fallen ill spread through the capital in no time.

"A few days ago that Madam Xie moved her children's coffins all the way from the south of the city to the west for proper reburial. You all heard about that, did you not?"

"The Xie family really are something contemptible. Those children were legitimate blood, and yet they were buried just anywhere on some hillside. Don't they fear retribution?"

"Such a fine daughter of the General's household, married off to that Xie Jingyu when he was nothing but a seventh-rank official. One truly cannot understand what the Yun family was thinking in choosing such a match."

"......"

"I heard from the medicine hall at Shandetan that the Xie inner household is a hotbed of discord, concubines poisoning each other to cause miscarriages. Those two children who died in infancy might well have been poisoned too, for all we know."

"From what people at the Xie household say, Madam Xie is gravely ill, unable even to manage the old madam's birthday banquet, and it seems she cannot get out of bed. One wonders if a concubine has been poisoning her."

"The mistress of the household cannot produce children, while every concubine has given birth to sons. The concubines are probably getting ideas, thinking that once the mistress dies, one of them will be promoted to principal wife."

"If Magistrate Xie cannot even manage the women of his own inner household, what does that say about his abilities as an official?"

chapters.title: A Thief in the Bedchamber
chapters.content:
The gossip circulating through the streets and lanes found its way back to the Xie household, and the old matriarch was so furious she smashed two teacups.

A family of their modest standing, the Xie clan, would not ordinarily let even the death of its mistress become public knowledge. But Yun Chu's identity was far too singular. She was the eldest legitimate daughter of a first-rank general's household, a celebrated jewel of the capital in her day. As many families had once nearly worn down the threshold of the Yun residence in hopes of securing a match, that many pairs of eyes now kept watch over the Xie family's inner court.

"She has plainly recovered. Who spread the word that she was dying?" the old matriarch said in a low, stern voice. "The servants in this household grow less and less capable of holding their tongues."

There was also the matter from before, when the He woman had poisoned Concubine Tao. No one knew who had let that slip either.

With both incidents spreading freely together, it gave the impression that the Xie inner court was an unusually disorderly place.

As the old saying goes: a man who cannot keep his own house cannot govern the realm. Would the court see fit to promote a man who cannot even manage the women of his own household?

Mama Zhou hesitated before saying, "Since the mistress fell ill, the eldest young miss has been the one making decisions, large and small. Things have indeed become rather muddled."

"Does the Xie family fall apart the moment it lacks a mistress to manage affairs?" the old matriarch said coldly. "Mama Zhou, go and call Ping'er to me. I shall personally attend to every matter of the birthday banquet, large and small. We cannot leave anyone grounds for gossip."

Mama Zhou received the order and went to see it done.

The past few days had brought clear skies, and the flowers in Sheng Residence were in bloom. Yun Chu sat in the receiving room reading a book.

Ting Shuang came to report: "When the eldest young miss first began assisting the mistress with household management, she had a number of older servants dismissed. Those servants resent her greatly. Whatever the eldest young miss assigns them, they carry out only seven parts in ten. The household is in a state of disorder. However, this servant has heard that the old matriarch intends to personally oversee the birthday banquet herself."

Yun Chu smiled faintly.

The banquet was only three days away. All the necessary preparations had already been made in full. Even if the old matriarch took charge now, it would change very little.

"Chen Bo has handed the management of four or five of the Xie family's shops over to He Xu," Ting Shuang continued. "The eldest young miss had He Xu handle all the purchasing for the birthday banquet. That He Xu truly has no fear, this servant did a rough calculation and found he has pocketed at least four hundred taels."

Even Yun Chu could not help but click her tongue. The old matriarch had only allocated three thousand taels for the banquet, and He Xu had swallowed four hundred of them. There were surely other servants who had helped themselves as well, this one taking thirty or forty taels, that one pocketing seventeen or eighteen. By the time it all tallied up, two thousand taels spent on the actual banquet would be considered a decent outcome.

"He Xu has been sending a good portion of what he embezzled to the one in the little temple," Ting Shuang murmured. "The He woman has injuries on her, and she has been considerably more obedient of late."

Yun Chu's smile deepened: "Then let her rest comfortably for a few days."

In a few more days, the He woman would not have such peaceful days to enjoy.

Ting Shuang already knew what Yun Chu intended to do. A shadow of worry settled over her brow: "Mistress, are you truly certain you want to go through with this?"

Yun Chu reached out and took Ting Shuang's hand: "I have been in the Xie household for five years now. Have you ever truly seen me happy?"

Ting Shuang shook her head.

In the first month after the mistress's arrival, she had been full of hope and longing. Then the master grew cold toward her, and later the child died. From that point on, the mistress had never again smiled from the heart.

All these years, the mistress's life had passed day after day in apparent calm, yet with no trace of any hope visible on the horizon.

In recent times, she had finally begun to see a different light in the mistress's eyes.

She worried for the mistress.

She feared something would happen that would make the mistress's days even harder to bear.

"Ting Shuang, you and I are the same age. You ought to be married by now," Yun Chu said, looking at her gently. "If there is someone you have feelings for, just tell me. If there is no one who has caught your heart, I will find a steady and honest man for you."

"Mistress!" Ting Shuang was so startled she dropped to her knees. "This servant will not marry. This servant will spend her whole life by your side serving you."

Yun Chu pulled her back to her feet.

Whether or not Ting Shuang ever married, she could not leave Ting Shuang in the Xie household any longer.

Having been given a second life, no one could say whether the old tragedy would repeat itself. She was afraid that Ting Shuang would once again perish in the great fire that had consumed the Xie household.

The sky gradually darkened, and the maidservants brought in the evening meal.

Though Yun Chu was no longer managing household affairs at present, she was still the official mistress of the house, and neither Xie Ping nor the older servants below dared to skimp on her food.

She had barely begun eating when a commotion arose from the front courtyard. Ting Feng came running inside to report: "Mistress, something is wrong! A thief has suddenly appeared at the small gate on the southeast side. All the manservants and older servants in the household have gone to catch him."

Yun Chu's brow drew together.

In four or five years of managing this household, all the gates of the Xie residence had been well guarded. Nothing so absurd as this had ever occurred.

She gave her instructions: "Keep the gates of Sheng Residence tightly secured. Unless something urgent arises, no one is to go out."

By now the sky had gone completely dark, and the matter of the thief at the front courtyard had set a number of hearts on edge.

But Qiu Tong was in Sheng Residence, and all the maidservants in the courtyard had witnessed her skills firsthand. With Qiu Tong standing at the gate, everyone felt considerably more at ease.

After a long wait, word came from the front courtyard: no thief had been found, and nothing unusual had appeared in any of the other courtyards. The whole thing was written off as a misunderstanding. Even so, Yun Chu did not let her guard down. She had the servants move in groups of three, with Qiu Tong leading, to patrol the courtyard throughout the night.

After her bath, Yun Chu entered the inner chamber and seated herself before the dressing table.

Ting Xue carefully removed her hair ornaments and combed out her hair, then stepped back with a bow, quietly pulling the door shut behind her.

Yun Chu sat on the edge of the bed, slipped off her shoes, and lay down. She reached for the quilt at her side and was just about to draw it over herself when she suddenly sensed that something was wrong.

She held her breath and listened. She heard shallow breathing that was not her own.

In that instant, her heart leapt into her throat.

She rose carefully and slid her hand beneath the pillow, feeling around until her fingers closed around a short blade.

This was the coming-of-age gift her grandfather had given her. Her name was engraved upon it, and its edge was honed to an extreme sharpness. She gripped the hilt in one hand, then wrenched the quilt aside with the other.

In the very instant the blade swept forward, her hand froze.

"Why is it you?"

Beneath the quilt was a child of porcelain-smooth beauty.

It was the little young lord of the Prince of Pingxi's household.

"You woman, how dare you point a blade at me! If so much as a single hair on my head is harmed, my royal father will not let you go!"

Yun Chu gave a faint pull of the corners of her lips.

She sheathed the blade and replied: "If your royal father knew you had sneaked into someone's bedchamber in the middle of the night, he probably would not let you go either."

Chu Hongyu gave a huff: "If I hadn't heard you were dying, I wouldn't have come at all. A perfectly good gesture, thrown away on an ingrate."

The little one crossed his arms over his chest and turned his back to her, leaving Yun Chu with only a view of one puffed-up cheek.

Yun Chu's heart softened at once.

So this child had heard she was ill and taken such a great risk to sneak into the Xie household on her behalf.

When she counted up their acquaintance, it was not particularly deep, yet the child had kept her so steadily in mind. She supposed that was her good fortune.

Perhaps it was the dream she had had that day, where her own son's face had shifted into the little young lord's face, that had caused her to feel an instinctive warmth toward this child.

She could not help reaching out a finger and poking him gently on the cheek.

In the ordinary way of things, Chu Hongyu despised having anyone pinch his cheeks. Even the imperial grandfather made him uncomfortable when he did it.

But now, he felt no aversion whatsoever. In fact, some part of him hoped the woman would poke him again.

Yun Chu knew when enough was enough. She poked him once and withdrew her hand: "My illness has already passed. As you can see, nothing is wrong with me. Let me have someone see you back to the prince's residence."

The little one's eyes went wide.

He had only just arrived, and this woman wanted to send him away. How thoroughly heartless.

He was about to speak when footsteps suddenly sounded outside the door.

chapters.title: I'll Let You Stay the Night
chapters.content:
"Master."

The maidservants of Sheng Residence dropped into curtsies one after another.

Xie Jingyu looked worn through with exhaustion.

That day in court, he had been impeached by a censor. He had been on the verge of a promotion to the upper fifth rank, but now that prospect was entirely gone.

If the rumors circulating through the streets continued to worsen, he feared he might even be demoted.

He had always had the Yun family connection quietly standing behind him, but this time the Yun family showed no regard for the Xie household's face at all, and he had no one to speak for him in court.

He left the court in low spirits and called again at the Yu residence, but this time Lord Yu would not even admit him through the door. He waited on the Yu family's doorstep for several hours until he finally accepted that Lord Yu had given up on him entirely, then made his way back to the Xie residence like a stray dog that had lost its home.

He stood at the entrance to Sheng Residence and looked toward Ting Shuang: "Has your mistress's illness improved?"

Ting Shuang lowered her gaze and said, "The mistress appears to have recovered, but in truth it is an ailment of the heart. She lacks the spirit to apply herself to anything."

Xie Jingyu removed his official cap.

It was not as if he did not know that Yun Chu's illness was one of the heart.

But the child was dead and had been properly buried. What was past should be allowed to pass. What was the use of clinging to it.

When she fell ill, the entire Xie household was thrown into unrest.

He had never known until now that the mistress of a house could exert such influence over a family.

He said, "Has the mistress retired for the night?"

"The mistress went to sleep a quarter of an hour ago," Ting Shuang replied. "If the master has something to attend to, you are welcome to come earlier tomorrow."

Xie Jingyu said nothing more. He turned and left.

As he walked out of Sheng Residence, he came upon Xie Shi'an on the narrow path ahead.

It was plain that Xie Shi'an had been waiting for him. The young man folded his hands in salute: "Father, the rumors from the city have reached the academy. They have most certainly reached the court as well. Were you impeached today by someone with ulterior motives?"

Xie Jingyu looked at his eldest son with a face full of admiration.

This son, who did nothing but travel between the Xie family's private academy and home, had nonetheless managed to deduce the situation at court. He was truly gifted beyond the ordinary.

"What are your thoughts?" he asked.

"There are two things that others are mainly talking about," Xie Shi'an said evenly. "First is the burial four years ago of the twin children of the Xie household. That matter is already settled, and the Xie family can only maintain silence. Second, the story of Mother's illness has been exaggerated more and more with each telling. With the old matriarch's birthday banquet coming very soon, if Mother attends, the rumors about unrest in the Xie family's inner court will collapse of their own accord."

Xie Jingyu nodded: "And do you believe your mother will attend the banquet?"

Xie Shi'an fell silent.

His mother had just suffered a tremendous blow. Whether she would cooperate in clearing the Xie family's name in the eyes of the public was something he could not say with certainty.

Xie Jingyu let out a slow breath: "Uncertain or not, we must try."

Father and son continued to talk as they walked away, their voices gradually receding into the distance.

Only once the sound of their voices had faded completely did Yun Chu release a quiet breath.

She glanced at the child nestled in the quilt: "Come, let me see you out of the residence first."

"I won't go!"

Chu Hongyu suddenly threw his arms around her waist, resting his head against her chest, every inch the picture of willful stubbornness.

Yun Chu reasoned with him gently: "Little young lord, you are not home at this late hour, and someone will discover it before long. Can you withstand the wrath of the Prince of Pingxi?"

She expected the child to be frightened. Instead, the little one lifted his chin in smug satisfaction: "This evening, my royal father was commanded by imperial decree to go suppress bandits. He will not be in the capital for the next few days. I also found a child the same age as me to impersonate me and remain in the prince's residence. Rest assured, no one will discover that I am gone."

Yun Chu stared at him, entirely at a loss for words.

At that moment, the window was given a soft, quiet knock.

Before Yun Chu had even risen to see what was happening, a cry of alarm came from outside the window.

"What sort of thief dares to lurk outside our mistress's window!"

That was Qiu Tong's voice.

Yun Chu glanced at the little one on the bed, and saw him scrambling frantically toward the edge in a rush to push the window open.

She caught him up in one arm, tossed him behind the bed curtains, and called out clearly: "Qiu Tong, bind the thief outside and send him to the authorities."

"No, you cannot!" Chu Hongyu broke into a frantic sweat. "He is not a thief. He is my guard. His name is A-Mao. Please do not send him to the authorities."

Yun Chu put on a deliberately stern face: "The thief who appeared at the Xie family's southeast gate just now was also your guard, I take it?"

The little one's face fell: "The Xie family gate always has people patrolling back and forth. I truly had no other option, so I had A-Mao pose as a thief to draw them away. A-Mao really has done nothing wrong."

When he made that face, Yun Chu's heart went soft.

She looked toward the window: "Qiu Tong, bring the one outside in."

She climbed out of bed and put on her shoes and outer robe, then took the little one by the hand and led him out of the inner chamber together.

Qiu Tong and Ting Shuang brought the guard inside together. The sight of a child suddenly materializing in the room made both women nearly drop their eyes from their heads.

Especially Qiu Tong, who knew martial arts. She had been inside the compound the whole time, yet had not detected a single soul inside the mistress's bedchamber.

Yun Chu made a gesture, and Ting Shuang immediately went to close the door.

"Mmm, mmm, mmm!"

The guard's mouth was stuffed with something, and he kept making muffled sounds.

Chu Hongyu rushed over to him and yanked out the dirty cloth: "A-Mao, are you all right?"

"This subordinate is fine," A-Mao said, looking his young master up and down with lingering fright. "Little young lord, are you unharmed?"

Qiu Tong was utterly bewildered: "Mistress, what is the meaning of all this?"

Ting Shuang had already recognized the child and was just as stunned: "Why is the little young lord of the Prince of Pingxi's household in the mistress's bedchamber?"

"Take advantage of the darkness and the commotion in the household," Yun Chu said. "Qiu Tong, see these two out. Do not let anyone see them."

If Xie Jingyu found out that the little young lord of the Prince of Pingxi had come to the Xie household, he would surely find ways to use this child to get close to the prince. She had no wish to see a child become a tool in Xie Jingyu's climb to power.

"I said I won't go, I won't go!" Chu Hongyu scrambled with all four limbs and climbed up onto Yun Chu, clinging to her. "I'm staying here. I won't go, I simply won't!"

Qiu Tong stepped forward, seized the child by the back of his collar, and hoisted him into the air: "Little young lord, young as you may be, you are still an outside male. It is improper for you to remain in our mistress's quarters. This servant will see you back to the prince's residence."

"Wuwuwu, I won't go!" The little one kicked his legs wildly in the air. "I went to so much trouble sneaking out of the prince's residence, and so much trouble getting into the Xie household, and you're going to send me away this fast? I never want to like you again, you're terrible, wuwuwu..."

A-Mao chimed in on his behalf: "In the days since the little young lord heard that the Xie mistress was ill, he has not been eating or sleeping well. He has lost several jin. He only managed to wait until the prince had left the residence, and then finally found his chance to slip away. Our little young lord has had no mother's love since he was small, so the Xie mistress might take pity and spare a thought for him..."

Yun Chu felt something press tight in her chest.

She reached out and took the child who was still kicking in the air into her arms.

She knew the little young lord of the Prince of Pingxi was four years old. But compared to Xie Shi'yun, who was the same age, he was far too thin, more like a child of three.

She said softly, "Then I will allow you to stay the night here. The moment dawn breaks you must leave. Is that all right?"

The little one went from tears to smiles in an instant and buried himself in her embrace.

chapters.title: I Like You So Much
chapters.content:
The night was hushed and deep.

Chu Hongyu was too excited to sleep. He wound his hands and feet around Yun Chu.

Yun Chu could have had two heads and still felt the headache. She had raised Xie Shi'yun with her own hands from infancy, yet Xie Shi'yun had never dared to be so unruly.

"Don't keep your eyes closed. Let's talk."

The little one lay sprawled over her and forcibly pried her eyelids open with his fingers.

"Little young lord, do you know what hour it is?" Yun Chu said wearily. "Children who sleep early grow tall. Come now, sleep."

"My name is Chu Hongyu. Call me Yu-ge'er, it's more familiar." The little one wrapped his arms around her neck and said softly, "And what shall I call you?"

Yun Chu truly had no idea what to do with him: "Call me Yiyi."

"No, Yiyi sounds too distant." Chu Hongyu tilted his head and thought for quite a while. "Can I call you Nianqin?"

Yun Chu was genuinely taken aback: "Yu-ge'er, you must not go saying things like that again. If anyone were to hear it, it is I who would be in trouble."

The little one hurried to explain: "I know you are already married, so you cannot truly be my mother. That is why Nianqin would be different, and since no one else would be around when I say it, it would not get you in trouble, would it?"

"You..."

The words of refusal were right there on the tip of her tongue, yet Yun Chu found she could not bring herself to say them.

Her heart had grown so soft it had no edge left to it. She had meant to stay cold and distant, hoping the child would leave sooner, but now she found her emotions slipping from her grip, and she reached out and drew the child into her arms.

"Mmm, you smell so nice," Chu Hongyu said, closing his eyes. "The same scent as the Nianqin in my dreams. I really do like you so much..."

The child murmured on and within moments had drifted into sleep.

Yun Chu gently stroked his head.

This child, who had the very same face as the child from her dreams, had found his way into her heart long before she had realized it.

How she wished the child were still alive, how she wished the child could lie here sleeping by her side. But all of it could only ever remain a longing that would never be fulfilled.

Yun Chu drifted slowly off to sleep.

The following morning, she was woken by an itch at the tip of her nose. She sneezed and opened her eyes at once.

There was the little one, holding a piece of thread and deliberately tickling the tip of her nose. Seeing her sneeze, he broke into a triumphant grin.

"Nianqin, you're awake! Good morning."

A single nianqin, and she found she could not summon any resistance toward him at all.

She picked the child up in her arms: "Yu-ge'er, get dressed. We will have breakfast first."

Chu Hongyu let her very obediently help him into his clothes, then took her hand like a good boy and followed her to the side room.

Because she had been ill, anyone coming to pay their morning respects was turned back at the courtyard gate by Ting Shuang. The other maidservants in the courtyard were each occupied with their various tasks, and in the side room there were only the most trusted few.

"What does Yu-ge'er like to eat?" Yun Chu smiled gently and asked him. "These lamb's milk steamed buns are quite good. Would you like to try one?"

Chu Hongyu lifted his little chin: "I want you to feed me."

She had expected to refuse, but Yun Chu instead picked up a bun with her chopsticks and held it to his lips. He bit into it. The flavor was much the same as in the prince's residence, yet he could not explain why it tasted so particularly good to him here. He ate one and wanted another, eating seven or eight in a row, each one fed to him by Yun Chu herself.

"Nianqin, you are so wonderful. I like you so much!"

He felt as though he had never known this kind of happiness before. His whole being seemed to be soaking in a jar of honey, like being in a dream.

Yun Chu smiled as she watched him: "Have you had enough?"

Chu Hongyu patted his round little belly: "I have never eaten this much before."

Yun Chu stood up: "Then since you've eaten your fill, it's time to go."

The words hit him like a thunderbolt from a clear sky, leaving Chu Hongyu standing stock-still in stunned disbelief.

This woman had suddenly been so kind to him, and it was all just to make sending him away go smoothly?

As happy as he had been a moment ago, he was now equally miserable.

His eyes blinked once, and tears began to spill down like a stream of golden drops.

Yun Chu kept her heart firm: "The little young lord has spent a night outside. It is time to return."

"Wuwuwa!"

Chu Hongyu suddenly burst into loud wailing, crying until he could barely catch his breath.

Ting Xue spoke up: "Mistress, this servant went out early this morning to make inquiries. The Prince of Pingxi is presently several dozen li outside the city, still on the mountain suppressing the bandits. He will not be returning to the capital for some time yet..."

When the third young master had once been kept at the mistress's side, she had been the maidservant chiefly responsible for caring for him. She understood well the nature of children this young. And she could clearly see that this little young lord genuinely liked their mistress.

The mistress had suffered so much. Having someone who truly liked her lingering nearby was not a bad thing.

She hoped the little young lord might bring the mistress a little closer to stepping out of the darkness.

Ting Shuang also said softly, "The Prince of Pingxi's residence is presently undisturbed, which means no one yet knows the little young lord has gone missing. There is no need for the mistress to worry."

Yun Chu let out a quiet sigh.

She suddenly felt a pang of tenderness for this child.

He was only four years old. He had spent an entire night away from home, and in that vast prince's residence, not a single person had noticed.

If this child had a mother, would his disappearance have gone undetected?

Ting Feng came in to report: "Mistress, the master has arrived."

Yun Chu glanced at the hour. It was about the time that morning court would have just concluded. In the past, after court, Xie Jingyu would attend to his official duties, and when those were done, he would spend time socializing with his colleagues, generally not returning until after dark. Now, with neither official duties nor social engagements remaining to him, she could roughly guess why he had come to Sheng Residence at this hour.

She reached out and wiped Chu Hongyu's tears clean, then said, "If you wish to stay with me here, you must behave and listen carefully. You must not let anyone other than those already here discover your presence. Can you manage that?"

Disbelief crept into Chu Hongyu's eyes: "Nianqin, you are really not going to send me away anymore?"

"You may stay temporarily," Yun Chu said, ruffling his hair. "Be good, and do not make a sound."

She rose and walked out of the side room.

She stood on the stone steps and saw Xie Jingyu under the covered corridor.

At twenty-eight, Xie Jingyu still carried himself like a graceful young man, enough to draw the eyes of every maidservant.

In her previous life, she had willingly raised so many concubines' children. In truth, she had perhaps also held some small hope that one day Xie Jingyu might look at her.

Now, having been reborn, she felt nothing for this man but a thorough and settled contempt.

"Why has the master returned home so early today?"

Her voice was detached, the question asked out of form.

Xie Jingyu looked at her with evident concern: "Are you feeling better?"

Yun Chu gave a small nod: "Fine, thank you."

Seeing she was unwilling to say more, Xie Jingyu did not press her. He paused, then said, "The old matriarch's birthday is in two days. Will you be able to attend, madam?"

"My appetite has not been well these past few days, and I fear I might dampen the guests' mood if I attend the banquet. However," she said, pivoting smoothly, "the Xie family did not manage a flower-viewing banquet this year, so this birthday banquet is the one occasion when everyone can gather and make merry. I ought naturally to come out and greet the guests. Do not worry, husband."

Xie Jingyu let out a breath of relief.

He had expected to have to spend considerable effort persuading her. He had not imagined Yun Chu would agree so readily.

He had misjudged her.

He was just about to say something further when Ting Yu walked into the courtyard carrying a bowl of soup: "The mistress has not recovered from her long illness, and this concubine specially made a restorative broth to bring over. I did not expect the master to be here as well."

Xie Jingyu's expression remained cool: "Take good care of your mistress."

With that, he turned and left Sheng Residence.

Watching his retreating figure, Ting Yu's face was entirely composed of disappointment. She had so rarely managed to encounter the master, and still she could hardly get a word in.

Yun Chu had been on the verge of going back into the side room when she saw Ting Yu approach her carrying the bowl of broth.

chapters.title: I'm Very Jealous of Him
chapters.content:
Yun Chu looked at Ting Yu with a complicated expression.

Ting Yu and Ting Shuang had been born in the same year and were both twenty this year. Ting Yu was already the mother of a four-year-old child.

From as far back as she could remember, Ting Yu and Ting Shuang had both been at her side serving her. Ting Shuang was steady and composed; Ting Yu was attentive and careful. The two had been like sisters to her.

When she was twelve years old, she had accidentally slipped and fallen into the water. It was Ting Yu who had jumped in and pulled her out, but Ting Yu herself had not made it ashore in time, and had as a result lain unconscious for more than half a month.

Ting Yu had saved her life. That was why, even after Ting Yu had crept into Xie Jingyu's bed behind her back, she had never truly blamed Ting Yu.

It was only later, when the Yun family fell, that Ting Yu chose to take the Xie family's side, and it was Ting Yu who had commanded Xie Shi'yun to carry that cup of poison to her.

The things of her previous life were not something she could let go of.

Ting Yu had saved her, but Ting Yu had also betrayed her. The two canceled each other out. And so her treatment of Ting Yu was cold and distant, nothing more.

Yet Ting Yu came to find her again and again.

A person with greed in their heart would eventually come undone by that very greed.

"Mother!"

Just as she was thinking all this through, Xie Shi'yun came running and flung himself into her arms.

This child had been brought to her side from the moment he was born. Apart from being nursed by Ting Yu, he had grown up entirely by her side for all other hours.

It was only when Yun'er had turned three that he moved out of her chamber and went to live with Ting Yu in the side courtyard.

"Mother, it has been so long since I shared a meal with you. It has been so long since I have seen you." Xie Shi'yun pressed his lips together in a pout. "Does Mother not like me anymore?"

Yun Chu's smile did not reach her eyes: "Yun'er is older now and must learn to observe proper conduct."

Ting Yu immediately drew her son back toward herself: "This concubine will be sure to discipline Yun'er properly from now on. Please, madam, drink the broth while it is still hot."

"The Yin concubine is now half a mistress of this household. There is no need to keep making the trip to the kitchens for these kinds of rough tasks," Yun Chu said coolly. "I am tired. You may all withdraw."

Ting Yu nodded and left with Xie Shi'yun.

"Yiniang, why is it that Mother no longer pays attention to me?" Xie Shi'yun was miserable. "It wasn't like this before..."

Ting Yu did not understand it either. Formerly the mistress had poured her whole heart into Yun'er, and now she would not spare even an extra word for him. What had gone wrong?

Yun Chu went into the side room. The moment the door was shut, Chu Hongyu shot over from the corner and wrapped himself around her.

The little one tilted his head back and asked, "That small child just now called you Mother. Is he a child you gave birth to?"

Yun Chu laughed: "Why do you ask?"

"I'm jealous of him," Chu Hongyu said, biting down on his lower lip. "Jealous that he can openly call you Mother. Jealous that he gets to see you every single day. I want to become him."

Yun Chu said softly, "You are yourself. You do not need to become anyone else."

"If not for my little sister still being at home, I would truly never want to go back," Chu Hongyu said, his large dark eyes wide and intent. "Nianqin, my little sister is very pretty and very lovely. She just cannot speak. Would you like a child who cannot speak?"

Yun Chu was somewhat surprised.

All of the capital knew that the Prince of Pingxi had recently gained a son and daughter, but she had never heard anyone mention that the prince's little commandery princess was mute.

Her voice grew gentler: "If she is as well-behaved and sensible as you, then of course I would like her."

Being praised for being well-behaved and sensible, Chu Hongyu grinned so broadly his mouth hardly seemed willing to close.

Just then, Ting Shuang came in to report on several matters, and the little one, very sensibly, said: "I'll go sit over there and read. I won't disturb Nianqin while she handles things."

He walked over to the low table by the side of the room, produced a book from somewhere, and began reading with great concentration, his short little legs dangling in the air, unable to reach the floor.

A smile rose to Yun Chu's face, one she herself had not noticed.

She turned her head and said softly, "Arrange for someone to keep watch at the Prince of Pingxi's residence. The moment there is any sign of movement, come back and report immediately."

Ting Feng received the order and went to make the arrangements at the front courtyard.

Ting Shuang took out the account books and went through last month's income from the outside shops and manors in careful detail.

Listening to the figures, Yun Chu's brow slowly drew together.

It was exactly as it had been in her previous life. The manors she owned outside the city were declining more and more with each passing year, on a downward slope that eventually led to selling them all off.

She would have to think carefully about this. Besides ice, what other kind of business might be worth pursuing?

While she and Ting Shuang were speaking, Chu Hongyu grew increasingly bored. He had no fondness for books, and sitting quietly for a quarter of an hour was already remarkable. The greater problem was that there were far too many characters in the book he did not recognize, and what he could not read he also could not understand. Keeping up appearances was genuinely exhausting.

"Nianqin, I need to use the privy."

The little one jumped down from the couch, and Ting Xue went to take his hand and lead him toward the rear privy.

Because there was now a small child in Sheng Residence, Ting Shuang had sent all the older serving women and maidservants out to busy themselves with preparations for the birthday banquet, leaving the whole courtyard with only the maidservants who had come from the Yun family.

Chu Hongyu used the privy, and then noticed a trail of ants on the windowsill. He followed the ants with great curiosity as they led him to the other side.

He was not sure where he had wandered to when he suddenly saw a group of people appear ahead of him, and he remembered Yun Chu's words just in time, ducking into the shrubbery at his side.

The people ahead were the old matriarch and Lady Yuan, who were strolling through the courtyard to admire the flowers.

"With you keeping watch personally, old matriarch, every preparation for the birthday banquet is in order. Nothing will go wrong," Lady Yuan said with a smile. "Jingyu has said that Chu'er will attend the banquet as well to help receive the guests, and once she does, the rumors circulating through the streets will dissolve on their own. There is no need for you to worry any further."

The old matriarch said coldly, "What? She, a junior, attends a senior's birthday banquet, and it is supposed to be some kind of favor? Am I meant to be grateful to her for it?"

Lady Yuan did not know what to say. The old matriarch had once been quite fond of Chu'er, but after these successive incidents, she had grown prejudiced against the girl, and nothing anyone said seemed to make any difference.

"She has not produced a single child for our Xie family. Childlessness is the foremost of the seven grounds for dismissal. Failure to respect elders is the second. Feigning illness and neglecting household duties is the third. Striking her husband is the fourth. Seven grounds, and she has already violated four. Can you tell me whether our Xie family can still keep her?"

Lady Yuan smiled bitterly to herself. Were they back on the subject of expulsion again.

Chu'er had only been somewhat willful in her behavior of late. Over the past four or five years she had been entirely proper and correct, giving no one any grounds for complaint in any direction. One could not write a person off entirely for a moment of willfulness.

But she knew that speaking up now would only stoke the old matriarch's fury further, so she swallowed all those thoughts back down.

"Her family's rank is a bit higher, but in what other way is she better than our Jingyu?" the old matriarch said bitterly. "Jingyu is learned, talented, and strikingly handsome. There is not a second man in all the capital who compares in both talent and appearance. Being matched with Yun Chu is something Jingyu should feel aggrieved about, and now to have been slapped across the face by her? When the opportunity arises, I will make sure Jingyu gives that slap right back..."

Hidden in the shrubbery, Chu Hongyu clenched his little fists tight.

Nianqin outstripped that fellow called whatever-Xie-whatever-Yu in every single way. This old woman's eyes were clearly clouded with age, to say something so ridiculous.

And she still wanted to hit Nianqin. What sort of daydream was she having.

Chu Hongyu very much wanted to leap out and give the old matriarch a piece of his mind.

But he was afraid that if his presence were discovered, Nianqin would certainly never allow him to come to the Xie household again.

What to do, then?

The little one's eyes darted back and forth, and in a moment a plan had formed.

The old woman wanted to hold a grand birthday celebration, did she? He would make sure she had a birthday she would never forget for the rest of her life.

chapters.title: Nianqin's Secret
chapters.content:
Sheng Residence was very quiet.

Yun Chu had been looking over the account books for a while, but something felt too quiet.

Her brow furrowed: "How long has Yu-ge'er been out?"

Ting Shuang was startled too. She had been so caught up in helping the mistress attend to things that she had only now realized the little young lord had been at the privy for far too long.

Just then, Ting Xue came in, perspiring all over: "Mistress, the little young lord has disappeared. This servant searched all through Sheng Residence and could not find him anywhere..."

Yun Chu's heart lurched. She rose swiftly to her feet, then steadied herself: "Go to the front courtyard first and see if A-Mao is still there."

The child had come in quietly, and perhaps had slipped out just as quietly by the same opportunity.

A-Mao was temporarily lodging in the front courtyard's wing room under the cover of being Ting Shuang's distant cousin. Ting Xue hurried over and came back with a pale face: "A-Mao is still there."

Which meant the little young lord had not left the Xie residence. He had simply gone somewhere unknown.

"It is entirely this servant's fault!" Ting Xue knelt down. "Please punish this servant, mistress."

Ting Shuang spoke up: "This is not the time for punishing anyone. Think carefully and quickly about exactly where and how you lost track of the little young lord."

"When the little young lord was using the privy, I was waiting at the door. After waiting for a long while without him coming out, I looked inside and found the window open. The little young lord must have climbed out through the window," Ting Xue said, on the verge of tears. "The small path outside the window leads to the Xie family's back garden. This servant went quietly to search the area but did not see the little young lord anywhere."

Yun Chu's heart grew heavy. There was a small lake in the back garden, and if the child had fallen in...

The very thought of that possibility sent a sudden rush of breathlessness through her chest.

She steadied herself and spoke: "Ting Shuang, find some reason, any reason, to send everyone in the garden away."

Ting Shuang received the order and went.

Yun Chu took the maidservants and older servants who had accompanied her from her dowry household and went to the garden. The Xie family's inner court was not particularly large, and the garden was smaller still: one manmade lake, one artificial hill, and the flower beds that had formerly been there replaced now entirely with jujube trees. The whole garden could be taken in at a glance, but the lake was thick with water grass and lotus, and what lay beneath the surface was impossible to make out clearly.

Ting Xue was trembling.

If the little young lord had drowned in the lake, her worthless life would not be sufficient recompense, and she would surely implicate the mistress as well...

She gathered her skirts and tied them up, preparing to wade in, when a voice suddenly came from behind her.

"Ting Xue-jiejie, what are you going down into the water for? Are you going to catch fish?"

Yun Chu spun around at once.

She saw Chu Hongyu in his fine brocade clothes, crawling out of the hollow trunk of a large tree. The trunk, for whatever reason, was entirely hollow inside, large enough to conceal one child with ease, which was why they had searched so thoroughly and still failed to find him.

However anxious and frightened Yun Chu had been a moment ago, she was now equally furious.

She pressed down her anger and said, "What were you hiding in there for? Do you have any idea how long we have been looking for you? Do you know how worried we have been?"

"I did not let anyone discover me. I only came out of the tree hollow once I saw that there was no one left in the garden," Chu Hongyu said, tugging at her sleeve and giving it a small shake. "Nianqin, please don't be angry. I know I was wrong. I will never again sneak off somewhere on my own..."

Yun Chu took him by the hand and brought him back to Sheng Residence. She handed off all remaining matters to Ting Shuang and personally sat with the child to read.

"You don't recognize this character? You don't recognize this one either?" Yun Chu's expression began to fracture. "You are four years old. Has your royal father not had you begin your education yet?"

Chu Hongyu made a pained little face: "He has, he has. But I don't understand what the tutor says and can't take it in... Nianqin, you teach me. I know I can learn it from you."

Yun Chu could see perfectly well that this little character had neglected his studies out of a love of play.

But he was only four years old, and with no one in the household to guide and look after him, it was only natural that he would be a bit wayward about such things.

All the same, if he was too fond of play and fell too far behind in his studies, without learning and an understanding of proper conduct, he would suffer greatly for it when he was grown.

"Yu-ge'er, why do we read books? Because books contain many important truths about life, and the more we read, the more of those truths we come to understand," Yun Chu said gently. "Before one can read books, one must know the characters, and learning characters is not actually a tedious or boring matter. Look at this character, chu, the chu in renzhi chu, and also the chu in my own name, written like this..."

She wrapped her hand around the little one's hand and guided him stroke by stroke across the paper.

Chu Hongyu applied himself seriously.

Characters that had seemed so impossibly difficult before, he found that in less than a quarter of an hour of study, he knew them all, and had even learned how to write them.

"Nianqin, you are so amazing!"

Yun Chu smiled: "It is you who are clever. Remember how it feels to learn characters now, and carry that feeling forward."

Chu Hongyu nodded with great enthusiasm.

Watching Yun Chu's warm smile, the little one was suddenly overcome with sadness.

While he had been hiding in that tree hollow, many of the Xie household's servants had passed by the tree in groups, and he had overheard a great many things about Nianqin's secrets.

He learned that Nianqin had once given birth to two children, but that those two children had died the moment they were born, and that Nianqin had fallen ill for a very long, long time because of it.

He learned that Nianqin and that person called whatever-Xie-whatever-Yu had a very poor relationship, and that the man never spent a night in Nianqin's quarters. The Xie household's servants all pitied Nianqin greatly.

He learned that all the children who called Nianqin Mother were not children she had given birth to herself.

He learned that Nianqin's days here were not good at all.

And yet Nianqin's smile was so warm, as though she hadn't a care in the world.

"Mistress, the servant who was sent outside the city to make inquiries has returned," Ting Feng came in to report. "Word is that the Prince of Pingxi has successfully routed the bandits. The prince's men took more than a hundred mountain bandits alive last night. Some fled before being captured, and the prince pursued them to press his advantage. He is expected to return to the capital the day after tomorrow."

"Those bandits are really quite feeble," Chu Hongyu said with a frown. "How did they get captured so easily by my royal father without putting up any resistance at all!"

"Yu-ge'er, it is not that the bandits are feeble. It is that your royal father is exceptionally capable," Yun Chu said, looking at him.
