"Every day those bandits continued to exist was another day that countless common people's lives were under threat. Your royal father subdued the bandits in a single day. That is what it means to have the hearts of the people on your side."

Chu Hongyu nodded with only partial understanding, then pressed his lips together: "Then I have to go back the day after tomorrow."

Yun Chu patted the top of his head: "Your royal father is away suppressing bandits, and you should be here diligently reading. When your royal father returns, recite the Sanzijing for him in its entirety. Your royal father will surely be very pleased."

"Really?" Chu Hongyu's face lit up. "Will he praise me?"

Yun Chu nodded: "I expect so."

The little one took up his book and settled into earnest recitation. When there were characters he did not recognize, he came to ask. When there was a line he could not understand the meaning of, he asked until he understood it and then continued.

Ting Shuang said quietly, "The little young lord is so well-behaved. How is it that the people outside all say he is thoroughly unruly and unmanageable?"

Yun Chu said, "A child is like a blank sheet of paper, and what the adults write upon it is what it becomes. The Prince of Pingxi is a stern man, and there is no princess in the household to offer guidance. It is only natural that the little young lord has become somewhat willful and defiant."

For the better part of the afternoon that followed, Chu Hongyu read diligently.

As evening came, Ting Xue had several servants carry in a large folding screen. The screen was embroidered all over with characters for "longevity" in every style and arrangement imaginable.

"Oh, these characters are really quite ugly," Chu Hongyu looked at it briefly and wrinkled his nose in disdain. "Who sent Nianqin this screen? There's not even a shred of sincerity in it."

Yun Chu let out a laugh: "This is Nianqin's birthday gift to send to someone else."

By now the child was calling her Nianqin at every turn, and Yun Chu had begun naturally referring to herself the same way without quite realizing it.

chapters.title: The Day's Confinement Is Lifted
chapters.content:
The screen before them had been embroidered on Yun Chu's instructions by the most unskilled needlewoman she could find, completed in a single day's work.

It was the birthday gift she intended to present to the old Xie matriarch. All told, it had cost fewer than two taels of silver.

In the past four or five years, she had devoted tremendous thought to the gift each year at the old matriarch's birthday. The first year she presented a coral centerpiece worth eight hundred taels. The second year she personally oversaw the fashioning of a full set of emerald and gold-thread hair ornaments. The third year... in short, each year's birthday gift had cost both time and money in quantity, and looking back on it now, she truly felt it had not been worth a single bit of it.

Look at this screen. Ugly as it was, she needed only to say she had embroidered it herself, and no one would dare say a word against it. They might even commend her for her filial devotion.

Yun Chu had the screen put away, and the maidservants brought out the evening meal one dish at a time.

She had ordered a table of mild and simple dishes that children enjoy, along with a steamed fish. She personally picked out all the bones for Chu Hongyu and placed the flesh in his bowl.

Chu Hongyu stood up on his chair, stretched out his little arms across the table, and ladled a bowl of chicken broth for Yun Chu.

When dinner was finished, the little one picked up his book and continued reading. The Three Character Classic, which he had barely been able to stumble through before, he could now recite haltingly through more than half of it.

Yun Chu left Ting Shuang to stay with the child and look after his reading, while she herself rose and went to the small Xie family shrine.

The shrine housed only one young nun and the He woman. For fear the He woman might come out and cause trouble again, Xie Jingyu had stationed two older serving women at the entrance to keep watch.

Seeing Yun Chu approach, the two women hastened to bow: "Greetings to the mistress."

Yun Chu said coolly, "Has that He woman been obedient and well-behaved these past few days?"

One of the women replied, "She has been lying face-down in her room all day tending to her injuries. Whatever food is sent in comes back out with the bowl wiped clean. She has been keeping herself in order."

Yun Chu gave a small nod and stepped inside. Ting Feng went ahead and pushed open the He woman's door.

The He woman was lying on her stomach, embroidering something. Seeing Yun Chu enter, her expression shifted briefly, then she lowered herself from the bed to pay her respects.

Ting Feng picked up the embroidery and brought it to Yun Chu.

Yun Chu glanced at it and smiled faintly: "Mama He is confined to this place and has still thought to embroider a birthday gift for the old matriarch. It is genuinely admirable to have that kind of heart."

The He woman lowered her eyes: "This hairband will be finished in half a day's more work. When it is, may I ask the mistress to do me the kindness of having someone deliver it to the old matriarch?"

"This is a birthday gift you have embroidered yourself. It is naturally more fitting for you to deliver it in person," Yun Chu said, her voice mild and gentle. "The old matriarch's birthday is a rare occasion for happiness. I will therefore lift your confinement for this one day, but remember: you are not to cause any trouble."

The He woman could hardly believe her ears.

She had gone to such lengths to frame the mistress for poisoning Concubine Tao, and had ended up with confinement as her punishment, and yet the mistress was now voluntarily lifting one day of that confinement?

She did not dare to rejoice too soon. Something told her that whatever was waiting for her was not likely to be good.

Yun Chu dropped those words and walked straight out.

Back at Sheng Residence, Chu Hongyu had already fallen asleep. The little one was still clutching his book, murmuring under his breath, and if you listened closely, he was still reciting the Three Character Classic in his sleep.

She smiled to herself, drew the book out from his arms, undressed the child, pulled the quilt over him, and lay down beside him.

She slept deeply that night, and when morning came, daylight had already grown bright.

She turned over to find the little one's spot beside her empty, and her heart gave a small, hollow lurch.

Ting Shuang smiled: "The little young lord was up very early. He said today is his last day in the Xie household, and that he wants to give you a gift, mistress."

Yun Chu followed Ting Shuang quietly to the side room and peeked inside. There was the little one, cradling a piece of wood in one arm, a short blade in the other hand, working on a wood carving.

His expression was so serious it looked as though he were attending to something of the greatest importance.

Yun Chu began to think. What could she give this child?

"Mistress, the concubines have all come to pay their morning respects."

Ting Shuang stayed in the side room to watch over the child while Yun Chu went out front.

Concubine Jiang, Concubine Tao, Concubine Yu, along with all the young masters and young misses.

"The mistress looks well. You must have made a full recovery," Concubine Jiang said with a smile. "Just in time for the old matriarch's birthday banquet."

"Since the subject of the banquet has come up, I would like to ask Ping'er something," Yun Chu said. "Has everything needed for tomorrow been prepared? If there are any matters you are uncertain about, we can discuss them together now."

Xie Ping replied, "The old matriarch has personally been overseeing the progress of the banquet. Everything is ready. Mother need not trouble herself with these small details."

The old matriarch had said that the moment the banquet was over, all the household management authority in the mother's hands would be transferred entirely to her. Until she was married out, the Xie household would be entirely under her management. For an unmarried girl to run a household in good order would be a considerable advantage in any marriage negotiations...

Yun Chu asked no further about the banquet and instead inquired one by one about the concubines and children's recent circumstances.

Concubine Tao's figure was growing heavier by the day. She was likely to give birth in the hottest part of summer.

Concubine Jiang had started young Xian'er on character recognition and reading, and they had just begun her education.

Concubine Yu, Ting Yu, not to be left behind, had sent Yun'er to study at the household's small schoolroom with the family tutor.

Xie Shi'wei, after the last session of household discipline, had calmed considerably and sat quietly through the morning greeting without a word.

Everyone chatted for a while, then dispersed.

On the way out of Sheng Residence, Xie Shi'yun tugged at Ting Yu's sleeve: "Yiniang, Mother doesn't like me anymore. Is it because there's another child?"

Ting Yu shook her head. It was not only Yun'er the mistress had grown cooler toward; she was the same with the eldest and second young masters. Even the master himself had received a slap across the face... Truthfully, even she, who had served the mistress from childhood and knew her temperament inside and out, could no longer see through what the mistress intended to do.

"Yiniang, I saw another child in Mother's courtyard," Xie Shi'yun said in a low voice. "Yesterday when I came to play near Mother's courtyard, I heard a child's voice coming from inside. It was a boy's voice. I waited for a very long time and then saw a boy come out from the side room. About the same age as me... It must be because of that child that Mother doesn't like me anymore!"

These were not the words of a child making things up. Ting Yu's expression shifted with sudden alarm: "You truly saw this?"

Xie Shi'yun nodded hard.

Ting Yu's hand tightened sharply.

The child was very likely someone from a branch of the Yun family. Could it be that, since the mistress had no children of her own, she was thinking of adopting one from the Yun family?

If the mistress truly raised a child of the same bloodline at her side, then her Yun'er would never again be able to win the mistress's favor.

Did the old matriarch know about this? Did the mistress-in-law? Did the master?

All manner of thoughts turned through Ting Yu's head, but she did not dare act on any of them. She was not certain what the mistress intended to do.

Yun Chu had only just come back to the side room when the little one hid what he was holding behind himself: "Nianqin, don't look at me. I'll give you a surprise in a little while."

"Very well, Nianqin will wait," she said, sitting down by the window and busying herself with something in her own hands.

She was also preparing a parting gift for the little one.

This was his last day, and just thinking that tomorrow he would leave the Xie household, a faint thread of reluctance stirred unexpectedly in her heart.

chapters.title: The Old Matriarch's Birthday Banquet
chapters.content:
After dinner.

Chu Hongyu pulled Yun Chu into the room and held out a wood carving with great ceremony, pressing it into her arms: "Nianqin, do you like it?"

It was a palm-sized carved figurine, just barely recognizable as a woman in a skirt and robe, and just barely recognizable as Yun Chu.

She examined it again and again with a heart full of delight: "Yu-ge'er, thank you. Nianqin likes it so very much. Nianqin also has a gift for you."

She produced a small pouch and handed it to him.

Chu Hongyu opened the pouch without another moment's delay and drew out a tiny doll sewn from scraps of cloth.

The doll was no larger than a thumb, yet its features and expression were so vividly rendered that anyone who looked at it would know at once it was Chu Hongyu.

"Wow, Nianqin, you are truly so talented! I love this doll so much!" the little one said with barely contained excitement. "I just wish it were a little bigger so I could hold it in my arms."

Yun Chu lifted him up and settled him on her lap, saying gently, "I made it purposely this small. You can keep it in your pouch and wear it with you every day. And remember: you must not let anyone know you came to the Xie household, and you must not let anyone know you call me Nianqin, or great misfortune will fall on me."

Chu Hongyu gave a solemn nod, then hesitated: "Can I tell my little sister?"

He had already mentioned earlier that his sister could not speak. Someone who could not speak could naturally not reveal any secrets. Yun Chu gave a small nod.

The little one jumped for joy.

Yun Chu could tell from his manner that the two siblings were on very good terms. That little girl must be just as endearing as he was.

Perhaps because he had to leave in the morning, the little one was especially clinging that night, arms and legs wrapped around Yun Chu, his head resting against her chest, refusing to close his eyes no matter what.

Yun Chu told him several stories and sang him several songs. They carried on until nearly midnight before the child finally fell asleep.

By the dim light, she looked at the sleeping child in her arms, and moved by something she could not have named, she pressed her lips gently to his cheek.

A single kiss, and the hollow emptiness in her chest felt as though something had quietly filled it.

She held the child close and sank into a deep, still sleep.

The next morning, the faint light of dawn had only just begun to slip through the window when Yun Chu opened her eyes. The child in her arms was already gone.

She was alarmed enough to leap out of bed immediately.

"Mistress, the little young lord rose and left at the second half of the third watch. Seeing that you were sleeping soundly, he would not allow any of us to wake you," Ting Shuang said, carrying in a basin of water. "Today is the old matriarch's birthday banquet, and every courtyard has risen early to be busy. Let this servant help you dress and do your hair."

Yun Chu held the wood carving in her hand. Only this thing remained to prove the child had ever been here.

She sat before the mirror and spent considerable effort banishing the child's face from her thoughts, then looked at her own reflection: "Keep the hairstyle simple."

Ting Shuang nodded and worked quickly, fashioning the simplest possible arrangement, fastening it with a plain jade pin. She then began to apply Yun Chu's makeup: the face covered in white powder, no rouge on the lips, no pencil to the brows, leaving her complexion entirely pallid. Finally a deep purple robe was put on, which against that paper-white face looked as though it might belong to a ghost.

The moment the dressing was finished, those coming to pay their morning respects had already arrived.

Because it was the old matriarch's birthday, Xie Shi'an had not gone to the academy, and he was waiting with the others in the receiving room.

Yun Chu came out, and everyone paid their respects.

Xie Shi'an raised his eyes to look at Yun Chu's face and then hesitated before saying, "Mother's color is so pale today. Are you unwell somewhere?"

"I have had a headache since the middle of the night. Right now my head feels as though it might split open," Yun Chu said, pressing at her temple. "Shi'an, do you think I look fit to go out and receive guests in this condition?"

Xie Shi'an pressed his lips together.

If his mother did not receive the guests, the rumors outside would likely worsen further.

But seeing his mother this wan and frail, any guest who laid eyes on her would be sure to have all manner of speculations.

"Mistress, I happen to have some lip color with me," Ting Yu stepped forward. "This concubine will apply some for you. It should improve your complexion a little."

Yun Chu nodded and let her fuss.

Once her lips were painted red, her face looked several shades paler than before.

Xie Shi'an said, "Mother has a naturally fair complexion. It is better without the lip color."

Ting Yu was a little sheepish and had to dab the rouge off with her handkerchief.

Ting Shuang, standing to the side, felt quietly indignant on her mistress's behalf. These people's only concern was whether the mistress's appearance might give rise to gossip about the Xie family. Not one of them was genuinely concerned about the mistress's health.

It was then she began to understand why the mistress had stopped showing warmth to the Xie household's children. Because every last one of them was an ingrate.

Even if the mistress were to pour her whole heart into raising these children, she was unlikely to receive a single word of gratitude in return.

Far better was the little young lord of the Prince of Pingxi's household.

Yun Chu stood and said with a smile: "Come, let us go and wish the old matriarch a happy birthday."

The group swept off together toward An Shou Hall.

The old matriarch was dressed in fresh finery and sat in the seat of honor looking vigorous and sharp. Lady Yuan had already arrived, and so had Yun Chu's father-in-law, Xie Zhongcheng.

Of all the Xie family's household members, the one Yun Chu had had the least dealings with was Xie Jingyu's father, Xie Zhongcheng. This father-in-law spent most of his time lodging at the manor outside the city and gave his full attention to managing the Xie family's business affairs.

She went in and paid her respects in turn, then looked toward the old matriarch and said with a smile: "Your grandson's wife wishes you a blessed birthday, old matriarch. May you be blessed as wide as the Eastern Sea, live as long as the Southern Mountain, and may this day come each year, and this occasion be celebrated each year."

The concubines and younger household members behind her came forward one by one to offer their birthday wishes.

The old matriarch beamed: "Good, good, all of you have such filial hearts. The future of the Xie family rests with every one of you!"

The Xie family in the capital consisted of just this one branch. When the birthday greetings were done, the presentation of gifts began.

Xie Zhongcheng had gone to a temple to pray for a longevity talisman on his mother's behalf, claiming he had knelt for nine days and nine nights at Hanshan Temple, the most efficacious in the outskirts of the city, before receiving one.

Lady Yuan gave the old matriarch a longevity jade vase.

Xie Jingyu presented a painting of celestial deer he had made himself.

Then it was Yun Chu's turn. Every year at the old matriarch's birthday, Yun Chu's gift had been the most costly among all the presents.

When the old matriarch saw Ting Shuang and Ting Xue carry in a large item, she could tell at a glance it was a folding screen.

"Old Matriarch, this is a hundred-longevity screen that your grandson's wife spent three months embroidering for you," Yun Chu said, pulling away the red cloth. "As the daughter of a military household, I have never been skilled at needlework. I put in whatever effort I could manage, though the result is rather poor. I hope the old matriarch will not mind."

Lady Yuan said, "A birthday gift is most important in the sincerity it carries. The quality of the needlework is another matter."

But when she looked at the characters for "longevity" stitched one after another across the screen, Lady Yuan found she could not quite bring herself to say more. Because they were truly quite ugly.

A screen like this, if displayed in a room, would only invite ridicule. It could only be stored away in the treasury, and yet in the treasury it would take up space...

The old matriarch's mouth gave an involuntary twitch. The worst needlewoman among her own serving girls produced work better than what Yun Chu had done. If the needlework was this poor, she ought not to have attempted it at all. This was nothing but embarrassing herself in public.

And yet filling an entire screen with a hundred longevity characters was no easy thing, most of all for someone with no skill at needlework. It was nothing short of laborious.

If she said anything even slightly dissatisfied, she would wound Yun Chu's dignity, and who knew what outlandish thing this granddaughter-in-law might do next.

"Chu'er is thoughtful," the old matriarch said against her true feelings. "To have prepared such a careful gift while still in the middle of recovering from illness, your filial devotion is genuinely moving."

Yun Chu lowered her head to demur.

The concubines and younger members each presented their gifts in turn, offering items such as clothing and shoes, or paintings and calligraphy, nothing particularly unexpected.

When the gift-giving was done, the old matriarch rose: "The hour is nearly upon us. It is time to open the doors and welcome the guests. Come, let us go to the front courtyard."

chapters.title: One Problem After Another
chapters.content:
By now the sky had fully brightened.

The front courtyard had long been set with chairs and tables. Because it was a birthday banquet hosted by the women of the household, the seating was not divided by sex. Families sat together at their own low tables, and several dozen had been prepared in all.

They had only just passed through the front courtyard where the banquet was laid and had not yet opened the main gate when a serving woman came hurrying over: "Eldest young miss, something has happened. You must come and decide what to do."

As it was Xie Ping who had been managing the banquet, the servants came to report to her directly.

Xie Ping was slightly displeased. This serving woman truly had no sense of occasion at all. With so many elders present, coming forward like this was deliberate humiliation.

She drew a breath and asked, "What has happened?"

The serving woman said, "Eldest young miss, the kitchen only just discovered when the ingredients were being prepared that the fish delivered early this morning are all tiny, no bigger than the palm of your hand. Small they might be, but they are also all dead. What are we to do?"

"What?" The old matriarch could not believe it. "What household holds a birthday banquet with dead fish?"

Was this not a bad omen, a curse upon her early death?

Xie Ping hurried to say, "Let me go and see."

The old matriarch's right eyelid kept twitching, and she could not rest easy: "The hour is still early. The guests will not arrive for some time yet. Let us all go and have a look."

Xie Zhongcheng, Xie Jingyu, and Xie Shi'an stayed in the front courtyard. The old matriarch led the women of the household to the kitchen.

When she saw the small fish floating belly-up on the surface of the water, the old matriarch's expression went dark and unyielding: "Who was responsible for procuring this fish?"

A serving woman said, "All the kitchen purchases have been handled by Steward He."

Xie Ping's hand clenched white-knuckled around her handkerchief.

She had trusted He Xu so completely, placing the greater part of the work in his hands, and yet this wretch had managed to cause her this kind of disaster.

Fish being small was one thing, but dead fish? How much money had he embezzled?

"Old Matriarch, it is I who failed to judge people properly," Xie Ping said, lowering her head. "I will immediately have someone go out to buy fresh large fish."

Lady Yuan sighed: "By the time the fish is brought back, the banquet will have already begun. There is no time."

Concubine Tao spoke up: "Then simply leave the fish course out."

"A birthday banquet cannot be without fish," Yun Chu said coolly. "These fish have been dead for roughly half an hour. Cooked with a stronger seasoning, the freshness can be masked."

The old matriarch looked toward Yun Chu: "Are you certain this will work?"

"The Yun household has a dish, crispy fish in hot and sour sauce. Deep-fried at high temperature and seasoned with evodia and aged vinegar, most people cannot tell the difference," Yun Chu said. "Yin Concubine Yu, this dish is one you know how to make. I leave it to you."

She spoke with complete composure, and the calm she projected made the previously flustered household feel as though they had found something solid to hold onto, as if the fish being dead were not so great a matter after all.

Ting Yu stepped forward: "Yes."

Of the four senior maidservants at the mistress's side, she was the one with a gift for cooking. She felt at last as though she had a use to serve.

She handed her child to the wet nurse, stepped into the kitchen, and as she entered she heard Lady Yuan speaking: "Chu'er, this household still needs you to be the one running things. If not for you, I truly would not know how to manage this..."

Concubine Jiang added, "The mistress has the mind of a true household manager. Of course a small matter like this is no challenge for her."

Ting Yu bit her lip as she went in. It was she who was stepping forward to solve the difficult problem at hand, and yet everyone was praising only the mistress, as though she did not exist at all.

The old matriarch's eyes were complex.

She had originally intended to hold a flawless birthday banquet and use it to take the household management authority back from Yun Chu. But trouble had arisen before the banquet even began, and here she was, relying on Yun Chu to sort things out.

She, the old matriarch, could not help acknowledging it herself: a legitimate daughter raised in a general's household was indeed, in every respect, a cut above most others.

"Check every item that was sent in from the morning purchases," Yun Chu said in a cool tone. "You are all old hands who know this kitchen inside and out. Handle whatever small problems you can manage yourselves. If there is something truly beyond you, report it immediately."

"Yes!"

Every serving woman and maidservant in the kitchen answered in unison.

Only then did the old matriarch lead the women's party to the front courtyard to receive guests.

A faint, sardonic smile curved Yun Chu's lips.

She had known that this birthday banquet would not go off brilliantly, but she had not expected the problems to be quite this severe.

The banquet had not even begun, and already a vat of fish lay dead. Heaven only knew what further disasters lay waiting ahead.

Still, was He Xu truly bold enough to purchase a vat of dead fish? She had a nagging sense that the fish had been deliberately suffocated by someone.

The coarser serving women of the household, though full of grievances toward Xie Ping, ought not to have dared to tamper with something as significant as a birthday banquet.

Yun Chu rather thought it was simply the old matriarch's bad luck.

The old matriarch and Lady Yuan, along with the younger children, sat in the front courtyard receiving room to talk. The concubines were not permitted to attend such occasions. Yun Chu and Xie Jingyu, accompanied by their eldest son and eldest daughter, Xie Shi'an and Xie Ping, stood at the main gate to welcome guests.

The first to arrive with birthday wishes was Xie Jingyu's subordinate, Lord Hu, who had brought his wife and daughter.

"Master Xie, Mistress Xie." Lord Hu bowed in greeting. "A small token of my regards, humbly presented."

Xie Jingyu returned the bow: "Shi'an, take Lord Hu inside to his seat."

Lord Hu looked at Xie Shi'an and remarked with feeling, "When I first called at the Xie household two years ago, the young master was only this tall. To see how he has grown."

Xie Shi'an exchanged pleasantries with Lord Hu as they went inside.

Yun Chu smiled and exchanged greetings with Lady Hu.

Lady Hu looked at Yun Chu's pallid complexion and said, "Word has it that Mistress Xie has been gravely ill, and yet you are here managing the banquet as well. That must be terribly taxing."

"Oh, not at all," Yun Chu replied. "This banquet has been entirely organized by this daughter of mine. I merely offered a few suggestions here and there. Every large and small matter was decided by Ping'er herself. With her helping me, I expect things will be much easier from now on."

Lady Hu looked at Xie Ping in surprise: "Xie Miss is only thirteen or fourteen, I believe? To organize a banquet of this scale single-handedly?"

Xie Ping said, "I have only Mother to thank for teaching me well."

This was as good as an open acknowledgment that the banquet had been organized entirely by her alone.

Several guests arriving at that moment happened to hear that a thirteen-year-old girl had organized this banquet, and could not help but regard her with expressions of admiration.

Xie Ping accepted every bit of that praise.

Just then, a serving woman came rushing over from the back in visible agitation.

Her heart gave a lurch. She immediately said, "There are a few matters I must attend to. Please excuse me for a moment."

She led the serving woman to the side and frowned: "What is it now?"

"Eldest young miss, the pork and mutton purchased for the kitchen are both at least ten jin short," the serving woman said, slapping her thigh. "There is no time to send someone out to buy more now..."

Xie Ping seethed with fury, grinding her teeth.

He Xu was still her maternal uncle, and yet he was going out of his way to make trouble for her.

She pulled at her handkerchief: "Then serve each bowl with slightly less. Today's guests are all officials of some means. None of them will begrudge themselves a mouthful or two of meat less."

The serving woman parted her lips as though to say something further, then finally swallowed whatever it was and accepted the order, turning to go back to the kitchen.

Xie Ping composed herself and returned to Yun Chu's side to continue receiving guests.

Every lady who arrived asked after Yun Chu's health. Though Yun Chu assured each one that she had recovered, her pallid face and slight frame made it plain to anyone who looked that she was holding herself together through sheer will.

At that moment, a Yun family carriage arrived.

After the Yun family had publicly provided a burial site for the Xie family's early-departed children adjacent to the Yun family ancestral grounds the last time, it had been the equivalent of an open rebuke to the Xie household. Now everyone was curious: with Yun Chu so ill, what attitude would the Yun family take toward the Xie household on this occasion?

chapters.title: The Marquis of Xuanwu Arrives
chapters.content:
Yun Chu personally escorted the Yun family visitors inside to offer their birthday wishes.

Three members of the Yun family had come: Yun's matriarch, Lady Lin; Yun family's first young mistress, Liu Qianqian; and Yun family's second young miss, Yun Ran.

"We wish the birthday star a day as brilliant as sun and moon, and years that never age," Lady Lin said, directing her attendants to present the gift. "A small token, inadequately expressed, offered in all sincerity."

The birthday gift was a large, full-bodied vase standing as tall as a person, its body adorned all over with graceful peony blossoms, threaded with gold, and undeniably fine. It was worth at least five hundred taels.

Yun Chu felt a small pang at the cost, but there was much she could not easily say to her mother in plain terms. To say too much would only cause her mother to worry and lose sleep over her days in this household.

From the size of this gift alone, the surrounding ladies could see that the Yun family had every intention of continuing its marriage alliance with the Xie household.

With the Yun family standing as a backer, the other ladies in attendance became somewhat more attentive in their manner toward the old Xie matriarch.

The women gathered with the old matriarch in the receiving room to talk, while the men were received by Xie Jingyu, with Xie Zhongcheng and Xie Shi'an in attendance.

Before long, the banquet hour arrived, and everyone took their seats according to rank and family.

Just then, the guard at the gate announced in a loud voice: "The Marquis of Xuanwu has arrived!"

An expression of astonishment crossed the old Xie matriarch's face.

The Marquis of Xuanwu was a member of the hereditary nobility far beyond the reach of the Xie family's connections. She had not sent an invitation to the Xuanwu Marquis household. How had the young marquis come to arrive?

Xie Jingyu's face changed suddenly, something unpleasant passing over it as he raised his eyes to look at the man walking in.

The Marquis of Xuanwu had inherited the title passed down from his ancestors three years ago and was only in his early twenties. He was dressed in a silver robe and held a folding fan, and carried himself with an air of natural distinction.

"This junior has come to wish the old matriarch a happy birthday," Qin Mingheng said as he entered, snapping his fan shut and presenting his gift. "This is a snow-skin cream from the imperial palace. When young women apply it, it makes the skin white as snow; when the elderly use it, it diminishes the lines in the skin. This junior wishes the old matriarch all blessings on her birthday and that she grow younger with each passing year."

Upon hearing it was something from the palace, the old matriarch's eyes lit up, and she rose hastily to her feet: "That the Marquis of Xuanwu has come all this way to offer birthday wishes is truly more honor than this old woman deserves."

"What is the old matriarch saying? Master Xie and I are close friends, so of course it is only right that I come to offer my congratulations," Qin Mingheng said, looking toward Xie Jingyu. "Why does Master Xie look as though he does not quite welcome my arrival?"

Xie Jingyu gripped his fist tightly and said, "The arrival of the Marquis of Xuanwu brings great honor to our Xie household. Please take the seat of honor."

A marquis's title placed one above all officials in the civil hierarchy, so Qin Mingheng was seated above the Yun family, right beside the host family.

Between Yun Chu and the young marquis sat only Xie Jingyu and one narrow passage.

She was not sure whether she was imagining things, but she had the sense that from the moment he entered, the young marquis's gaze kept falling on her, seemingly by chance.

Yet whenever she looked over, the young marquis was in conversation with someone else, so it rather seemed she had been imagining things.

Just when she had decided she had read too much into it, Qin Mingheng suddenly looked toward her: "I hear that Mistress Xie has been critically ill. I wonder how you are faring now?"

Every guest who arrived asked something to this effect, and Yun Chu had noticed nothing unusual in the question. She was just about to reply when Xie Jingyu spoke first: "Thank you for the marquis's concern. My wife has had only a mild chill. The rumors circulating outside have greatly exaggerated the matter. She has now recovered quite well."

The host, Xie Zhongcheng, rose and said, "I am grateful to all the distinguished lords, ladies, young misses, and young masters for taking time from your busy days to attend my mother's birthday banquet. We have laid out a modest spread here today; please accept this humble hospitality. If there is anything in our welcome that falls short, I hope you will all be forgiving. And now, let us raise our cups together!"

All those present raised their cups as one.

But as the wine touched the lips, expressions shifted here and there. For a banquet of this scale, no one could understand how the Xie family could have prepared such mediocre wine.

As guests of the house, however, one drank what the host provided and naturally made no comment about it.

Only Qin Mingheng spoke: "Tsk, tsk. This is the first time I have drunk wine this insipid. Master Xie, your household's wine is just like you as a man: too bland by far."

Xie Jingyu pressed his lips shut.

This Qin Mingheng had clearly come here looking to cause trouble. But rank and station being what they were, he had no means to send the man away.

Yun Chu also sensed it: the Marquis of Xuanwu appeared to have some quarrel with Xie Jingyu. Yet Xie Jingyu was a minor fifth-rank official, with no natural connection to any hereditary noble household. How had he managed to offend the Marquis of Xuanwu?

But that was not something within her sphere of concern. She sat in her seat with a faint smile, exchanging pleasantries with the ladies nearby.

Just then, the maidservants began to bring the banquet dishes out one by one.

Every table received the same spread: four main dishes, four hot dishes, four cold dishes, and four platters of fruit and confections. It looked fairly generous on the surface.

But Yun Chu noticed that every dish was served only half-full. It was plain to anyone looking that the kitchen had been cutting corners. Men might not notice such things, but every noblewoman present managed her own household and could see the situation at a glance. They exchanged discreet glances with one another, genuinely puzzled.

The Xie household was a fifth-rank family. Though they had come from humble origins, years of official position ought to have given them some footing. How could they not manage to put on a decent birthday banquet?

The old Xie matriarch was beginning to regret herself.

She ought never to have put a matter as significant as this banquet into the hands of an unmarried girl like Xie Ping.

Looking at the expressions on the ladies' faces, all dismissive and disdainful, as though the Xie household were some thoroughly undignified thing, she felt it keenly.

Xie Ping did not dare look at the old matriarch at all, keeping her head low and cursing He Xu comprehensively in the silence of her mind.

"What our guests may not know," Yun Chu said, speaking up, "is that the south has had no rain this spring. Come autumn, the harvest is likely to fail entirely, and there will surely be a great many displaced people seeking refuge. The Xie family has been reluctant to make this banquet too lavish and extravagant. For all the grand display a large banquet would provide would only save the Xie family's face, while that same silver, if used for disaster relief, could save dozens of lives. Between face and lives, I trust each of you carries your own measure of that judgment."

"Well said!" Qin Mingheng was the first to call out and applaud. "That Mistress Xie carries such concern for the people in her heart truly puts the rest of us to shame!"

The old matriarch was genuinely won over by this granddaughter-in-law of hers. With the banquet on the brink of becoming an occasion for mockery, this speech had turned the Xie family's deficiencies into an act of virtue.

Even the Marquis of Xuanwu had called out in approval, and who would dare say now that the Xie family's banquet was beneath them?

Sure enough, the dismissal in the guests' eyes faded considerably, and they spoke warmly of the Xie family's great merit and wished the old matriarch boundless good fortune and long life.

The old matriarch picked up her chopsticks: "We have been talking for quite a long time. Everyone must be hungry by now. Let us eat."

She lifted a piece of the crispy fish and tasted it, and found herself inwardly impressed. This was indeed the Yun household's own recipe. Even fish past its prime could be made this savory and delicious.

She was just marveling to herself when a jarring sound came from below.

Qin Mingheng bit into a meatball, immediately spat it out, and said loudly, "I know Master Xie serves in the Ministry of Revenue. I had not known until now that the Xie household was also in the salt trade."

The guests began to murmur among themselves.

"This dish is impossibly salty. It cannot be eaten."

"How can it be this salty? I've drunk two cups of tea and cannot wash the taste down. This is enough to salt a person to death."

"For the Xie household's kitchen to commit such a blunder, clearly there is a problem with the inner court's management. The mistress of the house is the eldest legitimate daughter of the Yun general's household. How can she not even manage a household properly?"

"It is because Mistress Xie has been ill of late. Look at her complexion, the illness can hardly have fully passed. Where would she have the energy to attend to things in the household? When all is said and done, it is the Xie young miss who lacks the ability to manage a household, and has made a mess of this banquet."

"I hear she was born of an outside woman, a concubine's daughter who was given the name of the legitimate eldest daughter. What would she know of managing a household?"

"Mistress Xie was just now helping to smooth things over. I wonder what she can say to smooth this over."

"..."

chapters.title: An Inauspicious Omen
chapters.content:
The old Xie matriarch personally tasted several dishes. Every single one was intolerably salty.

If one dish had been a touch too salty, it might have been put down to the cook's mistake. But the great majority of them had been salted with reckless abandon. It was plainly intentional.

She was furious enough to feel her head might come apart, and had no idea whatsoever how to explain any of this away.

Lady Yuan had never encountered a scene like this in her life and could only smile awkwardly.

Xie Ping kept her head as low as she could manage, trying to reduce her presence to nothing.

"I wish to offer an apology on behalf of the Xie family to all those present," Yun Chu said, rising to her feet with a genuinely contrite expression. "These failings at the birthday banquet are a reflection of my shortcomings as the household's mistress. I will first take it upon myself to drink three cups in penalty."

She had only just picked up her cup when Qin Mingheng spoke: "Everyone in the capital knows that Mistress Xie is still recovering from illness, and that this banquet was not arranged by her. It is not yours to take as a penalty."

"I am the official mistress of the Xie household. Even if I did not arrange it myself, these failings reflect my poor supervision, and the penalty is mine to bear," Yun Chu said, raising her cup and tipping her head back to drink.

Qin Mingheng's brow creased sharply, and he was in the act of rising when Yun Chu's cup was taken from her hand by Xie Jingyu at her side, who drank all three cups in her place.

Something in Qin Mingheng's eyes shifted and went dark. A faint trace of a smile hung at the corner of his mouth: "Master Xie and Mistress Xie are truly devoted to one another. It makes one quite envious."

For some reason she could not name, Yun Chu caught a thread of something almost like mockery in those words.

Setting aside that faint discomfort, she said, "The Xie household will arrange for someone to procure a full spread from a restaurant as quickly as possible. We ask our guests to bear with us in the meantime. For now, please allow us to serve the birthday peaches and longevity noodles. May everyone share in the blessings."

Lady Lin of the Yun family nodded: "I will have people assist with the arrangements as well."

With the Yun family's standing in the capital being what it was, and Lady Yun offering her help, everyone understood that the spread would arrive quickly. The atmosphere eased considerably.

The servants brought the birthday peaches out: shaped from flour into red peach forms, each one stamped with a large longevity character. The largest peach was placed before the birthday star, the old Xie matriarch, with a generous platter set out at every other table.

After the succession of mishaps, the old matriarch looked visibly diminished, but she gathered herself with some effort and reached out to cut open the peach.

As the peach was cut open, the old woman let out such a fright that she lurched backward again and again, toppling out of her chair entirely, and sent the longevity noodles crashing to the floor.

Everyone below looked up, and in a moment the room was utter chaos.

"Good heavens, why is the birthday peach full of worms!"

"Good lord. A real peach having worms is one thing, but how are there so many of these revolting things inside a peach made of flour?"

"This is an inauspicious omen!"

Yun Chu's eyes narrowed.

Last night, the little one had been talking in his sleep after he drifted off, murmuring something about worms. Could it be that all these mishaps at today's banquet had been his doing?

He Xu might be audacious, but he would only dare to pass off inferior goods and pocket a little silver. Dead fish, over-salted dishes, worms... this had Chu Hongyu's handiwork written all over it.

Was it that the little one knew she was having a hard time in the Xie household, and was acting out to vent her grievances on her behalf?

Seeing the old matriarch slumped in fright on the floor, and the Xie household in complete disarray, she did find a considerable measure of that grievance had indeed been vented.

"Everyone, please remain calm," Xie Jingyu stepped forward, doing his best to maintain composure. "A green caterpillar with a green pine is a symbol of the pine's hundred years, which is a propitious sign. We are sorry to have startled our guests. While the main spread has yet to arrive, may we ask everyone to take some tea in the meantime. The tea leaves are tribute tea from the western territories presented to the imperial court; please do have a taste."

The guests in attendance, apart from the Yun family and the Marquis of Xuanwu, were mostly lesser officials of the fifth, sixth, and seventh ranks, very few of whom had ever seen tribute tea in their lives. Hearing Xie Jingyu speak of it in these terms, one after another they set aside their thoughts of leaving early and settled back into their seats to drink the tea.

This tea had been personally overseen by Xie Jingyu, with Xie Shi'an watching every step of the preparation. Not a single detail had been allowed to slip, and only then had it been served before the guests.

Tribute tea being what it was, everyone who had been frightened moments ago broke into pleased expressions and began to talk warmly among themselves.

The old matriarch was taken away by the Xie family's women to wash and compose herself.

"Crash!"

A cup hit the floor.

Xie Ping's knees went soft with fright: "Old Matriarch, it is all my fault. I failed to prepare the banquet properly. I have brought shame on the Xie family. Please, beat me to death if you wish!"

The old matriarch lifted her foot intending to deliver a kick.

Lady Yuan intervened: "What's done is done. Blaming Ping'er now will accomplish nothing. Besides, Ping'er is an unmarried girl, still so young. It was never appropriate to put such a thing in her hands. Ping'er is too young, Chu'er is ill, and you yourself are not young, old matriarch. If we must assign fault, it is really mine. If I had any skill in managing a household, it would never have come to this, and the Xie family would not now be the laughingstock of the capital..."

"Mother, this is not the time for self-reproach," Yun Chu said coolly. "Mama Zhou, take a few people and have He Xu detained."

"That's right, bind He Xu up first," the old matriarch said through clenched teeth. "To tamper with the master's own birthday banquet, I see he has grown tired of living. When the banquet ends and the guests have gone, we shall see how I flay that skin off him!"

Xie Ping's whole body gave a tremor.

When the banquet was over, the old matriarch would surely punish her as well. She did not know what was waiting for her.

Mama Zhou immediately took people to go and seize He Xu.

He Xu had recently been living a life of considerable ease: Chen Defu had given him several shops to manage personally, and he now had a number of followers under him. Then came the old matriarch's birthday banquet, the greater part of which had been in his hands, and he had skimmed off no small amount from the proceedings. While the banquet was underway, he had used some of the silver he'd pocketed to buy wine and a pig's head, and was eating and gambling with a few of his underlings at the rear gate.

In the middle of all this good entertainment, Mama Zhou's people suddenly had him pinned.

"What are you doing! What is the meaning of this!" He Xu struggled violently. He had been drinking, and his strength was considerable, so much that the two older serving women could barely hold him.

Mama Zhou had someone bring a stick down on He Xu, then stuffed his mouth and had four of the larger serving women drag him away.

As they came under the covered walkway, they ran into the He woman, who had come looking for He Xu.

The He woman stared: "Mama Zhou, what is this about? What has Steward He done?"

"Matters that are not Mama He's concern need not be Mama He's business," Mama Zhou said coolly. "Today is the old matriarch's birthday, and there are many distinguished guests in the household. A person under censure such as yourself would do better not to wander about... The mistress pardoned Mama He for one day's confinement. That was the mistress's generosity. Mama He should not squander the mistress's goodwill."

With that, she left with He Xu still struggling and protesting.

The He woman's heart was gripped with anxiety. She quickly pulled several people aside to ask what had happened, and learned swiftly what had transpired in the front courtyard. Her heart dropped straight to the bottom.

He Xu being taken away was his own doing.

But why should her Ping'er's reputation be destroyed for any of this?

She suddenly understood. The mistress had feigned illness, and had dumped the entire birthday banquet into the hands of a thirteen-year-old girl, specifically to ruin Ping'er's reputation.

Shi'an'er had been punished by the mistress with kneeling in the ancestral hall.

Wei'er had been subjected to household discipline by the mistress.

And now Ping'er's marriage prospects had been ruined by the mistress.

The mistress's schemes were truly deep.

Once this banquet was over, Ping'er's entire life was finished.

She could not stand by and let this happen.

With that thought, the He woman ran toward the front courtyard. She needed to find Xie Jingyu and discuss a remedy.

chapters.title: Xie Jingyu Goes Missing
chapters.content:
In the front courtyard banquet hall.

With tribute tea for company, and Lady Lin of the Yun family there to smooth things over, and the Marquis of Xuanwu's presence lending the occasion some gravity, the guests were conversing in reasonably good spirits.

Xie Jingyu was in discussion with several colleagues about the current political situation when a young manservant came quickly to his side and murmured, "Master, Mama He says she has something important to report."

Xie Jingyu's brow furrowed slightly: "Tell her to bring it to me later."

The manservant nodded and left, then returned shortly, saying quietly, "Master, Mama He says it cannot wait. If it is inconvenient for the master to leave the table, she says she can come inside to report."

Xie Jingyu looked up.

He could see the He woman standing at the entrance to the banquet hall, looking very much prepared to walk in at any moment.

His expression darkened. He rose and went over to her, his voice low and cold: "What is so urgent?"

The He woman said, keeping her eyes down, "Master, everyone knows that the birthday banquet was organized by the Xie family's eldest young miss. And yet it has gone so badly wrong. If word spreads that the Xie family's eldest young miss is incapable of managing a household, which family will ever be willing to take Ping'er as their official mistress? Please, think of some way to help."

Xie Jingyu's expression was very poor.

Right now the Xie family had lost every shred of face and dignity. His first concern had to be the family, before he could think about the children's marriages.

Moreover, Ping'er was only thirteen. Marriage was a matter for two years hence. It was far too early to be speaking of it now.

Seeing that Xie Jingyu said nothing, the He woman said anxiously, "While the banquet is still underway, perhaps Ping'er could brew tea for the guests, or demonstrate some talent, to shift the impression somewhat..."

Xie Jingyu truly did not know what to say.

If this were a palace banquet, it would be perfectly fitting for the daughters of great families to dance and play music for the empress and consorts.

But most of those present were officials of lower rank than the Xie family. If Ping'er were to perform in public, that would be the real humiliation for the Xie household.

"Enough. I will see to it," Xie Jingyu said coldly. "Do what you are supposed to do, and stop hovering around the front courtyard."

The He woman had followed him for more than a decade and could hardly fail to read his thoughts. Her fingers tightened: "Master, Ping'er is our first child. She will also be the first of the Xie household's children to be married. If anything goes wrong with her marriage, all the children who come after will be in a very difficult position."

Xie Jingyu's voice went colder still: "What is this? Is that a threat?"

The He woman hurried to say, "That is not what I meant. I..."

In the middle of their exchange, someone passed through the flower shrubbery nearby.

Xie Jingyu pulled the He woman aside.

Before long, the servants returned with the full restaurant spread, carrying it in and setting it before the guests one dish at a time.

This was the finest cooking from the best restaurant in the capital. To eat there under normal circumstances required booking at least half a month in advance. To be able to feast on it here and now was a delight for many of the guests.

The old Xie matriarch finally let out a breath of relief, raised her cup to toast Lady Lin of the Yun family, and gave her silent thanks. She understood perfectly well that without the Yun family's intercession, Zuixian Tavern would not have had a full spread ready for the Xie household on such short notice.

"Where has Jingyu gone?" the old matriarch noticed the empty seat below. "Chu'er, do you know where Jingyu has gone?"

Yun Chu smiled: "Mama He said she had something important to report, so my husband went out. He should be back shortly."

An inexplicably bad premonition settled suddenly in the old matriarch's chest.

She looked toward Mama Zhou at her side: "Go. Find Jingyu and have him come back to attend to the guests at once."

Mama Zhou received the order and left.

Roughly a quarter of an hour later, Mama Zhou returned, lowering her voice: "This servant searched everywhere and could not find the master. There is no knowing where he has gone."

The old matriarch drew a deep breath.

That He woman was nothing but trouble. To call Jingyu away on such an important occasion, what matter could possibly be more pressing than his grandmother's birthday banquet?

She should have known better than to agree to Yun Chu's suggestion of pardoning certain misbehaving servants. But it was too late to regret that now. She said, "Keep looking."

Yun Chu lowered her head and drank a sip of tea, concealing the cold indifference in her eyes.

"Mistress Xie."

A low voice sounded at her side.

Yun Chu set down her teacup and looked up, composing her face into a proper hostess's smile: "Marquis, is there something you wish to say?"

Her smile, though not quite reaching her eyes, was brilliant as a flower in spring, and for a brief moment Qin Mingheng lost himself in it.

He drank a mouthful of wine and then, with his composure restored, said, "I have heard that Mistress Xie had two early-departed children reburied. I once spent some time living at a temple, and the master there told me that the spirit of a person reburied must be guided by a dharma master through forty-nine days of prayers and rites before finding peace in their next life. I know several dharma masters; would you like me to arrange this for you?"

The smile on Yun Chu's face became a little more genuine.

Apart from the Yun family, this was the first person who had given any thought to her dead children.

She smiled: "My elder brother has already made all such arrangements. Thank you for your concern, Marquis."

"Those two children carried Xie family blood as well. And yet their own father, who stands as the person in this world most responsible for them, has given them no thought whatsoever. A man who places so little value on his own flesh and blood, will he truly value the person who sleeps beside him?" Qin Mingheng's voice dropped several tones. "Has Mistress Xie never thought to plan for her own future?"

Yun Chu raised her eyes and met Qin Mingheng's deep black gaze.

She saw, in those eyes, something that looked genuinely like concern.

Could it be that the Marquis of Xuanwu was truly thinking about her future?

But this was the first time they had ever sat face to face and spoken. There was no bond of any kind between them, no more than there was between strangers.

How could this man possibly...

"Mistress Xie has poured her heart into the children of this Xie household. Will those children truly repay her with filial devotion?" Qin Mingheng took another sip of wine. "Some things, when they should be ended, should be ended."

Yun Chu pressed her lips together.

Even an outsider could see the matter for what it was. And yet it had taken her an entire lifetime of bitter experience to see through the people around her.

She understood what the Marquis of Xuanwu was hinting at. He was suggesting she take her leave of this marriage.

In this life, she would never do such a thing. A woman who returned to her family's home after a separation would cast a shadow over the marriage prospects of her sisters. She would not allow herself, in any way, to bring further trouble upon the Yun family.

When widowhood was an option, why would she choose separation?

Yun Chu said, "I thank the Marquis for his concern. My husband and I are devoted to one another. Whatever the Marquis means by 'when things should be ended,' I am afraid I do not understand."

Qin Mingheng's expression went dark in an instant.

A devoted couple, indeed.

Even after everything Xie Jingyu had done to her, she still spoke of devotion.

She was the celebrated eldest daughter of the Yun household, the most beautiful woman in the capital in her day, and here she was, left to wither away in the Xie family...

"Old Matriarch, I have another matter to attend to. I shall take my leave."

Without waiting for the old matriarch to respond, Qin Mingheng rose and departed.

That a marquis could attend the banquet at all was already a mark of distinction for the Xie household. Leaving early was entirely within reason, and no one thought anything of it.

But Yun Chu had a faint sense that the Marquis of Xuanwu had left in anger at what she had said, and had walked out because of it.

The banquet ran to its end, and still Xie Jingyu had not appeared. The old matriarch's expression grew darker by degrees.

Even so, she maintained a strained smile for the guests: "The Xie household has engaged an opera troupe. Ladies and young misses, please follow us to the inner courtyard. We shall choose which pieces to see."

Most of the male guests departed after the banquet concluded. The female guests followed into the back courtyard to watch the opera.

Yun Chu led the party there. The courtyard had been arranged with tea and refreshments, all fully in order, and the ladies settled in quietly and began to listen.

When several acts had gone by and the enjoyment had grown a little stale, one of the ladies suggested taking a turn about the garden.

chapters.title: A Sordid Scene in the Inner Court
chapters.content:
The Xie family's compound was not particularly large, with only a small garden.

Yun Chu and Lady Yuan, mother- and daughter-in-law, led the group of ladies on a circuit of the garden. The general feeling was that there was not much to see.

One lady said uncertainly, "I have heard that Mistress Xie has planted a great many jujube trees in the compound. I wonder whether the jujube flowers have bloomed yet at this time of year."

Yun Chu replied with a smile, "Jujube flowers do not open until May at the earliest."

"The blossoms being out or not makes no difference," Lady Hu said helpfully. "Let us go and have a look at something different. In matters of fengshui, a jujube tree signifies prosperous and abundant descendants. Let us all go and share in the blessings."

The ladies present were none of them of the same standing as the eldest daughter of the Yun household, and so naturally they fell in with Lady Hu's lead one by one.

Lady Yuan said, "The jujube trees are planted along the wall on the southeast side of the compound. If our guests do not mind that jujube trees make poor viewing, please follow me this way."

The party followed toward the southeast.

This area had formerly been a proper garden, planted with whatever flowers suited the season, with a flower-viewing party held here every spring and autumn. This year it had been changed over entirely to jujube trees.

These were mature jujube trees transplanted from outside the capital. Every one of them stood taller than the courtyard wall, their branches full and leafy.

Lady Hu said, "It looks as though they will already bear fruit this year. I shall have to come to the Xie household and ask Mistress Xie for some jujubes to taste when the time comes."

Yun Chu said politely, "Once the fruit is in, the Xie household will have some sent to each residence. Please do not mind the tartness of fresh jujubes."

"Oh, I think I hear something," a lady with particularly sharp ears said. "Coming from that direction."

Lady Yuan looked: "That is a small courtyard within the Xie compound that no one presently occupies. It is only maidservants who go to clean it."

Her words had barely settled when a gust of wind carried the sounds from that small courtyard clearly to them all. And what those sounds were was something entirely unfit for polite company.

The faces of every woman in the group changed at once.

Among them was one whose husband was a political rival of Xie Jingyu's. Both men held fifth-rank positions and were competing for the same promotion above the fifth rank.

The Xie family had no particular advantage now, it was true, but who could say for certain?

She spoke up: "That is a very strange sound. Let us go and see."

She led the way toward the source.

Yun Chu smiled faintly.

She had specifically suggested to Xie Ping that Lady Yuan be added to the guest list. Lady Yuan had not disappointed her expectations.

Lady Yuan, a woman of forty or fifty years, was quite capable of discerning what kind of sounds those were. Seeing Lady Yuan lead the group toward that direction, she was genuinely alarmed.

Yun Chu gave her mother-in-law a light, quiet pull and said in a low voice, "The Xie household's servants would not dare this kind of thing in broad daylight. If we prevent these ladies from having a look, who knows what they will make up about the Xie family's inner court afterward. Letting them look is the better option."

This was a reasonable argument. And it was the old matriarch's birthday banquet; all the servants were fully occupied with it, and none of them could possibly have time to sneak away here for something like this.

There is nothing there to see. If she acts cagey and guarded, she would only invite the story that the Xie family's inner court is a place of scandalous disorder.

At this thought, Lady Yuan steadied considerably, and with Yun Chu looking perfectly composed beside her, she felt as though she had something solid to stand on. She smiled: "It is probably wild cats making their noise."

A dozen or so people walked a short distance and reached the unoccupied little courtyard.

As they entered, the sounds became unmistakable, enough to make several of the younger, more recently married ladies flush and lower their eyes.

"This would be the first time I have heard wild cats carrying on like this," Lady Yuan said briskly. She stepped up onto the raised threshold, reached out, and shoved the door open. "Let us see what sort of wild cat this might be."

The door swung open, and what the assembled women saw clearly was a man and a woman on the couch inside, their clothing half-removed, entangled together.

When the faces of that man and woman became clear, Lady Yuan was rooted to the spot, the sound of thunder detonating in her mind, and she nearly fainted then and there.

Several of the younger ladies with more delicate sensibilities stumbled backward in retreat.

For women of Lady Yuan's age and experience there was nothing in the world so very shocking. She began to speak at once, in a voice heard by everyone.

"Is that not Master Xie!"

"On the old matriarch's own birthday, what is Master Xie doing here in a corner of the compound with one of the household's serving girls?"

"We noticed Master Xie's absence during the banquet, and it turns out he was back here carrying on with a servant woman, all in a tangle, with no sense of propriety. Had we come a little later..."

Several of the ladies looked at Xie Jingyu with contempt, and at Yun Chu with a great deal of sympathy.

Yun Chu stood as though she could not believe what she was seeing, utterly motionless and unresponsive, until Lady Yuan gave her a tug.

Lady Yuan's voice was trembling: "Chu'er, what do we do, what are we to do..."

Yun Chu seemed to come back to herself at last. She moved quickly up the steps, bent down, picked up the clothing from the floor, and draped it over both Xie Jingyu and the He woman.

Positioning herself in front of them, she looked out at the gathered ladies and said, "Our guests have misunderstood. This woman is not a serving girl of the Xie household. She is Concubine He. She has a gift for singing, and I had asked her earlier to go to the front courtyard and sing to entertain the guests. But she is in poor health, and I expect she was taken ill partway there, so my husband brought her here to rest..."

Lady Yuan's violently trembling heart finally steadied a little.

A concubine was one thing; having the encounter be with a serving girl would have been another matter entirely.

Once again she was struck with admiration for this daughter-in-law. Even in chaos this complete, she could still think up a reason to smooth it over. The Xie family truly could not do without Yun Chu.

But this excuse only made the assembled ladies feel more sympathy for Yun Chu than before.

A husband, together with a concubine, in this far corner of the estate during the banquet, wrapped together like this. He had given his official wife no shred of dignity whatsoever.

They had all heard that Mistress Xie could not have children, and now even her husband's basic respect had been taken from her. One could only imagine how difficult such a life must be.

Here she was, clearly devastated and in anguish, and yet she still had to come forward to protect her husband's face and the Xie family's reputation. The treasured daughter of the Yun general's household had been reduced to this...

"I expect Mistress Xie still has a great deal to attend to. We will take our leave."

"Mistress Xie, do take care of yourself. We shall gather again another day."

The ladies, with admirable tact, made their excuses one after another.

When they reached the front courtyard, the ladies still watching the opera had no idea what had happened, but looks were being exchanged all around, and so one by one everyone offered their farewells.

Once outside the Xie residence, the ladies finally felt free to speak openly.

"Those of you who stayed for the opera haven't heard what happened. We caught Master Xie in the act with one of his concubines in the back courtyard."

"In broad daylight, hiding away to do such things. Was there really no other time available?"

"That concubine must be outstandingly beautiful, or Master Xie would not have been so reckless."

"Now that you mention it, I recall that concubine looking somewhat mature in years. Not particularly striking in appearance, either. Quite inferior to Mistress Xie in every respect."

"So it seems Master Xie has a particular taste for older women..."

When word of what had happened in the back courtyard reached the old matriarch, her head rang so violently with shock and fury she nearly fainted on the spot.

Lady Lin of the Yun family's face had gone dark as still water, the kind of calm that preceded an eruption.

She knew of Concubine Yu, Concubine Jiang, and Concubine Tao. When had a Concubine He entered the picture?

And Xie Jingyu, on the day of his grandmother's birthday banquet, had been caught in a compromising position with a woman, and had her own daughter come forward to make excuses on his behalf.

What a world of humiliation her daughter must have swallowed.

"Mother, go home first," Yun Chu said, personally seeing the Yun family out. "Sister-in-law, please take good care of my mother. I am fine."

Liu Qianqian's gaze was full of worry.

The men of the Yun family also took concubines, but taking a concubine required the official wife's consent, and nothing would occur before that. This was a complete and utter disregard for the official wife.

And Xie Jingyu had behaved like this even with members of the Yun family present at the estate today. What it must be like for Yun Chu to live here under ordinary circumstances, one could only imagine...

chapters.title: Who Could Have Planned Against You
chapters.content:
When the guests had all departed.

In the now-empty courtyard, only the Xie family remained.

Though the old Xie matriarch was ordinarily in robust health for her age, falling ill rarely, she was now slumped in her reclining chair, utterly without strength in her body.

"You reckless, contemptible creature!"

The old matriarch looked at the two kneeling before her and hurled a teacup down at them.

The shards of porcelain sliced open the side of Xie Jingyu's face. It seemed to bring him back to himself; the fog that had clouded his mind lifted suddenly, and his memories of just before it descended came rushing in.

He clenched his fist: "Grandmother, I was set up."

The He woman was also gradually recovering her senses. All she could remember was that she had been pulled by Xie Jingyu to a small courtyard beside the artificial hill to talk. As they were talking, the two of them had quarreled.

Not wanting to have a complete falling-out with Xie Jingyu, she had reached for the teapot on the table and poured a cup, handing it to him.

The two of them sat face to face drinking tea, and then... then she could not remember anything after that. She had only the faintest, hazy recollection of having been with Xie Jingyu in the full heat of something, with the banquet guests standing around them...

She also remembered being addressed as Concubine He.

"A setup?" The old matriarch sat upright. "Who would bother to set you up?"

"Naturally it would be the He woman," Concubine Tao said, placing both hands over her heavily swollen belly, her voice cool. "Who in this household doesn't know that Mama He has harbored feelings for the master that she ought not to have? Drugging the master in a situation like this, isn't it just her plan to make a done thing of it, to turn herself from a servant into a mistress?"

The He woman opened her mouth at once: "It was not me. I did not set the master up. And I never wanted to become a concubine..."

"If not you, then who?" The old matriarch's eyes looked as though fire might shoot from them at any moment. Though she knew, privately, that the He woman had never harbored ambitions to become a concubine, the Xie family had been brought to such bitter disgrace today, and it was all because the He woman refused to stay in her place. If she had stayed quietly in the little temple where she was confined, none of this would have happened.

Xie Jingyu was silent for a long moment before saying: "The Yuan family."

He and Lord Yuan were both fifth-rank officials in the Ministry of Revenue. Lord Yuan had been in this position for over a decade and was approaching forty, and had never had the opportunity to advance. Now a position above the fifth rank had opened up, and it had been all but certain to go to Xie Jingyu himself, until Lord Yu had inexplicably withdrawn his favor, and then with the rumors that had swept through the capital involving the Xie and Yun families, the position had suddenly become anyone's to claim.

If word of his intimate entanglement with a household servant spread to the court, he suspected any promotion was out of the question for the next five or six years.

Lord Yuan must have seized on this chance to stamp him down and eliminate him from the running entirely.

The He woman pressed her lips together.

She had a persistent feeling that the Yuan family's reach did not extend quite this far. She felt as though someone within the Xie household had planned this against her. Of those with the capability to do such a thing, only a few of the concubines and the mistress herself would qualify. But none of them should have had any motive to bring another woman to the master's side. No reason to act.

Think as she might, she could not identify whose hand she had fallen into.

"Pursuing whose fault it is at this moment is entirely pointless. The immediate concern is to find a way to minimize the damage," Yun Chu said, evenly. "An official of the court found together with a serving girl of the household, on his grandmother's birthday banquet: if word of this reaches the censors, my husband would not merely miss the promotion, he might be demoted and stripped of real power... It was precisely with this in mind that I called Concubine He by the title of Concubine He before those ladies, so as not to give anyone grounds for further talk. In order to keep our story consistent now, the name He should be formally entered in the Xie household's register without delay..."

Lady Yuan let out a long sigh of relief: "Chu'er, you have thought of everything."

"No. I will not be a concubine," the He woman said, her face gone white. "Mistress, I never wanted to be a concubine."

Concubine Tao looked frightened: "The He woman once attempted to harm my unborn child. If she becomes a concubine, my child's life will be in danger."

Xie Jingyu said: "The He woman cannot become a concubine."

Concubines Jiang, Tao, and Yu, along with Ting Yu, each allowed a flicker of relief to cross their faces.

They had always known it. The He woman was no longer young, no longer particularly appealing. The master had no genuine regard for her, and no amount of self-promotion would win her even a sliver of his care.

Yun Chu felt increasingly certain that the He woman's background held something of consequence.

The more stubbornly the He woman resisted the role of concubine, the more Yun Chu needed to place her firmly in it. Otherwise, what had she arranged all of this for?

She said, "Does my husband have a better proposal, then?"

Xie Jingyu pressed his lips together.

He could not think of a second option.

"I do have one other solution," Yun Chu said, pausing briefly. "Have Mama He take a cup of poison and be done with it. The matter would pass naturally."

The He woman crumpled to the floor outright.

Xie Jingyu's lips were pressed so firmly together they were white, and he fell into deep and difficult deliberation.

The old matriarch said in a hard voice, "Concubinage or the cup. Your choice."

Lady Yuan could genuinely not understand: "He woman, you have feelings for Jingyu, and yet you will not agree to become his concubine. Is being a concubine some form of unbearable suffering?"

The He woman was shaking throughout. Tears welled in her eyes, and she looked toward Xie Jingyu with desperate, pleading uncertainty.

Xie Jingyu closed his eyes briefly and said quietly: "Then have Concubine He entered in the Xie family genealogy register."

Under the current dynasty, even concubines could be entered in the family register, a practice that had come about centuries ago when a renowned Lady of National Protection had greatly elevated the status of women as a whole.

Yun Chu stepped forward and helped the He woman to her feet: "Concubine He, from now on we serve the master together as members of one household. We are family. What is your birth name?"

The He woman was still deep in a state of bewildered distress. Out of sheer instinct, she answered: "He Lingying."

Yun Chu wore a light smile: "The father-in-law is ordinarily very busy; there is no need to ask him to return to the house specifically for this occasion. Husband, why are you still kneeling? Come, let us go open the ancestral hall and have the genealogy register brought out, to record Concubine He's entry."

Xie Jingyu struggled to his feet with some difficulty.

His movements were unsteady; he could barely keep his balance.

Yun Chu took a slight step to the side, mostly out of concern that Xie Jingyu might sway and land on her, as she had no particular wish to wash herself several extra times that evening.

She turned and walked out ahead.

Watching her retreating figure, Concubine Tao let out a quiet sigh. How was it that she could never manage to be as unflappable as the mistress? The mere thought of another woman by the master's side made her chest feel as though it were being pierced with pins. Her one consolation was that she was carrying a child now, which gave her at least some foundation. And the He woman was not young; conceiving would likely prove difficult. Given enough time, the master would probably forget this woman entirely.

Yun Chu and Xie Jingyu left the courtyard together with the He woman.

The moment they had gone, the old matriarch said sharply, "Bring that man with the surname He before me."

Mama Zhou had long had He Xu waiting to the side, anticipating this moment. With the matter among the household's principals now settled, it was He Xu's turn to face reckoning.

Mama Zhou pressed He Xu to his knees before the old matriarch and produced a large bundle: "Old Matriarch, this was found in He Xu's room."

The old matriarch looked inside. It was silver, white and gleaming, amounting to several hundred taels.

"You audacious wretch!" The old matriarch aimed a kick at him in fury.

He Xu had come into the Xie household with the He woman all those years ago, presenting himself as her clansman and elder brother, and so had been given some accommodation. That connection had allowed him to rise, in four or five years, to a senior steward's post with real authority in the outer household. The Xie family had treated these two siblings with generosity, and yet the two of them had turned around and worked together to undermine the household: one inflicting humiliation of the worst kind upon the Xie family, the other quietly skimming silver from the household's funds.

Mama Zhou continued: "This servant also checked with several shops just now and learned that the shops Steward He has been managing have been running at a loss for half a month."

Those shops were on the main commercial street, and there was no earthly way they should have been running at a loss. It was abundantly clear that He Xu had been pocketing the takings.

"Give him twenty strokes of the rod and throw him out!" The old matriarch's head was ready to burst. "He is never to set foot in the Xie household again!"

He Xu's mouth was stuffed and he made muffled sounds of protest, but four broad-shouldered serving women pinned him down and landed twenty strokes across his back. A grown man, and he went limp with the pain and lost consciousness. He was then hauled out and left in front of a derelict temple on the outskirts of the city where beggars gathered.

chapters.title: What Am I to Do
