chapters.content:
With Xie Jingyu as the head of the Xie household, it was most fitting for him to open the ancestral hall and bring out the genealogy register.

The entire process was very simple: write the He woman's name in the register, offer incense, and perform the ritual obeisance. From this moment forward, the He woman was a formal member of the Xie household.

Yun Chu spoke with a pleasant expression: "Concubine He may take up residence in the Bihe Garden."

The He woman was somewhat surprised.

Bihe Garden sat adjacent to the Xie family's garden, one of the finest locations in the compound, ordinarily used to receive distinguished guests. She had not expected the mistress to give it to her.

Xie Jingyu's expression was layered with complexity.

He found his thoughts going back four years, when Yun Chu had been heavy with child and he had crept into Ting Yu's bed. He still remembered Yun Chu's face that morning: the loss in her eyes, the hurt, the anguish, the disbelief. And he had sensed, very clearly, that Yun Chu had cared deeply about him then.

But now, from first to last, she wore a light smile that revealed nothing, no disappointment in him, no animosity toward the He woman.

She seemed, entirely, not to care about him at all anymore.

Something swelled in Xie Jingyu's chest that he could not quite name.

"I imagine my husband and Concubine He have matters still to discuss between themselves. I will go and attend to other things."

Yun Chu gave a slight curtsy and turned to walk out of the ancestral hall.

After her figure disappeared through the doorway, the He woman opened her mouth to speak, and received a resounding slap across the face from Xie Jingyu before she could say a word.

The blow left the He woman stunned.

She pressed her hand to her cheek: "It was not me. Truly it was not me. I know my own station. I would never have dared to aspire to become a member of the Xie family..."

"I know it was not you. But if not for you, I would not be in ruins," Xie Jingyu said. He could already picture in full the manner in which people at court would look at him the following day, and drew a long breath. "It was you who gave the Yuan family their opening to act against me. It is you who has blocked my path to advancement..."

The He woman's tears fell steadily.

She could not believe it. She had been struck across the face by the man she loved most. Her heart was in genuine agony.

But she knew that if this matter was not properly explained, the day she became a concubine would be the day their bond cracked apart beyond repair.

"Master, are you truly certain it was the Yuan family?" the He woman said, her voice choked. "Why have you not considered that the mistress may have planned all of this? She is the official mistress of this household. The entire Xie compound is under her management. For her to arrange something like this would be simplicity itself. Otherwise, how do you explain the mistress lifting my confinement today? How do you explain her leading so many people directly to that small courtyard?"

Xie Jingyu's face showed a cold smile: "Your meaning is that Yun Chu arranged all of this so that you could become a concubine?"

A wife, no matter how little regard she had for her husband, would surely never arrange for her husband to be caught in flagrante with another woman in full public view.

"Yun Chu was broad-minded enough to accept you, and yet you repay her with nothing but suspicion." Xie Jingyu turned away sharply. "If you create any further trouble in this household, the Xie family will not keep you."

He said this and walked out.

The He woman crumpled entirely onto the floor, covering her face as she wept.

Yun Chu walked slowly back to her own courtyard. She had only just stepped through the entrance when someone dropped to their knees in front of her.

It was Xie Ping.

Her face was a picture of terror, and she clutched the hem of Yun Chu's skirt: "Mother, what am I to do? My reputation is entirely ruined. What am I to do..."

She had made a mess of the Xie family's banquet, and every time anyone spoke of this occasion in the future, they would think of the Xie family's eldest young miss. What family would ever want to take her as their official mistress?

She had once even entertained hopes of becoming the Fourth Prince's consort. Now every one of those hopes had crumbled to nothing.

"Mother, help me..."

Xie Ping wept until she could barely breathe.

Yun Chu helped her to her feet: "Ping'er, did I not tell you once before? You are still young. Making a mistake is not the end of it; correcting yourself earnestly is what matters."

Xie Ping cried: "Mother, tell me. How do I correct it?"

"The turnaround, at the latest, would have to come at next year's birthday banquet for the old matriarch. So you would need to wait one year." Yun Chu said, looking at her with a smile. "Think carefully: what occasion might the Xie family have for a banquet in the nearer future?"

Xie Ping stopped crying and began to think in earnest.

The old matriarch was still living, which meant neither grandfather nor grandmother could hold a birthday banquet. There could be no flower-viewing gathering either. Would a tea party work?

But the Xie family's standing was so modest, and matters were in such a poor state, that no one of any consequence would come to a tea party.

"Shi'an'er's prefectural examination is coming up very soon," Yun Chu said. "If he were to pass and become a shengyuan, would the Xie family not then have cause to hold a banquet?"

Xie Ping's expression shifted with a trace of uncertainty. A shengyuan degree was common enough; holding a banquet for it would only invite ridicule.

"A shengyuan degree may be commonplace, but a top ranking in the examination is not," Yun Chu said with a smile. "If a household's child took first place in the prefectural examinations anywhere in the capital, who would not hold a grand celebration?"

Xie Ping's eyes went wide: "Mother, I understand."

For the sake of the Xie family's name, for the sake of her own name, Xie Shi'an must take first place in the prefectural examinations. There was no second option.

Yun Chu's thoughts drifted to her previous life. When Xie Shi'an had taken first place, Xie Jingyu had just been promoted to the rank above fifth, and father and son had toasted the guests at the banquet with complete and confident ease.

It had been a long day, and by now the sky had gone entirely dark.

In the quiet that followed, the child's face floated once more to the surface of her mind.

She went quickly to the inner chamber, where the very ugly wood carving sat on the table by the window. She took it in her hand, and the restlessness in her chest settled a little.

She slept well that night.

She woke in the morning to a clear sky. Spring was retreating gradually; there was already something of early summer in the air.

Xie Shi'an was the first to come for the morning greeting, his manner entirely composed, as though the events of the day before had left no impression on him at all.

When the morning greetings were done, he went to the academy to study. Then the concubines arrived with the younger children.

This was the first morning greeting since the He woman had formally become Xie Jingyu's concubine.

"Concubine He's complexion is looking rather well," Concubine Tao said from her seat, with a transparent air of deliberate provocation. "The Bihe Garden must have excellent fengshui."

Ting Yu felt genuinely put out. The courtyard she had been given when she first arrived had not even had a proper name. What was so deserving about the He woman that she got the Bihe Garden, while she and Yun'er were housed in the most out-of-the-way corner of the entire compound?

All manner of thoughts in her mind, she kept her face pleasant and said, "The master must be quite taken with Concubine He."

No matter what the various concubines said, the He woman remained silent, her head down, standing properly and correctly to the side.

Yun Chu said, "As it happens, the household is about to have summer garments made. I will have two serving women come and take Concubine He's measurements later, four complete sets for spring, summer, autumn, and winter."

The moment the He woman raised her head, she found herself looking directly into the unfriendly eyes of the other three concubines, and did not dare accept the offer, hastening immediately to decline.

Yun Chu continued: "You are half a mistress of the Xie household now. Dressing too poorly reflects poorly on the master. What is yours to accept, accept it. Pushing it back and forth like this is rather small-minded."

The He woman could only say, "Thank you, mistress."

When the exchange was done, Yun Chu dismissed them all with a wave of her hand.

As they were leaving, Ting Yu looked around carefully and saw no sign of a child anywhere. She decided that Yun'er must have been seeing things.

Ting Feng stood to the side and said, with poorly concealed indignation, "Mistress, that He woman deliberately threw herself at the master, and yet you are this kind to her?"

"You are not to call her 'the He woman' going forward. She is Concubine He now," Ting Shuang said. "The mistress has her own plans. You, a maidservant, need not concern yourself with it. Go to the front courtyard and see if Chen Bo has arrived yet."

She knew perfectly well why the mistress was treating Concubine He with such consideration. The higher the mistress elevated her, the harder Concubine He's days in this household would become.

chapters.title: I Will Not Seek Separation
chapters.content:
Ting Shuang relayed the gossip she had gathered from outside to Yun Chu.

"By last night the Xie family's affairs had spread all through the capital. Everyone is saying that Xie Jingyu of the Ministry of Revenue has an appetite for women, and that on his grandmother's own birthday he was caught in broad daylight carrying on with a concubine. They also say the concubine is rather old, and not particularly attractive, and that Master Xie has unusual tastes... In short, people everywhere are talking about the Xie family. The master's reputation is thoroughly ruined. And naturally the word is also out that the eldest young miss lacks the skill to manage a household."

Yun Chu asked: "What is the old matriarch's reaction?"

"Word has it she began smashing things in her room first thing this morning, and every servant waiting on her has been frightened into silence," Ting Shuang said quietly. "A physician was also sent for this morning. He says the old matriarch is suffering from excessive agitation of the liver, and has prescribed quite a few remedies."

"With the gossip about the Xie family spreading everywhere, would the old matriarch not simply fall more and more ill?" Ting Xue fretted. "When that happens, will it not be our mistress who has to go and nurse her?"

Ting Shuang shook her head: "Last night the Prince of Pingxi returned to the capital with seventy or eighty bandits in chains. Everyone's attention in the city has been drawn away by that. There is a new sensation every day in the capital; within ten days people will have forgotten all about the Xie family's business, and the old matriarch will naturally recover on her own."

Just then, Ting Feng came in with Chen Defu from the front courtyard.

"Greetings to the mistress," Chen Defu said, bowing. "Last night, following the mistress's instructions, this servant went to the derelict temple outside the city and found He Xu there just as expected. His back end had been beaten raw, and the beggars at the temple had stripped the clothes off his body. He was lying outside completely bare. Left like that with no one to help him, he likely would not have survived three days. This servant brought him into the city, found an inn, and had a physician come to treat his wounds. He woke this morning."

Yun Chu closed the lid of her tea bowl and said: "Chen Bo, please continue taking good care of He Xu, and when a suitable moment presents itself, have him introduced to the gambling houses."

He Xu was an inveterate gambler. He had been running small gambling games inside the compound and gathering manservants to play with him every day. She did not believe He Xu could resist the lure of a proper gambling house.

She went on: "The name He Lingying, please look into it carefully. Report back to me on any trace you find, no matter how small."

Chen Defu lowered his head in acceptance: "Yes, mistress."

After Chen Defu left, Ting Shuang said softly, "Does the mistress suspect that Concubine He's background is not what it appears?"

Yun Chu did not conceal it from her: "Concubine He may be the daughter of a condemned family. Only, in the past fifty years or so, no Xie clan has been among those in the capital whose households were confiscated or who were sent into exile, so I am not entirely sure whether my suspicion is correct."

Ting Shuang's eyes went perfectly round.

If Concubine He was from a condemned family, the law required that such women and their descendants serve in the pleasure quarters for all generations. Yet the Xie household had now taken her in as a concubine.

The consequences of that were something she did not dare to contemplate.

And Concubine He becoming a concubine of the Xie household had been something the mistress had engineered herself.

The mistress was placing herself in opposition to the entire Xie household.

Ting Shuang broke out in a cold sweat: "Mistress, please go to the Yun family and discuss this with the eldest young master first."

Yun Chu asked: "Discuss what?"

"You are standing against the entire Xie household..." Ting Shuang's voice fell as low as it could go. "Why? Why?"

She had always imagined the mistress was only having Concubine He become a concubine in order to hold a better grip over her. She had not imagined in her worst moments that the truth was something a hundred times more alarming.

Yun Chu said: "Xie Jingyu is not a worthy husband. I have endured him for four years. I cannot endure him any longer."

Ting Shuang's tears began to fall: "Then please go back to the Yun family and ask the old general to come forward and arrange a separation between the mistress and the master."

"No. I will not seek a separation," Yun Chu said, with a faint smile. "I will not leave the Xie household."

She would not give the Xie family any chance of rising. She intended to watch the Xie household come apart, piece by piece, with her own eyes.

Just then, the serving women who had come to report on household matters stepped into the room, saw Ting Shuang weeping in a flood of tears, and were quite taken aback.

The serving women were already cautious in the presence of their official mistress, and now that the most authoritative of the great maidservants had been reduced to tears before her, every last one of them was on their best behavior, and they laid out everything that had gone on in the household during the time of the mistress's illness, one matter after another, without holding anything back.

Yun Chu gave her instructions in a cool tone.

She sat in the seat of authority, her manner composed and unhurried, and yet the serving women found her presence peculiarly reassuring. With the mistress here, even if something went wrong, there was always a way to address it. It was nothing like having the eldest young miss in charge: a heap of things dispatched with no rhyme or reason, leaving everyone without any idea of what to do first.

When the serving women had withdrawn, Yun Chu had a carriage prepared and went to call on the Yun family.

After everything that had happened at the Xie household the previous day, her family must have spent the whole night without sleep. She had to go in person.

She had only just reached the gate of the Yun residence when the guards hurried inside to announce her, and in a moment Lady Lin and Yun Ze came out quickly to receive her.

"Mother. Elder brother." Yun Chu said, her manner easy. "I heard the Prince of Pingxi has returned to the capital after routing the bandits. Why is my brother not over at the Prince of Pingxi's residence to offer congratulations?"

Yun Ze's face was not in a good way: "Something this significant has happened to you, and you ask me how I have the heart to go to the Prince of Pingxi's residence. Do you have any idea how worried Mother has been all night?"

"It is only that Xie Jingyu has taken another concubine. There is no need for Mother to worry over a small thing like this," Yun Chu said, taking Lady Lin's arm with a smile. "For me, one concubine more or one concubine less makes no difference."

Lady Lin felt the pain of it like a knife turning in her chest: "Chu'er, this match was one I selected for you with the greatest care, and yet it turned out to be such a heartless and ungrateful wretch. He is a man of no family background who, within five short years, rose from the seventh rank to the full fifth rank entirely through the backing of our Yun family. How dare he treat you with such contempt. Your brother and I have discussed it. We want you to separate from Xie Jingyu. You are still young..."

"Mother, please do not raise the subject of separation again," Yun Chu said, looking at her seriously. "My days with Xie Jingyu are not without their ability to continue. And I am willing to continue them."

Her gaze was steady. There was not a trace of hesitation or inner conflict in it.

Lady Lin let out a long sigh.

Yun Ze said nothing more either.

He was only a seventh-rank official at present, but he bore the surname Yun, and that alone made his position unlike any ordinary seventh-rank official's.

He would do what needed to be done, so that Xie Jingyu could feel, firsthand, the difference between having the Yun family's support and losing it. Whether the Xie household could still hold its ground in the capital without the Yun family standing behind it was a question worth asking.

To dare treat his sister with contempt was to invite consequences.

"Enough of this subject," Yun Ze said, his voice warm. "Your sister-in-law made a restorative broth herself. You must drink a good deal of it when we sit down."

Lady Lin took her by the arm and walked her toward the main hall: "Wait just a little while longer. Your father will be returning to the capital soon. When he does, I will have your father invite Xie Jingyu for a drink."

Yun Chu's face lit up with genuine delight: "Father is coming back to the capital?"

In her previous life, when the Yun family fell, her father had been seized from the front lines and thrown directly into the prison below the court. She had spent every last resource she had trying to see her father one final time, and had not succeeded.

Counting the years, she and her father had been apart for at least ten.

"Look at you light up," Lady Lin also smiled. "Your father is most fond of you. If he knew the grievances you have been suffering at the Xie household, the Xie family would have a great deal to answer for."

Yun Chu spent the time in good spirits, ate midday meal at home, and then prepared to return to the Xie compound.

Yun Ze saw her out personally, saying as he walked her, "Chu'er, I am your own full brother. There is nothing you should ever hide from me."

"I know, elder brother," Yun Chu said, laughing the way she used to when she was small, without any restraint. "I just hope my brother doesn't come to find me a nuisance, that is all. It is getting late. I must be going."

She was just about to board the carriage when a carriage came from around the corner of the lane and blocked the way out.

The curtain was lifted, and a man in a black brocade robe jumped down from inside.

Yun Ze and Yun Chu quickly bowed: "Greetings to the Marquis of Xuanwu."

The man who had arrived was none other than Qin Mingheng, the Marquis of Xuanwu.

chapters.title: The Marquis Picks Up a Handkerchief
chapters.content:
"Lord Yun, Madam Xie."

Qin Mingheng greeted them each in turn, his gaze sweeping over Yun Chu with its usual composure.

Yun Ze spoke up: "Allow me to see my sister to her carriage first. I apologize for making the Marquis wait a moment."

Qin Mingheng stepped aside. "Not at all."

Yun Chu gave Qin Mingheng a small nod, then took Tingshuang's hand and boarded the carriage. Yun Ze remained where he stood, watching until the carriage disappeared down the main road. Only then did he turn back to Qin Mingheng. "Marquis, after you."

Qin Mingheng's brow furrowed slightly. "Lord Yun, I've just recalled an urgent matter I must attend to. Shall we discuss that business again at this same hour tomorrow?"

Yun Ze clasped his hands in a bow and watched Qin Mingheng board his carriage.

Once the carriage had moved beyond the boundary of the Yun estate, Qin Mingheng drew a white handkerchief from his sleeve.

When Yun Chu had stepped into her carriage a moment ago, the snow-white cloth had fluttered to the ground. His gaze had been trailing her the entire time, so he had been the first to move, sweeping it up and tucking it into his sleeve.

He lifted the handkerchief now and brought it to his nose. A look of quiet satisfaction spread across his face.

His thoughts drifted to that night five years ago: she had been dressed in red bridal robes, a red veil draped over her head, lying on his bed.

He had come so very close. One moment more, and he could have tasted her sweetness, could have taken her as his own...

The memory of what had happened five years ago brought a dark hatred flooding back across his features, and without realizing it, he tore the handkerchief clean in two.

The carriage drew to a gentle stop before the Xie residence.

Yun Chu reached into her sleeve out of habit, and found nothing. "Tingshuang, do you have my handkerchief?"

Tingshuang shook her head and searched everywhere she could, but the handkerchief was nowhere to be found.

"Never mind. It was just an ordinary handkerchief. If it's lost, it's lost."

Yun Chu waved a dismissive hand.

A handkerchief with no name embroidered on it was hardly a personal article. It didn't much matter if someone had picked it up.

In the days that followed, Yun Chu turned her attention to carefully sifting through the eligible young men of good standing, intent on finding a worthy husband for her half-sister Yun Ran.

Her grandfather and father had spent years campaigning on the battlefield and amassed great military distinction; her paternal aunt was a favored consort in the imperial palace. The Yun family was one of the foremost great houses in the capital, and precisely because of that, to avoid arousing the imperial family's wariness, Yun women could only marry down.

Marrying down, however, did not mean marrying just anyone. There were many considerations to weigh.

Having lived one life already, Yun Chu was well acquainted with how many things would unfold. There was no one better suited to choose a good match for her half-sister.

The capital was full of promising young men. After three or four days of deliberation, Yun Chu narrowed her choices to two families. She wrote their names on a slip of paper, folded it into an envelope, and had Tingshuang find a servant boy to deliver it to the Yun household.

It was not solely her decision to make. Her mother would still need to make inquiries about both families, and in the end, her half-sister would have to give her own consent.

With that settled, she returned to the courtyard to practice her horse stance.

Beyond the horse stance, Qiutong had also arranged a basic set of moves. As time went on, the intensity would increase gradually. Yun Chu did not find it tiring; if anything, the more she practiced, the more she wanted to. Perhaps, being the daughter of a military family, she had simply been born with a fondness for this sort of thing.

After training, she bathed, and Tingshuang came in to report: "Madam, Concubine Tao and Concubine He are requesting an audience."

Yun Chu knew perfectly well why those two had come to Shengju.

Ever since Lady He had become a concubine, Concubine Tao had made a habit of picking quarrels with her. The more Lady He yielded, the more Concubine Tao pressed.

Over the past few days, Lady He had been antagonized more times than she could count, and having reached the end of her patience, she had finally brought the matter to Yun Chu.

"Please, Madam, you must stand up for me." Lady He lowered her head. "Concubine Tao has gone too far. She bribed every single maidservant and matron in my courtyard..."

Concubine Tao replied without the slightest sign of agitation: "Madam, you may not be aware, but the entire Xie household knows that Concubine He rose from servant to mistress. Everyone talks behind her back. She and I both serve the Master, so we are like sisters, in a way. How could I stand by while such things were being said? I spent a little silver to make those maids and matrons hold their tongues. I was doing it for Concubine He's benefit. How could she come before Madam to speak ill of me?"

Lady He felt a sharp ache in her chest.

Since the day she had moved into Bihe Garden, there had been no peace: dead fish stuffed inside her bedding, every lamp and candle in her rooms made unusable, trouble with her food... She had watched carefully and discovered that the two maids and two matrons assigned to serve her had all been paid off by Concubine Tao to make her life miserable in these ways.

She held Xie Jingyu's instructions firmly in mind: she was not to cause any more trouble. So she had gritted her teeth and endured.

But that very morning, one of her serving maids had stolen her dressing case. There was no money inside; it held the dried umbilical cords and baby teeth of Ping'er, An'er, and Wei'er. She had kept them close always. Now they had been taken, and she had no way forward but to ask the Madam to restore order.

"Madam..." Lady He drew a deep breath. "I will say nothing of the rest. I only want Concubine Tao to return that case."

The moment she heard this, Concubine Tao dissolved into great heaving sobs. "Madam! I have done nothing but think of Concubine He's wellbeing, and now she accuses me of stealing her case. Since I fell with child, the Master has given me more jewelry than I can count. Who would covet her little box? Madam, I truly did not steal anything. Please, I beg you, stand up for me!"

Yun Chu took Concubine Tao's hand and spoke in a gentle voice. "Don't cry. Mind the child."

Concubine Tao wept on, and discreetly exchanged a glance with the maid at her side.

The maid immediately slipped out of the room.

Not long after, the little maidservant who served Lady He came running in. "Madam, Concubine He's case has been found under the bed. It seems Concubine He put it there herself and forgot."

Concubine Tao's weeping grew more wretched still. "And there you have it! Concubine He tries to harm my unborn child, and when I repay her unkindness with kindness she is still not satisfied. She has deliberately staged this entire scene to frame me for theft. Madam, I am utterly wronged..."

The corner of Yun Chu's mouth curved ever so slightly.

Concubine Tao's performance was truly too clumsy. Only someone willing to play along could allow it to continue like this. Any other mistress of the household would have had Concubine Tao punished long ago.

She gave Concubine Tao's hand a gentle pat, then turned a cool gaze on Lady He. "Concubine He, when you once schemed against the child in Concubine Tao's womb, the entire Xie household let it pass without a word, and even allowed you to become a mistress. Yet you have shown no remorse, and have laid hands on Concubine Tao again. If Concubine Tao were to suffer a fright and miscarry, what punishment would you deserve?"

Lady He felt she had been wronged to the depths of her soul, and she hurried to defend herself. "Madam, I..."

"Enough. There is no need for further words." Yun Chu cut her off. "For the next three months, your monthly allowance is to go directly to Concubine Tao, as a small comfort for the unborn fourth young master."

Lady He could not believe what she was hearing.

A concubine's monthly allowance was two taels of silver. That was her only income now, and all of it was to go to Concubine Tao. What was she supposed to live on?

But when she met Yun Chu's unwavering gaze, she understood that no protest she made would change anything. The Madam was clearly taking Concubine Tao's side.

Leaving Shengju, Lady He wrapped her arms around herself, feeling helpless.

Unless she had absolutely no other choice, she would not go to her three children for help.

Xie Jingyu had struck her across the face and was plainly tired of her. She would not humiliate herself by seeking anything from him.

Her brother, He Xu, had been beaten and thrown out by the Old Madam just a few days before. He was a worthless wretch she could not rely on.

Then she remembered: there was a sum of money in He Xu's hands, a full two thousand taels of silver. With money, she would not believe those maids and matrons would still choose Concubine Tao over her.

At this thought, Lady He hurried toward the outer gate of the residence.

chapters.title: He Xu Was Always a Gambler
chapters.content:
Lady He hurried to the front gate of the Xie residence.

She was stopped at once by the two servant boys on guard. "Without the Madam's permission, concubines from the inner quarters are not permitted to leave through the main gate."

Lady He knew this rule existed in the Xie household, but she had never imagined she herself would be bound by it.

To think that when she had been Matron He, serving always at the Master's side and enjoying his full trust, no one in the entire household had dared to show her anything less than full respect.

In those days, she could go wherever she liked within the Xie residence, and no one would dare stop her when she wished to go out. Everyone had addressed her respectfully as Matron He, and no one had ever dared show her a cold face.

Yet now that she had risen from servant to something between mistress and slave, she somehow commanded even less standing than she had as a bondwoman.

Before, she had thrived by leaning on the Master's favor. Now that the Master wanted nothing to do with her, she had only herself to rely on. She needed to get some silver in hand first, to bring those maids and matrons willingly to her side.

With this in mind, Lady He made her way back to Shengju.

After Tingshuang went in to announce her, she was brought into the side parlor.

Yun Chu set down the account book she had been reading. "What business does Concubine He have outside the residence? To my knowledge, you are from Jizhou, and your family is still there, yes? If you need to purchase something, there are servant boys and matrons here who can be sent with a word."

Lady He bowed her head. "I have a small sum deposited at a money house and wished to withdraw it. I would not feel at ease leaving such a matter to someone else."

"Money is indeed not something to be careless about." Yun Chu nodded. "All the same, it is not entirely safe for a woman to go out unaccompanied. I will have a driver appointed to you."

Lady He thanked her at once.

The carriage made its way to the bustling market district and stopped before the money house. Lady He told the driver to wait and went inside, circling through the premises and into a small lane at the side.

In that lane stood a small courtyard that belonged to her. When Xie Jingyu had first come to the capital with her and the children, before they had been permitted into the Xie residence, they had lived here for several years. He Xu had been thrown out of the Xie household and must have come here.

She reached the courtyard gate and tried her key, but it would not turn, no matter what she did.

An older woman she had once known well, who lived at the gate of the neighboring courtyard, called over to her: "Lady He, I haven't seen you in ages. I thought I'd never see you again once your courtyard was sold."

Lady He was startled. "I never sold this courtyard."

"That brother of yours brought someone from the estate agent's and sold it six months ago for just twelve hundred taels." The woman shook her head. "I meant to tell you beforehand, but I had no way of knowing where you lived. I ran into your brother on the street just half a month ago. He was hobnobbing with a bunch of gamblers. You'd best be careful, Lady He."

Lady He's heart sank.

That worthless brother of hers had sold the courtyard for next to nothing.

She had paid eighteen hundred taels for it originally. With land prices in the capital as high as they were now, it should have fetched around three thousand taels. He had the gall to let it go for twelve hundred.

Back in Jizhou, he had gambled every day. She had gone to great lengths to reform him, and he had promised her he would never set foot in a gambling house once they came to the capital. She had always believed he had kept his word. She never could have imagined he had sold the courtyard behind her back.

And the two thousand taels she had left in his keeping, she need not even wonder: surely those were gone as well.

Lady He forced a smile, exchanged a few pleasantries with the woman, and set off briskly for the capital's gambling dens.

She had barely reached the entrance when she saw a man being beaten, covering his head with his hands and pleading wildly for mercy.

"This is what happens when you borrow from us and don't pay back!" A hulking man hauled the figure on the ground to his feet and landed a hard punch. "This is just a little interest. If you don't return the money within three days, we'll start cutting off fingers!"

The onlookers scrambled backward in alarm.

Lady He let out a cry and rushed forward. "Let him go!"

The hulking man fixed her with a cold stare. "What is he to you? Pay off what he owes and we'll release him."

He Xu, seeming to have spotted a lifeline, shouted out: "I owe them two taels of silver, two taels turned into twenty with interest. Hurry up and pay them back for me!"

Lady He drew in a sharp breath.

Borrow two taels, repay twenty. What was that if not robbery?

Never mind twenty taels; she didn't have so much as twenty copper coins on her.

"You still have jewelry, don't you? Hand it over quickly, or I'll be beaten to death!"

The instant He Xu finished speaking, fists came raining down from the men around him, and within moments his face had swollen to the size of a steamed bun.

For all his faults, he was still her brother. Lady He did not have the heart to stand by while her own flesh and blood was set upon by a group, so she called out at once: "All right, all right. I'll pay his debt."

She removed the two jade bangles from her wrist, the hairpin from her hair, and a finger ring, and handed them all over.

The hulking man took the items and gave them a shake. "Smart enough. Call it settled. Now get out."

He Xu scrambled to his feet and pulled Lady He away.

"The one condition I set when I brought you to the capital was that you would never touch gambling again. And now you've lost everything. Can you face your own conscience?" Lady He could have gladly wrung his neck. "Go back to Jizhou right now. Don't stay here making trouble for me."

He Xu sneered. "So you've become a concubine in the Xie household and now you don't see me as your brother anymore? Give me money. I need to win my losses back."

Lady He's vision went dark. She nearly fainted.

Her courtyard was gone, the two thousand taels were gone, every piece of jewelry had been stripped from her, her last resources had been squandered completely, and she had said nothing about any of it. Yet this worthless man had the nerve to turn it around on her.

"This is all I have left. Take it, every last coin." Lady He flung the copper pieces to the ground. "As far as I'm concerned, I have no brother."

She turned and walked away.

She expected He Xu to come after her, but when she looked back, she saw her brother crouched on the ground, picking up the copper pieces one by one, and then heading back into the gambling den.

Lady He had never felt such despair. She should never have brought He Xu to the capital.

She could barely manage her own situation now. He Xu was beyond her. If the gamblers beat him to death, it would be no more than he deserved.

After Lady He had gone, a servant boy stepped out from around the corner and approached He Xu. "With just a few copper coins, Steward He, you won't get very far. Wouldn't it be better to borrow a bit more and try to win it back?"

He Xu sighed. "Those money houses all want property or jewelry as collateral before they'll lend."

"I know a place that accepts fingers and arms as collateral," the servant boy said persuasively. "One finger can get you ten taels of silver. Steward He is a very skilled gambler, just a little short on luck. Come a few more times, and I'm certain you'll win back those thousands of taels you lost..."

He Xu was visibly tempted, and followed the servant boy into a small lane nearby.

Tingfeng relayed every detail of this to Yun Chu.

Yun Chu was tending the incense. She stirred the ash and said in a flat, unhurried voice: "Fingers and arms are worth very little. Have someone tell him that if he uses the most important thing a man has as collateral, he can borrow two hundred taels."

Tingfeng stood rooted to the spot.

Tingshuang gave her a shove. "What are you waiting for? Go."

Yun Chu closed the incense burner. The clean, quiet fragrance of pine wood drifted through the room.

In her past life, Tingfeng and Tingxue had been violated by He Xu. She would therefore rid the world of that particular menace first, and ensure He Xu never had the chance to harm any woman again in this lifetime.

chapters.title: Learning Martial Arts Clears the Meridians
chapters.content:
Yun Chu continued her practice in the courtyard.

Qiutong instructed her carefully through the basic forms. When she finished the sequence, she was drenched in sweat.

"Mother..."

A figure appeared at the courtyard gate.

She wiped her face and looked up. It was Xie Shiwei.

She spoke in an even tone. "What brings Wei'er here?"

Since the last time she had administered household discipline to Xie Shiwei, he had stopped coming to her courtyard except for the morning greeting, which suited her fine. Out of sight, out of mind.

"Mother, I want to learn martial arts too."

Xie Shiwei walked in and summoned his courage to say it.

Since his last transgression, his food and clothing had been reduced by half. He went to bed slightly hungry every day and had no silver to spend.

He had come intending to admit fault and beg his mother's forgiveness, hoping she would restore things to how they were before.

But then he had seen his mother practicing, each movement and posture striking and precise, and he was suddenly seized by the urge to learn a few techniques himself.

He was no good at studying. His father scolded him daily, and the Old Madam and his grandmother always lectured him. He had come to believe he was truly hopeless.

But now he suddenly understood: he simply had no interest in books. That didn't mean he couldn't learn anything. He felt he might do well on the martial path, and perhaps not fall so far behind his elder brother.

Yun Chu looked down into Xie Shiwei's eyes.

This illegitimate son had not inherited Xie Jingyu's gift for scholarship, but he had a natural ferocity about him. In her past life, after he had entered the Yun family military camp, he had made company commander within a year. With the Yun family's backing, Xie Shiwei had advanced on the martial path with remarkable ease.

She would not give Xie Shiwei that opportunity again.

"It is rare that you have this kind of ambition. Then you shall learn alongside me." Yun Chu spoke in a warm tone. "Qiutong, begin by clearing his meridians."

Qiutong was a little surprised. The Madam surely knew that a beginner in martial arts needed only the horse stance to build up the body's foundation; clearing the meridians was something that came much later, and could not be forced open this early.

Tingshuang murmured to her, "Just follow the Madam's instruction."

Qiutong nodded, walked over to Xie Shiwei, and said, "Second Young Master, forgive the intrusion."

She took hold of his right arm and gave it a sharp downward pull. There was a crack, and Xie Shiwei let out a cry of pain, instinctively trying to pull away.

Qiutong gave him no chance. She found the meridian points along his arm, pressed down hard, and wrenched again.

"It hurts, it hurts, it hurts!" Xie Shiwei was drenched in sweat. "Let me go! Let go! I'm dying!"

Yun Chu settled into the rattan chair. "Your father told you to study properly. You said reading was too dull. The Old Madam doted on you and said nothing. Now you have come to me of your own accord and asked to learn martial arts. Since it was your own choice, there is no reason to give up halfway. Clearing the meridians before training is an exclusive method of my Yun family, and it is the very foundation on which my grandfather and father built their martial skill. I have always treated you as if you were my own son, so I will not hold anything back from you. It hurts a great deal at first, but grows easier with time."

Xie Shiwei's face had gone white with pain. "H-how long will the meridians need to be cleared?"

"Until you stop feeling pain. That is when it's done." Yun Chu's lips curved slightly. "My father took three months. My brother could not endure even a year of it and gave up the martial path entirely."

Xie Shiwei nearly collapsed right where he stood.

He managed to stammer: "What if I don't clear the meridians?"

"Without building the proper foundation, one can only ever be an ordinary fighter, fit only to serve as a common foot soldier on the battlefield." Yun Chu's voice was even. "To become a general like my grandfather or my father would be entirely out of the question."

Xie Shiwei stood in place, his lips pressed tight.

He wanted to learn martial arts, but the process was far too agonizing. At least three months, at the very least...

"Qiutong. Continue."

At Yun Chu's command, Qiutong lifted Xie Shiwei by the ankles, pulled off his shoes, and pressed her fingers hard into the acupuncture points on his soles.

Xie Shiwei's screams came one after another.

Lady He had just returned to the Xie residence and was on her way to the main courtyard to report back, but before she had even stepped inside, she heard her son's cries.

She rushed in, took one look at the scene before her, and said in alarm: "Madam, what has the Second Young Master done wrong?"

Tingshuang said, "The Second Young Master asked to learn martial arts with the Madam. She is clearing his meridians."

At these words, the blood rushed to Lady He's head.

The Madam had never looked kindly upon children who were not her own. If Wei'er was going to study martial arts under the Madam, he was walking straight into a trap. Truly, he had lost his mind.

Besides, studying was so much easier. Why suffer needlessly by learning to fight? Had anyone not noticed that of the Yun family's last generation there remained only one old general, and of the generation after, only Yun Chu's father? And in Yun Chu's own generation, the family was no longer sending their descendants down the martial path at all. That spoke clearly enough: it was not a road worth taking.

If even the Yun family had turned away from that path, and yet the Madam was sending her son down it, what could she possibly be thinking?

Yun Chu glanced up. "Concubine He, standing there without leaving... could it be that you also wish to learn martial arts?"

Lady He said quickly: "The Second Young Master looks tired. Perhaps he should rest a moment before continuing."

Yun Chu nodded, and Qiutong immediately released the boy. Xie Shiwei collapsed to the ground.

Lady He rushed over to check on her son.

Yun Chu rose from her chair. "Concubine He and Wei'er are close. Do stay and look after him for a while."

She turned and withdrew into the inner chamber, and all the maids followed after her.

Lady He seized the moment. "Wei'er, martial arts are useless, completely useless. Go tell the Madam you don't want to learn. Do it now."

Xie Shiwei had been put through the wringer, his voice hoarse from screaming. He had never been someone of firm resolve, and Lady He's words shattered what little remained: "But Mother said there's no giving up halfway."

"Just say you're willing to study properly. Isn't that enough?" Lady He helped him to his feet. "The Xie family is a family of scholars. Is it not right that the younger generation should study?"

Xie Shiwei pulled a long face. "But studying is so hard..."

"And is martial arts not hard? Look at yourself after just the first day. Will you have any peace going forward?" Lady He said with great feeling. "Some unnecessary suffering we simply don't have to take on. Be good."

They were still talking when Yun Chu stepped out from the inner room. "Wei'er, let us continue clearing the meridians. Qiutong used just one tenth of her strength before. She will now use five tenths. Are you ready?"

Xie Shiwei stumbled back a step in terror.

That small fraction of strength had already nearly killed him. If she increased it further, he really would die here.

"Mother, can I... can I stop learning...?"

Yun Chu's expression cooled. "No. You must continue. This was the path you chose. Qiutong, proceed."

Qiutong walked toward Xie Shiwei.

He burst into tears on the spot. "Mother, I was only curious. I wasn't really going to learn. I was wrong, I truly was wrong..."

Yun Chu frowned. "Learning is not a game. You cannot simply say you no longer wish to and be done with it."

"I'll study properly from now on, I promise." Xie Shiwei kept backing away. "Father said the Xie family passes down its legacy through scholarship, and every child must study. I'll do as Father says."

Yun Chu let the corner of her mouth lift.

Children this age were all the same: tell them to do something, and they wanted nothing to do with it.

For at least the next three to five years, Xie Shiwei would not bring up martial arts of his own accord again. And by the time he reached twelve, thirteen, or fourteen, taking up the martial path would be far, far more difficult.

After Lady He had seen Xie Shiwei back to his courtyard, she returned to her own Bihe Garden. The fallen leaves scattered across the courtyard had not been swept, and she felt a weariness that settled into her very bones.

She did not understand how it had come to this...

chapters.title: The Rules of the Gambling Den
chapters.content:
Lady He was not the kind of woman who accepted her fate.

When the entire family had hit rock bottom, had she not picked herself up and found her way back to the capital?

Twenty years ago, her mother had supported the whole family on embroidery alone. She too would use that same craft to establish herself in the Xie household.

Lady He found a way to buy silk thread and set about embroidering handkerchiefs with exceptionally intricate techniques.

Yun Chu instructed her people: "Buy some of He's handkerchiefs. Keep whichever ones have distinctive needlework. I have a use for them."

Tingshuang acknowledged the order and arranged for someone to make the purchase.

Lady He had not expected the handkerchiefs to sell so easily, and began thinking about embroidering larger, more valuable pieces, such as decorative screens.

One day, Chen Defu came hurrying in to report: "Madam, that He Xu has run up a debt of ten thousand taels and fled the capital. Old Servant has already arranged for four people to follow him. What are your orders from here?"

A cold smile curved Yun Chu's lips. "From here, naturally, we ensure that he is no longer capable of doing what men do."

Chen Defu hesitated. "But if we hand him over to those people, he may not survive..."

"Have a few men take care of it." Yun Chu's expression was as cold as ice. "He took the money, so he must pay the price. Is that not the rule of the gambling den?"

When He Xu had borrowed the money, a lien had been signed as collateral. Taking what the document specified was permitted under the laws of the current dynasty.

She was bent on revenge, but she would not cross the law.

Her grandfather had upheld the Yun family's integrity and reputation until his dying day. She, too, would not bring shame upon the Yun name.

The following afternoon, Chen Defu came again: "Madam, it is done. They gave him medicine; he pulled through. He is still on his way, heading for Jizhou."

Yun Chu nodded. "Have you found anyone by the name of He Lingying?"

Chen Defu shook his head. "There are not many people surnamed He in the capital, and no one by that name."

"Then have someone make further inquiries in Jizhou." Yun Chu rose, took a large box from the table, and handed it over. "Chen Bo has worked hard on my behalf these past days. This is a small token, some tea leaves. Please accept it."

Formerly, Chen Bo's mind had been wholly occupied with managing the shops. It was busy work, but his heart had been at ease. Now, though he appeared to have nothing pressing to do, the burden on his mind was considerable.

Chen Defu did not dare accept the gift and waved it away repeatedly.

He was a bondservant born into the Yun household; the Yun family had shown him great kindness. Handling matters for the Madam was only right and proper. How could he accept valuable tea leaves as payment?

"There is still much ahead that will require your help, Chen Bo. If you refuse, I will have no choice but to send you into retirement."

At that, Chen Bo could only take the tea.

Yun Chu continued by discussing the business of selling ice. Originally, Chen Defu had been purchasing large quantities of ice blocks under the guise of a southern merchant, without exposing the Yun family connection. Going forward, the plan was the same: arrange for a southerner to open an ice trading house in the capital, ready to open its doors to customers at the end of the fifth month.

All of this would be delegated to Chen Defu's people, so as not to reveal anyone's identity.

"The estates from my dowry sold at good prices." Yun Chu spoke up. "All together, the money is enough to buy one large manor."

The estates under her name had been yielding less and less each year. Selling them now would still fetch a reasonable price; waiting any longer would only diminish their value further.

Chen Defu looked up. "Old Servant knows of several large estates on the outskirts of the capital whose owners are looking to sell. Shall Old Servant go and make inquiries?"

Yun Chu shook her head. "I have my eye on the Wu family estate north of the city."

Chen Defu could not hide his shock.

Some twenty-odd years ago, the Wu family had been a rising great house in the capital. The family patriarch held an official position at court, and the family's commercial ventures had also been doing well. But then the Wu family members began falling ill one by one with a mysterious ailment, from the elders down to the children, none spared. To pay for treatment, they sold off asset after asset, and a great family that had seemed so solid simply ceased to exist. In the end, all that remained was the estate outside the city.

That estate was not especially large; it centered around a mountain, with a lake and a small wood, and had everything one might want. The last surviving member of the Wu family had sold it to the Zou family for twenty thousand taels.

The Zou family had no sooner taken possession of it than word spread of haunting. The Zou family's luck had seemed to suffer as well, and they had sold the estate at a loss without delay.

A merchant who did not believe in such things had purchased it next, and with the same result: the moment the estate changed hands, he was already looking for a middleman to unload it at whatever price he could get.

But everyone in the market who wanted an estate had heard the strange stories, and no one dared take it on. The estate had been left stranded in the merchant's hands ever since, without a buyer.

"That estate has been derelict for over twenty years now," Chen Defu said with a sigh. "The land there is fertile, very good for crops, with excellent harvests year after year. There's no telling how the ghost stories got started, and now a perfectly good estate has been ruined by them. Madam, might you consider looking at other properties? There are many better options."

Yun Chu thought back to her past life. Around the time she turned thirty, a fire had broken out at the Wu estate. The overgrown wild grass burned away, and only then did people discover that a vast natural hot spring lay hidden beneath. A consort's family from the palace had claimed it and proceeded to make a handsome profit from it every year.

As for the original ghost stories, they had long since been forgotten by the river of time.

Since she now possessed the advantage of foresight, she would not allow the estate to sit empty for so many more years.

She stood up. "Come. Let us go and take a look at the estate."

Chen Defu was alarmed. "Madam, you truly mean to buy that property? Please reconsider."

"The Zou family paid twenty thousand taels for it, and probably sold it to the merchant for around fifteen thousand. So how much do you think I can get it for?" Yun Chu smiled. "Price is not the concern. Let us first go and see what the haunting is actually about."

Though she had lived a second life, she still put no stock in such things. In her estimation, the haunting was very likely the work of human hands.

Chen Defu's brow furrowed deeply. "Madam, it is getting late. Might Old Servant arrange for a few Taoist priests to accompany us tomorrow instead?"

"Ghosts only come out at night." Yun Chu was already heading for the door. "Though we should certainly bring more people. Have all the stout manservants and matrons in the household come with us."

Not only Chen Defu, but Tingshuang was also rooted to the spot in astonishment.

She had known the Madam had grown considerably bolder of late, but not to this extent.

No household in all the capital dared take on that haunted estate, for fear of bringing misfortune upon their family. Yet the Madam was doing the very opposite.

Then again, the Madam was already positioned against the Xie family. Perhaps this was not so difficult to understand after all.

Tingshuang went out and gathered the stout matrons together, telling them they were going to the Madam's dowry estate to collect some things left behind. She did not dare mention the haunted property; if she did, not a soul would go.

The sun was sinking in the west as Yun Chu led the group out of the city.

When word of this reached the Old Madam, she could scarcely believe it. "I am lying sick in bed and she has not come to see me once, and now she goes out of the city at a time like this?"

Matron Zhou lowered her head. "The Madam sent ginseng this morning, which shows her regard."

The Old Madam knew Yun Chu had done what was required of her. She had rather liked this granddaughter-in-law before, but now she seemed to find fault with her at every turn.

She drank her medicine and leaned back against the bedboard. "So she has sold off all her estates?"

"Perhaps the Madam is short of silver," Matron Zhou offered.

"Ha. She took over twenty thousand taels from me some time ago. She is the wealthiest person in this household, and yet she is selling off her estates. A woman does not touch her dowry unless she has no other recourse." The Old Madam narrowed her eyes. "What does she want with so much money all of a sudden?"

"Old Servant suspects..." Matron Zhou lowered her voice. "The divine physician who came to treat the Empress has arrived in the capital. Old Servant imagines the Madam may be raising funds to seek treatment for herself. What woman does not wish for a child of her own?"

The Old Madam had heard of this physician as well. Because of his extraordinary skill, the demand for his consultations had become so great that he had raised his fee to an astronomical sum: reportedly five thousand taels just for a single examination, and for a full course of treatment, tens of thousands of taels could vanish in the blink of an eye.

Seen in that light, Yun Chu's behavior made a kind of sense. In any case, if she recovered and bore a child, it would still be of Xie blood. Let her do as she pleased.

chapters.title: There Is a Ghost in the Estate
chapters.content:
They made their way north of the city.

Beyond the city gate, the road turned rough. After nearly half a shichen, the sky had grown fully dark by the time they finally arrived at the estate gate.

The estate had been said to be haunted for more than twenty years. Apart from the farmers living nearby and the people hired to maintain the grounds, few others were well acquainted with the matter.

The stout manservants and matrons Yun Chu had brought with her, for instance, gazed curiously at the overgrown estate before them, puzzled as to why nothing had been planted there.

"Madam, the gateway is all weeds. There's no need for you to go in." Chen Defu spoke up. "Old Servant will take a few people and reconnoiter first."

Yun Chu studied the entrance to the estate carefully, and a smile slowly appeared on her lips. "At first glance, yes, it is all tangled overgrowth. But notice, Chen Bo: if you part the grass to the left and to the right, you will find a narrow path, nearly impossible to see. Someone inside must use this path to come and go."

Chen Defu stared in astonishment. "You mean someone actually dares to live in there?"

Yun Chu said nothing, only smiled.

People feared ghosts three parts; ghosts feared people seven parts. Even if there were truly a ghost, there was little reason to be afraid.

She went first, stepping into the parted grass. Her skirt snagged on the overgrowth; with every step forward, more threads were pulled loose, and before long one panel of the garment was ruined.

Chen Defu hurried ahead of her, stamping down the weeds to clear a path.

Tingshuang went in front with a lantern, while Tingfeng and Tingxue lifted the hem of Yun Chu's skirt on either side.

The matrons and manservants followed in a rustling crowd. It was only then that they began to sense something wrong: it was fully dark now, and not a single lamp had been lit anywhere in the estate.

Once inside, the weeds reached head height. Moonlight filtered down, tree shadows swayed, and little Tingxue, who frightened easily, had gone white as paper.

Chen Defu cleared a path with the others and led Yun Chu into the main hall, wiping down the chairs with his own robe before respectfully inviting her to be seated.

Tingshuang had even brought a pot of tea from the carriage, and now set it to brew there in the hall.

When the tea was ready and its fragrance filled the air, the night had grown even deeper.

Chen Defu, Tingshuang, and the rest gradually felt their courage return. With so many of them together, surely not even a fierce spirit would dare to show itself.

"There is more tea than we need. Let everyone have a few sips to wet their throats. We'll be getting to work shortly."

Yun Chu smiled and passed the tea around.

The matrons were accustomed to nothing but coarse tea; tea this fine and fragrant was a first for them all, and they helped themselves to several cups.

Before long, one of the matrons clutched her stomach. "Madam, would it be all right if Old Servant steps out to relieve herself? I'll be right back."

Yun Chu nodded. "It's dark out. Have two others go with you."

Two other matrons also needed to go, so the three of them went out together. Outside, the weeds were at head height in every direction, with no way to tell where anything was, least of all the privy. The three put their heads together and, finding a spot dense with vegetation, loosened their sashes and crouched down...

Then came the sound of rustling.

One of the matrons called out loudly: "We're over here! If you need to go, find somewhere else!"

But the footsteps drew closer...

Those sitting in the main hall heard the matrons' screams erupt, one after another.

Tingxue's whole face trembled. "There really is a ghost, isn't there..."

"Don't say that." Even Tingshuang's voice wavered slightly. "The Madam has sent Chen Bo out. Everything will be fine."

Before she had finished speaking, Chen Defu returned with the three matrons, two of whom had already fainted from fright. The third was babbling incoherently: "A ghost, a terrible ghost, with fangs this long, and it was going to eat us..."

The matron spoke, then rolled back her eyes and fainted as well.

Chen Defu reported: "Madam, by the time Old Servant and the others arrived, the thing had already fled. It was extraordinarily fast, and vanished into the trees. Gone completely."

The trees in the grove were tall and dense, the undergrowth thick; in the dark, with none of them familiar with the terrain, going in would mean getting lost immediately.

The matrons and manservants in the hall were badly shaken. None of them had expected there to truly be a ghost here, and thoughts of retreat stirred in every heart.

Yun Chu stood up. "Come. Let us go and have a look."

The manservants and matrons exchanged glances.

They could not understand it: was the Madam not afraid? How could she be so composed, without the slightest sign of alarm?

They could only say: a mistress was a mistress, beyond comparison with people like them.

With Yun Chu leading the way, the others found something to anchor themselves to, and their thoughts of retreat slowly faded. They gathered around her and moved outside.

Chen Defu and four manservants went ahead, and soon reached the spot where the three matrons had been. The grass in one direction had been flattened; they followed that direction and, after some fifteen or twenty steps, arrived at the edge of the small wood within the estate.

The grove was darker still, the trees denser. To enter was to risk losing one's way entirely, ghost or no ghost.

Yun Chu closed her eyes and breathed in deeply.

Before setting out, she had added a certain unnamed fragrance to the tea: something her mother had once created for pleasure during idle hours, which Yun Chu had always been fond of. She had discovered over time that it lingered extraordinarily well. Even when swallowed, it would pass through the body and emerge again, carrying the scent with it, and more powerfully so.

The matrons had drunk the tea, then relieved themselves. Whatever had passed by would certainly have picked up the scent.

Yun Chu inhaled for a moment, then opened her eyes and pointed due south. "Chen Bo. This way."

Chen Defu nodded and pressed forward with the four manservants.

There was no sign of any human passage here. But looking closely, one could see that the weeds bent with a consistent regularity in one direction, the mark of someone long accustomed to passing through without disturbing them.

Yun Chu led the group deep into the grove, where a thatched cottage came into view. Though it sat tucked in the heart of the wood, it looked tidy, and there was the lingering warmth of a cooking fire.

Chen Defu could not believe it. "So there truly is someone living here."

Tingfeng frowned. "Who would have the nerve to play at ghosts in this place? Chen Bo, let's seize them and question them."

Yun Chu made a small gesture of refusal.

She walked to the door of the cottage and spoke in a calm, level voice: "Madam Wu, Young Master Wu. Let us meet."

Before setting out to purchase this estate, she had already looked into the background of its first owners, the Wu family.

After the Wu family members had fallen ill one by one and died, they had been buried in the family ancestral ground. She had sent someone to visit the site, and found that in that expansive burial ground, two headstones were missing.

One belonged to the last surviving Wu matron, and one to the young master who had been barely a year old at the time.

In her past life, ten years later, a fire had broken out there, and she believed that fire had claimed the lives of this mother and son. That was why the haunting had simply come to an end.

After Yun Chu finished speaking, there was no response from within the cottage.

She was in no hurry, and continued: "A renowned physician has recently arrived in the capital. Does Madam Wu not wish to have him examine and treat the Young Master?"

At these words, a stir came from inside the cottage. Presently, a bent woman leaning on a walking stick hobbled out.

Yun Chu was taken aback.

The matron had only been around twenty when she gave birth to her child. Twenty years had passed, so she must be around forty now, yet she looked like a woman of sixty. What had she endured to age like this?

Before Yun Chu had fully recovered from her surprise, another figure emerged from the cottage.

This person's entire face was covered in blisters the size of an infant's fist, some of them cracked and weeping. The face was deeply alarming to look upon. He reached out to steady his mother; his hands were covered in blisters as well, and his body beneath his clothing was surely the same.

Yun Chu knew this must be the young master of the Wu family, suffering from the same hereditary ailment that had taken the rest of his kin.

chapters.title: Encountering the Little Commandery Princess
chapters.content:
Leaving the estate, it was nearly the hour of Xu. In the capital, the curfew ran from the second quarter of Xu until the fifth watch before dawn; if they did not return to the city now, they would have to wait until morning.

Tingshuang helped Yun Chu into the carriage and asked quietly: "Madam, you agreed just like that to help treat the Young Master Wu?"

Yun Chu nodded.

More than twenty years ago, the Wu family members had fallen ill and died one by one, until only the youngest, the Young Master, survived. Madam Wu had made the swift decision to sell off all the family's remaining assets and travel far and wide in search of doctors. With nothing left to their name and no place to live, they had moved into this estate.

The estate had been passed down from the Wu family's ancestors, and was the only property the family had retained at the end.

But a family named Zou had schemed to force them into selling it for far less than it was worth. At the time, the estate had been maintained like an imperial garden, with carved rafters and painted beams, pavilions and terraces, rare and precious flowers throughout; it should have sold for at least thirty thousand taels. In the end, Madam Wu had received only twenty thousand.

Once the Zou family took possession, they demolished the Wu ancestral hall at once, and were on the verge of burning down the small wood. With nowhere to turn, Madam Wu had devised a scheme: by pretending to haunt the place, she frightened the Zou family badly enough that they sold the estate at a loss. As for the misfortune that befell the Zou family afterward, that was entirely coincidental.

When the merchant took over next, Madam Wu, with the young master then three or four years old, had played at haunting together, and between them scared the merchant into falling ill.

Moreover, Madam Wu had gone out by day to tell the surrounding villagers the estate was haunted, and so the story spread from one to ten and ten to a hundred, until no one would dare take it on. The merchant sent people from time to time to check on the property, but each time they were driven away by the young master, who had grown by now into a young man. He required no disguise at all: that face alone, and the foul odor of his festering wounds, were enough to make a person faint on the spot.

"The Wu mother and son are pitiable people, to have lived all these years in darkness with no way out." Yun Chu said. "This estate is the ancestral property passed down through the Wu family. If I buy it and use the money it earns to treat the Young Master's illness, there is nothing wrong in that."

Tingfeng said, "But that physician charges five thousand taels just to examine a patient. It would take three to five years for the estate to earn that much, wouldn't it?"

Yun Chu only smiled.

Once the hot spring was discovered, in the coming winter alone it could earn at least fifty thousand taels. Paying the Young Master's medical fees would be a trifling matter by comparison.

She did not think of herself as a great-hearted philanthropist, but she would lend a hand when she was able. Perhaps it was precisely because she had formed many such bonds of goodwill that heaven had allowed her to return to this twentieth year of her life.

"Madam should have her own pulse taken as well." Tingshuang's heart ached. "Madam is still young. Once the condition is treated, she could still have a son of her own..."

Before the last word had left her mouth, the sound of crying suddenly came from outside the carriage.

Yun Chu said at once: "Stop."

The driver drew in the reins, and the carriage slowed to a halt.

Tingshuang lifted the curtain. Yun Chu looked out; they were already inside the city, close to the curfew hour, and the road held not a single pedestrian, only a night watchman passing by.

The crying seemed to come from a small alley.

Without stopping to think, Yun Chu stepped down from the carriage and made for the alley, her maids close behind.

The lane was lit only by the faint wash of moonlight. Faintly she could make out a small white shape huddled against the wall.

The crying was coming from this small figure.

Yun Chu quickened her step, and soon saw clearly: it was a little girl who looked to be about three years old. Her long hair fell loose and tangled around her, her head buried between her knees, her small shoulders hitching as she let out soft, broken cries like a kitten's mewing.

Yun Chu also noticed that the child had no shoes on.

Her heart went soft at once, and she quickly gathered the child into her arms. "Why are you out here alone? Where are your mother and father?"

The little girl lifted her face. It was a tiny face, with very large and round eyes brimming with tears that rolled down one after another. She stared at Yun Chu with a momentary look of bewilderment, and then, with a great cry, buried herself against Yun Chu's shoulder and wept.

Yun Chu was flustered at once. "Don't cry. There, there. If you keep crying you'll look like a little striped cat."

But the child only cried harder, her tears soaking through Yun Chu's shoulder until the cloth was wet through.

Yun Chu felt an inexplicable ache rising in her own chest.

The child she cherished most had been Xie Shiyun, but even when Xie Shiyun was hurt and crying, she had never felt this particular sensation, as though a knife were being turned in her heart.

She held the little girl close, patting her back gently, walked out of the lane, climbed somewhat awkwardly into the carriage, and sat down. Humming a soft song, she cradled the child until the crying slowly quieted.

When she was just about to try speaking to her, she saw those beautiful eyes close. The little girl had fallen asleep in her arms.

Yun Chu felt her heart fill with a quiet warmth. "Tingshuang," she said softly, "go with Chen Bo and walk the nearby streets. See if any family is searching for a child. If everything matches, bring them here."

Tingshuang left to carry out the order.

The carriage was drawn to the side of the road, leaving only Yun Chu holding the child, Tingfeng and Tingxue waiting below the carriage, and the driver holding the horse.

At that moment, a group of people came from nowhere and surrounded the carriage.

Leading them was a matron of forty or fifty, who fixed the carriage curtain with a cold stare. "Search it."

Four or five guards stepped forward immediately.

"What do you think you're doing?" Tingxue stepped in to block them. "Our Madam is in there! Have some respect!"

The matron's expression was hard as stone. "A carriage stopped on the roadside at this hour is already suspicious. What decent woman is still out in the streets so late without going home? Search it!"

Tingxue was nearly beside herself, and was about to protest further when the sound of a child's crying suddenly came from within the carriage.

A flash of relief crossed the matron's face. "The Commandery Princess is in the carriage!"

She shoved Tingxue and Tingfeng aside, grabbed a guard's arm for support as she clambered up, and threw back the curtain in one motion.

She saw at once the girl being held by Yun Chu, and in one stride she reached them, seized the child under the arms, and pulled her out.

The little girl had already been crying; jolted so suddenly, she erupted into an even more frantic wail.

Yun Chu's gaze turned hard. "Let her go."

"You let her go!" The matron glared furiously. "You dared to take away our Commandery Princess. I'd say your days are numbered! No matter what household you belong to, it ends here for you!"

As she spoke, she pulled the child toward her with force.

Yun Chu had been holding the child around the waist, and not daring to resist with more force, she quickly released her grip.

The little girl thrashed and kicked in the matron's hands, her crying growing breathless, and the pink and white of her small face was already turning a shade of purple.

"Release the child at once!"

Yun Chu's voice rose sharply, every trace of her usual composure replaced by an overwhelming force of presence.

It was not Yun Chu's bearing that frightened the matron, but the purple color spreading across the little Commandery Princess's face, which made the matron's knees buckle. She hastily laid the child on the soft cushion of the carriage seat.

"It's all right now, no more crying..." Yun Chu's voice became as gentle as still water. "Will you let me hold you?"

The matron's expression darkened. "And who are you to call yourself our Commandery Princess's..."

Before she could finish, the little girl stretched out both short arms and flung them around Yun Chu's neck.

Yun Chu settled the child on her knee and pointed gently toward the matron. "Do you know this person? Is she from your household?"

The little girl only held on, saying nothing.

Yun Chu looked up. "If she says yes, I will let you take her."

The matron could hardly believe what she was hearing. She had to obtain a stranger's permission to take away her own little mistress?

And yet the little mistress was nestled against this woman with such trust. Trying to take her by force would get nowhere.

She said, "Our little Commandery Princess cannot speak. By the Madam's logic, am I to leave here without the Princess today?"

Yun Chu paused.

This child could not speak?

Wait.

She recalled: Yu'er had once told her that he had a sister who could not speak. And Yu'er's sister was surely a Commandery Princess.

This little girl was a child of the Prince of the Western Regions?

But was the Prince of the Western Regions' child not four years old? This little girl looked about three...

chapters.title: Someone Is Going to Throw Herself Down a Well
chapters.content:
While the two sides were at an impasse, the sound of rapidly approaching hoofbeats reached them.

A dozen or more horses drew to a stop ahead of the carriage. At their head was a blood-sweat horse bearing a commanding figure in a black cloak.

Yun Chu looked up and recognized him at once: it was Chu Yi, the Prince of the Western Regions.

Chu Yi swung down from his horse, walked to the carriage, and stopped a few paces away without coming closer. "So it is Madam Xie," he said.

Yun Chu held the child and stepped down from the carriage. "Greetings, Prince of the Western Regions. This subject's wife would like to ask the Prince how it is that in such a great and well-staffed princely residence, a child this small was allowed to wander out alone in the middle of the night."

She knew that the affairs of the Prince of the Western Regions' household were none of her concern.

But then she thought of how Yu'er had slept in the Xie household for several nights without anyone coming to collect him, and of this tiny girl lost in the night streets, and she felt a pang of sorrow on both children's behalf.

There was also something that was not quite right: the child's own father was standing right before her, and yet the little girl was entirely unmoved. That was not normal.

The emotion rose in her and she could not stop herself from speaking.

Even though the person before her was the renowned and formidable Prince of the Western Regions, she was not the least bit afraid.

Chu Yi met her gaze. When he spoke, his voice was a little rough. "I have been occupied with official affairs of late and have neglected the children. This is indeed a failing on my part as a father."

The attendants of the Prince of the Western Regions exchanged looks of astonishment.

They had served the Prince for many years, and in all that time they had never once seen him bow his head in apology to anyone. This Madam Xie was the first.

Yun Chu herself had not expected this Prince to be so mild-mannered.

She looked down at the child in her arms. "Your father has come for you. Go home with him."

The little girl did not even glance at Chu Yi; she pressed herself against Yun Chu's shoulder, clinging on with both arms and legs, clearly unwilling to go.

"Changshen. Father has come to take you home." Though Chu Yi had done his best to soften his tone, it still came out heavy. "You said you wanted a cat. Father promises. Will that do?"

The little girl's head came up slowly. She fixed her dark eyes on Chu Yi, something uncertain in their depths.

Chu Yi nodded. "Father doesn't lie. Be good. Come to Father."

The little girl seemed to deliberate for quite some time before she finally opened her arms, reluctant and slow, and went to Chu Yi.

A sudden emptiness settled into Yun Chu's arms.

The little girl hung loosely around her father's neck, and looked back at Yun Chu with great, reluctant eyes that were slowly filling with a blur of tears.

Yun Chu reached up and touched her head gently. "There are bad people out in the night. You must not run off like this again."

The little girl pressed her lips together and gave a tiny nod.

Chu Yi looked at Yun Chu. "Madam Xie has done us a great service. If there is ever anything you need, please do not hesitate to ask."

Yun Chu dipped in a curtsy. "It was nothing worth mentioning."

Chu Yi gave her a small nod, gathered the child in his arms, and swung back onto his horse.

The little girl held her father's neck, keeping her wide eyes fixed on Yun Chu until Yun Chu's figure slowly disappeared into the dark of the night. Only then did she look away, and settled, deflated, against Chu Yi.

Back at the Prince's residence, Chu Yi had all the household servants assembled in the front courtyard. Dozens of people trembled where they stood.

He sat in his chair, a natural authority about him that needed no anger to enforce it, and said coldly: "Tell me. How did the Commandery Princess come to leave the residence in the middle of the night?"

When he had been at the capital magistrate's office conducting an overnight interrogation of mountain bandits, his household staff had come to inform him that Changshen had disappeared. His heart had plunged as if into a vat of boiling oil.

He had immediately summoned a contingent of guards to search the entire city, and at last found the child safe. Fortunately, nothing had happened to her.
