Changshen had long wished to keep a cat. Because of her delicate constitution, however, exposure to cats brought on a rash, and he had never agreed to it. Tonight, Changshen had been clinging stubbornly to that Madam Xie, and he'd had no choice but to use the promise of a cat to persuade Changshen to come to him. But the cat was not the reason Changshen had left the residence.

The household staff trembled in the courtyard.

Chu Yi's gaze came to rest on the matron who attended the child most closely.

The matron had no choice but to speak. "Toward evening, this servant saw the Commandery Princess at her painting. She had drawn a woman and written the word 'Mother' beside her. She also wept for a while. This servant believes the Commandery Princess left the residence at night because she wished to find her mother..."

A shadow passed through Chu Yi's eyes.

He could give the children anything they asked for. Only this, never.

He pressed the feeling down and said coldly: "The Commandery Princess is four years old. How is it that a four-year-old child who wanted to leave the residence simply walked out? From her courtyard alone, she would have had to pass through at least five gates. Each of you will tell me how this happened."

While Chu Yi was questioning the servants in the courtyard, Chu Hongyu slipped into his sister's room, sent the maids away, and climbed straight onto the child's bed.

He wrapped his arms around his sister and spoke in a low voice.

"Changshen, I know you're missing Mother too. I'll tell you a secret. The truth is, I've found Mother. It's just a bit complicated to get there, which is why I haven't dared tell you until now..."

"But running out of the residence in the middle of the night was wrong. Promise me you won't do it again, and I'll take you to see Mother."

Changshen's long lashes, fine as feathers, fluttered. A light came alive in her large, dark eyes.

She moved her hands rapidly through a string of signs.

Chu Hongyu laughed. "I'm not lying to you. I really did find Mother. She's very beautiful, very gentle, she likes me very much, and I'm sure she'll like you too."

Changshen's hands flew with excitement.

"Father promised you a cat? That's wonderful. But you can't touch the cat, you'll break out in red spots everywhere and it will itch terribly. We'll keep the cat in my courtyard..."

The brother and sister talked on until they drifted, gradually, to sleep.

That night, Yun Chu herself barely slept. The figures of Yu'er and the little Commandery Princess shifted through her mind, the two of them laughing one moment and crying the next, and then calling out to her together: Mother.

The sky had not yet lightened when Yun Chu woke.

She sat up, took the wooden carving from the table, and ran her fingers over it for a long while. Her heart grew steadier.

When she had finished dressing, the morning visitors arrived.

Xie Shian was waiting in the side hall in a fresh set of robes, and Yun Chu suddenly remembered: the prefectural examination was today.

She had been so busy with one thing after another that she had momentarily forgotten.

She recalled how she had specially prepared so many things for Xie Shian: congee for good fortune, soup for the top candidate, the first-rank banquet dishes, wine named after the moon palace laurel...

Yun Chu lifted a cup of tea and handed it to Xie Shian herself. "In the examination hall, the most important thing is to keep a clear and steady mind. This is a cup of plain tea. Drink it, and let it wash away all restlessness so you may rise above the rest."

"Thank you, Mother."

Xie Shian took the tea and drank it.

The other concubines in the room all offered words of good omen; the young masters and young ladies each wished him success in becoming a licentiate, and for a moment the atmosphere was warm and full of harmony.

Lady He quietly slipped a talisman she had obtained into Xie Shian's hand.

Yun Chu smiled and said, "An'er, your father and I will both see you to the examination grounds today. Your father should be waiting in the front courtyard. Come, let us go."

Xie Shian nodded.

The two were just about to leave when a matron came rushing into Shengju, her face drained of color. "Madam, something terrible has happened! Someone is going to throw herself down a well!"

Lady He snapped sharply: "Can't you see the First Young Master is about to go and sit his examination? What are you saying such inauspicious things for now? Get out!"

If this nonsense interfered with her son's success in the examination, she would wring this matron's neck.

The matron, her face a picture of alarm, pressed on: "Madam, we've just pulled her back from the well's edge. Now she's trying to throw herself at the wall, and she's looking everywhere for scissors to do herself harm. Oh, what is to be done?"

Yun Chu frowned. "Who is it that wants to end her life?"

"It is Jiu'er, from the Second Young Master's courtyard," said the matron.

At that, Yun Chu remembered. In her past life, on this same day, a maidservant in Xie Shiwei's courtyard had made a scene about wanting to die. At the time, she had been rushing to see Xie Shian to the examination grounds and had asked Tingshuang to handle it, but the maid had not been properly watched, and in the end had jumped into the lake and drowned.

Afterward, she had arranged a generous sum of burial money for Jiu'er's parents, but had never looked into the reason why Jiu'er had wanted to end her life.

chapters.title: Xie Shian's Prefectural Examination
chapters.content:
"Tingfeng, Tingxue, the two of you are to take turns watching over Jiu'er. Until I return, you are not to leave her side for so much as a moment."

"Tingshuang, take my token and go and look into this properly."

Yun Chu gave her instructions in calm succession.

"Qi Matron, take some people to the Second Young Master's courtyard and tie up the Second Young Master. He is to wait there until I come to deal with this."

Xie Shian, standing to one side, said in surprise: "Mother, what does this have to do with Shiwei?"

Yun Chu's voice was even. "A maidservant in his own courtyard is trying to take her life. And you say it has nothing to do with him? An'er, you still have your examination. Don't let it delay you. Come."

Lady He forced a smile. "The Madam will handle it fairly. First Young Master, go to your examination with peace of mind."

Xie Shian knew this was not a matter for him to worry about, and nodded, following Yun Chu to the front courtyard to meet with Xie Jingyu.

The three of them rode to the examination grounds together. This was the prefectural examination, held once every three years, and many hopeful scholars had come full of ambition.

Under the current dynasty's regulations, students studying at the capital's prefectural school were not required to sit the preliminary county examinations; they could proceed directly to the prefectural examination. Students of the Imperial Academy did not even need to sit the prefectural examination, and could participate directly in the metropolitan examination.

Xie Shian alighted from the carriage and bowed. "Father, Mother, thank you for seeing me here. I'll go in."

Xie Jingyu nodded, his eyes fixed on his son as he entered the examination grounds.

Yun Chu's expression was mild, showing nothing in particular.

Just then, a voice came to her ear: "Madam Xie."

She turned her head and found Qin Mingheng, the Marquis of Xuanwu, in full official dress standing at her side. She quickly stepped back and dipped in a curtsy. "Good day to you, Marquis."

Xie Jingyu heard the voice and came over at once, positioning himself smoothly in front of Yun Chu. "This official pays his respects to the Marquis."

When Qin Mingheng saw this gesture, his expression soured at once. He gave a slight smile and said, "I have been appointed as the examination supervisor for the western section this time. I wonder, which section is the young Xie candidate sitting in?"

Xie Jingyu's hand tightened. An'er was sitting in the western section.

From the day he and Yun Chu had become engaged, he and Qin Mingheng had been at odds. Fortunately, the Marquis of Xuanwu's title carried no real authority behind it; otherwise, Qin Mingheng would certainly have made things difficult for him at every turn in his official career.

Xie Jingyu clasped his hands and said, "The Marquis must have supervision duties to attend to. This official will not take up any more of your time. Farewell."

He led Yun Chu away toward the carriage.

Once they were walking, Qin Mingheng closed his eyes and breathed in the air around them, catching the same scent as that handkerchief. He drew in a slow, satisfied breath.

Back in the carriage, Xie Jingyu's expression was still poor.

Yun Chu felt no interest in whatever had passed between those two men. She said, "Does my husband have other plans for today, since it's a day of rest?"

Xie Jingyu was inwardly surprised. This was the first time Yun Chu had ever asked about his schedule. Did she want him to accompany her somewhere?

His expression eased slightly. "Just some routine official matters, nothing pressing. Why does my wife ask?"

"This morning, before we left, a matron came to report that a maidservant in Wei'er's courtyard was trying to end her life." Yun Chu spoke unhurriedly. "The last time I administered household discipline to Wei'er, I drew the Old Madam's displeasure. I am not well placed to act again, so I was hoping to ask my husband to step in."

Xie Jingyu's brow furrowed. "A maid who won't behave herself can just be sold off. There's no need to make such a business of it."

At this, Yun Chu gave a small laugh. "Pass judgment on a maid without so much as looking into the matter?"

Her laugh made Xie Jingyu feel, without being able to say quite why, the sting of mockery: mockery of his failure as a scholar to reason carefully, mockery of his poor management of his household, mockery of him, of the Xie family, a whole catalogue of things packed into a single expression...

"My husband may go and attend to his official duties. I won't trouble him with matters of the inner household."

Yun Chu finished speaking just as the carriage arrived at the Xie residence. She lifted the curtain and stepped out without waiting for Xie Jingyu, and walked straight inside.

Xie Jingyu pressed his fingers to the bridge of his nose and let out a long breath.

In the five years since she had come to the household, managing the inner quarters had been left entirely to Yun Chu. This was the first time she had come to him, and no matter how busy he was, he had to take the time to look into it.

He jumped down from the carriage and followed after Yun Chu, making his way to Xie Shiwei's courtyard.

The Old Madam and the First Madam, along with several of the concubines, were all gathered there. Tingshuang stood outside the door of one of the side rooms, her expression grave.

"Jingyu, you've finally come back!" The Old Madam had been weakened by illness, and leaned on her matron's arm as she rose. "Look what your wife has done. She had Wei'er tied up, and when I tried to have him released, I was told it must wait until she returned. She may be the mistress of this household, but she is not God Almighty!"

The Old Madam had been truly worked up.

Admittedly, Wei'er had been somewhat unruly in the past, but he had been so well-behaved of late. A maid threatening to end her life was hardly reason to punish Wei'er. The last time, the incident at the banquet had been plain to see, and Yun Chu had taken charge as though the household could not function without her. Was she now growing ever more reckless because of that?

"Your granddaughter-in-law would not dare set herself up as God Almighty." Yun Chu walked over and curtseyed with measured composure. "This granddaughter-in-law offers her morning respects to the Old Madam. Today's matter happened to coincide with An'er's prefectural examination, and I had no time to inform you beforehand. Please be seated, Madam. Let my husband handle it. Tingshuang, tell us what happened."

Tingshuang stepped forward and lowered her head. "The Madam directed this servant to look into the matter, so this servant questioned every maidservant, matron, and manservant assigned to attend the Second Young Master. It turned out there is not a single one among them who has not been punished by the Second Young Master..."

Lady He stood behind the Old Madam and could not stop herself from interrupting: "It is perfectly proper for a young master to punish those who serve him. What is there to say about that?"

Tingshuang sighed quietly and glanced at the maids.

All the maids rolled up their sleeves and pulled their collars open, revealing wounds that were terrible to look upon.

Yun Chu pressed her lips tight.

In her past life, three or four maids in Xie Shiwei's courtyard had met untimely deaths. Later, he had taken in seven or eight concubines, four of whom had died in his bed.

In fact, there had been maids who came to complain to her early on; but every time she was on the verge of looking into it, the matter had been swept away by Lady He, then still Matron He, aided by the Old Madam's indulgence and Xie Jingyu's willful blindness. As the boys' non-biological mother, she had found it difficult to press further.

Looking back now, she knew that at least ten or twenty women had died at Xie Shiwei's hands, from what she could account for alone.

"Please stand up for us, Madam! Whatever mood the Second Young Master is in, good or foul, he takes it out on us. There is not an unmarked spot on our bodies, save for our faces."

"The Second Young Master likes to use a whip. My back is covered in welts. If he punished us for making mistakes, we could understand it; but we never make mistakes, and yet we are beaten every day. This is no life we can bear."

"The Second Young Master made this servant stand with a flowerpot balanced on her head for an entire day. When she did not hold steady, he had her soaked in the water cistern for a whole night."

The several maids assigned to Xie Shiwei poured out their grievances one after another.

Lady He said coldly, "If you had served the Second Young Master properly, why would he punish you? Besides, the Second Young Master is only eight years old. How much harm can a child do with a whip..."

"Silence!" Xie Jingyu's voice was sharp with fury. "You are a concubine. No one asked for your opinion. Get out."

Lady He stood stunned for a moment.

She was Wei'er's mother. What gave them the right to say she had no standing to speak? What had she said wrong?

The tendons on the back of Xie Jingyu's hands stood out.

In these past years he had been advancing steadily in his official career, occupied with his duties, out before dawn and home after dark, and even on days of rest he had been buried in matters to address. He had neglected the children's upbringing far more than he should have. He had always assumed Wei'er simply had no love for learning, and had thought to himself: with An'er as his eldest, the second boy would be adequate enough. He had never, never imagined Wei'er capable of something like this.

He finally understood why Yun Chu had brought him here to handle it himself.

Because this was no longer something Yun Chu could handle.

chapters.title: Flogging Xie Shiwei
chapters.content:
The Old Madam, too, grasped the gravity of the situation.

The greater a noble family, the more it prized its kindness toward those in its service. If it became known that the household mistreated and tormented its servants, the damage to the family's reputation would be enormous.

This could not be allowed to spread outside these walls.

Before she could say a word, Xie Jingyu said coldly, "Bring Jiu'er out. I want to hear for myself why she wanted to die."

Jiu'er was brought out from the side room, unkempt and hollow-faced, and sank to the floor where she knelt. She looked at Yun Chu and broke into heaving sobs. "Madam, I truly do not want to go on living. Please put me out of my misery."

Yun Chu went over and helped her up. "Jiu'er, the Master is here. Whatever wrong you have suffered, tell the Master yourself."

Jiu'er looked at Yun Chu and saw in her face a steadfast, gentle light, as though it had lent her a measure of strength.

Without a word, she lowered her head and undid the buttons at her collar, baring her slight frame. On her body were welts from a whip, new ones layered over old, crossing one another, a sight that turned the stomach.

"Mere whip welts are no reason to go around looking for death," the Old Madam said mildly, having looked the girl over. "You girls are young and careless in your duties; a young master disciplining his servants is not so unreasonable. Granted, the Second Young Master is a child and didn't know his own strength, and if he hurt any of you, that reflects a lapse in the Xie household's oversight. This is what I propose: I will give each of you ten taels of silver for your injuries, and have you moved to a different courtyard to work. What do you say?"

Though the Old Madam's voice was mild and gentle, there was an undercurrent of pressure in it.

If these girls were sensible, they would take the money and let the matter drop. If they kept pressing, it would not remain this simple.

Yun Chu gave a cold, quiet laugh to herself.

In her past life, every time Xie Shiwei had done wrong, this was exactly how it had been smoothed over, until she died without ever seeing him face the punishment he deserved.

She turned to Xie Jingyu. "Is the Old Madam's meaning also my husband's meaning?"

Xie Jingyu's hands, clasped behind his back, tightened. He knew he had to take a clear stance. If he did not, Yun Chu would never again exert herself to manage and correct these children.

He was too busy with his duties. He needed Yun Chu's capable hands to keep the Xie household steady and make it prosper.

He fixed his gaze on Jiu'er and said coldly, "Is it because the Second Young Master whipped you that you did not wish to go on living?"

Jiu'er raised her arm. With the thumb and forefinger of her other hand, she pinched hard at her skin, and at the tip of her fingers there suddenly appeared a silver needle, while a pinprick of blood welled from her arm.

"The Second Young Master wanted to know how many needles a person's body could hold, and used me to find out," Jiu'er sobbed brokenly. "Half a year ago the Second Young Master began inserting needles into me. The first time, it was ten needles in my back. From then on, one more needle every day. There must be nearly two hundred in me now. The slightest movement sends pain through my whole body. Any time I dared to pull a needle out, the Second Young Master's whip was waiting for me. This servant can feel those needles reaching my vital organs. Every day it hurts so terribly. This servant truly cannot bear to go on living..."

The courtyard fell completely silent.

Only the sound of Jiu'er's weeping.

Even the maid who shared a room with her had not known that on those nights the Second Young Master summoned her, it was for this.

The Old Madam's lips parted but she could find nothing to say.

Lady He had long known her son had a taste for such things, and felt not a flicker of surprise. She only could not understand why the matter had been allowed to grow this large.

Concubine Tao, heavy with child, was so frightened by all of this that her heart pounded and her legs nearly gave way beneath her.

Yun Chu's chest seized.

Xie Shiwei was only eight years old, barely eight, and already he had contrived something this brutal. She did not dare imagine what those concubines who later died at his hands had endured: whether they had been tormented to death or had ended their own lives, every one of those deaths must have been steeped in blood and despair.

"Bring that wretched boy out!"

Xie Jingyu, so consistently mild in front of others, let out a sudden roar of fury.

Two matrons pushed the bound Xie Shiwei out from the side room. A cloth had been stuffed in his mouth; he caught sight of the Old Madam and let out muffled, desperate sounds in her direction.

The Old Madam had not yet managed to speak when Xie Jingyu said, his voice like iron, "Bring me the Second Young Master's whip."

Someone below immediately produced the whip.

It was the soft leather whip suited for a child to handle, not as lethal as a stiff riding whip, but the pain it inflicted was no less than that of a paddle.

Xie Jingyu raised the whip and brought it down.

With his mouth stopped up, Xie Shiwei could not cry out even in agony. His hands and feet were bound, and he could only writhe on the ground like a worm.

The whip cracked down, again and again, seven or eight strokes to the same place without mercy. The back of Xie Shiwei's robe split open under the blows, flesh laid bare, the cloth stained red.

"Master!"

Lady He could bear no more. She flung herself forward and threw her body over Xie Shiwei, taking the force of the next lash herself.

She knew she should not show too much care for the children in front of others, but there was no mother in the world who could stand and watch her own child be beaten like this.

"The Second Young Master is still young. Master, please have mercy!" Lady He pressed herself over Xie Shiwei, pleading.

The Old Madam came back to herself and rose to her feet. "Jingyu, if you keep striking him at that rate, you'll kill the child. It has already happened. Even if you beat him to death, what will that change? Think about how to educate Wei'er properly. Think about how to get Jiu'er treatment. Think about how to limit the damage from all of this as much as possible."

Xie Jingyu was a scholar; wielding a whip was not his domain, and by now he was already breathing hard with the effort.

He hurled the whip aside and said coldly, "Xie Shiwei, what you have done fills me with the deepest shame as your father. I am humiliated to have a son like you."

The Xie family had been a family of scholars for generations. How had it produced something like this?

If this wretch was allowed to simply grow up, whatever reputation the Xie family had built across three or four generations would be destroyed completely.

"The Xie family cannot set you right!" Xie Jingyu's voice turned fierce. "I am sending you to enlist in the army."

The Old Madam was horrified. "Absolutely not. The army is a place for the poor and lowly; it is back-breaking and harsh, and if he goes to the front lines and meets with some accident, his life is gone."

Xie Jingyu drew a deep breath. "Military discipline is absolute. Only that environment can change Wei'er's ways. Otherwise, the day he kills someone or commits some outrage, the Xie family won't be able to cover for him. Wife, your father has many trusted men in the capital. Could you see your way to using your connections to find Wei'er a suitable posting?"

A smile came to Yun Chu's lips.

She had not expected this moment to arrive seven or eight years earlier than it had in her past life.

In that life, she had agreed without hesitation, and sent Xie Shiwei into the camp that the Yun family maintained in the capital's outskirts, making him a trusted member of the Yun family's forces. The consequences had been devastating, and she would never attempt it again.

"My husband may not be aware." Yun Chu said with a note of difficulty. "A few days ago, when Wei'er asked to study martial arts, I had Qiutong examine his frame and sinews. He has no natural aptitude for the martial path. If he were sent to the army, he could only serve as a common foot soldier, and in the military a common foot soldier stands at the very bottom, like the lowest-ranking maidservant in a household. Does my husband truly have the heart to send him there?"

Xie Jingyu had not yet spoken when the Old Madam immediately said, "Wei'er is only eight. If he is sent to the army as a foot soldier, what is to stop the others from bullying him? Even with the Yun family's forces keeping an eye on him, they cannot watch him every moment, and if something happens in a moment of inattention, what then?"

Lady He said urgently, "Master, the Second Young Master promised the Madam before that he would study diligently. He has turned over a new leaf, he truly has."

Xie Shiwei, for his part, nodded his head with as much energy as he could manage.

chapters.title: I Have Said All I Intend to Say
chapters.content:
Sending Wei'er to the army had only been a suggestion born of desperation for Xie Jingyu.

Now, calmer, and thinking it over, there were indeed too many things to be wary of.

He fixed Xie Shiwei, still sheltered in Lady He's arms, with a cold stare. "Have you truly made up your mind to study?"

Lady He quickly pulled the cloth from Xie Shiwei's mouth.

"Father, I was wrong. I know I was wrong and I will never do it again." Xie Shiwei wept and sobbed. "I will study hard and work as diligently as Elder Brother. Please do not send me to the army, Father!"

Qiutong's treatment in his mother's courtyard had given him a visceral understanding of the suffering martial training involved. He had no desire to be subjected to more.

As long as he could stay in the household, he would willingly apply himself to his studies.

Heedless of the welts on his back, he crawled on his knees to where Xie Jingyu stood and pleaded, "Father, please give me one more chance."

"My husband, please give Wei'er another chance. Even if he must eventually enlist, he is too young for it now. If he fails at his studies, there is still time to send him then." Yun Chu bent down and helped Xie Shiwei to his feet. "Wei'er, your father had you flogged for your own good. You must not resent him for it in your heart. Since you have promised to apply yourself to your studies, you must not be idle. From the hour of chen you are to go to the schoolroom; you may not return to your own courtyard until the hour of shen. Can you do this?"

In the position he was in, there was nothing Xie Shiwei could not agree to. He nodded as fast as he could.

Yun Chu continued, "You and Yun'er began studying at roughly the same time. But you are considerably older than he is, and if you cannot even surpass Yun'er, that will prove you have not been applying yourself. If your father again wishes to send you to the army, I will not stand in the way a second time."

"Mother, I will study hard!"

Half dead with pain as he was, Xie Shiwei could only agree to everything.

Lady He, pained for her son, said, "Master, Madam, the Second Young Master's back is bleeding heavily. Please allow this concubine to take him for treatment."

The Old Madam spoke up as well. "Matron Zhou, please fetch a physician at once!"

Xie Shiwei was borne away to his bedchamber, and the Old Madam and the First Madam followed to see how badly he was hurt.

Xie Jingyu turned to Yun Chu. "There are a few things remaining to be settled; I will have to ask my wife to manage them. If anything requires me to step in, please say so."

Yun Chu lowered her eyes. "I can handle what remains. My husband may attend to his duties."

Xie Jingyu curled his fingers. The force of those few lashes had raised blisters on his palm, and in this moment he felt a twinge of regret for having struck so hard.

He could only hope Wei'er would truly apply himself. Not to bring glory to the family name, only to grow into a man who stood upright in the world.

Yun Chu turned to the maids who had been serving in Xie Shiwei's courtyard and asked them all to rise. "The ten taels the Old Madam promised each of you will be sent to you later today. Whatever courtyard you wish to be transferred to, you have only to come and say so. And if you do not wish to remain in the Xie household at all, I can also see that your bond-contracts are returned to you."

Several of the maids, at the mere thought of the Second Young Master, felt fear rise in them.

They were more afraid still that once he recovered from his injuries, he would use them to take out his revenge. The Madam could not protect them forever.

Three of the four maids, all except Jiu'er, decided together that they would take their bond-contracts and leave.

These maids had all been purchased from a middleman after the household grew in number, and their bond-contracts were in Yun Chu's keeping.

She had the contracts brought at once and handed them back one by one. On top of the ten taels the Old Madam had promised, she quietly added five taels of her own to each, called a physician to treat and write out prescriptions for each of the maids, and then made arrangements for them to leave the residence.

Yun Chu stood at Jiu'er's bedside holding the last bond-contract. "Do you truly want to stay in the Xie household?"

Xie Shiwei had a powerful vengeful streak. Every one of these maids who had spoken out against him would face retaliation, but Jiu'er most of all, for having made the matter so large.

She did not understand why Jiu'er was so determined to stay.

A physician had removed dozens of needles from Jiu'er earlier, and her body was badly weakened. She cast her eyes down, concealing whatever lay in their depths. "This servant has no father or mother; apart from the Xie household, this servant has nowhere to go. Furthermore, this servant believes that after what happened today, the Second Young Master will certainly reform. Madam, this servant wishes to stay and continue serving the Second Young Master."

Yun Chu gave a quiet smile.

Jiu'er reminded her too much of herself.

When she had first returned to this life, she had held the same feelings: wherever she had fallen, she would rise from that same place, rather than run far away.

She said in a gentle voice, "There are still many needles inside you. You will need the physician to see you three more times before they can all be removed. We will discuss the question of your staying or leaving after that. For now, rest and recover. I will arrange for a matron to look after you."

A look of guilt came into Jiu'er's eyes.

She had stayed for a different reason, and yet the Madam was still so good to her.

If only she had been assigned to the Madam's own courtyard from the beginning... This body of hers, even when healed, would never fully recover. Her whole life had been ruined...

Yun Chu went and looked in on Xie Shiwei.

Though Xie Jingyu had struck hard, he was a scholar at the end of the day. The injuries looked worse than they were; the skin had been broken but no more. The physician had prescribed an ointment, and with instructions to keep the wounds dry, he said the welts would scab over in about three or four days.

Yun Chu's laugh was cold and without warmth.

Jiu'er had barely escaped with her life, and Xie Shiwei had suffered no more than this slight punishment.

Since the Xie family would not take it upon themselves to teach Xie Shiwei to be a decent person, the world outside would have to do it for them. And when that day came, it would be a great deal more than a few lashes...

After three days of recovery, Xie Shiwei was on his feet again.

Not daring to lie in bed any longer pretending to rest, he dragged himself to the small schoolroom in the household on the third day, wounds and all.

Jiu'er had undergone needle removal three or four times, and still not all of them had been taken out.

Yun Chu sighed inwardly.

Xie Shiwei was truly a monster.

"Madam, this servant feels much less pain now." Jiu'er knelt before her. "Madam's great kindness cannot be repaid. All this servant can offer is this bow."

She touched her forehead to the floor three times, then continued: "This servant will go now to attend the Second Young Master."

Yun Chu had her rise. "Once you are back at Wei'er's side, he will make things difficult for you. How much more can this frail body of yours take? I know what you intend to do."

Jiu'er looked up, unable to believe her ears.

Yun Chu met her gaze. "Lying low will only earn you more suffering. When the moment comes, act quickly. I have said all I intend to say. Go."

Leaving Shengju, Jiu'er could still not quite believe it.

The Madam clearly knew she intended to take revenge on the Second Young Master. Why had she not driven her from the household? Why had she said act quickly instead...

Why? What reason could there be...

Yun Chu arranged for a matron to follow Jiu'er quietly and keep watch, in case the girl came to harm again. Having saved Jiu'er, she was not going to do it by halves.

By now it was nearly dusk. Yun Chu set aside what she had been working on and walked to the front courtyard, where Xie Jingyu had been waiting for some time, visibly anxious.

The three days of the prefectural examination had ended, and Xie Shian would be coming out of the examination grounds at any moment. A father's nerves were understandable.

The two of them boarded the carriage together. Several times Xie Jingyu drew in a breath as though to say something, then found he had nothing to say, and remained silent. By the time they reached the examination grounds, it was still the same.

"There are too many people over there. I'll stay on this side," Yun Chu said casually. "I'll wait for An'er here."

Xie Jingyu gave it no particular thought, nodded, and went toward the main gate where the crowd was thickest.

chapters.title: Negotiating for the Estate
chapters.content:
Yun Chu sat in the carriage, drinking a cup of hot tea. Before long, a man's voice came from outside: "Madam Xie, I am the proprietor of the Dou Trading House. Might I ask the Madam for a brief word?"

That haunted estate had first been sold by the Wu family to the Zou family, and the Zou family had later let it go at a loss to the Dou Trading House, where it had been sitting in the Dou family's hands ever since.

She recalled that in her past life, following the fire, the Dou family's estate had been directly seized by the family of a consort from the palace. Merchants occupied the lowest rung of society, ranked below even ordinary farmers, and would never dare stand against the imperial family. In the end, the estate had simply been handed over to the palace consort.

Yun Chu lifted the curtain.

Two people stood below the carriage: the head of the Dou family and his wife, both of them somewhere in their mid-forties.

She took Tingshuang's hand and stepped down. "Three nights ago I brought people to your Dou family estate without warning. An apology is owed in person, but I have been too occupied with one thing and another these past few days..."

"The First Young Master was sitting for his examination. Of course Madam Xie would have been busy," Dou Furen said quickly. "That estate has been sitting empty; having Madam Xie rest there for a while would be the estate's good fortune. I only hope you were not given a fright?"

Yun Chu sighed softly. "I was in fact looking for a large estate to purchase, and had heard that one has a mountain and a lake, so I went to have a look. But then..."

She shook her head slightly and said no more.

A gleam of hope lit up Dou Furen's face.

After all this time, not a single person had shown any interest in that estate. At last, it seemed, a willing buyer had turned up.

Still, she had heard that Madam Xie had brought quite a group of people in, and had them carried out when they left: clearly they had been badly frightened. Persuading Madam Xie to buy the estate would take some effort.

Dou Furen hesitated a moment before speaking. "Madam Xie may not be aware that all those stories of the estate being haunted are not quite as they appear. It was the farming families nearby who were envious of the fertile land there and deliberately invented those tales to put people off. When our Dou family took possession, those farmers kept coming to make trouble, and as merchants we were not in a position to get into disputes with farmers. Since the Dou family could afford the loss, we simply left the estate as it was."

Yun Chu smiled to herself.

If they truly did not need the money, they would not have come looking for her.

In those days, a farmer's income for an entire year was about two taels of silver. The estate had cost at least ten thousand taels, and no matter how wealthy a person was, that was a sum to feel the loss of.

Dou Fu, the head of the family, added, "We in the Dou family paid twelve thousand taels to the Zou family for this estate. If Madam Xie is genuinely interested, we can let it go for eight thousand."

Yun Chu shook her head.

The Dou family's appetite was quite something.

The estate had been derelict for over twenty years, and yet they still expected eight thousand taels. If it had been kept up all this time, she would have been willing to pay ten thousand. But asking eight thousand for this, they were plainly taking advantage of her status as the eldest daughter of the Yun family, assuming she knew nothing of commerce, and trying to wring as much out of her as they could.

"Eight thousand taels is quite a bargain, but..." Yun Chu lowered her voice. "My husband does not want me to buy that estate. He says it carries bad luck and could affect his advancement at court. Even if I truly wanted it, there is nothing to be done."

Tingshuang, standing nearby, said, "Our Madam does love the mountain on that estate. She had been thinking of using her personal savings to buy it, but she does not have enough..."

Dou Furen quickly asked, "How much would the Madam be able to manage?"

Yun Chu held up three fingers.

The smile froze on Dou Furen's face. She had thought Madam Xie was a willing buyer, but it seemed she was prepared to bargain very hard indeed.

Business had been poor of late, and the Dou Trading House had closed several of its shops. They were in pressing need of silver to keep things moving; otherwise, the two of them would not have come here to waylay Madam Xie in person.

Dou Fu was a merchant, and bargaining was his foremost skill. "One final price: five thousand taels. The deed can be drawn up right now."

Yun Chu shook her head. "This is all I have."

The estate had been abandoned for over twenty years, and was said to be haunted into the bargain. Even after taking it on, to say nothing of a refurbishment that might cost ten thousand taels at the very least, simply changing the minds of those who already knew about its reputation would not be straightforward.

More to the point, she did not have a great deal of silver to hand.

While the Dou husband and wife were hesitating, Yun Chu's expression changed. "My husband is coming. Never mind, I won't buy it. Please leave quickly."

The Dou husband and wife looked at each other: "..."

A moment ago they had thought three thousand was too little; and now, it seemed, even three thousand was gone.

But Xie Jingyu was already walking toward them with Xie Shian, and however reluctant the Dou family was, they had no choice but to step aside, waiting for another chance another day.

Xie Jingyu glanced after the retreating figures with curiosity. "Who were those two?"

Yun Chu smiled and said lightly, "Merchants who have done business with the Yun family. They came to pay their respects."

She turned to Xie Shian. "How did you do, An'er?"

A smile spread across Xie Shian's face. "A top-three placing should not be too great a problem."

Back at home, the Old Madam saw that Xie Shian had returned with the look of a man who had done well, and knew this grandson of hers was bound to pass as a licentiate. Twelve years old and already a licentiate, and ahead of Jingyu at the same age.

Xie Ping sat nearby and asked, "If Shian takes the top place in the examination, will our Xie family hold a banquet?"

Xie Jingyu took a sip of wine. "Of course."

The Old Madam felt the same. "The youngest person to take the top place in all the capital, that is something to celebrate. Why wouldn't we? Chu'er, what do you think?"

Though the Old Madam had turned cool toward Yun Chu, on matters of real importance she still found herself looking to her for guidance.

"Many of the families in the capital who have carefully cultivated their sons cannot match An'er. If he truly takes the first place this time, it reflects well on the Xie family. People outside have been saying rather unkind things about us of late; once the banquet is held, those voices will die on their own." Yun Chu smiled. "If the Old Madam trusts me, I will arrange the banquet. Would that be acceptable?"

The Old Madam was only too pleased. "Then I will leave it in Chu'er's hands."

Xie Ping looked at Yun Chu and said, "Mother, may I help as well?"

After the incident at the last banquet, she had stopped helping her mother with household management. She had been avoiding it long enough. She needed to face it.

This banquet for the top candidate would naturally be more elaborate than a birthday celebration for the Old Madam, and she was determined to redeem herself at this one.

Though the examination results had not yet been posted, the Old Madam had already made up her mind that Xie Shian would take the top place, and in her happiness she could not help but sigh. "If only Wei'er were as gifted in his studies..."

When Xie Shian returned from the examination grounds, he had learned what had happened in the household: Wei'er had been given a severe flogging by his father and had spent two days in bed, but had gone to the schoolroom today.

"An'er, go and see how your brother is doing," said the First Madam. "Seeing how well you have done, Wei'er may well decide to buckle down from here on."

Xie Shian nodded, turned, and walked to Xie Shiwei's courtyard.

All the serving staff in the courtyard had been replaced with stout matrons. One of them was tending a pot of medicine at the gate; seeing him approach, she was about to bow.

He made a small gesture for silence and quietly pushed open the door. Inside, Xie Shiwei was lying on his stomach, reading.

As an elder brother, seeing an irresponsible younger sibling showing signs of improvement gave him a genuine sense of relief, and he felt that his father's lashes had been entirely warranted.

But when he drew closer, his expression darkened immediately. He pulled the book out of Xie Shiwei's hands. "Is this all you ever read?"

The book was a picture story, its pages filled with blood and violence rendered in crude illustrations.

"Elder Brother..." Xie Shiwei was horrified. "Please don't tell Father or Mother. I beg you, Elder Brother."

Xie Shian placed the picture story on the candle stand; within moments it had caught fire and was burning.

He pressed down his anger. "After Father punished you like that, you still haven't changed. You are clearly beyond saving."

"Elder Brother, I have changed, truly. The work the tutor assigned is just too difficult..." Xie Shiwei ransacked his mind for excuses. "I studied for a while and needed to relax, so I picked this up. I really have changed, I really have..."

Xie Shian looked at the large, unsteady characters scrawled on the desk.

chapters.title: How Dare You Dodge
chapters.content:
Xie Shian could hardly believe anyone could write so badly.

The characters Xie Shian himself had written when he first began his studies at three years old were far better than those produced by Xie Shiwei at eight.

"Eight years old, still copying out 'Human beings are born inherently good,' and not a single character written properly. Have you no shame?" Xie Shian was so frustrated that he spoke without thinking. "No wonder Father beat you. If I were in his position, I would sooner wring your neck."

Xie Shiwei feared, first and foremost, his father Xie Jingyu, and second, Elder Brother Xie Shian. Elder Brother was too accomplished; standing next to him made Xie Shiwei feel like a bundle of straw.

He tugged Xie Shian's sleeve. "Elder Brother, I genuinely want to study, but it's too hard, truly too hard. I can't manage it no matter what I do, and I can't help that. Mother said if I can't even surpass Yun'er, I'll be sent off to be a soldier. Elder Brother, help me say something to Father. I don't want to go to the front lines and die..."

Xie Shian pulled his sleeve free and said sharply, "You can't do well in your studies, you won't go to the military. Do you intend to be useless your whole life?"

"I... could I learn to do business?" Xie Shiwei scraped the depths of his imagination. "I'm slow to learn, I know, but I'm still young. Slowly, little by little, I'm sure I could manage..."

Xie Shian pressed his lips together.

The Xie family would certainly grow larger in the years to come. Someone would need to hold up the family banner at the front, and equally, someone was needed in the rear to manage the commercial side and provide a steady flow of income.

He could not trust an outsider for that. Only a full brother would do.

After a moment's consideration he said: "Mother told you to keep up with Yun'er. All you need to do is deal with Yun'er. If you cannot manage even that, you deserve to go to the front lines and have an enemy take that empty head of yours. "

He swept his robe aside and walked out.

Xie Shiwei scrambled to the desk and grabbed for the picture story, but it was already burned to nothing. He beat his chest in fury.

He looked up, and saw a figure entering the room. He snatched up the candlestick and flung it. "You again! Everything is your fault!"

The person who had entered was Jiu'er.

She stepped aside and it missed her, clattering to the floor.

"How dare you dodge!" Xie Shiwei was furious. "You little wretch, who gave you the nerve?"

Jiu'er bowed her head. "Replying to the Second Young Master: the Madam has arranged for a physician to check on this servant every other day. If this servant has any new injuries, the Madam will call the Second Young Master to account. This servant is also worried that the Second Young Master's own injuries are not yet fully healed."

At this, Xie Shiwei's fury intensified.

But he genuinely did not dare lay hands on Jiu'er again.

Jiu'er lowered her eyes and picked up the candlestick from the floor, then went quietly about her work.

While Xie Shiwei's days were becoming increasingly grim, the Xie household itself was filled with a festive air.

The Old Madam had already directed Yun Chu to begin preparing for the upcoming examination celebration banquet.

Other families would not dare make such preparations before the results were posted, but the Xie family had this confidence.

Yun Chu had organized so many banquets of this kind that most of it required little deliberation; she left the bulk of it in Tingshuang's hands, reserving her own attention for the one thing that required careful thought: the guest list.

She drafted a list and sent it to Anshoutang.

The Old Madam looked it over and was taken aback. This granddaughter-in-law of hers had actually proposed inviting the Director of the Imperial Academy, a senior third-rank official at court. How could an official of that standing come to drink wine at the home of a fifth-rank bureaucrat?

Yun Chu smiled and explained: "Old Madam, what you may not know is that the prefectural school where An'er studies was established under the direction of the Imperial Academy. Every year the Academy selects two of the prefectural school's best students to transfer there. An'er has taken the top place in the prefectural examination, meaning he is the finest student the school has produced. This autumn, he will certainly enter the Imperial Academy. The Director of the Academy has a deep regard for exceptional students and will naturally come to offer his congratulations."

The Old Madam was familiar with both the prefectural school and the Imperial Academy, but had not known that students from the prefectural school could enter the Academy.

She opened her eyes wide. "If I remember rightly, the students of the Imperial Academy are all members of the imperial family and the nobility. Can An'er truly be admitted?"

"As long as An'er holds the top place from this examination, it is settled beyond doubt." Yun Chu smiled gently. "The Emperor wishes to find outstanding young students to serve as companions to the imperial princes, so that those princes will be spurred to greater diligence."

"Amitabha, may the heavens protect us!" The Old Madam pressed her palms together toward the sky, then looked at Yun Chu. "You really do think of everything. Now that we have invited the Director of the Academy, he will be more inclined to look after our An'er in the future."

Yun Chu continued, "All the tutors at the prefectural school must be invited as well. And An'er's fellow students, should we include them?"

The Old Madam nodded at once. "Most of the students at the capital's prefectural school are sons of officials. These are the connections An'er will rely on throughout his career at court. They must be invited."

"There is one person," Yun Chu said. "The young heir of Xuanwu Marquis Estate: the last time, the Marquis came of his own accord to wish the Old Madam a happy birthday. With An'er's celebration at hand, should we not invite the Marquis?"

"We did not send an invitation to the Xuanwu Marquis Estate the last time, which was our oversight. We cannot commit the same error again." The Old Madam reminded her, "We will be hosting so many officials and people of rank this time. The banquet must not be meager; offer plenty of new and distinctive dishes. Also, I want you to oversee the kitchen personally. We cannot have a repeat of what happened at the last occasion."

Yun Chu bowed in acknowledgment.

Returning to her courtyard, she set the guest list aside and sat at the desk to begin a painting.

The haunted estate was effectively already in her possession; now was the time to plan carefully how it should be renovated and rebuilt once it was hers.

Everything would center on the hot spring, and around it she would build a pleasure estate for the nobility and great families to enjoy.

Yun Chu was absorbed in her drawing when Tingfeng came in to report: "Madam, Concubine Yu and the Third Young Master have come. It seems they have something important to say."

She set down her brush and folded the drawing away. "Show them in."

Concubine Yu came in with Xie Shiyun, and mother and son bowed together.

"Madam, this concubine has something to report." Concubine Yu lowered her head. "This afternoon I went to the schoolroom to bring the Third Young Master some clothing, and I saw with my own eyes the Second Young Master bullying Yun'er. The Second Young Master is much bigger and stronger, and he pushed the four-year-old Third Young Master right to the edge of the lake. He nearly fell in. Madam, please stand up for Yun'er."

Yun Chu turned to the child. "Yun'er, is this true?"

Xie Shiyun kept his head bowed and said nothing.

"Tingshuang, send for the Second Young Master."

Lessons were over by now, so Tingshuang went directly to Xie Shiwei's courtyard to bring him.

After everything that had happened of late, Xie Shiwei had added one more name to his list of people who frightened him most, and that name was Yun Chu.

He entered Shengju with his eyes down and his manner subdued, none of his usual swagger and arrogance anywhere to be seen.

"Greetings, Mother." Xie Shiwei bowed respectfully. "I wonder what matter Mother has called me here for?"

Yun Chu said, "Concubine Yu says she saw with her own eyes that you tried to push Yun'er into the lake. Is this so?"

Xie Shiwei looked startled. "Yun'er is my younger brother. How could I want to harm him? Concubine Yu must have been mistaken."

Concubine Yu raised her head. "Second Young Master, how can you deny what you yourself did? I was not the only one who saw it; the maid at my side saw it clearly as well!"

"And the maid at my side also saw that I did not push Yun'er," Xie Shiwei replied with an air of total innocence. "Mother, though my conduct has been poor, I would never raise a hand against my own younger brother. What is more, I have already turned over a new leaf. I ask Mother to restore my good name."

chapters.title: Xie Shian Takes the Top Place
chapters.content:
Yun Chu gave a faint, humorless smile.

A leopard cannot change its spots. Xie Shiwei would never truly reform.

After taking that beating, he had simply learned to disguise himself.

Yun Chu said, "Concubine Yu says you pushed him; you say you did not. One says one thing and one says another, each with their own version. Why not let Yun'er speak for himself?"

Xie Shiyun kept his head bowed, his hands twisting together.

Concubine Yu was nearly frantic with impatience. "Yun'er, the Madam is here. You can tell her the truth. The Madam is kinder to you than anyone; she will certainly stand up for you."

Xie Shiwei's mouth tightened almost imperceptibly, and then he said: "Yun'er, the tutor has told us that children must not tell lies."

"Mother, Second Brother did not bully me..." Xie Shiyun's head sank even lower. "My姨娘... my姨娘 must have been mistaken."

Concubine Yu could not believe what she was hearing, and wanted to say more.

Yun Chu set down her teacup. "Wei'er says he did not push; Yun'er says the same. Concubine Yu, is this not you making something out of nothing?"

Concubine Yu opened her mouth to protest: "Madam, this concubine did not make anything up..."

"I have a great many things to attend to. You are all dismissed." Yun Chu picked up her book and began to read.

Tingshuang made a gesture of invitation.

Concubine Yu led Xie Shiyun out, her expression cold. "I saw with my own eyes that he bullied you. Why could you not admit it to the Madam?"

"What is Concubine Yu saying?" Xie Shiwei came strolling past. "In fact, Yun'er and I were only playing. Concubine Yu took it seriously. She even went to the Madam about it, and the Madam is so busy; there's no need to trouble her with such small matters."

He spoke pleasantly, then threw his arm around Xie Shiyun's shoulder. "Yun'er, the tutor set us work to do. Let's go and write it together."

Once they were well clear of Concubine Yu, Xie Shiwei's voice dropped. "You did well in front of the Madam just now. I am satisfied. Remember this: in the future it will be my elder brother who runs the Xie household. If you are not obedient, once my elder brother becomes the head of the family, I will have him drive Concubine Yu out of the Xie residence and have her become a woman of the streets, and you will hold your head low for the rest of your days."

"Second Brother, I'll obey, I'll be obedient to you!" Xie Shiyun, at the thought of his mother being driven away, was so terrified that tears sprang to his eyes.

His mother no longer cared for him as she once had. If even Concubine Yu, the only person who looked out for him, were to leave, what would become of him?

With eyes blurred by tears, he sat and wrote out the work the tutor had assigned. He had always written each character slowly and carefully, but with Xie Shiwei watching over him, he could only produce something scrawled and barely legible, even to himself.

Xie Shiwei looked on with great satisfaction. He only needed to write a little better than Yun'er, and neither his father nor his mother would scold him again.

As the fifth month arrived, the temperature rose steadily.

Waking early one morning, Yun Chu found a light sweat already on her brow.

"It was still cold as midwinter in the fourth month. How did it turn so hot so quickly?" Tingfeng looked up at the sky. "It will probably be clear skies for the next half a month or more."

Yun Chu knew it would be far more than half a month; for the next four or five months, until the tenth month, it would grow hotter and hotter. Fortunately, there would be a few heavy downpours in between; without them, drought would set in and the harvests would fail, making life even harder for the common people.

She said, "Is there any news yet?"

Today was the day the prefectural examination results would be posted. She had sent two servant boys to watch the board, and the notice should have been put up by now.

Before the words were out of her mouth, Tingxue came running in, breathless: "Madam, the magistrate's office has sent someone to announce the happy news! The First Young Master has been awarded the top place in the examination and has passed as a licentiate!"

A smile came to Yun Chu's face, though it stopped short of reaching her eyes.

After everything the Xie household had been through, Xie Shian had still managed to take first place. She had to admit, the boy was born for scholarship.

If only Xie Shian were not destined to turn his hand against the Yun family, she would not have wanted to ruin someone who might have served his country well.

She said quickly, "Go and call the Old Madam, the First Madam, the Master, the concubines, and all the young masters and young ladies. We will all go to the front gate together to receive the congratulations!"

Xie Zhongcheng, rarely at home, had already returned to await the news, and at the announcement of congratulations from the magistrate's office, he was the first to move, striding straight to the front gate. Xie Jingyu was already standing at the foot of the Xie residence's steps with Xie Shian.

Four yamen runners arrived with drums and gongs, drawing everyone nearby to gather around.

"To pass as a licentiate at only twelve years old, and to take the top place, what a remarkable young man."

"Xie Daren was personally named top of the imperial examinations by the Emperor himself. I would say this young Xie will go just as far; perhaps one day the family will have two successive examination champions."

"With a father and mother who are such fine teachers, and the Yun family behind them as support, this First Young Master of the Xie family is sure to place first in the triennial examination and rise to the very top of the court."

"..."

The crowd who had gathered buzzed with admiration, every glance directed at Xie Shian full of praise.

Xie Shian stood tall, his bearing full of youthful confidence. In that moment he seemed to see himself ten years hence: perhaps not at the very head of the hundred officials, but certainly a figure of great weight at court...

The Old Madam had each of the four runners who had come to announce the news given a generous red envelope, ten taels of silver apiece: a handsome gesture.

Xie Zhongcheng clasped his hands and addressed the onlookers: "The Xie family will hold a banquet on a day to be announced. All who have the leisure are welcome to come and share in the good fortune."

The crowd responded with cheerful agreement.

Once the well-wishers had dispersed, the entire Xie family surrounded Xie Shian.

The Old Madam touched his head. "An'er, from now on the Xie family is counting on you."

Xie Zhongcheng said, "When your grandfather was your age, he had not even passed the preliminary examination. Seeing you take the top place in the prefectural examination is as though your grandfather's old dream has finally been fulfilled. Keep applying yourself, and aim for first place in the next provincial examination as well."

The First Madam was overjoyed. "An'er has made something of himself; Wei'er, you must not fall behind, and Yun'er too!"

Lady He was moved nearly to tears.

When An'er had been only three years old, his tutor had said he had extraordinary potential for scholarship and urged her to find him an excellent teacher without fail.

In those days, An'er had no recognized status and could only attend the most ordinary of private schools. She had worked and schemed repeatedly to have him formally acknowledged into the family, and in the end, all of it had been worthwhile. An'er had fulfilled every hope placed in him, and his future was bright.

Her eyes, blurred with tears, turned toward where Xie Shian stood; she laughed and wept at the same time.

Concubine Tao, standing nearby, found this slightly strange. Celebrating An'er's success was of course cause for joy, but for a concubine to be quite this exuberant seemed somewhat excessive.

If it were like the Madam, who had no children of her own and treated An'er as though he were her own flesh and blood, then joy this great would be understandable.

But a concubine who had her own children on the way... rejoicing was natural, but she could not help but worry that the Master might invest too much in the First Young Master and neglect her own child...

What was Lady He celebrating about?

Yun Chu arranged a round of gifts to be given to all the household servants and then asked: "Old Madam, when shall we hold the banquet?"

The Old Madam looked to Xie Jingyu.

"Tomorrow is an official day of rest; it is a good occasion to host a wide gathering." Xie Jingyu looked at Yun Chu. "Does my wife think it can be arranged in time?"

Yun Chu nodded. "Everything has been prepared over the past few days. The banquet can go ahead whenever you wish."

The First Madam said warmly, "With Chu'er managing this household, there is almost nothing that needs worrying about. Ping'er, you must learn more from your mother."

Xie Ping bowed her head quickly. "Yes, Grandmother. I will."

With the banquet the next day, there were still things to attend to; Yun Chu had Tingshuang take Xie Ping to manage the remaining details.

Tingshuang, trained from childhood by Yun Chu's own mother, was someone she trusted completely.

No sooner had she finished giving instructions than a servant came to report that Dou Furen had requested an audience.

chapters.title: Buying the Estate at a Low Price
chapters.content:
Yun Chu had Dou Furen shown in.

The wife of a merchant occupied an extremely low position in society in this era; merchants as a class could rarely expect to set foot inside the home of an official. Dou Furen came in with her eyes cast down, not daring to look around, and after passing through several gates she at last arrived at the reception hall of Shengju.

"Greetings, Madam Xie."

Dou Furen bent as low as her body would allow in a respectful bow.

"Dou Furen is too formal. Please sit down. Tingxue, bring tea."

Once she had had some tea, Dou Furen relaxed and smiled. "I have come without sending a card ahead of time; I hope I have not disturbed Madam Xie."

Yun Chu said pleasantly, "I walked into your Dou family's estate without permission the other evening. Dou Furen did not hold it against me."

At that, Dou Furen felt that this Madam Xie was gracious and easy to be around, and she came straight to the point. "The last time, Madam Xie said three thousand taels. My husband and I have talked it over, and we feel it can be agreed upon."

Yun Chu spoke up. "Dou Furen surely knows that my son has just taken the top place in the prefectural examination. The Xie family is riding a wave of good fortune at this very moment, and I am genuinely worried that the estate's reputation might affect our luck. So..."

Dou Furen was filled with regret.

When Madam Xie had said three thousand taels that day, she should have agreed immediately. Even if the sum was small, it at least stopped the bleeding; the longer the estate sat unsold, the greater the loss.

Still, the fact that Madam Xie had let her in surely meant she still wanted the estate.

She ventured carefully: "What if we say two thousand taels?"

Yun Chu appeared to think it over.

Dou Furen shifted in her seat with growing discomfort.

After a long pause, Yun Chu finally spoke. "A transaction should suit both parties. Two thousand is clearly a loss for the Dou family, and I would not want you to feel you had been poorly treated and come back to me later about it. Let it be three thousand. I will send someone with you to the deeds office to draw up the papers right away. Only, I hope Dou Furen will keep this quiet."

Dou Furen was delighted. Yun Chu had Chen Defu accompany the Dou family to complete the formalities.

With that matter settled, Yun Chu took the Xie family's invitation cards and went in person to the Yun family to invite her own relatives to the banquet.

"An'er's future is beyond all reckoning." Yun Ze said with feeling. "There is no one in all the capital his age to compare with him."

Lin Shi added: "At the end of the day, he is not your own child. You have raised him for four years, but he is not very close to our Yun family either. Xie Jingyu may be worthless, but that is not An'er's fault. You ought to put in more effort for him. In your later years, he is the one you will have to depend on."

Yun Chu's fingers tightened around the handkerchief in her hand.

In her past life, her mother and elder brother and sister-in-law had said exactly these same words, urging her to give everything of herself to the Xie family's children. They had hoped those children would care for her in her old age.

But the children she had poured herself into raising had, in the end, sent her to her death, and sent the Yun family to its ruin.

"The last time I sent a list of two families for Ran'er, you chose the Dai family, didn't you, Mother? I have specially invited Dai Furen and the Dai second son today. You and Dai Furen can have a talk, and I will take Ran'er to have a look at the young gentleman." Yun Chu smiled. "It's Ran'er's own agreement that matters in the end. Only with her nod can this match be considered settled."

Yun Ran, standing to one side, flushed to the roots of her hair.

Yun Chu shifted the subject. "There is one more matter: a renowned physician has come to the capital and is presently staying in the palace to treat the Empress. Could Mother perhaps help me arrange to have the physician come out for half a day?"

Lin Shi's face broke open in a burst of joy. "Chu'er, you have finally come to your senses. No matter what it takes, Mother will bring that physician to you."

She had dreamed for years of seeing Yun Chu have a child she could call her own.

Yun Chu neither confirmed nor denied it.

Let her mother be pleased for now, and spare her the worry.

By the time she returned from the Yun family to the Xie residence, the sky had already darkened. Rather than going back to Shengju, Yun Chu made a circuit of the kitchen, confirming that all the preparations were in order, and then returned to her courtyard for dinner.

Back in her room, she saw the wooden carving sitting on the windowsill and let out a quiet sigh. She had not seen the child for quite some time, and a vague, inexplicable fondness came over her.

And the little Commandery Princess who had been lost in the night, she recalled: the Prince of the Western Regions had called out a name that sounded like Changshen. Chu Changshen, was it? A lovely name.

Yun Chu's mind drifted through one thought after another until sleep came. The next morning, while it was still dim, Tingshuang slipped in and called her softly awake.

She put on a somewhat formal set of robes, arranged her hair in a cloud of loops, and pinned in a red-gold pearl ornament that swayed as she moved, finishing with a light dusting of powder.

Once dressed, Xie Ping was the first to arrive to pay her respects, as Yun Chu had told her to come early. The banquet was being held on short notice and was bound to have a few gaps; starting early was the only way to address any problems before they arose.

Xie Ping followed Yun Chu into the kitchen, where Yun Chu called together every matron on staff, asked about each item in detail, and personally tasted the ingredients to check that they were fresh.

Xie Ping could not help feeling ashamed.

When she had been in charge of the Old Madam's birthday banquet, she had never done anything like this herself. She had simply told the maids and matrons under her what to do.

No wonder Mother managed the household better with every passing month. There was so much still for her to learn.

After Yun Chu had made the rounds of the courtyard, the sky was fully bright and the Xie family members were rising one by one and making their way to the front courtyard, all except Xie Shiwei, who was nowhere to be seen.

Xie Jingyu frowned. "It seems I was too lenient last time."

"Today is a happy occasion, my husband. Do not let it trouble you." Yun Chu spoke up. "I will go and wake Wei'er."

She walked to Xie Shiwei's courtyard and found Jiu'er standing at the bedchamber door. "Go in and call the Second Young Master to get up."

Jiu'er murmured, with her eyes still down, "Last night the Second Young Master drank quite a bit of wine, and when he woke half a shichen ago he complained of a headache. He has likely..."

Yun Chu glanced at Jiu'er. "Is this what you call revenge?"

Jiu'er's expression went rigid. How did the Madam know she had deliberately gotten the Second Young Master drunk?

Her intention had been to make him miss the First Young Master's banquet, provoking the Master's anger and earning him another severe beating.

"Not worth doing if it barely leaves a mark." Yun Chu shook her head. "Many officials of rank are coming to the Xie household today. As a son of the Xie family, the Second Young Master must be at the front gate to receive guests. Whatever means you use, make sure the Second Young Master is awake within one quarter of an hour."

Jiu'er hurried inside to rouse him.

Before long, Xie Shiwei came out in fresh clothes, though with his face somewhat puffy from the night's drinking.

Yun Chu said in an even tone, "You are only eight years old and already drinking yourself to sleep. If your father finds out, you will be kneeling in the ancestral hall. Today is your elder brother's celebration banquet. This matter is set aside for now. Compose yourself. Many officials of rank will be bringing their own sons, and you will need to keep them company and entertain them. Remember: those are all people of high standing. Be careful not to offend any of them."

Standing nearby, Jiu'er's gaze shifted almost imperceptibly.

She thought she had just begun to understand what the Madam meant.

Yun Chu brought Xie Shiwei to the front courtyard.

The Old Madam and the First Madam waited in the rear courtyard to receive the female guests.

Xie Zhongcheng was in the front courtyard to host the male guests.

Yun Chu and Xie Jingyu stood with their children at the Xie family's main gate to welcome the arrivals.

The first family to come was Councilor Yuan's family, Yuan Furen, and their son, all three arriving neatly together from their carriage.

"Congratulations, Lord Xie." Yuan Daren came forward and clasped his hands. "I have brought my son today in hopes that he may learn a thing or two from the young Xie. I ask not for the top place; as long as my boy can pass as a licentiate, it would be as though my Yuan family's ancestors had intervened on our behalf."

Passing as a licentiate was not some towering achievement, but it was the first step into the world of officialdom, and therefore a matter of great importance.

Xie Jingyu made a welcoming gesture. "Lord Yuan, please come in. Shian, take Lord Yuan and the young master inside."

Yun Chu had Xie Ping escort Yuan Furen inside.

Once the Yuan family of three had entered, Xie Jingyu quietly told the servant at his side: "Keep a close eye on that family. Report any unusual movement to me at once."

The last time it had been the Yuan family who had been behind the trouble, bringing humiliation to the Xie household. If the Yuan family dared try anything this time, he would show no mercy.

chapters.title: The Half-Sister's Marriage Discussion
chapters.content:
The guests arrived in a steady stream.

The front and rear courtyards gradually filled with voices and movement.

Before long, the Xuanwu Marquis Estate's carriage drew up, and Xie Jingyu's expression darkened at once.

But as a minor fifth-rank official, no matter how deeply he detested the Qin family, he had to receive them with a smile. "Marquis, Marchioness, Young Lord, your presence brings luster to our Xie household. Please come in."

Qin Mingheng arrived with his marchioness, Lady Luo, and their eldest legitimate son, a boy of about six, fair-complexioned and tidy.

"I remember when I was still unmarried, I attended the young lord's full-moon celebration with my mother," Yun Chu said pleasantly to the marchioness. "In the blink of an eye, the young lord has grown so big."

Lady Luo smiled with a natural warmth. "I also attended Madam Xie's departure ceremony with the Marquis when you left your family home."

A few words exchanged, and the two women found themselves strangely at ease with one another.

Given the Qin family's standing, Yun Chu led them personally to the rear courtyard, where the assembled ladies all rose to offer their respects.

Lady Luo had a gentle disposition and made no display of rank; she settled comfortably into the company before long.

Yun Chu went back to the front gate to receive more guests.

Around the expected time, the Yun family arrived. Being family by marriage, all of the Yun household had come except the eldest general, too old for such outings, and the general holding the front lines. Yun Furen Lin Shi, the eldest Yun son Yun Ze, his wife Liú Qianqian, their eldest son and daughter, and three of Yun Chu's half-siblings on her father's side: a whole family together, giving the Xie family very generous face.

Yun Chu brought her own family inside and made sure Lin Shi was seated beside Dai Furen, and the two ladies found a great deal to say to one another.

Lord Dai held a fifth-rank official position at court, and his second legitimate son was nineteen this year, having passed as a licentiate two years before. That was naturally far less impressive than Xie Shian, but by most standards it was quite respectable. The sons of noble families in the capital either inherited their father's titles and estates, or sat for the metropolitan examination directly; before they actually entered the examination hall, no one could say what they were made of. Those of somewhat lower birth were a different matter: if a young man had passed as a licentiate, it meant he could earn a living by scholarship and that he was diligent and committed, far better than the average privileged wastrel.

Lin Shi was quite pleased with the Dai second son, and felt that Dai Furen as a future in-law would be easy to get along with; Dai Furen, naturally, was more than satisfied with a daughter of the Yun family. Neither party found anything to take exception to, and the match was more than half settled.

Yun Chu came over and said: "Ran'er, come with me to fetch some fruit wine to offer the ladies."

Yun Ran stood, docile, and followed at Yun Chu's side.

She followed Yun Chu to the inner gate, the boundary between the outer and inner courtyards, where a covered walkway ran alongside it.

From there, a group of young men in the outer courtyard could be seen at some distance, Xie Shian among them, talking together.

Yun Chu said softly, "The one in the blue robe, the taller one, that is the Dai second son. Have a look and tell me what you think."

Yun Ran looked up briefly, then quickly dropped her eyes again. Her ears flushed red all the way down. Almost imperceptibly, she gave a tiny nod.

Yun Chu found herself thinking of long ago, when her own mother had done the same thing for her: standing behind a screen, stealing a look at Xie Jingyu.

Xie Jingyu had been such a fine-looking young man in those days. She had taken one look and immediately nodded her agreement, and so had become a Xie family wife.

Because she herself had been soaked to the bone in that rain, she would ensure her younger sister was kept well out of it.

The Dai family was the one she had chosen from among hundreds of families, and it was the very best she had found. Ran'er would live without worry for the rest of her life, married into that household.

Once Yun Ran had given her approval, the next step was for Yun Chu to walk past with Yun Ran so the Dai second son could catch a glimpse of her, and then the matter would be fully settled.

Along the way, Yun Ran's face was so red it was like a ripe persimmon ready to drop.

Yun Chu went to the front courtyard to receive the last wave of guests, and as she finished, noon had arrived. The banquet formally began.

The men were in the front courtyard; younger boys, whether seven or eight years old and not yet expected to know better, were kept in the rear courtyard with the women.

The most senior ladies occupied the places of honor, with Yun Chu and the Old Madam hosting them personally.

Several of these ladies had attended the Old Madam's birthday banquet, and had come today with some lingering anxiety, half expecting another mishap. By the time the banquet was halfway through, they had fully relaxed: this gathering had been handled with genuine skill, no less impressive than anything their own households might have put on, and in some ways rather more so.

After a few rounds of wine, Lady Luo could not resist saying: "Lord Xie achieved first place in the imperial examinations, and his eldest son looks set to do the same. The Xie family's fortune is something to admire, but more than anything, the Xie family clearly knows how to raise children. Might Madam Xie share how the Xie family manages the children's upbringing?"

Yun Chu deflected at once. "The Marchioness is too kind. They say children aged five and six could make even a dog tired, yet the young lord is so well-behaved; clearly it is the Marchioness who excels at raising children."

"Him? He's a perfect little demon," Lady Luo said, shaking her head. "The whole household is at their wit's end with him. A bird flies past and he pulls out two feathers; I fully expect him to grow up to be the most notoriously unruly scoundrel in all the capital."

"Mother!" The Xuanwu Marquis's heir was right there, and his face crumpled at hearing his own mother speak of him like this in public.

"Children are thin-skinned," the Old Madam said with a smile. "Wei'er, you and the young lord are about the same age. Take the young lord and go and play."

Xie Shiwei's mouth tightened. The young lord was about six, a little child, and Xie Shiwei had no patience for small children, who always seemed to have runny noses.

His instinct was to refuse, but he felt the Old Madam's cold eye land on him.

The Old Madam was practically willing him to understand: the person before him was the Xuanwu Marquis's heir; forming a connection with the Marquis household could only do him good.

Xie Shiwei might not grasp the finer points of this calculation, but he knew clearly enough that if he refused, the Old Madam would scold him once the banquet was over, and if the Master then grew angry, he would be in real trouble.

He quickly stepped forward. "Young lord, let me take you around the rear courtyard. There are plenty of interesting things to see."

The Marquis heir had been bored to exhaustion for some time; grown women talking about things that held no interest for him, and he was desperate for a change of scenery. He followed Xie Shiwei readily enough, and the two headed off to the rear courtyard.

Yun Chu turned and said, "Jiu'er, keep close to the Second Young Master and the young lord. Be careful that neither of them trips or gets hurt."

Jiu'er lowered her head and went quickly after them.

While the women in the rear courtyard talked, the banquet in the front courtyard was also drawing to a close.

Xie Shian had taken a group of boys of similar age to the garden to play pitch-pot, while Xie Jingyu had arranged a tea-tasting and poetry recital for the scholarly guests.
