After a couple of rounds, Lord Yuan rose from his seat. "All this poetry is of flowers and the moon; nothing very original. I hear the Xie family has a grove of jujube trees. Jujube has such excellent associations. Why don't we all go to the jujube grove and compose something on that theme?"

Every scholar present knew perfectly well that jujube, in the language of good omens, carried the wish for sons to come early. Lord Yuan was making a pointed remark about the Xie family having no legitimate firstborn son.

They considered themselves colleagues and friends of Xie Jingyu; none of them were going to chime in at a moment like this.

At that, Qin Mingheng let out a short laugh. "I hear this jujube grove was planted by Madam Xie herself, which is rather uncommon. Come; let us go and see it."

When the most senior person present had spoken, the rest had no choice but to follow.

chapters.title: Xie Shiwei Causes Trouble
chapters.content:
The Xie residence was not large, and so the jujube grove was not far.

Before they had even drawn close, one could see the long row of jujube trees planted along the courtyard wall. They had not been in the ground long, but already showed a vigorous life: their branches lush and leafy, rustling softly in the wind.

Beneath the jujube trees, a group of children played. The older ones had gone with Xie Shian to the front courtyard for pitch-pot, while those seven years old and younger were at play here, full of noise and running about.

"Dense green boughs above the jujube tree; a bird cries out in the bright, breezy sky," one of the gentlemen could not help reciting. "When these trees are grown, the view here will be all the lovelier."

Lord Yuan said with a cheerful smile, "With so many jujube trees planted in the household, Lord and Lady Xie's wish is certain to come true."

Qin Mingheng's expression darkened.

Did that woman still cherish the hope of bearing a child with Xie Jingyu?

Did she know that the two children she had once borne were abandoned at the gate of his Xuanwu Marquis estate by Xie Jingyu himself?

Two barely-living infants, no bigger than a palm. On a bitterly cold snowy night, wrapped only in a single threadbare bed curtain, their small faces frozen to a blue-purple...

If she knew, would she hate Xie Jingyu?

No, she would hate him more. She would hate him for nearly sending those children to their deaths.

While Qin Mingheng was lost in thought, he heard his son's voice and looked over. He saw his son and the Xie household's second young master in a dispute.

The Xuanwu Marquis's heir fixed his eyes on the cricket Xie Shiwei had caught and was holding, and shouted furiously, "I saw that cricket first! It's mine!"

He stretched out his hand and ordered Xie Shiwei to hand it over.

"I caught it first," Xie Shiwei said with a snort. "It's your own fault for being too slow."

The six-year-old Xuanwu Marquis heir was beside himself with rage. "How dare you defy me! Who gave you the nerve? I'll say it again: hand it over!"

He carried about him the natural authority that came with being born into the nobility; and Xie Shiwei suddenly recalled who he was dealing with: the Xuanwu Marquis's eldest legitimate son, someone even his own father could not afford to offend.

If he antagonized the young lord of the Xuanwu Marquis estate, his father would certainly berate him harshly.

With this recognition, he looked reluctantly at the cricket in his hand, hesitating over whether to give it up.

"Second Young Master, the cricket was found on the Xie family's grounds, so it is the Xie family's property." Jiu'er stepped forward and spoke quietly in his ear. "The young lord of the Marquis estate may be of somewhat higher standing, but that does not give him the right to take what belongs to the Xie family. What would that say of the Xie family's dignity?"

This was exactly what Xie Shiwei had been thinking. The cricket was found on Xie family grounds, and he was the one who caught it. Why should he give it away?

He lifted the cricket high above his head. "If the young lord wants it, come and take it."

He was considerably taller and holding it high; the Xuanwu Marquis heir could not reach it, and in his fury shoved Xie Shiwei hard.

Xie Shiwei shoved back on instinct. He was two years older and stronger; the push sent the Xuanwu Marquis heir straight to the ground, followed by a cry of pain.

Xie Shiwei looked over and saw blood flowing from the young lord's hand where it had struck the stone. He stood frozen for a moment, then walked over quickly and bent down, about to help the boy up.

At that moment, a large hand seized him from behind and flung him aside.

He fell to the ground and looked up to see the Xuanwu Marquis, Qin Mingheng, looming over him in fury.

"M... Marquis..."

Xie Shiwei managed to get the word out.

In the next instant, Qin Mingheng's booted foot came down hard on Xie Shiwei's knee.

There was a crack.

The sound of bone breaking, sharp and distinct. Xie Shiwei's face went immediately white, and then a howl of agony tore out of him.

In the rear courtyard, Yun Chu and the Marchioness Lady Luo were chatting pleasantly. Lin Shi sat with Dai Furen discussing their children. The Old Madam and the First Madam were enjoying easy conversation with several other ladies.

The atmosphere in the rear courtyard was one of complete harmony.

Then, a matron came rushing over, her face stricken with alarm. "Madam, something has happened."

From the moment the banquet began to now, when it was nearly over, the Old Madam's mood had been excellent, because the thing she feared most had never come to pass. Just when her last worry had been on the verge of settling peacefully into her stomach, the servant's three words were like a clap of thunder striking her chest. She truly dreaded another disaster as absurd as the one at the birthday banquet.

Yun Chu's voice was calm. "What is it?"

The matron lowered her head. "The Xuanwu Marquis's young lord's fingers are bleeding a great deal..."

The Old Madam's heart settled slightly, and she let out a slow breath. "Children of five or six are at the most mischievous age. Hurting a finger by accident is nothing unusual. Has a physician been called...?"

Lady Luo shot to her feet, cutting the Old Madam off. "How did his fingers come to be hurt?"

"It was the Second Young Master..." The matron's head hung low. "The Second Young Master pushed the young lord, and the young lord fell on a stone and the fingers began to bleed."

"What?!" The Old Madam stood up so abruptly that her chair toppled over. She clutched the table, and said each word separately: "It was Wei'er who caused the young lord to be hurt?"

When the matron nodded, the Old Madam's vision began to go dark. Only the servants holding her up kept her from sinking to the ground.

The damage from last time had only cost the Xie family their reputation.

But injuring the Xuanwu Marquis's heir was as good as making an enemy of the Xuanwu Marquis himself. The consequences were too dreadful to contemplate.

The Old Madam was nearly faint with fear. She looked up, and saw Yun Chu standing perfectly composed. For some reason she could not name, the sight of it was like finding a solid place to stand; the strength came back to her limbs.

"Please do not alarm yourself, Marchioness. Let us go and see what has happened." Yun Chu said. "The jujube grove is this way."

Lin Shi's chest grew heavy.

The Xuanwu Marquis kept only one marchioness and had no concubines or serving women in his household; Lady Luo had given him only this one legitimate son over all these years. Husband and wife had poured everything into this single child; he was the apple of their eyes, held so carefully and loved so dearly, and now their precious son had been made to bleed at the Xie family's home. This would not be easy to smooth over.

Lin Shi followed as well.

When they reached the jujube grove, the physician was just coming out of the room. "The young lord's fingers have not reached the tendons or bone, but there was significant blood loss and he will need careful tending for about a month. The Second Young Master's leg is more serious. Even after it heals, his gait will not be quite the same as before."

Xie Jingyu's body swayed.

His eyes blazing, he looked at Qin Mingheng.

The young lord had only cut his fingers and shed a little blood; Qin Mingheng had responded by crushing his son's leg. Wei'er was only eight years old. His future was destroyed.

Qin Mingheng looked at him coldly. "A mere illegitimate son of yours, raised in the name of the legitimate line and given the status of a recognized heir, still does not stand on equal footing with a son of the Xuanwu Marquis estate. Even if all four of his limbs were broken, it would be hard to satisfy my fury. This matter will not be left here. You, Lord Xie, have been permissive of a son who dares to attack the young lord of the Marquis estate: this is defiance of his betters and an act of great impropriety. I will petition the Emperor to have justice done."

The moment the word "Emperor" was spoken, the Old Madam could no longer support herself. Her eyes rolled back and she fell unconscious at the courtyard gate.

Xie Jingyu's fists clenched until his knuckles ached.

The Marquis estate wielded no real power, but maintained extremely close ties with the imperial family. Qin Mingheng needed only a few words dropped in the Emperor's ear to make the Xie household's life very difficult indeed.

Wei'er's leg was a done thing; there was no undoing it. He could not sacrifice the entire Xie household on top of it.

He released his fist and clasped his hands together. "This official has been remiss in educating his son. That the young lord was injured is the Xie household's fault. I ask the Marquis to show his great magnanimity..."

Qin Mingheng's face was cold, and it was clear he was far from satisfied.

At that moment, Yun Chu walked in through the gate, went to stand before Qin Mingheng, and dipped in a slow, composed curtsy. "Marquis, I ask you to set aside your anger..."

chapters.title: This Is Going Too Far
chapters.content:
Qin Mingheng looked down at Yun Chu, who stood only a few steps away.

This was the closest they had ever stood in front of others. He breathed, and caught the faint fragrance rising from her.

His mind drifted back to that night five years ago: she had been breathtaking the night of her wedding, and five years had left no trace on her face. She was still as beautiful as ever.

"The Xuanwu Marquis's young lord was injured at the Xie household; the fault is certainly ours. But a child with a broken leg has already paid a price of his own making..." Yun Chu said, her head lowered. "The Xie family will bear all costs of the young lord's treatment, and will provide the finest remedies for this month of recovery..."

Watching her lower herself like this, Qin Mingheng felt a surge of anger rise within him.

The last time he had seen her, she had still been the eldest daughter of the Yun family, her chin lifted with pride, the very picture of confidence.

How had five years in the Xie household taught her to grovel like this? For the sake of the Xie family, how could she allow herself to be reduced to something so humble?

Qin Mingheng's fury only deepened. "Does the Marquis estate lack this little bit of silver? Madam Xie, do you think this settles everything so neatly?"

"Then what, in the Marquis's view, would be fitting?"

Lin Shi came forward from the side.

This was a matter between the Xie household and the Marquis estate. It was natural for Chu'er to step forward and offer apologies, and Lin Shi had no intention of interceding on the Xie family's behalf.

But she had watched the Xuanwu Marquis pour all his anger on Chu'er alone, while the entire Xie household stood by and not one of them stepped up.

The Old Madam had conveniently fainted to escape the situation; Xie Zhongcheng stood back with his hands behind him; the First Madam bowed her head in fear; Xie Jingyu stood silent to one side. As for the others, they were children: there was nothing they could do.

In this great Xie household, it was her daughter who had been left to stand alone at the front.

Lin Shi walked forward and, without drawing attention to it, stepped in front of Yun Chu. She raised her head. "The Marquis's young lord hurt one finger; a few days of care will heal it. The Xie household's second young master has lost the full use of one leg. Is that punishment not enough?"

The Marquis estate was a hereditary nobility, but held no real power. The Yun family, however, was a powerful military family with armies under its command, and the mistress of the Yun household had no reason to lower her head before the Marquis estate.

Yun Chu let out a quiet sigh.

With her mother stepping in, the Xuanwu Marquis could swallow whatever anger he still held, however great it was. How fortunate for the Xie family.

"Marquis, let us leave it at this." Lady Luo had already had the nurse take the child back to the Xuanwu Marquis estate's carriage. In truth, it was only a surface injury; by now it was nearly scabbed over, and it would be fully healed by the following day. There was truly no need to make such a scene. As for the Xie second young master, the kneecap had been crushed; walking in the future would be difficult...

"As my wife says." Qin Mingheng looked at Yun Chu. "Madam Xie is the daughter of a general's family. And yet she has raised a child like this. Truly it brings shame upon the Yun family's name. If she does not manage him properly, and he grows up to commit further outrages, she would do well not to let the Yun family suffer for it."

He said his piece, turned, and walked out. Lady Luo curtseyed to Lin Shi and Yun Chu, and followed.

With the Xuanwu Marquis estate departed, the other guests exchanged glances and one by one began to make their farewells as well.

Reaching the Xie family's front gate, they could not help but talk among themselves.

"Does the Xie family have some ill fortune about it? Two consecutive gatherings and both end like this."

"Did any of you see the Xuanwu Marquis's expression? He looked as though he could have devoured the Xie family whole. The Xie household and the Marquis have made an enemy of each other now."

"The Xie family's eldest son has only taken the top place in the prefectural examination. He is still at least ten years from any real position at court. Having offended the Marquis estate, the Xie family is finished."

"Don't forget the Xie family's connection to the Yun family by marriage. Just now, Yun Furen spoke up for the Xie family; that shows the two families have not fallen out."

"The Xuanwu Marquis relented in the end largely because his marchioness interceded. One cannot help but remark: what good fortune the Marchioness has, to have found so devoted a husband in the Xuanwu Marquis. That great estate of his, and not a single concubine or serving woman."

"..."

Yun Chu saw the Yun family to the gate and held Lin Shi's hand. "In the narrow view this was a children's quarrel, in the wider view this was the Xie household indulging a son in attacking another. The Xuanwu Marquis has a grievance he cannot vent; that anger will keep burning and will come back to trouble the Xie family in ways seen and unseen. Mother, please do not let yourself be drawn any further into this."

Lin Shi reached up and lightly touched Yun Chu's hair. "The last time, on account of the two children, your elder brother had a drink with the Board of Revenue Minister, intending to find some way to make things difficult for Xie Jingyu. Now it seems your elder brother need not go to that trouble. With the Xuanwu Marquis holding a grudge, that is enough to give him some bitterness to swallow, and then he will know: without the Yun family's protection, the Xie household is nothing."

A quiet warmth spread through Yun Chu.

This was what family meant: without needing to be told anything, they would stand at the front for her.

Just now the Xuanwu Marquis had spoken coldly to her, and her mother had seen it. She would certainly find a way to make him answer for it.

"Mother, please do not worry about me. Be careful on the way back." Yun Chu watched the Yun family's carriage until it was out of sight, then turned and walked back inside.

The Old Madam had come around by now, leaning on a matron's arm, and said in a weak but outraged voice: "The Xuanwu Marquis is going too far, simply going too far! Wei'er has lost a leg, his life is ruined, and still he won't release this household! What grounds does he have to go before the Emperor? We should be the ones lodging a complaint! He is a grown man of eight feet, and he crushed the leg of a son of the Xie household. The Emperor would certainly censure him!"

Xie Zhongcheng closed his eyes. "The Xuanwu Marquis's great-grandfather once saved the Emperor's ancestor at the cost of his own safety; the imperial family owes the Marquis estate an old debt of gratitude. The Emperor will naturally take the Marquis's side. What is more, the Xuanwu Marquis has only this one son; naturally that son is worth more than an illegitimate boy born of a serving woman..."

The First Madam's lips trembled. "Is that all? Does the Xie family simply swallow this humiliation?"

"The matter is far from over." Yun Chu came in from the doorway. "The Xuanwu Marquis left while his anger still burns. That fire can reignite at any moment."

Xie Jingyu knew this perfectly well. As long as Qin Mingheng held on to that grievance, there would be no peace in his future.

The Xie family had come this far through such effort. Was it all to stop here?

"Master, what is to become of Wei'er..." Lady He spoke up from the side in a small voice, barely keeping her tears from falling. "A renowned physician has come to the capital. Please... please let the physician come and treat Wei'er. He is only eight years old; he cannot be left like this..."

The Old Madam nodded. "Yes, yes; the physician must come at once. Wei'er's situation is the most pressing thing. Treat the injury first, then we can speak of everything else."

"Father, is it truly right to treat Wei'er's leg?" Xie Shian said in a measured voice. "It is precisely because the physician said Wei'er's leg was broken that the Xuanwu Marquis's fury was somewhat tempered. If Wei'er is healed, the Marquis will feel the Xie family has paid no meaningful price. I imagine Father can see what the consequence of that would be."

Lady He raised her eyes in disbelief.

An'er was Wei'er's own brother. How could he say something so heartless?

Brothers should stand together and face the world as one. How could he abandon Wei'er like this?

Yun Chu gave a cold, barely perceptible curl of her lip. This was something Xie Shian was capable of saying, because this man was selfish and coldhearted to the very core.

Xie Jingyu looked at Yun Chu, and for a flicker of a moment seemed to see mockery at the corner of her mouth. When he looked again, Yun Chu was only pressing her lips together with a look of concern. He must have been mistaken. He asked: "Wife, what is your view?"

Yun Chu raised her eyes, just about to reply.

Out of the corner of her vision, through the window behind Xie Jingyu, she caught sight of something beyond the two-meter-high outer wall, where a cluster of tall trees grew in a corner. From that shadowed corner, two small heads had just popped up.

She recognized those two faces. They were the young lord and the young Commandery Princess of the Prince of the Western Regions' estate.

chapters.title: Listen to Mother
chapters.content:
Yun Chu's pupils contracted sharply, and her breath caught.

"Madam, what is the matter?"

Seeing her expression change, Xie Jingyu felt a stirring of unease.

Yun Chu pulled her gaze back and steadied her voice. "An'er's words are not without reason. As for exactly how to handle Wei'er, my husband and the Old Madam can deliberate further. I have a slight headache; I will go and rest."

She said this, turned, and walked out.

Outside, she found Jiu'er kneeling in the courtyard, as though waiting to be dealt with at any moment.

"This has nothing to do with you." Yun Chu looked at her. "The Second Young Master has been hurt and will have a foul temper; you had better stay away from him for now. My courtyard is short a maid for sweeping. Come and help me for a couple of days."

Without waiting for Jiu'er to respond, Yun Chu walked quickly toward the rear of the courtyard.

This was the side yard closest to the jujube grove, situated at the very back of the Xie residence, and on the other side of its outer wall ran one of the city's small lanes.

With the guests dispersed, the Xie household's servants had all gone to the front courtyard to clear away. In this part of the grounds, not a single soul was in sight.

"How odd, I thought the Xie family was holding a banquet today." Chu Hongyu craned his neck left and right from the top of the wall. "Why is no one about?"

"Young Lord!" Amao's voice came from below. "You and the young Commandery Princess hold on tight. I am about to let go."

Chu Hongyu scrambled onto the wall properly and reached for his sister. "Changshen, hold this brick; push with your legs and you'll be up."

The little girl's pink fingers gripped the wall bricks and she heaved herself upward with all her strength, her small face flushed red with the effort, and still she could not quite make it.

"Changshen, if you can't get up, we won't be able to see Mother." Chu Hongyu reached to help her, then called down to the person below: "Amao, a little higher; just a little higher."

Amao's face was a picture of misery. It was no one's fault but his own that he was not tall enough, and no amount of tiptoeing would change that.

Even so, with a final effort from the little girl, she managed at last to pull herself up to the top of the wall.

Amao let out a deep, relieved breath. He pressed his palms together, blew on them, and then ran up the wall with his feet, dropping silently down into the courtyard below. He checked that there was no one in sight, then looked up and stretched out both arms. "Young Commandery Princess, jump; do not be afraid. I will catch you."

This was the first time Chu Changshen had ever done anything like this.

She wobbled to her feet on the wall, looked down, and immediately felt dizzy with fear.

But the thought of Mother, right here, just beyond this wall, Mother whom she was about to see at last, filled her with all the courage she could hold.

Her long lashes, fine as feathers, swept closed. She spread her arms and jumped, falling into Amao's hold. He set her down gently on the ground, then looked up. "Young Lord, come down quickly. Old Servant thinks someone is coming."

Chu Hongyu nodded. He was just rising when he saw two figures appear around the corner. He moved to hide, then realized one of them was Yun Chu.

He broke into a delighted grin and opened his mouth to call out "Mother."

Yun Chu raised her hand quickly and pressed one finger to her lips.

The Xie family was still nearby; if the young lord made a noise and drew the Xie household's attention, the Xie family would use it as a way to curry favor with the Prince of the Western Regions.

"Shhh!"

Chu Hongyu copied the gesture.

In his excitement, his foot slipped, and the next moment he was toppling forward and down.

Yun Chu's heart stopped cold.

Amao, still standing below the wall, caught him just in time.

"Yu'er, did I not tell you last time that you must not come to the Xie household again without permission?" Yun Chu kept her expression deliberately stern. "And not only have you come yourself, but you have brought the young Commandery Princess along to climb the wall with you. What would have happened if you had fallen?"

Chu Hongyu poked at his fingers. "Changshen has been dreaming about Mother every day, and as it happens, Father is not here. So I brought her to see you. Mother, look, this is my sister. Her name is Chu Changshen."

He had barely finished speaking when his sister, normally timid and wary of strangers, tumbled into Yun Chu's arms like a little rolling snowball.

Yun Chu smiled with her whole face and gathered the child close. "Changshen, I have missed you too, all these days."

Chu Hongyu's round, dark eyes went wide in disbelief. "Mother, when did you meet Changshen? How come I didn't know?"

"A few nights ago, Changshen slipped away from the estate and I happened to find her." Yun Chu took Chu Hongyu's hand with her other arm. "This is not the place to talk. Come back to my courtyard first."

Tingshuang had already cleared all the servants from this part of the grounds. They walked all the way back without passing a single person.

In the familiar courtyard, Chu Hongyu was quite at home. He grinned. "Mother, Father got an imperial edict and has gone to Jizhou on business. He won't be back for half a month. So Changshen and I will stay here with you for half a month!"

Yun Chu frowned. "Half a month is too long. I am afraid that will not do."

"Then how long can we stay?" Chu Hongyu put his arms around her neck. "Whatever Mother says, that is what we will do. We listen to Mother."

The little girl climbed onto her knee and threw her arms around Yun Chu's neck from the other side. The two of them were small but surprisingly strong; each seemed determined to pull her neck toward themselves, and she felt it twisting one way and then the other until it was nearly in a knot.

Chu Hongyu was put out. He was sharing Mother with his sister, and his sister was trying to have her all to herself. He wished he had left her behind.

But then he caught sight of the light that had come into his sister's dark eyes, and he felt the trip had been entirely worth it.

Changshen had always been delicate and sickly. At four she was still smaller and thinner than a child of three, and she had not spoken a word. The physicians said there was nothing wrong with her throat; it was a different kind of condition brought on by years of frail health, a withdrawal from the world, an inability to see beyond her own small interior life. That small world had room only for him, her brother, and occasionally for their father, but only when Father happened to say precisely the right thing.

This was the first time he had ever seen Changshen accept another person like this.

He liked Mother so much himself; he had always known Changshen would feel the same.

"You may stay for two days." Yun Chu liked both children very much, and drew them each close with one arm. "While you are in the Xie household, you must stay in my courtyard. No going out on your own. Can you do this?"

Chu Hongyu's voice rang out clearly. "Yes."

The little girl blinked her great eyes and nodded.

Yun Chu tapped both their noses in turn. "The two of you crawled through who knows what just now and look like a pair of muddy little monkeys. Time to bathe."

She truly had no words. These two little ones had slipped in carrying a small pack on Amao's back, and inside it was nothing but a change of clothes.

She sent Tingshuang and Tingxue to bathe Chu Hongyu, while she herself bathed the little girl. When she had removed Changshen's dress, her heart clenched as though seized by a fist.

She had known the little girl was thin, but not like this: nothing but bones, not a scrap of flesh anywhere except perhaps her face, which was the only place she seemed to have kept any roundness, and which made her so impossibly sweet to look at.

Looking closer, she could see faint needle marks scattered all over the child's body.

They were very clear, quite different from any sign of deliberate harm; they looked more like the marks left by years of regular acupuncture.

"Changshen, Changshen..."

She murmured the name, and some half-formed understanding began to rise in her, a sense of why the Prince of the Western Regions might have given his little Commandery Princess this particular name.

Her feelings complicated, she bathed the little girl. In the middle of it, Tingshuang's voice came from outside the door. "The Master is here. He says it is urgent and he needs to speak with the Madam."

Yun Chu scooped the little girl out of the tub, dried her off, and helped her into her dress, then smiled. "I'll step out for a moment."

The little girl gripped her hem, her great eyes looking up at her, as though afraid that once she walked away, she would not come back.

"Good girl. I'll be right back."

Those soft pink hands finally let go of her.

chapters.title: Leaving Him No Way Out
chapters.content:
Xie Jingyu waited in the outer reception room.

He had been sitting for some time before he saw Yun Chu emerge from the inner chamber.

He clasped his hands behind his back and said in a low voice: "I spoke with the Old Madam. We have decided to send Wei'er to the estate in the outskirts of the capital. What does my wife think?"

"It is not a bad place for him. A bit of hardship will teach him some sense." Yun Chu looked up. "When does my husband plan to send Wei'er?"

Xie Jingyu said each word deliberately: "Now. Immediately."

Yun Chu asked, "Should we not wait until Wei'er has recovered somewhat before sending him?"

"The Xuanwu Marquis is still at the height of his anger. If the Xie household does not show some response at this moment, the Marquis will keep this matter lodged in his heart." Xie Jingyu pressed his lips together. "Let Wei'er endure a little discomfort."

Yun Chu laughed inwardly and said nothing.

Xie Jingyu and Xie Shian, father and son: they were cast from the same mold. Both gifted scholars, both coldly self-interested.

In truth, there was nothing for her to feel wronged about from her past life. If Xie Shian could cast aside even his own younger brother, how much less would he care about a stepmother with no blood connection to him?

"Once Wei'er is sent away, the Xie household will still need to go and make a formal apology." Xie Jingyu looked at the woman across from him. "Wife, come with me."

Since he had already decided to bow his head to the Xuanwu Marquis estate, he might as well do it thoroughly. However the Marquis chose to humiliate or insult or berate him, he would endure it. In a few more years, once An'er had achieved something, the Xie family would eventually recover every bit of face it had lost.

Yun Chu's brow creased slightly.

She had no desire to go with Xie Jingyu and suffer the Marquis's cold treatment.

While she and Xie Jingyu were speaking, two small fuzzy heads appeared from behind the standing screen.

"Changshen, look at that man. He is Mother's husband." Chu Hongyu lowered his voice. "What do you think is good about him compared to our Father? Why did Mother marry him instead of Father?"

Chu Changshen blinked her large, uncomprehending eyes: she had no answer either.

"Prrrpt."

An odd sound came from Chu Hongyu's rear.

Chu Changshen's delicate little nose wrinkled, and she promptly covered it with both hands.

"Prrrpt. Prrrpt."

Two more sounds in quick succession.

Xie Jingyu, waiting for Yun Chu's answer, heard something stir behind the screen, and at the same moment a peculiar smell reached him.

He frowned. "Smells rather like spoiled food."

He moved involuntarily toward the screen.

Yun Chu had already glimpsed the two little silhouettes swaying behind it.

She was suddenly very tired. Yu'er had clearly not stayed in the inner chamber as told, and had brought Changshen out with him.

"My husband!"

Yun Chu called out to stop him.

"Very well; I will go with my husband tomorrow to the Xuanwu Marquis estate to offer our apologies. My husband should have the gifts of contrition prepared."

Xie Jingyu's steps halted. He looked at Yun Chu. "Thank you, wife."

Yun Chu could only hope he would leave quickly. "Is my husband not still sending Wei'er to the estate? It is getting late; it will soon be too late."

At this reminder, Xie Jingyu finally went out.

The moment he was gone, Yun Chu stepped quickly behind the screen. She had been ready to put on a stern face, but the sight before her stopped her: Chu Hongyu stood with both knees pressed inward and his hands alternately clutching his small belly and his small bottom, hopping in place on the spot, his entire face flushed crimson.

Laughter rose in her before she could stop it. "Come along. Mother will take you to the privy."

Meanwhile, Xie Jingyu and his men arrived at Xie Shiwei's courtyard.

He looked around the room. Since Xie Shiwei had been subjected to household discipline a month ago, all his belongings had been removed by Yun Chu's order.

Yun Chu had said: heaven, when it means to confer a great mission upon someone, first makes their will suffer and their sinews and bones toil. The living conditions were already sparse enough; and yet Shiwei had shown not the slightest improvement.

A few days ago, when Wei'er had mistreated the maids, he should have sent the boy far away without delay. At the very least, he should have had him confined to the ancestral hall for several months. Had he done so, today's disaster would never have happened.

But there was no point saying this now.

Xie Jingyu's expression was dark. He walked into the inner chamber and looked at Xie Shiwei lying on the bed, white and bloodless, and said one word at a time: "Shiwei, you have disappointed me beyond measure. I have given you one chance after another, and each time you have shown not a trace of remorse, committing one offense after another. Today, I am having you taken to the estate in the capital's outskirts, where you will live permanently. Rest and recover your health there, and at the same time, reflect on yourself. I hope that the next time we meet, father and son, I can see you in a new light."

Xie Shiwei was still in the agony of his broken leg, and when he saw Xie Jingyu come in, he had thought his father had come out of concern.

He never, never could have imagined he would hear these words: that his father was actually going to send him to the estate.

He looked at Xie Shian, who stood behind Xie Jingyu, and cried out: "Elder Brother, please say something to Father for me. Tell him I have changed, I truly have changed. This time it was an accident. It was the Xuanwu Marquis's young lord who tried to take my things first, and he was the one who pushed me..."

"Enough!" Xie Jingyu's voice cracked with anger. "This is the situation you have brought about, and still you place the blame on others. Do you not see where you went wrong?"

Xie Shian let out a slow breath. "Shiwei, the Xuanwu Marquis said that even cutting off all four of your limbs could barely satisfy his anger. Sending you to the estate is to protect your life. It is something Father does with no other choice. You must understand the depth of Father's feeling."

Xie Shiwei's face went white with fear.

His leg was already broken, and still the Xuanwu Marquis wanted more; he wanted all four of his limbs broken...

If he was sent all the way out to the estate in the outskirts, would that not make it even easier for the Xuanwu Marquis to have him killed?

"Father, I was wrong..." Xie Shiwei rolled himself off the bed. "I truly know I was wrong. I beg you, please give me one more chance..."

Lady He wept. "Master, Shiwei is still young; there is still time to guide him..."

"Father, I will change for the better, I promise!" Xie Shiwei sobbed breathlessly. "Only please do not send me away. I will do anything you ask, anything."

He was only an eight-year-old child. His leg was broken. To be sent so far away like this was to leave him with no way out at all...

"Come!" Xie Jingyu said coldly. "Take the Second Young Master to the carriage."

Two servant boys came in and hoisted Xie Shiwei up from either side, carrying him out between them.

A carriage was waiting in the courtyard, with Xie Zhongcheng sitting inside. He sighed. "Wei'er, from now on you will stay with your grandfather at the estate. An estate is not such a bad place. Once you have set your mind right, your father will naturally bring you back to the capital."

"No, no!" Xie Shiwei struggled wildly. Every time his leg was so much as touched, the pain was enough to tear his soul from his body. "I don't want to go to the estate. Father, give me one more chance. Mother, Mother, save me..."

He had completely lost control, and cried out in Lady He's direction, calling her mother.

Xie Jingyu's eyes darkened. The two servant boys did not dare delay further; they hauled Xie Shiwei up and dumped him into the carriage. When he thrashed about violently, they produced rope and bound him, then stuffed a cloth into his mouth.

Lady He's tears fell like a string of broken beads.

She had not yet come to terms with the reality of Wei'er's ruined leg, and now she was to bear the agony of being separated from her child as well. It felt as though her heart had been split in two; she wept until she nearly lost consciousness.

Several of the other concubines stood at the not-too-distant entrance to the courtyard, and looks of puzzlement passed between them.

Concubine Tao was the first to speak. "Have any of you noticed that Concubine He seems almost too invested in the young masters? When the First Young Master passed the examination, she was the most jubilant of anyone; and now that the Second Young Master is being sent away, she is more grief-stricken than anyone. Is it because her feelings for the Master run so deep that they extend to all his children?"

Concubine Yu and Concubine Jiang said nothing, only held their own children closer and silently reminded themselves: do not cause trouble...

chapters.title: A Complete Family
chapters.content:
Yun Chu and the two children played in the inner chamber.

Since coming back to this life, her heart had never felt so full. It was like a teacup filled to the brim with clear water, fragrant and overflowing, a scent she could never breathe in enough of.

She kept thinking: if those two children of hers had not been lost, would they be about this age by now...

Tingshuang stood outside, listening to the laughter and talk from within, and the corners of her mouth curved upward too. She hoped, with all her heart, that the Madam could always be this happy.

Before long, Tingfeng came in from outside. "The Second Young Master will be leaving for the estate shortly. Is the Madam being asked to come and see him off?"

Tingshuang hesitated for a moment, then shook her head. "Tell them the Madam has a headache and is not feeling well."

If the young lord and the young Commandery Princess had not appeared, the Madam would certainly have gone to see him off, leaving no ground for criticism.

But the Madam had said she would allow the young lord and the young Commandery Princess to stay in the Xie household for only two days, which amounted to twenty-four hours. How brief that time was; it was not to be spent on the Second Young Master.

Yun Chu's whole being was occupied by the two children in front of her; she had entirely forgotten about Xie Shiwei, who was on the verge of being sent away.

"Changshen, your eyes are so beautiful; your smile is beautiful too." She looked at the two children before her. "Yu'er, sit with Changshen. Mother wants to paint your portrait."

Chu Hongyu put his arm around Chu Changshen, and the two children sat obediently on the daybed, their dark eyes open and round, looking for all the world like a pair of plump New Year's poster children, though both were rather too thin.

Yun Chu thought to herself: if these two children were in her care, she would make sure they were both well-fed and round.

She talked to the children as she painted. She had never been diligent about martial arts training when she was small, but she had never missed a single lesson of her other studies; her tutor had frequently praised her painting and calligraphy.

In less than half a shichen, two lifelike little figures appeared on the paper.

"Oh, how beautiful." Chu Hongyu tilted his head. "But the painting is missing someone."

Yun Chu asked, "Who is missing?"

"Mother, of course." Chu Hongyu pulled Chu Changshen to her feet. "Changshen, you paint Mother. Put all three of us together."

His sister never spoke; she was not fond of company; but when she was alone she liked to fill paper with paintings. Father had once hired dozens of tutors to teach her, and in the end only one female tutor had managed to communicate with her at all. She had learned quickly and painted everything with great skill.

Chu Changshen picked up a brush and began to paint, swiftly and without hesitation.

With just a few strokes she sketched the outline of a woman alongside the girl in the painting.

Chu Hongyu pouted: his sister had painted Mother next to herself, not next to him. He had found Mother first...

Chu Changshen painted on. When the woman's outline was done, she began on the robes: two or three touches of ink, and peach blossoms bloomed across the cloth. The robes were finished quickly, then she set to work on the hair, carefully and precisely. When everything else was done, one thing remained: the face. A blank face, without a single feature.

Chu Hongyu murmured, "Changshen's favorite person to paint is Mother, but we have never seen our real mother, so whenever Changshen paints Mother, she never draws the face..."

Yun Chu felt something catch in her chest.

To have never seen the woman who gave you life, and yet to keep painting her, over and over: the longing of both children for their mother went without saying.

She said gently, "Yu'er, may I ask, with no intention to pry: why is your mother not with you?"

"Father said Mother died giving birth to us." Chu Hongyu lowered his head. "When Changshen and I were born we were only as big as an adult's palm, very small and very light, and we nearly died too. Father took us to a physician to keep us alive. I was well again by the time I was one; Changshen was in treatment until she was three, and has only been getting a little better this past year..."

"That is all past now, all behind you." Yun Chu gathered both children into her arms. "Whatever suffering came before, all the days ahead will be sweet."

"Yes, yes!" Chu Hongyu raised his face, his eyes bright as stars. "We have found Mother, and you will love us just like our real mother did, won't you?"

Yun Chu nodded with certainty.

Chu Changshen wriggled free of her arms, picked up the brush, and began to draw the woman's face. Stroke by stroke, with great care.

As she worked, the little girl glanced up at Yun Chu from time to time. When the face was done, Chu Hongyu let out a cry of wonder: "Changshen, that looks exactly like Mother!"

Yun Chu looked, and it was true: the features and their expression, even the faintest trace of a smile, were all her own. Anyone who knew her, even in passing, would recognize it at once.

She was just reaching out to take the painting for a closer look when the little girl would not allow it, and picked up the brush again.

Three more strokes, and a tall man stood at the woman's side. A few more, and a face appeared: Yun Chu recognized it immediately as Chu Yi, the Prince of the Western Regions.

"Changshen, why did you put Father in it." Chu Hongyu's small face crumpled. "I can't stand Father. I wish he would never come back."

Yun Chu pressed her hand over his mouth. "Don't say such things. If your father truly never came back, it would mean he had died at the hands of bandits. That would mean countless innocent people suffered, and it would also mean that you and Changshen had no father to protect you."

While she spoke to Chu Hongyu, Changshen had already finished the man's full figure.

On the paper: the man upright and full of life. The woman graceful and gentle. The boy spirited and bright. The girl as finely made as carved jade.

Four people, alive on the paper, just like a complete family.

The three of them, one large and two small, were still admiring the painting when Tingshuang's voice came from outside the door: "Madam, a servant boy who went out just now has come back with news: the Prince of the Western Regions left and then returned, and is already back at the Prince's estate."

Her voice had barely faded when Tingfeng came running in from the outer courtyard. "Madam, Amao says the Prince of the Western Regions has discovered that the young lord and the young Commandery Princess are missing, and is leading people to search the entire city for them."

Yun Chu sat bolt upright.

If the Prince of the Western Regions discovered that both children were in her care, she would be jumping into the Huanghe River without clearing her name.

She said quickly: "Yu'er, Changshen, hurry up and get dressed. I will have Qiutong take you out. Tingfeng, tell Amao to be ready to meet them at the south side gate of the Xie residence."

Chu Hongyu went pale with fright. When his Father was in a rage, it was over for him, and all the people around him would go down with him.

He had brought Changshen into this mess too.

He scrambled off the daybed and straightened his clothes, then followed Qiutong with Chu Changshen.

Yun Chu and Tingshuang walked ahead. They were just about to leave the courtyard when voices came from the gate: the matrons greeting someone. "Good evening to Concubine Yu. Good evening to the Third Young Master."

And then Concubine Yu and Xie Shiyun walked into Shengju.

Qiutong and Tingshuang drew together, quietly shielding the children behind them.

"I heard the Madam has a headache. I have come with a soup for her." Concubine Yu held a tray in both hands. "Madam is not feeling well; she should be resting. If there is anything to be done, please let this concubine help."

"As it happens, there is something I would ask you." Yun Chu said. "Come inside with me."

A flutter of happiness went through Concubine Yu. The Madam had kept her at a distance for so long, and at last here was an opening. She immediately took Xie Shiyun's hand and followed Yun Chu inside with eager steps.

Qiutong and Tingshuang angled quietly to one side, and the moment Concubine Yu and Xie Shiyun had gone in, they lifted the children in their arms and slipped out of Shengju.

chapters.title: Prince Pingxi Searches the Residence
chapters.content:
Yun Chu walked into the flower hall with Tingyu.

Looking at the pastries on the table, she said, "I remember the mung bean cakes you make are softer than usual. When you have time, make some and send them to me."

Tingyu beamed with joy. "Yes, Madam. This servant will go make them right now."

As long as Madam was willing to employ her, sooner or later she would return to Madam's side. Like before, she would regain her dignity, and who in the residence would dare give her cold looks again?

Yun Chu nodded. Just as Tingyu was about to withdraw, a matron rushed in anxiously. "Madam, Prince Pingxi has brought many people and says he wants to search the Xie residence."

Yun Chu's fingers gripping the teacup suddenly froze.

People from Prince Pingxi's residence had arrived so quickly — this was somewhat beyond her expectations. Fortunately, Qiutong and Tingshuang had already left with the two children.

Tingyu said in shock, "Although Prince Pingxi holds high rank and great power, he doesn't have the authority to search private residences, does he? Could it be that some thief has escaped, so Prince Pingxi..."

"It's the Young Lord and Young Princess from Prince Pingxi's residence who have gone missing," the matron said hurriedly. "The Master has already gone to the residence gate to respectfully receive Prince Pingxi. He specifically sent this old servant to report to Madam and have the concubines and young ladies in the residence avoid the situation."

Yun Chu nodded and immediately had someone notify the female family members.

Just as she finished giving instructions, she heard many voices — people from Prince Pingxi's residence had already searched their way to the rear courtyard.

In all of the capital, only Prince Pingxi would dare to act this way.

The First Prince was the Crown Prince and needed popular support — he would never casually search private residences and invite impeachment from all the officials.

The other princes lacked the capability to back themselves up — how would they dare do such a thing?

Seeing Xie Jingyu accompanying Prince Pingxi as they drew closer, Yun Chu, as the mistress of the household, naturally couldn't hide away like the concubines.

She stood up and went forward. "This one greets Your Highness."

Chu Yi's gaze fell upon Yun Chu.

For some reason, he thought of that night when she held Changsheng in her arms.

Under the moonlight, her skin was like white porcelain. That night, in his dazed state, he had felt that her beautiful eyes resembled Changsheng's very much.

Now, with daylight to see by, he could see even more clearly — not only did the eyes look alike, even the shape of the lips seemed as if carved from the same mold.

He paused before speaking. "Lady Xie, pardon the intrusion."

At that moment, the four guards who had been searching Sheng Residence emerged and shook their heads at Prince Pingxi.

He narrowed his eyes slightly.

Two hours ago, just as he was about to depart for Jizhou, the Crown Prince had suddenly fallen ill. The Emperor had urgently issued edicts summoning him back. After he returned to his residence and was just preparing to take his eldest son, Brother Yu, to the Eastern Palace to visit the sick, he learned that Brother Yu had gone missing, and Changsheng had also disappeared with him.

He immediately assembled personnel to search the entire city.

The first residence he went to was the Eldest Princess's residence, because Brother Yu was close to the Eldest Princess.

The second place he came to was the Xie residence. Perhaps because of how Changsheng had been so reluctant to part from this Lady Xie that night, he vaguely felt that the two children might have come here.

But the search had found nothing.

"Lord Xie, Lady Xie, pardon the disturbance."

Chu Yi turned to leave.

Just then, a child's voice rang out. "There's a shoe over there!"

Yun Chu turned her head to see Xie Shiyun, who had been held by Tingyu's hand all along, suddenly rush over and point into the flower bushes while calling out.

Following Xie Shiyun's pointing finger, her breathing stopped for a moment — it was Brother Yu's brocade boot.

Chu Yi's footsteps also stopped. Looking at that shoe, though his daily official duties kept him busy and naturally he didn't personally put shoes on his children, he felt this shoe looked somewhat familiar.

"That's not my shoe," Xie Shiyun's childish voice rang out. "Whose shoe fell here?"

Tingyu immediately noticed that Yun Chu's expression had changed. She quickly pulled back her own son.

Xie Shiyun pressed his lips tightly together.

He had said long ago that there were other children in Mother's courtyard, which was why Mother no longer liked him, but his concubine mother didn't believe him.

Now he had finally found evidence. Since Prince Pingxi was also here, he would borrow Prince Pingxi's people to find the children in Mother's courtyard.

Tingyu covered her son's mouth, her peripheral vision sweeping toward that shoe.

It indeed wasn't Brother Yun's shoe, but one could tell at a glance it was the shoe size for a three or four-year-old child. In the residence, there was only one boy of that age — Brother Yun.

This proved that in Madam's courtyard, there truly were other children.

Was Madam really going to adopt other children?

Tingyu's emotions became extremely complicated.

Yun Chu's expression only changed slightly before returning to normal. She quickly walked over and picked up the small shoe from the flower bushes. "Yesterday I had the maids in the courtyard searching everywhere for a shoe. So it fell here. This is for my maternal nephew's upcoming birthday — I specifically had someone make it in the capital's most fashionable style."

Chu Yi nodded. "Much obliged. This prince takes his leave."

He quickly departed with the guards.

Just then, Yun Chu saw Qiutong and Tingshuang walking in from outside. The two nodded at her, and only then did her anxiously suspended heart finally settle back into her stomach.

Chu Yi walked to the gate and was about to search the next location when a servant came to report. "Your Highness, the Young Lord and Young Princess have been found. They sneaked out of the residence to stroll on the streets, with Guard Mao accompanying them."

As the words fell, two nannies carrying the two young masters walked before Chu Yi.

Both little ones knew they had done wrong. They hugged the nannies' necks tightly, buried their heads, and didn't make a sound.

Chu Yi looked at Chu Hongyu, his gaze involuntarily moving downward to land on his feet. Then his eyes narrowed. "Where are your shoes?"

Chu Hongyu's two little feet rubbed together. "Don't... don't know where I dropped them."

"Oh?" A cold smile floated to the corners of Chu Yi's lips. "Why don't you tell me how your shoe ran to the Xie residence?"

Chu Hongyu's little face turned pale in an instant. His instinct was to deny it. "No, I didn't go to the Xie family..."

Chu Yi's voice grew colder. "When did I say you went to the Xie family? You've simply confessed without being pressed."

Before he could finish speaking, the little girl lying in the nanny's arms suddenly came to her senses. Opening her large, dewy eyes, she reached out two short arms toward him.

In that moment, Chu Yi's heart softened at once.

Before Changsheng turned two, she spent most of her time in unconscious sleep. After she passed two years old, she finally improved somewhat, but she needed regular acupuncture. Each acupuncture session made her cry loudly, and she grew increasingly resistant to him, this father who forced her to undergo treatment.

By the time she reached three years old, Changsheng's illness had finally greatly improved, but her eyes had lost their light.

She wouldn't actively look at him, this father. She wouldn't let him hold her even once. She was unwilling to stay with him for even a quarter-hour...

This was the very first time in history that she had actively reached out her hands, wanting him to hold her.

Chu Yi let Chu Hongyu off and embraced his daughter.

Chu Hongyu breathed a huge sigh of relief.

In the past, even when Father was scolding him until his head dripped blood, even if his sister heard it, she had no reaction whatsoever.

But now, his sister would actually take the initiative to help him out of trouble.

After staying with Mother for a while, his sister seemed somewhat different.

chapters.title: Keep This Secret for Me
chapters.content:
The sky had already darkened.

Yun Chu's gaze fell upon Xie Shiyun. "Brother Yun, Mother asks you — whose shoe do you think this one in my courtyard should belong to?"

Her voice was calm without fluctuation, but Tingyu could sense the hidden anger in Madam's voice.

She quickly spoke up. "Madam, Brother Yun, he..."

"I'm asking Brother Yun. Concubine Yu, go stand to the side first." Yun Chu's voice was very light. "Brother Yun, you know that Mother dislikes children who lie the most."

Tingyu was nearly dying of anxiety.

But Tingshuang stood right beside her, staring at her coldly. She didn't dare make any movement at all.

Xie Shiyun stood before Yun Chu with his head lowered.

A month ago, every time he came to Yusheng Residence, he would be held on Mother's lap. Back then, as long as Mother was made happy, she would give him many good things.

During this period of time, Mother had grown increasingly cold toward him.

Clearly he hadn't done anything wrong, so why had he lost Mother's favor?

He felt wronged, truly too wronged.

Thinking this way, two lines of tears appeared on Xie Shiyun's face. Golden beans kept falling down. He raised his head and said through his tears, "Mother, have you raised another child, so you don't want Brother Yun anymore?"

Yun Chu steadied her mind and spoke. "What do you mean by 'raised another child'? What does that mean?"

"Mother, don't lie to me anymore. I saw everything." Xie Shiyun cried loudly. "I saw that in Mother's courtyard there's a boy about the same age as me. Mother held him and smiled at him. He's going to be Mother's son from now on, isn't he? Mother will never love me again..."

Yun Chu's fingers tightened.

As expected, she had guessed that Brother Yun must know something. Otherwise, with Brother Yun's timid nature, he would never have mentioned the shoe in front of Prince Pingxi.

She turned her head to look at Tingyu. "Did Concubine Yu also see it?"

Tingyu's fingers twisted tightly together.

She bit the tip of her own tongue and said, "In response to Madam, this concubine saw nothing. Brother Yun must have seen wrong. This concubine will manage Brother Yun well and won't let him speak carelessly before the Old Madam and the Master."

Yun Chu lowered her eyes.

Her courtyard was no longer safe either. She absolutely couldn't let those two children come to the Xie residence again.

She took a sip of tea and sighed. "Brother Yun didn't see wrong. There truly is a child sent by the Yun family in my courtyard, prepared to be adopted under my name as my legitimate son. It's just that I've always felt this doesn't conform to propriety, so I haven't mentioned this matter to the Old Madam or the Master. Concubine Yu, before I make a decision, you must keep this secret for me."

Tingyu could hardly believe it.

The truth was actually just as she had guessed — Madam really was going to adopt a child with Yun family blood.

This truly didn't conform to propriety and violated ritual law!

But as long as the Yun family decided on it, there would be no room for the Xie family to refuse. No matter how much this matter violated ritual law, it would become reality.

She gripped her handkerchief tightly. "This concubine will forever be Madam's person and will definitely keep Madam's secret sealed tight."

Yun Chu looked at her quietly.

The opportunity had been given. It just depended on whether Tingyu would cherish this chance.

Later that evening, people from outside came to report that Prince Pingxi had taken the Young Lord into the palace. Yun Chu knew this matter had thoroughly passed.

The next morning, just after getting up, Yun Chu felt the oppressive heat.

People in the residence came to pay respects as usual. With one less Xie Shiwei, it seemed nothing had changed.

Yun Chu distributed the Xie residence's affairs and continued researching the layout and facilities of the hot spring estate. After the hour of the dragon, Xie Jingyu returned to the residence after court. She changed her clothes and walked to the front courtyard.

Xie Jingyu had already changed out of his court robes. In his hand he carried a gift box for making amends. "This is a superior inkstone. Does Madam think it will do?"

Yun Chu spoke. "Marquis Xuanwu's residence doesn't lack such things. What he wants is just an attitude."

Xie Jingyu also thought so.

The husband and wife got into the carriage and sat facing each other. The two were very close.

Yun Chu tilted her head slightly. She lifted the carriage curtain just a little and looked toward the bustling street outside.

Xie Jingyu looked at her delicate white profile. For some reason, he felt that Yun Chu seemed to be getting further and further away from him, like clouds at the edge of the sky — visible but untouchable.

If she still had even the slightest bit of expectation toward him, he would be willing to try to forget that night when she lost her virtue.

But the depths of her eyes looking at him no longer held any light. The affection between them as husband and wife had become thinner than paper.

Bringing her to Marquis Xuanwu's residence, he knew what he would have to pay, yet he still brought her.

"Madam."

Xie Jingyu's throat tightened.

He couldn't help but call out.

Yun Chu put down the curtain and turned her head. "Husband?"

"All these years, have you ever blamed me?"

Hearing this question, Yun Chu almost laughed.

In her previous life, of course she had blamed, resented, hated — but what of it?

Before the blood feud of her family, what did these things count for?

"What are you saying, Husband?" Yun Chu spoke warmly. "I am a woman of the Xie family. The Xie family's honor and disgrace are more important than my life. Coming to Marquis Xuanwu to apologize is my duty. How could I blame you, Husband?"

Xie Jingyu's voice was dry. "Madam, you know that's not what I'm asking about."

Yun Chu lowered her eyes. "Bearing branches and spreading leaves for the Xie family is also my duty. Since I don't have this ability, it's normal for you not to come to my chambers, Husband. I won't harbor resentment."

"I want to make amends for my wrongs." Xie Jingyu looked at her eyelids. "Tonight I'll go to Yusheng Residence..."

Yun Chu's fingers tightened. Without raising her head, she said, "Husband, my body is somewhat inconvenient."

The expression on Xie Jingyu's face gradually faded.

Regardless of whether she was truly inconvenient or falsely inconvenient, he could tell that she simply didn't look forward to him going to Yusheng Residence.

The carriage traveled smoothly all the way to the gate of Marquis Xuanwu's residence.

After getting out of the carriage, Xie Jingyu presented his calling card. The guard at the gate took the card inside to report.

Qin Mingheng was in the courtyard playing with his dog. He threw the frisbee in his hand, and the dog leaped up to catch it, then came over wagging its tail.

"Marquis, Lord Xie requests an audience."

Qin Mingheng glanced at the calling card and said with a cold laugh, "Have him wait outside."

The reason he had gone to Old Madam Xie's birthday banquet last time was because he heard Yun Chu had fallen gravely ill, so he took the opportunity to go see her.

He had never looked up to Xie Jingyu as a person — too despicable and shameless.

Qin Mingheng continued playing with the dog.

At this moment, he heard two young servants discussing in low voices not far away. "Lord Xie has offended our Marquis. He won't have good days ahead."

"The Yun family's eldest daughter once topped the capital. Who knows why she would marry down to Lord Xie? Once a first-rank legitimate daughter, now she actually has to accompany him to the Marquis's residence to bow her head in apology. How lamentable and pitiful."

Qin Mingheng's movements suddenly stopped. He inquired, "Lady Xie also came? Why didn't you say so earlier?"

On such a hot day, she was standing outside being exposed to the sun for so long — how could her delicate skin like white porcelain withstand such intense sun exposure?

He immediately spoke. "Let them in."

The young servant quickly ran toward the residence gate.

chapters.title: Please Enlighten Me, Marquis
chapters.content:
The sun in the fifth month was indeed growing more and more intense.

They had been standing for less than a quarter-hour when a young servant ran out and said, "Lord Xie, Lady Xie, please follow me inside."

Yun Chu had thought Marquis Xuanwu would deliberately make things difficult for Xie Jingyu for a while. She hadn't expected him to let them in so quickly.

This was the first time in both her lives combined that she had entered Marquis Xuanwu's residence.

Pavilions and waterside gazebos, carved beams and painted rafters — one could tell the Qin family ancestors had been people of great taste.

The young servant led them into the garden. Summer flowers bloomed like brocade, butterflies fluttered everywhere. Just as they walked in, suddenly there was a dog's bark.

A large hound as tall as a person charged out from the side, barking wildly at Xie Jingyu. Xie Jingyu, a scholar, had never seen such a display before and retreated repeatedly in fright.

Yun Chu stood in place without moving. This large hound had a rope tied around its neck — it simply couldn't pounce and bite them.

"Lady Xie has such courage!" Qin Mingheng emerged. "Lord Xie, an eight-foot tall man, is actually inferior to a woman. Tsk tsk."

Xie Jingyu's expression was ugly.

He lowered his head and cupped his hands. "Marquis, this official and my wife have come bearing thorns to apologize. Yesterday when the Marquis brought the Young Lord to the Xie family to drink wine, it gave the Xie family face. But this official failed to teach his son properly, causing my worthless son to injure the Young Lord. My worthless son's leg is ruined for this lifetime. This official has sent him to an estate to reflect. He has received the punishment he deserves. I beg the Marquis to be magnanimous and give this official a chance to atone."

Yun Chu took the inkstone from Tingshuang's hands and respectfully presented it with both hands. "This is an extremely rare Songhua inkstone. I ask the Marquis to accept it with a smile."

Qin Mingheng didn't enjoy reading and couldn't care less about any Songhua inkstone, but this was an inkstone Yun Chu had personally delivered.

He walked over and received the inkstone. After glancing at it, he held it in his hand playing with it, then looked askance at Xie Jingyu. "Lord Xie doesn't think that bringing your wife to apologize will make this Marquis let this matter go, does he?"

Xie Jingyu's fingers secretly clenched tight. "I ask the Marquis to enlighten me."

"Five years ago, Lord Xie came to my door begging me to produce an extremely rare divine medicine." The corners of Qin Mingheng's lips curved in a smile. "At that time, what price did Lord Xie pay? Do you still remember?"

Xie Jingyu's heart sank heavily.

Five years ago, on the eve of his wedding to Yun Chu, his mother Yuan Shi's illness had suddenly worsened. She vomited blood constantly all day, spending most of her time unconscious.

He inquired everywhere and finally learned that Marquis Xuanwu had divine medicine passed down from his ancestors, said to be able to cure a hundred illnesses.

He used the Yun family's connections to gain entry to the Marquis's residence. When he knelt before Marquis Xuanwu requesting the divine medicine, the Marquis had proposed a demand that made him tremble all over even now when he recalled it.

"Lord Xie's wedding night — may I have it instead?"

He still remembered the sinister look when Marquis Xuanwu said these words, as if he wanted to devour him alive.

Only then did he know that Marquis Xuanwu, who had married the Luo family's daughter, actually harbored unusual thoughts toward the General's residence's legitimate eldest daughter, Yun Chu.

"What is Lord Xie thinking about? Your expression is so ugly?" The mockery at the corners of Qin Mingheng's mouth deepened. "This is all because this Marquis has been a poor host. Someone, serve tea to Lord Xie and Lady Xie."

A maid brought up two cups of tea and placed them before Yun Chu and Xie Jingyu.

Yun Chu's upbringing told her that when visiting, when the host served tea, whether thirsty or not, one must symbolically take a sip — this was the etiquette of being a guest.

She picked up the teacup and brought it to her lips.

"Madam."

Xie Jingyu cried out.

Yun Chu's tea-drinking motion stopped. She turned her head. "What is it?"

Qin Mingheng leaned back in his chair. "What, does Lord Xie think there's a problem with my tea?"

Xie Jingyu gripped his cup tightly.

Bringing Yun Chu to the door — hadn't he anticipated this very scene?

Five years ago, Yun Chu had used that one night to exchange for his mother's life.

The current Yun Chu was long no longer that pure young lady from the General's residence. Using her one night again to exchange for the Xie residence's peace — what was wrong with that?

Having clearly already made such a decision, why did he feel hesitation when seeing this cup of tea?

He discovered for the first time that he truly was an extremely hypocritical person.

Xie Jingyu spoke slowly. "Be careful the tea is hot."

Yun Chu lowered her eyes. "Thank you for the reminder, Husband."

She brought the teacup to her lips and lightly took a sip, but didn't swallow the tea. She used her handkerchief to wipe the corners of her mouth, imperceptibly spitting that mouthful of tea onto the handkerchief.

Though her movements were very small, Qin Mingheng had been watching her with his peripheral vision the whole time, so naturally he saw.

He couldn't help but laugh mockingly. His tea had nothing in it at all, yet she was so vigilant she wouldn't drink a single sip.

Yet five years ago, in the nuptial wine she and Xie Jingyu shared, there had been enough knockout drug to render a grown man unconscious.

At this moment, Luo Shi came with maids, her face full of smiles. "Lord Xie and Lady Xie have both come to our door. Marquis, please don't hold yesterday's matter against them anymore."

"I received some good tea. Lady Xie, please come sit in my courtyard for a while." Luo Shi smiled at Yun Chu. "It just happens to be the noon hour. Will Lady Xie accompany me for lunch?"

Yun Chu naturally wouldn't refuse. She rose and followed Luo Shi to the rear courtyard.

The two had just left when the smile on Qin Mingheng's face disappeared completely. He said coldly, "Lord Xie isn't leaving yet — do you wish to stay and dine with me?"

Xie Jingyu clenched his fists. "This official takes his leave."

Watching his figure disappear at the Marquis residence gate, Qin Mingheng's expression grew even colder.

It was such a selfish, despicable scoundrel — where was he worthy of Yun Chu?

He walked to the study and pressed a mechanism. Inside was a painting room. The walls were covered entirely with portraits of the same woman. On the table was also a handkerchief.

He took down a portrait and murmured, "Yun Chu, I'm the one who wronged you. If I had defied the imperial decree and not married Luo Shi, could I have become husband and wife with you..."

He married the Luo family's daughter, and she became the Xie family's wife.

In Luo Shi's courtyard, Yun Chu drank tea and accompanied her for a meal. She was extremely careful, secretly spitting everything that entered her mouth onto her handkerchief.

It wasn't that she was overly guarded against people, but Marquis Xuanwu and Xie Jingyu clearly didn't get along. She had to be carefully on guard.

After chatting with Luo Shi for a while, she learned that the rumors in the outside world were true — besides Luo Shi, Marquis Xuanwu's residence had no second woman.

Which man in this dynasty didn't have three wives and four concubines? Yet Marquis Xuanwu could do this for Luo Shi.

When the time was about right, Yun Chu bid farewell to Luo Shi, then went to the front courtyard to meet up with Xie Jingyu.

The young servant in the front courtyard told her that Xie Jingyu was in Marquis Xuanwu's study discussing matters, and asked her to sit briefly in the study's side hall.

Yun Chu nodded and followed to sit in the side hall.

Ice basins had been placed on all four sides of this side hall. Even though the sun was fierce, one couldn't feel the heat at all.

chapters.title: Xie Jingyu Is Unworthy
chapters.content:
Yun Chu sat briefly in the side hall.

Then she saw a figure slowly walking over. She stood up to bow. "Marquis."

With her peripheral vision, she glanced behind and didn't see Xie Jingyu.

"Is Lady Xie waiting for Lord Xie?" Qin Mingheng sat down in a chair. "Then I must apologize — actually, Lord Xie left long ago."

Yun Chu frowned.

Since Xie Jingyu had left early, why had the Marquis residence's young servant still brought her here?

She turned her head and discovered that the maids and matrons who had been waiting at the side hall entrance earlier had all withdrawn at this moment.

Qin Mingheng looked at Tingshuang standing behind her. "You may leave first."

Tingshuang stood without moving.

Yun Chu spoke lightly. "A lone man and woman together in a room violates propriety. This is this subject's wife's trusted maid. Whatever the Marquis has to say, please speak freely."

Qin Mingheng raised his eyes to look at her. "Lord Xie left Lady Xie alone at the Marquis residence. Lady Xie still guards her virtue for her husband like jade — don't you find that laughable?"

"The Marquis meeting alone with a married woman also makes this subject's wife find it laughable." Yun Chu raised her eyes. "The outside world all says Marquis Xuanwu's deep affection for the Marchioness never wavers. Is that truly the case?"

A man who deeply loved his wife would never trick her, a married woman, into coming here alone.

Thinking of this, Yun Chu turned to leave.

She had the confidence to turn and leave because she was the Yun family's legitimate eldest daughter.

She had just taken a step when Qin Mingheng's angry voice came from behind. "Stop."

Yun Chu's steps paused, then continued walking outward.

"Lady Xie, some time ago you reburied your child who died young. Are you so certain that those two sets of bones were your children?"

Yun Chu pressed her lips tightly together.

The man behind her had actually precisely grasped her weakness.

She could be certain that Marquis Xuanwu must have been watching her for some time. What exactly was his intention?

She took a deep breath, turned around, raised her eyes and said coldly, "Whatever the Marquis wants to say, please speak plainly."

"This identity of Lady Xie truly doesn't match you. You're so intelligent — why don't you think about why Xie Jingyu left alone?" Qin Mingheng approached her. "He's not even afraid of leaving you alone at the Marquis residence to make him a cuckold. Why are you afraid of being alone in a room with me?"

Yun Chu retreated a step, avoiding his approach.

"Yun Chu."

Qin Mingheng called her by name directly.

Yun Chu's brows furrowed tightly. She felt repulsed and retreated again.

"Divorce him. Xie Jingyu is unworthy." Qin Mingheng braced one hand against the door frame behind Yun Chu and the other hand against the wall, trapping her in a small space.

Tingshuang was so frightened she lost her voice. She quickly moved to block herself behind Yun Chu.

Qin Mingheng reached out and pushed, directly pushing Tingshuang out.

He bent down, approaching Yun Chu's ear. "If you divorce, I'll also divorce immediately. I can marry you..."

"Slap!"

A resounding slap struck Qin Mingheng's face.

This was the second time Yun Chu had slapped someone.

She hadn't expected she would actually strike Marquis Xuanwu's face.

"Marquis Xuanwu, please conduct yourself properly!" Yun Chu knocked aside his hand bracing the door frame and stepped out over the threshold. She turned her body sideways, her eyes flashing with icy light. "You truly should divorce. You're completely unworthy of your wife."

Having said this, she turned and left. Tingshuang quickly supported her. The master and servant ignored the iron-faced Qin Mingheng and walked directly outside the Marquis residence.

The carriage they had arrived in was actually gone.

Yun Chu's face turned cold to the extreme.

She didn't return to the Xie residence but went to the ice shop that was about to open.

Chen Defu had purchased a large compound — the front for the shop, the back as a warehouse. It would be called Chen Family Ice Shop.

It was selected to open in mid-May. Because those who could afford to buy ice blocks were wealthy people, the ice price was set relatively high — two taels of silver per pound.

She gave Chen Defu some of her own suggestions and adjusted the price increases before leaving the ice shop.

At this time, it was still early, and Yun Chu had eaten almost nothing for lunch. She found a restaurant, and the master and servant pair ate to their hearts' content.

After dining, they slowly drank some tea. The evening colors gradually descended.

Yun Chu was in no hurry to return. She took Tingshuang to stroll the capital's night market.

When the lanterns were first lit, many small vendors would push carts to the streets to sell various trinkets. Since marrying, Yun Chu had never come to browse again.

She saw someone selling kites and thought Brother Yu would definitely like flying kites.

She saw someone selling sugar figurines and thought Changsheng would definitely like eating sweets. She really liked seeing Changsheng smile sweetly.

Before she knew it, Yun Chu had bought a whole pile of things.

When the sky had completely darkened, Yun Chu and Tingshuang returned to the Xie family.

Her front foot had just entered Sheng Residence's door when Xie Jingyu arrived on her heels.

Yun Chu sat in her seat, looking at him coldly. "Why didn't Husband wait for me before leaving together?"

Xie Jingyu examined her from the strands of her hair to the soles of her feet. She seemed exactly the same as when she left this morning, yet seemed somehow different.

His gaze made Yun Chu's heart grow colder bit by bit.

So for the sake of the Xie family, he could actually hand her, a living person, over to another man with both hands.

If she hadn't sensed something was wrong, what would have happened after drinking that mouthful of tea — she simply didn't dare imagine.

So Xie Jingyu had started scheming against her from this time.

When the Yun family was still prosperous, he actually dared to have such twisted designs on her. Where did he get such audacity?

"Why did Madam return so late..."

Xie Jingyu slowly asked.

"Why did I return so late — why doesn't Husband ask yourself?" Yun Chu stared at him. "The carriage sent you back to the residence but didn't return to the Marquis residence to fetch me. I walked back, so naturally it took some time."

Seeing she only showed slight emotional fluctuation, Xie Jingyu guessed that she must have been drugged unconscious like on their wedding night and didn't know what had happened.

So she didn't know of his baseness.

He breathed a sigh of relief, full of apology. "It's my fault. I shouldn't have been busy with official duties and neglected Madam."

"You and I as husband and wife need not speak of such things." Yun Chu acted as if she didn't care about this matter at all, asking with concern, "Has Marquis Xuanwu accepted the Xie family's apology?"

Xie Jingyu nodded. "The Marquis said he would no longer pursue this matter."

Yun Chu smiled faintly.

Marquis Xuanwu had received a slap from her. This matter wouldn't be settled so easily.

chapters.title: The Ice Shop Opens
chapters.content:
Just as Yun Chu had expected.

The next day she heard that Lord Yu had bitterly scolded Xie Jingyu at the palace gates and transferred all the official documents that Xie Jingyu had been responsible for to Lord Yuan.

Although Xie Jingyu had the Yun family as backing, he hadn't smoothly advanced to upper fifth rank. Plus, the Xie family had recently made frequent blunders and offended Marquis Xuanwu. Many people at court were waiting to see an even bigger joke.

"Father, this might be a good thing." Xie Shi'an picked up the fragments on the floor, his tone calm. "These past five years, the Xie family has been too prominent. The top scholar rode through the streets on horseback, then immediately married a first-rank general's legitimate daughter. In just five years, promoted two ranks — those who advance in office so quickly in this dynasty can be counted on one hand. How many people are jealous of Father? Now that Father has been relieved of his official duties, it can be considered giving those people what they wished for. Father can properly rest for a period of time."

Xie Jingyu's expression was dark. "Marquis Xuanwu has no intention of letting the Xie family off."
